<!-- foundations/usage.md -->

# Using WebKit in an app

> Start from a block, find a component, import it tree-shakeably, app-level setup and the quality checklist.

## Overview

`@aziontech/webkit` is the Azion design system: a set of themed, accessible Vue 3 components. This project depends on it. When you build or review UI here, reach for a webkit component first, import it with the flat path, and style with `@aziontech/theme` tokens. This skill is the paste-safe reference for doing that right.

## Start here: one app layout, then each screen is a page body

The chrome is composed **once**, in `App.vue`, around `RouterView`, from the layout of the surface:

```vue
<script setup>
  import ConsoleLayoutRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/console-layout-root'
  import { navigation } from './navigation'
</script>

<template>
  <ConsoleLayoutRoot
    :navigation="navigation"
    :breadcrumbs="$route.meta.breadcrumbs ?? []"
    :account="{ name: 'Jane Doe', email: 'jane.doe@example.com' }"
  >
    <RouterView />
  </ConsoleLayoutRoot>
</template>
```

- **Console:** `ConsoleLayout` — navigation rows `{ id, label, icon, href }` (an in-app `href` is
  followed with the app's router, no `@navigate` wiring needed) and the active row follows the
  route; `actions`, `account-menu`, `search`, `header-leading`, `breadcrumbs`, `notifications` and `tools` slots. A page
  opens the shared palette with `useConsoleLayout().openSearch()`
  (`@aziontech/webkit/use-console-layout`); a body that also renders on its own calls
  `useConsoleLayout({ optional: true })`, which returns `null` outside a layout. Bind `v-model:navigation-open` to persist the rail or
  to offer `Collapse sidebar` in the palette (`search` slot + `@search-select`). A page sets its own
  trail, control crumb included, with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`, and a full-height workspace puts
  `data-layout-fill` on its root (never `calc(100dvh - …)`).
- **Site:** `SiteLayout` — `navigation` and `footer` are the `SiteHeaderSection` and `SiteFooterSection` data. The
  site is dark: `<html data-theme="dark">`. `SiteFooterSection` binds its language select with
  `v-model:language`; switch the locale from that value.
- **Docs:** `DocLayout` — the docs tree, section links, `outline-groups`, and `actions`,
  `navigation-footer`, `aside`, `footer` slots. The document scrolls. The page feeds the "On this
  page" rail by itself: every `DocHeading` with an `anchor` (level 2 or 3) and every
  `DocChangelogEntry` registers with the layout, in document order, so App.vue passes nothing per
  page and a page never renders `DocLayout`; a page with no anchored heading (the docs home) shows no
  outline rail and no `aside`. A drill row
  (`type: 'drill'`) opens in place and the rail's Back reads `Back to Docs` (`rootLabel` renames it);
  never add a hand-made Back row.

The shell blocks (`shell/console`, `shell/site`, `shell/docs`) are these layouts with
the real navigation: copy one as your `App.vue` and replace its stand-in body with `<RouterView />`.
`npx @aziontech/webkit add shell/console` writes the block into your views folder and prints the
path (`src/views/console.vue`): move that file to `src/App.vue`, and skip the route it suggests.
A page never renders its own `<main>`, `AppLayout`, `Sidebar`, `AppHeader`, `SiteHeaderSection`,
`SiteFooterSection` or `Command`. Every platform block is a page body; the one exception is a screen with no rail — a
create flow (`create/*`, headed by the `top-bar/creation-bar` bar) or a
signed-out screen (`auth/sign-in`): route it outside the layout (a route meta `App.vue` reads), and
it keeps its own bar and `<main>` (`webkit-navigation`). An app with two surfaces (a marketing site
and its docs) does the same: `App.vue` picks `SiteLayout` or `DocLayout` from a route meta
(`meta: { layout: 'docs' }`) around one `RouterView`, and every page stays a body. The `shell/docs`
variants are such bodies: `webkit add shell/docs --variant Article` copies the shell (your App.vue
or docs layout) and the page side by side.

## A screen begins from a block

Before composing anything, check whether the screen already exists as a block:
`npx @aziontech/webkit search <the screen in plain words>` ("login", "account settings", "delete
confirmation"), or the `webkit` MCP `search_blocks`. Read the best one with
`npx @aziontech/webkit view <block-id>` (or `get_block`), then start the screen with
`npx @aziontech/webkit add <block-id>` (`--variant <state>` for another state): it copies the SFC
into the views directory, checks its imports, records it in `webkit.blocks.json` and prints the
route entry. `npx @aziontech/webkit diff <block-id>` later shows what you changed against the
canonical block, and `npx @aziontech/webkit remove <block-id>` (`--dry-run` first) deletes a copy you
no longer need with its `webkit.blocks.json` entry, then lists the imports left to remove. Before adapting it, read the guidelines (`view`, or the `guidelines` field
`get_block` returns): when to use the screen and when another block fits better, what each building block (A,
B, C…) is for, do and don't, the copy rules and the accessibility rules. If "When not to use"
matches your case, switch to the block it names. Then change only the content of the copy,
keeping to the guidelines. Only when no block fits, compose from components (below).

A block takes its data through props and emits its actions; it fetches nothing. `add` copies its
data files beside it (`<name>.sample.ts`, and an API adapter when the block ships one). To go live,
do not rewrite the block: render it from the routed page that owns the request and pass what the
request returns (its `## Data` guidelines list the props and events):
`<TableView :resources="rows" :loading="pending" :error="message" @refresh="load" @retry="load" />`.
A data prop left out renders the sample; pass `[]` for none, and delete the `.sample.ts` file and
its import once real data flows. A state variant (`--variant Empty`) is the same block with other
props, so it imports the primary instead of copying it. A marketing band is a page section, not a block (rule
`webkit-sections`).

## Headers and the docs home — never hand-build these

- **Every app header has search.** A console, demo, docs or site header puts `SearchTrigger`
  (`@aziontech/webkit/search-trigger`) first in `AppHeader.End`, opening a `Command` palette;
  it draws `Search … ⌘K` (`Ctrl K` off macOS) on a wide bar and the magnifier on a narrow one, and
  binds the shortcut. `ConsoleLayout`, `SiteLayout` and `DocLayout` already carry it, wired to
  their palette (rule `webkit-header-search`, lint `webkit/require-header-search`).
- **A docs home is `shell/docs --variant Landing`.** It opens on `DocHero` (display
  title with air above it, deck, `Get started` then `CopyPromptButton` — the dark "Copy prompt"
  chip carrying the Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Cursor marks — and a note), then the first section
  opens on `DocAgentCard` ("Your AI agent, fluent in Azion" with the inline Copy prompt; "Prefer the
  guided route?" with the orange Agent setup over a halftone) above the Console, CLI and API
  `DocCard`s (`az az-azion`, `az az-azion-cli`, `az az-azion-api`). Framework templates use the
  brand-colour icons (`az-color az-react`). Do not substitute `DocPageHeader`, a `DocPrompt` or a
  `DocCard` with an overline for these.

## Which skill for which task

Structure and states first, polish last:

- **Structure:** `/webkit-ux-heuristics` (right component per moment) · `/webkit-ui-states` (loading,
  empty, error, async) · `/webkit-form` · `/webkit-create-surface` (page vs drawer) · `/webkit-errors`
  (where a failure goes) · `/webkit-tables` · `/webkit-lists` · `/webkit-navigation` (shells,
  levels, breadcrumb, and drawers: never the way into a resource; `large`, then at most one `medium`)
- **Layout:** `/webkit-layout` · **Words:** `/webkit-microcopy`
- **Foundation:** `/webkit-quick-cleanup` (tokens, typography, spacing rhythm)
- **Cross-cutting:** `/webkit-theming-dark-mode` · `/webkit-data-viz` · `/webkit-ai-surfaces` (AI chat
  and agent actions)
- **Polish:** `/webkit-motion-polish` → `/webkit-final-polish`
- **Verify:** `/webkit-ui-verify` (real browser, both themes, several widths, axe)
- **Adopting WebKit in an existing app:** `/webkit-adoption`
- **A whole product screen, end to end:** `/webkit-product-screens` (the routing table: which skill
  or rule owns each design problem, and what enforces it)
- **An Azion web page (site, product or Solution page, campaign):** `/webkit-site-pages`, under rule
  `webkit-site-pages` (the Web Design Guide, SD-01 to SD-25)
- **Azion API:** `/webkit-azion-api` (CORS, the dev and edge proxy, where the personal token
  lives) · `/webkit-query-explorer` (a Metrics or Events GraphQL explorer from WebKit pieces)

## How to find a component

Do not guess a component name or import path. Look it up.

1. Ask the webkit MCP. The server exposes tools grounded in the exact webkit version this project installed. Arguments are JSON fields of the call; required ones are in bold, and `surface` is `app`, `site` or `docs` (console screens: `app`):
   - `search_blocks` — **`query`** (the screen in plain words), `surface`, `fragments` (boolean). Start every screen here.
   - `get_block` — **`id`**, `variant`, `sections` (`["guidelines"]` or `["sfc"]`).
   - `suggest_component` — **`need`** (what you are building, e.g. `"a ranked top list"`), `surface`; the block, section or component that fits, with alternatives.
   - `search_components` — **`query`**, `surface`.
   - `get_component`, `get_import`, `get_usage_example`, `get_best_practices` — **`name`** (kebab-case, e.g. `"bar-list"`).
   - `list_components` — `category`, `surface`, `cursor`, `limit`; `list_categories` — none; `list_tokens` — `category`; `list_assets` — `kind`, `query`.
   - `validate_usage` — `import`, `classes`, `component`: confirm a subpath is real and a class string is allowed.
2. No MCP? Read `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/llms.txt`. It links one Markdown page per block (`llms/blocks/<id>.md`: guidelines, variants, the primary SFC), per component (`llms/components/<name>.md`: props, events, slots, examples, accessibility, do and don't, with the same data as JSON in `<name>.json`) and per foundation (`llms/foundations/`: tokens, color, typography, spacing, motion, i18n, RTL, devices). `llms-full.txt` is every page in one file.
3. Read the catalog directly. `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/catalog.json` has an `imports` object; every key is a real published subpath (`button`, `empty-state`, `table`, ...). If a subpath is not a key there, it does not exist.

## App-level setup (`setup` in the catalog)

A few components need **one-time wiring in the app entry before first use** — the catalog entry (and `get_component` on the MCP) carries it in a `setup` field. When `setup` is non-null, apply it BEFORE emitting code that uses the component, and check whether the project already has it (do not duplicate).

- **Toast**: fire-from-anywhere (`toast.success('Saved')`) only renders if a region is mounted. Wire the service once in the entry — `import { ToastPlugin } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast'` and chain `.use(ToastPlugin)` onto `createApp()`; the plugin mounts the region automatically (options: `app.use(ToastPlugin, { position: 'top-end' })`). A manually mounted Toaster also counts — never add both blindly (the store keeps only the first region active, but one wiring is enough). `npx webkit doctor` flags toast usage with no wired region.

- **Theme (light or dark)**: with no `data-theme` the theme follows the device (`prefers-color-scheme`). An app that is always dark sets `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` in `index.html` (`<html lang="en" data-theme="dark">`), so the first paint is dark, and an app that is always light sets `data-theme="light"`; a toggle writes `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` (`'dark'` / `'light'`), and a `.dark` class on an ancestor works too. Every token switches with it — never add per-theme classes (`/webkit-theming-dark-mode`).

- **WebkitProvider (languages)**: mount it once at the app root; pass `locale` when the user chose one, or leave it unset to follow the device locale (`en-US` on the server and until mount, then `navigator.language`). Every built-in string a component ships (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) then reads from the locale's catalog, and dates, numbers, file sizes and plurals format with `Intl` for that locale; `dir` follows the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left). English is built in; Portuguese and Spanish are opt-in: import them from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR` and `@aziontech/webkit/locales/es` and pass them through `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), or the provider falls back to English and warns in development. With no provider every component formats for the device locale and reads English text. Only what people read follows the locale: send the `v-model` value to your server (Calendar a `Date`, DateRangePicker ISO 8601 instants, TagEditor `key`/`value` pairs), never a printed label. A label prop you pass still wins over the catalog; `messages` renames a built-in string for the whole app. Import it as `import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'`.

```vue
<!-- App.vue -->
<script setup>
  import { es } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/es'
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'

  const catalogs = { 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider
    :locale="user.locale"
    :catalogs="catalogs"
  >
    <RouterView />
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>
```

In your own components, `useLocale()` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-locale` returns the active `locale`, `dir`, `t(key, params)` and the `Intl` helpers (`formatNumber`, `formatDate`, `formatRelativeTime`, `formatList`, `formatFileSize`, `plural`), so your numbers and dates match WebKit's. `t` reads the provider's catalog; pass the English messages it should fall back to when no provider is mounted (`useLocale(en)`, with `en` from the same import).

## Must Have

- ✅ Flat import: `import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'`.
- ✅ PascalCase binding matching the last path segment: `@aziontech/webkit/icon-button` -> `IconButton`.
- ✅ One `WebkitProvider` at the app root with the user's locale and the catalogs of every language the app offers.
- ✅ Color, spacing, radius, and typography from `@aziontech/theme` tokens (`var(--primary)`, `var(--spacing-md)`, `text-button-lg`).
- ✅ `import './webkit.css'` (the theme, the fonts and `./webkit.sources.css`, as `webkit init` writes it) and `import '@aziontech/icons'` once near the app entry (e.g. `src/main.ts`).
- ✅ `webkit()` from `@aziontech/webkit/vite-plugin` in `vite.config`: it keeps `src/webkit.sources.css`, the WebKit files Tailwind compiles, in step with your imports. Without Vite, run `npx @aziontech/webkit css` after adding or removing a WebKit import.
- ✅ The tree-shakeable `<name>-root` path (or specific sub-components) when you only need the root.
- ✅ Icons via the `@aziontech/icons` font: side-effect import once (`import '@aziontech/icons'`) + the icon CSS classes.
- ✅ Artwork and icon names from the published lists: `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/foundations/` (`illustrations.md`, `diagrams.md`, `line-figures.md`, `brand-marks.md`, `icons.md`) or the MCP `list_assets` (`variant`, plus a `query` such as "ddos" or "delete"). Icon classes are `az az-<name>`, and `az-color az-<name>` for a colour logo; pick one by what it stands for (`list_assets` gives each icon's group, category and meaning, and a product icon names only that product). WebKit 6 uses only the Azion set: write `az az-check`, never the removed `pi pi-check` set (the default `@aziontech/icons` entry no longer loads it; `webkit migrate v6` rewrites old classes).
- ✅ A webkit component reused instead of a hand-rolled or third-party equivalent.

## Must Not Have

- ❌ Category-prefixed import: `@aziontech/webkit/feedback/skeleton`.
- ❌ `/src/` or deep-internal imports: `@aziontech/webkit/src/components/...`.
- ❌ Barrel import: `import { Button } from '@aziontech/webkit'` (no barrel exists).
- ❌ Binding that disagrees with the path: `import Chip from '@aziontech/webkit/chips'`.
- ❌ Hardcoded color: `#fff`, `rgb(...)`, `hsl(...)`, `text-[#1e40af]`, or raw Tailwind palette (`bg-blue-600`).
- ❌ Restyling a webkit component: `<Button class="bg-(--primary)">`, `:class`, `style` on its tag. Use its props; put your classes on your own wrapper or in its slots. Only layout utilities (size, flex and grid placement, order, logical margins) may sit on the tag, each optionally behind a breakpoint prefix (`sm:` to `2xl:`): `w-full`, `h-full`, `max-w-*`, `min-w-*`, `max-h-*`, `min-h-*`, `flex-1`, `flex-auto`, `flex-initial`, `flex-none`, `grow`, `grow-*`, `basis-*`, `shrink-0`, `self-*`, `justify-self-*`, `place-self-*`, `order-*`, `col-span-*`, `col-start-*`, `col-end-*`, `row-span-*`, `row-start-*`, `row-end-*`, `m-*`, `mx-*`, `my-*`, `mt-*`, `mb-*`, `ms-*`, `me-*`.
- ❌ An illustration, diagram, figure or mark name guessed from a file in `src/` or from the page title: an unknown illustration renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder, an unknown diagram or figure draws nothing.
- ❌ `ai ai-<name>`, `ai-cor ai-<name>` or `ai-color ai-<name>`: the old base classes are gone in WebKit 6. Use `az az-<name>` and, for a colour logo, `az-color az-<name>` (never `az-<name>-color`).
- ❌ A default/namespace binding of `@aziontech/icons` (`import Icons from '@aziontech/icons'`) — it is a font; import it for side effects only.
- ❌ A custom Button, Modal, Table, Tooltip, etc. when webkit ships one.
- ❌ Passing a translated label to every instance (`aria-label="Fechar"` on each close button) instead of setting the locale on `WebkitProvider`.

## Common Patterns

### Import + tokens

Tokens style **your own** markup around a component. The component keeps its own look and changes
it only through its props (`variant`, `size`); a class or style on its tag is restyling it (rule
`webkit-style-override`):

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
</script>

<template>
  <section
    class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md) rounded-(--shape-card) bg-(--bg-surface) p-(--spacing-lg)"
  >
    <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">Changes apply to every domain.</p>
    <Button
      variant="primary"
      label="Save"
    />
  </section>
</template>
```

### Compound vs tree-shakeable root

`Table` (and every other composition component) has two import shapes. Lead with the compound, the
form the examples and blocks use; reach for the root path only when you render the root alone:

```ts
import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table' // compound: Table.Row, Table.Cell, ...
import TableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root' // root only, no dot-notation parts
import TableRow from '@aziontech/webkit/table-row' // one part on its own
```

Bind each import to the PascalCase of its path: `table-root` is `TableRoot`, never `Table`, so
`<Table.Row>` never appears on a binding that has no parts.

### Lazy-load a heavy overlay

```js
import { defineAsyncComponent } from 'vue'

const Dialog = defineAsyncComponent(() => import('@aziontech/webkit/dialog'))
```

### Docs pages: code samples and diagrams

- A code sample is `DocCodeGroup`. Set `language` on every sample; the block shows a label header
  with its readable name (Shell, JavaScript, JSON) by default.
- A **command** block holds only what the reader runs; its copy control copies exactly that (a
  leading `$ ` prompt is drawn but not copied). What the command prints goes in the sample's
  `output` field, drawn as a separate muted "Output" block with no copy control, or in prose. Never
  write output into the command as `# HTTP/2 200` (lint `webkit/no-output-in-command`, rule
  `webkit-code-samples`).
- A standalone printout (a deploy log) is `<DocCodeGroup type="output" …>`, not a "Text" sample.
- A flow diagram in a docs column is `Diagram` with one `row`: in the docs column it stacks, the
  nodes are centred, connectors run through the centre of each node and an edge label sits on its
  line. Do not offset nodes or labels to fake that.

### Logos, badges and photos

Logos, compliance badges and illustrations ship in the package: import the file and pass the URL
(`import magalu from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/magalu-extended-color.svg'`, then
`logo: magalu`). Names follow `<brand>-<extended|symbol>-<color|mono|reversed>` (`extended` is the
wordmark, `symbol` the mark; `color` for light surfaces, `reversed` for dark ones, `mono` in one
ink); `catalog.json` lists every file under `imports` with `"kind": "asset"`. A client wall
(`ClientQuotesSection`, `LogoWall`) on the dark site shows each brand in colour: `-extended-color` where it
reads on black (GPA, Zoop, HeroSpark, Magalu), `-extended-reversed` where the colour logo has dark
lettering (Axur, Contabilizei, Dafiti, Global Fashion Group); a one-ink registry `mark` only for a client with no
logo file. Photos, covers,
banners and clips are your content: pass URLs your app serves, or
`@aziontech/webkit/assets/placeholder-image.svg` / `placeholder-clip.webm` until you have them.
Never copy a root-relative `/marketing-components/…` or `/media/…` URL from azion.com or the docs
site: your app does not serve it (lint `webkit/no-root-relative-asset`).

### Large data and server rendering

- Pass the whole list: `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `LogViewer` and `CodeBlock` mount long lists (over 300 rows) in chunks as they scroll into view, and `Tree` renders collapsed children only when expanded. Do not page or slice the data yourself to make them fast.
- `Chart` takes 10k points per series; its hidden data table keeps an even sample of 1,000 rows, so turn on `tableView` when people need every value on screen.
- `PhoneInput` loads its flag sprite the first time the country list opens; the closed field costs no image download.
- Every block and example renders on the server (`renderToString`). Keep `window` and `document` out of `setup` in your own screens: read them in `onMounted`.

### App entry (styles + icons)

```ts
// src/main.ts
import './webkit.css' // the theme, the fonts and the WebKit files this app imports
import '@aziontech/icons'
```

`src/webkit.css` imports `./webkit.sources.css`, one `@source` per WebKit file the app imports, so
the stylesheet holds only the classes of the components you use. A bare `import '@aziontech/theme'`
compiles no component class: the components render unstyled.

## Quality Checklist

Before you finish UI work in this project:

- [ ] Every webkit import is flat (`@aziontech/webkit/<name>`), no category, no `/src/`, no barrel.
- [ ] Every binding is PascalCase of its subpath's last segment.
- [ ] No hardcoded colors — all color/spacing/typography via `@aziontech/theme` tokens.
- [ ] Icons imported individually; the whole set is never bulk-imported.
- [ ] Root-only usage takes the `-root` path; heavy overlays are lazy-loaded.
- [ ] No custom component reinvents something webkit already provides (checked via MCP or `catalog.json`).
- [ ] `./webkit.css` and `@aziontech/icons` are imported once at the app entry, and `npx @aziontech/webkit css --check` passes (the Vite plugin keeps it so).
- [ ] `WebkitProvider` wraps the app once with the user's locale, and `catalogs` registers every non-English language the app offers.

## Part B — using a webkit component in your project

Install the ESLint plugin and enable the `recommended` preset — **every rule is `error`**, so
off-pattern usage fails your lint.

```js
// eslint.config.js
import webkit from '@aziontech/webkit/eslint-plugin'
export default [...webkit.configs.recommended]
```

| Do this | ❌ Avoid | ✅ Do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Import** | `import { Button } from '@aziontech/webkit'` | `import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'` |
| **No internal / typo** | `@aziontech/webkit/src/…` · `…/buton` | `@aziontech/webkit/button` |
| **Tree-shaking** | `import Table` (compound) when you only render the root | `import TableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root'` |
| **Don't override styles** | `<Button class="p-8" />` | compose inside its slots, or use a `styleSeam` component |
| **No deprecated** | importing a deprecated component | the suggested replacement |
| **Tokens, not colors** | `class="text-[#fff]"` | `class="text-(--text-default)"` |
| **Icons** | `import Icons from '@aziontech/icons'` | `import '@aziontech/icons'` (side-effect) |

**Discover the API before you write it:** the webkit MCP server (`npx -y @aziontech/webkit-mcp`, wired
into `.mcp.json` by `init`) answers
`list_components`, `get_component`, `list_tokens`, `suggest_component`, `get_best_practices`,
and `validate_usage` — so an AI (or you) gets the right import / token / prop _before_ the lint
has to reject the wrong one.

<!-- blocks/account/account-hierarchy.md -->

# AccountHierarchy (`account/account-hierarchy`)

> The account hierarchy: organizations, groups and workspaces in one `DataTable` with tree rows (`get-sub-rows`, `v-model:open-keys`, a treegrid with the row-focus keyboard map) and row selection.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/account/account-hierarchy/account-hierarchy.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("account/account-hierarchy")`
- Components: Alert, Avatar, Button, Card, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, Input, KeyValueList, Link, MultiSelect, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Select, Table, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellId`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTags`, Tabs, Tag, Toast, Tooltip, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

manage resources; resource hierarchy; account hierarchy; organizations and workspaces; resource tree; tree table; move resources; bulk actions on a tree; gerenciar recursos; hierarquia de contas; organizações e workspaces; árvore de recursos; mover recursos

Where an account admin arranges the account's hierarchy. Workspaces sit under groups, groups under organizations, and a role binding set on a parent applies to everything under it, so where a workspace lives decides who can reach it. The page shows the whole hierarchy as one tree table, lets the admin select across levels and act on the selection (move, label, delete), and shows the role bindings and labels of the one resource selected. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Any parent and child structure of billable or permission-bearing resources: organizations, groups, folders, projects, workspaces.
- Bulk changes where the position in the hierarchy matters (moving under a new parent, deleting a branch).

## When not to use

- A flat list of one resource type: use `view/table-view`.
- Switching the current account: use the account switcher in `shell/console`.
- Editing who belongs to a team: use `account/team-permissions`.
- A read-only file or folder browser: use `view/file-browser`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Toolbar — `Button`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- C. Resource tree — `Input`, `Card`, `DataTable`, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellId`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTags`, `Avatar`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `Link` (required)
- D. Details panel — `Card`, `Tabs`, `KeyValueList`, `EmptyState`, `Tag` (required)
- E. Move — `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `Field`, `Select` (required)
- F. Labels — `Dialog`, `Field`, `MultiSelect` (required)
- G. Delete — `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- H. Empty and failure — `EmptyState`, `Alert` (conditional)
- Outcomes — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/account/account-hierarchy.md](blocks/account/account-hierarchy.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `AccountHierarchyResource`, `AccountHierarchyRoleBinding` and `AccountHierarchyProps` are exported from `account-hierarchy.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample hierarchy the block renders when `resources` is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `resources`, `currentId`, `roleBindings`, `selectedKeys`, `loading`, `error`.

Event: `refresh`, `retry`, `move`, `labels`, `delete`, `undo`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/account/account-hierarchy.md](blocks/account/account-hierarchy.md).

## Do

- Keep selection per row: selecting a group does not select its workspaces; Delete then says how many are inside.
- Open the destination after a move so the moved rows are visible.
- Say what moves with a resource, and what happens to its inherited bindings, before the move.
- Keep deleted resources recoverable and link to where they wait.

## Don't

- Don't offer a resource, or anything inside it, as its own new parent.
- Don't hide the chevron behind hover; leaves keep a blank space of the same width so names align.
- Don't put a separate expand button in the tab order; the row is the tab stop and Arrow Right and Arrow Left open and close it.
- Don't delete a branch without counting what is inside it.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Manage resources`. **Create:** `Create Workspace`, `Create Group` (the entity keeps its capital, as in `Create Team`).
- **Search:** `Search resources`; no match `No matching resources`, `No resource matches “…”.`, `Clear search`.
- **Bulk:** `Move`, `Labels`, `Delete`; row menu `View details`, `Move`, `Edit labels`, `Delete`.
- **Panel:** `No resource selected`, `1 resource selected`; empty states `Select a resource`, `Several resources selected`, `No labels`; `Select a resource to see its role bindings and labels.`; `Select a single resource to see its role bindings.`; `This resource has no labels.`
- **Toasts:** `2 resources moved to Digital services.`; `3 resources scheduled for deletion.` with `They stay in Resources pending deletion for 30 days.`; `Labels updated on 1 resource.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The table is a `treegrid` labelled by the Resources heading. Rows carry `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-expanded` when they have children, and `aria-selected` when selected.
- One row is in the tab order. Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between rows, Home and End go to the first and last, Arrow Right opens a row or moves into it, Arrow Left closes it or goes to its parent (mirrored right to left), Enter toggles it and Space selects it. Tab reaches the checkbox, ID copy and row menu of the focused row.
- The chevron is pointer-only and hidden from assistive technology; the row's `aria-expanded` is the state.
- The action row is a `role="group"` named `Resource actions` (plain Tab order, no arrow-key toolbar); disabled bulk buttons stay visible so the actions are discoverable.
- The details heading is a polite live region, so a change of selection is announced.
- Dialogs trap focus and return it to the button that opened them.

## States

- Default: two organizations, three groups and six workspaces (`resources`); the first organization and its first group open, nothing selected, and every action wired.
- Selected: one workspace selected (`selectedKeys`); bulk actions enabled and the details panel filled.
- Empty: no resource (`resources` is `[]`); an empty state with Create Workspace.
- Loading: the first load (`loading` with no `resources`); the table's loading rows.
- Error: the hierarchy did not load (`error` is set); a danger Alert with the message and Retry.

## Related

- `account/team-permissions` — what a role binding grants.
- `account/users` — who the members of a binding are.
- `view/table-view` — the flat list page this one extends with tree rows.
- `view/file-browser` — moving objects between folders with the same Move dialog pattern.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Selected` · `Empty` · `Loading` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/account/account-hierarchy.md](blocks/account/account-hierarchy.md), `get_block("account/account-hierarchy", { variant })`.

# ActivityHistory (`account/activity-history`)

> The account's audit log: a `PageHeader` with Documentation over one controls row (`PropertyFilter` on event, category, user and IP address; a `DateRangePicker` for the period, last 30 days by default; Refresh, Downloa…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/account/activity-history/activity-history.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("account/activity-history")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, CopyButton, DataTable, DateRangePicker, EmptyState, IconButton, PageHeader, PropertyFilter, Table, `TableCellTime`, Tag, Tooltip, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

activity history; audit log; audit trail; account activity; security log; who did what; user activity; event history; histórico de atividades; log de auditoria; trilha de auditoria; atividade da conta

The account's audit log. An admin or a security reviewer answers "who did this, from where, and when": a token that was revoked, a role that changed, a sign-in that failed, a plan that was upgraded. They narrow the log by period, category, person and address, read the newest events first, copy an IP address into another tool, and export what they found. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The account or organisation audit log: sign-ins, security changes, member and role changes, billing changes, deploys.
- Any append-only list of events people search by who, what, where and when.

## When not to use

- Request logs or metrics explored over time with a chart: use `view/events-explorer`.
- The deploy history of one resource: use `detail/deployment-logs` or the details page's history tab.
- A short "recent activity" card on a dashboard: use `Item` rows in a `Card` and link here with View all.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)
- C. Period — `DateRangePicker` (required)
- D. Listing actions — `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- E. Event table — `Card`, `DataTable`, `TableCellTime`, `Tag`, `CopyButton`, `useCollection` (required)
- F. No match and empty period — `EmptyState` (required)
- G. Load failure — `Alert` (conditional)

What each part takes: [blocks/account/activity-history.md](blocks/account/activity-history.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `ActivityHistoryEvent` and `ActivityHistoryProps` are exported from `activity-history.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample events and the fixed clock the block renders when `events` and `now` are left out (the events never show while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `events`, `now`, `range`, `loading`, `error`.

Event: `refresh`, `retry`, `update:range`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/account/activity-history.md](blocks/account/activity-history.md).

## Do

- Write each event as a past-tense sentence with the object's name: `Revoked personal token “Nightly export”`.
- Show the newest first and keep the exact time on the tooltip.
- Keep IP addresses left to right and copyable.
- Keep the period and the filters in the controls row, the export last but one, preferences last.

## Don't

- Don't let anyone edit or delete an event from this page.
- Don't put the period in the property filter, or show a period with no events as an error.
- Don't truncate the event sentence without the full text on the row.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Activity history`. **Filter:** `Filter activity`. **Period:** `Activity period`.
- **Categories:** `Sign-in`, `Security`, `Users`, `Billing`, `Deploy`.
- **Empty period:** `No activity in this period`, then `Nothing happened in the account in the selected period. Select a longer period to see older events.` and `Show the last <next preset>`; at 90 days, `Nothing happened in the account in the last 90 days, the longest period events are kept.` with no action.
- **No match:** `No matching events`, `No event in this period matches these filters.`, `Clear filters`.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- No `main` of its own (the layout's is the only one); the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`; the table is named `Activity history`.
- The filter and the period picker carry `aria-label`s; icon buttons have names that match their tooltips.
- Category is text in a tag, never colour alone; the relative date has the exact time on its tooltip.
- User and IP cells keep their own direction (`dir="auto"`, `dir="ltr"`) inside a right-to-left page.

## States

- Default: ten events over three weeks, the last 30 days selected, with filter, period, refresh, export, preferences, sorting and paging wired.
- Empty: the period (`range`, the last 15 minutes) holds no event; a flush empty state offers the next longer period, the last hour.
- Loading: the first load (`loading` with no `events`); the controls and the table's loading rows.
- Error: the log did not load (`error` is set); a danger Alert with the message and Retry.

## Related

- `view/table-view` — the list page this one follows.
- `account/personal-tokens` and `account/team-permissions` — the screens whose changes are logged here.
- `view/events-explorer` — events over time with a chart and a document pane.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Empty` · `Loading` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/account/activity-history.md](blocks/account/activity-history.md), `get_block("account/activity-history", { variant })`.

# Billing (`account/billing`)

> The Billing page of the account settings: a `PageHeader` with the last update, Refresh and Documentation over `PageTabs` (Bills, Payment methods).

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/account/billing/billing.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("account/billing")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, CurrencyAmount, DataTable, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, IconButton, KeyValueList, PageHeader, PageTabs, PaymentBrand, PropertyFilter, SectionHeader, Skeleton, StatusIndicator, Table, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, Tabs, Tag, Toast, Tooltip, `use-collection`, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

billing; billing page; invoices; invoice history; download invoice; subscription plan; current plan; payment methods; default card; billing email; faturamento; faturas; histórico de faturas; plano de assinatura; métodos de pagamento; cobrança

What the account pays, what it paid and which card it is charged to. An admin checks the current plan and the next charge, moves to another plan, finds and downloads an invoice, and keeps the cards on file current: which one is the default, which ones to remove. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The billing page of an account or organisation: plan, invoice history and payment methods.
- Downloading or exporting past invoices.
- Choosing the card invoices are charged to.

## When not to use

- Comparing plans and upgrading: use `account/change-plan-drawer`, which this page opens from Change plan.
- Entering a new card: use `account/payment-method-card`.
- Usage charts and quotas: use a `dashboard` block.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Button` (required)
- B. Tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)
- C. Load failure — `Alert` (conditional)

- G. Invoices table — `DataTable`, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, `useCollection` (required)
- H. No invoices and no match — `EmptyState` (conditional)
- I. Payment information — `StatusIndicator` (required on the Payment methods tab)

# DeploymentSettings (`account/deployment-settings`)

> The account's Build and deployment settings.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/account/deployment-settings/deployment-settings.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("account/deployment-settings")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, Pagination, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PropertyFilter, RadioGroup, SaveBar, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, Skeleton, Switch, Table, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTime`, Tag, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-lists`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

build and deployment; deployment settings; deployment defaults; binding policy; deployment policy; environment bindings; rebind environment; shared deployment setting; build e deploy; configurações de deploy; padrões de deploy; política de deploy; vincular ambiente

How every deploy in the account routes. A Deployment Setting holds a binding policy (whether a version locks the resource IDs it shipped with) and a deployment policy (one live version, or a URL per version); every environment of every service publishes with exactly one, linked automatically to a setting that matches its own deployment policy. On this page an admin sets the defaults the next service starts with, sees which environment publishes with which setting, points two environments at the same setting so one deploy reaches both, and manages the settings themselves. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Account-wide defaults for how new resources deploy, saved together.
- An overview of which environment uses which shared configuration, with a way to rebind each one in place.
- Managing a list of reusable deployment or routing configurations.

## When not to use

- The deployment settings of one service: use `edit/edit-resource#DeployableSettings`.
- Only the create form: use `create/create-drawer#DeploymentSettings`.
- Running a deploy: use `create/deploy-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. What a Deployment Setting is — `Alert` (required)
- C. New service defaults — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingsRow`, `Select`, `Switch`, `SaveBar` (required)
- D. All services — `Accordion`, `Input`, `Tag`, `Select`, `Pagination` (required)
- E. Deployment Settings controls — `PropertyFilter`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- F. Deployment Settings table — `DataTable`, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTime`, `Card`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `ConfirmDialog`, `EmptyState`, `useCollection` (required)
- G. Create and edit drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `Field`, `Textarea`, `RadioGroup` (required)
- H. Loading and no services — `Skeleton` (conditional)
- Outcomes — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/account/deployment-settings.md](blocks/account/deployment-settings.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `DeploymentSettingsProps`, `DeploymentSettingsSetting`, `DeploymentSettingsService` and the other types are exported from `deployment-settings.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample settings, services and defaults the block renders when those props are left out (and never while `loading` is set).

Prop: `settings`, `services`, `defaults`, `defaultDraft`, `currentUser`, `loading`, `saving`, `error`.

Event: `save`, `discard`, `refresh`, `bind`, `create`, `update`, `clone`, `delete`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import, and persist `bind`, `create`, `update`, `clone` and `delete` the same way.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/account/deployment-settings.md](blocks/account/deployment-settings.md).

## Do

- Offer only settings whose deployment policy matches the environment's; an environment cannot publish with any other.
- Say when a setting is shared, in the table and on every environment row, and warn when a rebind makes a deploy reach more services.
- Keep the defaults behind one SaveBar, and say that Default is never changed when Apply to existing is on.
- Say how many services fall back to Default before a setting is deleted.

## Don't

- Don't offer Edit, Clone or Delete on Default; every environment falls back to it.
- Don't apply the defaults to existing settings without the explicit switch.
- Don't let the deployment policy change on an existing setting; the environments bound to it depend on it.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Build and deployment`. **Action:** `Create Deployment Setting`; the drawer titles `Create Deployment Setting` and `Edit Deployment Setting`, the submits `Create Deployment Setting` and `Save changes`. The label does not change on the way in.
- **No match:** `No matching services`, `No service or setting matches “…”.`, `Clear search`.
- **Sections:** `New service defaults`, `All services`, `Deployment Settings`.
- **Policies:** `Strict`, `Flexible`; `Single`, `Versioned`.
- **Tags:** `System`, `Shared`, `Linked automatically`, `Shared · 2 services`, `1 on a shared setting`.
- **Toasts:** `Deployment defaults saved.`, `checkout-api · Production now publishes with storefront-production.`, `preview-versioned created.`, `legacy-rollout deleted.`
- **Errors:** `This field is required.`, `A Deployment Setting with this name already exists.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The services search is named, and a search with no match is announced as a status.
- The filter is named Filter Deployment Settings; Refresh and Download CSV are icon buttons with an accessible name and a tooltip; the row menu is named `Actions for <setting>`.
- The Services cell is focusable so its tooltip with the service names is reachable by keyboard.
- The SaveBar motion has a `motion-reduce` fallback.

## States

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

## Do

- Name who is affected before requiring MFA.

The drawer is the Checkout of `account/change-plan-drawer` (What's included as a `PlanFeatureList`, the charge, the payment method and the billing address); keep its fields and copy identical to that block rather than diverging.
- Profile: step 3 of 3 (`step` is `2`), the usage and role questions, the onboarding-session switch and Create Organization, which emits `submit` and locks the step while `loading` is set, then answers in one `Alert` in the card: `Organization created.` when `loading` turns off with no `error`, or the `error` message (`The organization wasn't created. Check your connection, then retry. Your answers are kept.`) with Retry.

## Related

- `auth/sign-in` — the screen before it.
- `account/change-plan-drawer` — the upgrade drawer the Plan step opens.

- organization

- Disabled: while the upgrade submits (`disabled`), the Change action is disabled.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/account/personal-tokens/personal-tokens.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("account/personal-tokens")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, CopyButton, DataTable, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, `FieldDescription`, IconButton, Input, PageHeader, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PasswordInput, PropertyFilter, Select, SettingsSection, Table, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellStatus`, `TableCellTime`, Textarea, Tooltip, `use-collection`, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

personal tokens; personal access tokens; api tokens; api keys; access tokens; create token; revoke token; copy token once; token expiration; tokens pessoais; token de acesso; chaves de api; criar token; revogar token

The Personal tokens page of the account settings. A person creates a token for a script, a CI job or the CLI, copies its secret the one time it is shown, sees which tokens are still alive and when each expires or was last used, and revokes one that leaked or is no longer needed. The secret never comes back: the list shows only the name, status and dates, and a lost secret means a new token. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Credentials a person creates for themselves to call the API: personal tokens, API keys, deploy keys.
- Any secret the server returns once: the same reveal dialog (warning, masked value, copy) applies.

## When not to use

- Team or service credentials with roles and scopes managed by an admin: start from `account/team-permissions` and add a scope field to the create drawer.
- Secrets the product stores and shows again (environment variables): use `edit/variables` with masked values.
- A single key shown on a resource's details page: use `CopyButton` beside the value in `detail/resource-detail`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Controls row — `PropertyFilter`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)

- D. Row actions — `DropdownMenu` (required)
- E. No match and empty — `EmptyState` (required)
- F. Load failure — `Alert` (conditional)
- G. Create drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelBody`, `SettingsSection`, `PanelFooter` (required)
- H. Fields — `Field`, `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `FieldDescription` (required)
- I. One-time reveal — `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `PasswordInput`, `CopyButton` (required)
- J. Confirmations and outcomes — `ConfirmDialog` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/account/personal-tokens.md](blocks/account/personal-tokens.md).

Event: `refresh`, `retry`, `create`, `revoke`, `delete`.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/account/personal-tokens.md](blocks/account/personal-tokens.md).

## Do

- Show the secret once, masked by default, with a copy button and a warning that says it will not be shown again.
- Say the exact expiry date while the person picks the duration.
- Warn in the Status column a week before a token expires.
- Revoke behind a confirmation that names the token and what breaks.

## Don't

- Don't show a secret, or part of one, in the list.
- Don't let a token be edited or extended; create a new one.
- Don't offer Delete on a live token; revoke it first.
- Don't toast the reveal; the secret belongs in the dialog, where it can be copied.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Personal tokens`. **Create:** `Create Personal Token` on the page, as the drawer title and on the footer submit.
- **Status:** `Active`, `Expires in 3 days`, `Expired`, `Revoked`. **Last used:** relative time, or `Never used`.
- **Reveal:** title `Copy your new token`; warning `Copy the token and store it somewhere safe, such as a secret manager. After you close this dialog, it cannot be shown again; create a new one if it is lost.`
- **Revoke:** title `Revoke token`; description `Scripts and tools that use “<name>” stop working right away. You cannot undo this.`; button `Revoke token`; toast `Token “<name>” revoked. Requests that use it are now refused.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- No `main` of its own (the layout's is the only one); the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`.
- The `PropertyFilter` (Filter tokens) and every icon-only button carry an `aria-label`; the row menu is named `Actions for <token>`.
- The drawer and the dialogs trap focus, are named by their titles and return focus to their trigger; the first invalid field takes focus after Create.
- The reveal labels the secret field `Token`; the copy result is announced once, by the `CopyButton`.

## States

- Empty: no token (`tokens` is `[]`); the heading and a flush empty state with Create Personal Token.
- Loading: the first load (`loading` with no `tokens`); controls row and the table's loading rows.
- Error: the list did not load (`error` is set); a danger Alert with the message and Retry replaces the table.
- Created: the one-time reveal dialog open after Create (`secret` holds the returned token).

Who can do what in the account. An admin keeps one team per role (Administrators, Developers, Security, Finance), sees what each grants and how many people it covers, and creates or edits a team by ticking View and Edit per resource in one matrix. ## When to use

- Role-based access for an account or organisation: teams, roles or groups that bundle permissions.
- Any grant of view and edit rights over a fixed list of resources.

## When not to use

- Inviting people or assigning them to teams: a users list with a team `MultiSelect` per person.
- Credentials that act as one person: use `account/personal-tokens`.
- Feature flags or plan entitlements: use `settings/settings-form`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Controls row — `PropertyFilter`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)

- Outcomes — through `toast`

CreateTeam and EditTeam are separate pages with their own form state.

Prop: `teams`, `loading`, `error`.

Event: `refresh`, `retry`, `row-action`, `delete`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/account/team-permissions.md](blocks/account/team-permissions.md).

## Do

- Grant through teams only, and say so in the page description.
- In the matrix, make Edit imply View: checking Edit checks View, clearing View clears Edit.
- Give each area a group checkbox that is indeterminate when partly checked.
- Show how many permissions are selected out of the total while editing.
- Say how many people lose access before a team is deleted.

## Don't

- Don't list permissions as a long paragraph in the table; use `TableCellTags` with `+N`.
- Don't offer an Edit checkbox for a resource that has no edit action; show a dash with a hidden "Not available".

## Copy

- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The matrix is the `DataTable` (role `table`) named by its `aria-label`, with column headers Resource, View and Edit and one row group per area whose first row holds the area's checkbox.
- Each matrix checkbox is named `View <Resource>` or `Edit <Resource>`; the area checkbox is named by its label and reports mixed when partly checked.
- After a failed save, focus moves to the name field or to the permissions filter.
- Members are a list named `Members`; after Remove, focus moves to the next member's Remove button, or to Add member when the list is empty.
- The filter is named Filter teams; Refresh and Download CSV carry an accessible name and a tooltip.
- The Back button of the creation frame is named `Back to Teams and permissions`.
- Table name links say where they go on their tooltip; the row menu is named `Actions for <team>`.

## States

ai action approval; approve ai action; user authorized action; agent asks permission; human in the loop; tool call approval; confirm agent command; allow tool; aprovar ação da ia; autorizar ação do agente; confirmar comando; aprobar acción de la ia; approve an agent action; tool approval in chat

The moment an assistant needs permission. The reader asked for something that changes their account — a deployment, a purge, a deletion — and the assistant stops before doing it: it says what it found, shows exactly what will run, and waits for Approve or Deny. The decision stays in the thread as text, and the assistant reports what happened next, so the conversation is also the record of what ran and who allowed it. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: it fills the layout's content region (`grow basis-0 min-h-0`, never `h-dvh`), so only the log scrolls, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use ai-action-approval when an AI assistant proposes an action with side effects inside a conversation (ToolApproval).
- The assistant is about to call a tool or run a command with side effects: deploy, purge, change a rule, delete.
- A one-time decision about a consequential action, made inside the conversation.
- An irreversible action: add a typed confirmation to the card.

## When not to use

- Read-only calls (listing, reading metrics): record them with `ToolCall` and continue without asking.
- Tools the reader already allowed for this conversation: record the call, do not ask again.
- A destructive action the reader started from the UI, not the assistant: use `ConfirmDialog` (see `edit/delete-dialog`).
- Several fields to fill before acting: link to the create or edit page; the card only approves or denies.

## Building blocks

- A. Conversation frame — `Conversation`, `PromptInput`
- B. Request — `ChatMessage`
- C. What the assistant checked — `ToolCall`, `StreamingResponse`
- D. Authorization card — `ToolApproval`, `CodeBlock`
- E. The action running — `ToolCall`
- F. Outcome — `ChatMessage`, `CopyButton`, `Button`

What each part takes: [blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md](blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md).

## Data

The block takes the proposed action and its outcome through props and emits every decision; it runs nothing. `AiActionApprovalAction`, `AiActionApprovalOutcome` and `AiActionApprovalProps` are exported from `ai-action-approval.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample deployment the block renders when `action` is left out.

Prop: `action`, `v-model:decision`, `run`, `outcome`.

Event: `approve`, `deny`, `stop`, `retry`, `send`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md](blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md).

## Do

- Show exactly what will run, with the real identifiers.
- Label the approve button with the verb of the title.
- Dismiss the buttons as soon as the reader decides and show the outcome in text.
- Acknowledge a denial and say nothing ran.
- Expire a request the reader leaves undecided and say nothing ran.
- Require typing the resource name before an irreversible action.

## Don't

- Don't run anything before Approve.
- Don't focus or pre-select Approve, and don't trap focus in the card; it is part of the conversation, not a dialog.
- Don't ask again for a tool the reader allowed for this conversation.
- Don't hide the command behind a summary; show it.
- Don't show secrets or tokens in the command or the tool details.

## Copy

- **Title:** a question naming the action, with the command or tool in code: ``Allow `azion deploy --env production`?``, "Delete the domain `old.example.com`?".
- **Description:** what changes and what stays, e.g. "Deploys build `b-4821` of storefront to production. The current version stays available for rollback."
- **Buttons:** Deny and the verb of the title (Deploy, Delete); "Approve" only for a generic tool call.
- **Typed confirmation:** "Type old.example.com to confirm" (built in).
- **Outcomes:** Approved, Denied, Request expired (built in).
- **Assistant after a denial:** "Got it, nothing was deployed."; **after expiry:** "This request expired. Nothing was deployed."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", present tense.

## Accessibility

- The card is a group named by its title and described by its description; it does not trap or take focus.
- Outcomes are text announced through a polite live region; status color is never the only signal.
- Tool calls announce their status changes (Running, Completed, Failed) through `StatusIndicator`.
- The typed confirmation has a visible label; Approve is disabled until it matches.
- Keyboard order: request, tool calls, response text, command, phrase field, Deny, approve.

## States

- Pending: the deployment waiting for Deny or Deploy (`decision` left at `pending`); Deploy emits `approve` and the page runs the call.
- Irreversible: a domain deletion (an `action` with `variant: 'danger'` and `confirmationPhrase`) that needs the domain name typed before Delete enables.
- Approved: `decision="approved"`, `run="success"` and the assistant's report as `outcome`.
- Denied: `decision="denied"`, `run="denied"` and the assistant's acknowledgement as `outcome`.
- Expired: `decision="expired"` and an `outcome` that says nothing ran.
- Error: `decision="approved"`, `run="error"` and an `outcome` that says what failed and that `b-4790` still serves, with Retry.

## Related

- `ai/ai-chat` — the conversation this card lives in.
- `ai/ai-chat-drawer` — the same flow in a drawer over a resource page.
- `edit/delete-dialog` — confirming a destructive action the reader started.
- `skills/webkit-ai-surfaces` — when to ask, what to show and how to record the outcome.

`Pending` (primary) · `Irreversible` · `Approved` · `Denied` · `Expired` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md](blocks/ai/ai-action-approval.md), `get_block("ai/ai-action-approval", { variant })`.

# AiChat (`ai/ai-chat`)

> The full-page generative AI assistant: a header with the assistant's name, a Preview `Tag` and New chat; before the first message an `EmptyState` that says what the assistant knows, over vertical support prompts from…

- Surface: app

## Asked as

ai chat; ai assistant; chatbot; copilot; chat with ai; generative ai chat; assistant page; ask ai; llm chat; conversational ui; prompt and response; streaming response; chat de ia; assistente de ia; assistente virtual; conversa com ia; chat con ia; asistente de ia; artifact; artifact canvas; generated file; code canvas; canvas de artefato; artefato gerado; full page chat

A full page where a person talks with the generative AI assistant about their account: they ask in their own words, watch the response arrive, check where it came from, and keep going with a follow-up or a new question. The page is the conversation; everything else (header, composer) stays still while only the log scrolls. Use it as the assistant's home; on a resource page, open the same conversation in a drawer with `ai/ai-chat-drawer`. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: it fills the layout's content region (`grow basis-0 min-h-0`, never `h-dvh`), so only the log scrolls, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use ai-chat when the conversation is the page (an assistant page).
- A dedicated assistant page (Console → AI assistant) where the conversation is the main task.
- Open-ended questions across the whole account: how-to, troubleshooting, explaining settings or metrics.
- A conversation the reader expects to scroll back through and continue.

## When not to use

- Help about the page the reader is on, next to their work: use `ai/ai-chat-drawer`.
- The assistant proposes an action that changes the account: add `ai/ai-action-approval` to the conversation, never run it from a response.
- One generated paragraph in a page (a summary of a chart): render `StreamingResponse` in place, no chat.
- Searching documentation by keyword: a search field and results list are faster than a conversation.

## Building blocks

- A. Header — `Tag`, `Button`
- B. Empty state — `EmptyState`, `SuggestionGroup`
- C. Message log — `Conversation`
- D. Prompt — `ChatMessage`
- E. Response — `ChatMessage`, `Reasoning`, `StreamingResponse`
- F. Sources — `Sources`
- G. Response actions — `ChatMessage`, `CopyButton`, `IconButton`
- H. Follow-up questions — `SuggestionGroup`
- I. Composer — `PromptInput`
- J. Artifact canvas — `ChatMessage`, `PromptInput` (Artifact)

What each part takes: [blocks/ai/ai-chat.md](blocks/ai/ai-chat.md).

## Data

The block takes the conversation through props and emits every action; it calls no model. `AiChatMessage`, `AiChatProps` and `AiChatFeedback` are exported from `ai-chat.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the starter prompts the empty state renders when `suggestions` is left out, plus the sample threads the variants pass. The draft in the composer stays local.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/ai/ai-chat.md](blocks/ai/ai-chat.md).

## Do

- Show the loading text only after a second; a response that arrives faster streams directly.
- Keep actions visible on every complete response, not on hover.
- Cite sources inline with numbers and list them under the response.
- Let the reader stop a response and keep what streamed, marked as stopped.
- Keep the composer usable while a response streams so the reader can draft the next prompt.
- Return focus to the composer when a response finishes.

## Don't

- Don't auto-scroll while the reader is reading an older message.
- Don't render model output as HTML; `StreamingResponse` renders Markdown as elements only.
- Don't show actions or feedback on a response that is still loading or streaming.
- Don't use the feedback thumbs for anything but the AI response.
- Don't put more than five support prompts or three follow-ups on screen.
- Don't call the assistant by a person's name or make it apologize; state what happened.

## Copy

- **Title of the page:** `AI assistant`; the Preview tag while in preview.
- **Empty state:** a question the reader would ask themselves, e.g. "How can I help with your Azion account?", and one sentence on what the assistant can read.
- **Support prompts and follow-ups:** written as the reader would ask, under 72 characters, e.g. "How do I purge the cache of one URL?".
- **Placeholder:** `Ask a question`, no end punctuation.
- **Disclaimer (hint):** "The AI assistant can make mistakes. Check important information before you act on it."
- **Loading:** `Generating a response` (built in); `Loading <what>` when fetching data.
- **Error:** what happened, in one sentence, e.g. "The connection was interrupted before the response finished.", with Try again.
- **Stopped:** "You stopped this response."
- **Feedback:** Helpful, Not helpful, Feedback submitted (built in).
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, "select" not "click", "response" not "answer", no "please".

## Accessibility

- The log is a named `role="log"` whose own live behavior is off; a polite live region reads each finished response once, with its author.
- Each message is an `article` named by author and time; avatars are hidden from assistive tech because the author line names the author.
- Responses are `aria-busy` while loading or streaming; the caret is hidden.
- The composer is named Prompt, described by its counter and disclaimer; Enter submits and an IME composition never does.
- Feedback thumbs are toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`, and the submitted state is a status message.
- Keyboard order: header, log (focusable to scroll), each message's links and actions, follow-ups, composer.
- Alignment never carries meaning alone: every message has its author line.

## States

- Empty: `messages` left out or `[]`, with the empty state and four support prompts; selecting one emits `send`.
- Streaming: `loading` with the last assistant message part-way written: its caret, the busy region and Stop in the composer.
- Error: `error` set: the last answer keeps its partial text, with the error line and Try again.
- Artifact: two turns that wrote top-orders.sql in two versions, the canvas open beside them on version 2; a follow-up fills the composer.
- LongThread: six earlier turns as `messages` that overflow the log, opened on the newest response, with `followUps`.
