# DeploySuccess (`create/deploy-success`)

> The outcome screen a create flow ends on, in the terminal column of the wizard page: a heading with its lead and, for a Git source, the scope as a Tag; the deployment card with a preview tile, the service name with a…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/deploy-success/deploy-success.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/deploy-success")`
- Components: Button, Card, CodeBlock, IntegrationCard, Item, Link, SectionHeader, Tag, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

deploy success; deployment successful; deployed; success page; deployment complete; next steps after deploy; wizard finish; deploy concluído; sucesso do deploy; aplicação publicada

The screen a create flow ends on. The user has just watched a deploy finish and needs three answers before leaving: is it live and where, what exactly was created or bound along the way, and what to do next. The page answers them in that order in the terminal column of the wizard, then offers one way out to manage the resource.

## When to use

- A create flow (a template deploy, an import from Git, a source or provision wizard) has finished and the resource is serving, or was created for the first time.
- The flow created or bound more than one resource and the user should see each one.
- A resource was made from the CLI and nothing serves it yet: the CliCreated state shows how to deploy it.

## When not to use

- The run is still going or has failed: keep the create-flow card of `detail/deployment-logs` (InCreateFlow) on screen.
- A resource created from a form that does not deploy: end on the resource's page with a success toast that names it, as `skills/webkit-create-surface` describes; there is no outcome screen.
- An item added inside a resource from a drawer: use `create/create-drawer` and close it on save.
- The onboarding steps for a CLI resource on its Overview tab: use `detail/get-started`.

## Building blocks

- A. Outcome heading — `Tag` (required)
- B. Deployment card — `Card`, `Tag`, `Button`, `Link`, `Tooltip` (required)
- C. Resources list — `Card`, `Item`, `Tag` (required)
- D. Next steps — `IntegrationCard` (required)
- E. Get started — `SectionHeader`, `ToggleGroup`, `CodeBlock`, `Card` (optional)
- F. Manage — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/deploy-success.md](blocks/create/deploy-success.md).

## Data

The block takes what the flow made through props and emits its actions; it fetches nothing. `DeploySuccessProps`, `DeploySuccessDeployment`, `DeploySuccessResource` and `DeploySuccessNextStep` are exported from `deploy-success.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample deployment, resources and next steps the block renders when a data prop is left out.

Prop: `title`, `description`, `deployment`, `resources`, `nextSteps`, `getStarted`.

Event: `next-step`, `manage`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/deploy-success.md](blocks/create/deploy-success.md).

## Do

- Lead with the outcome and the live address; the user came to see it work.
- Tag every resource Created or Bound so the list doubles as a receipt of what the flow touched.
- Open the domain and the repository in a new tab with `Link target="_blank"`, and a `Tooltip` saying so.
- Drop the scope tag and the repository row when the flow had no Git source.
- In CliCreated, replace the deployment card with next steps that deploy the resource, and add the Get started paths for the CLI and GitHub Actions.

## Don't

- Don't celebrate: no confetti, no exclamation, no emoji. State the fact.
- Don't put more than one Recommended tag among the next steps.
- Don't add a Deploy again or Create another action; the user starts a new flow from the Creation Center.
- Don't leave the screen without a way into the resource; Manage is required.
- Don't repeat the resource list inside the deployment card.

## Copy

- **Heading:** the object and the past-tense result in sentence case, e.g. "Resource deployed", or "Resource created" when nothing serves it.
- **Lead:** one sentence with a period, e.g. "You deployed a new resource." followed by "Source:" and the source tag. Never a dangling fragment after the period.
- **Status tag:** one word, e.g. "Live"; resource tags "Created" or "Bound".
- **Links:** verb first, e.g. "Visit site", "Add custom domain"; tooltips name the target, e.g. "Open acme/web-app in a new tab".
- **Next steps:** title verb first in two or three words, e.g. "Customize domain", "View analytics"; description one sentence with a period.
- **Exit:** "Manage service", the verb and its object.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no ampersand, no "please".

## Accessibility

- The heading is the page's only `h1`; the service name and the section titles are `h2`.
- The preview tile is decorative (`aria-hidden`); Visit site names the address.
- Links that open a new tab say so in their `Tooltip`, not only with the external-link glyph.
- Glyphs in rows and cards are decorative and carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the Created or Bound tag gives the state in words.
- A next-step card is one focusable link or button with a visible focus ring; its title and description are its name.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading, deployment card, resources, next steps, Manage.

## States

- Default: a deployed service from a Git source (`deployment` with a `source`), with the scope, the deployment card, four `resources` and three `nextSteps`.
- CliCreated: a resource made from the CLI that nothing serves yet; `:deployment="null"` leaves out the deployment card, one resource row, next steps to deploy it here or on a new service, and `get-started` shows the Get started paths.

## Related

- `detail/deployment-logs` — the run this screen follows (InCreateFlow).
- `create/deploy-template` — a flow that ends here.
- `create/create-wizard` — its CreateAndDeploy variant ends here with its own title.
- `detail/get-started` — the source of the CLI and GitHub Actions steps the CliCreated state embeds; CliCreated copies its section verbatim, so change the command copy there first and copy it here.
- `detail/resource-detail` — where Manage leads.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `CliCreated`. Code: [blocks/create/deploy-success.md](blocks/create/deploy-success.md), `get_block("create/deploy-success", { variant })`.

# DeployTemplate (`create/deploy-template`)

> The deploy template page, a focused flow outside the console shell: the creation header with Back to Creation Center and the Start from a template crumb, the template preview card naming the repository it clones from,…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/deploy-template/deploy-template.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/deploy-template")`
- Components: Accordion, AppHeader, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, Checkbox, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, Input, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupInput`, `InputGroupRoot`, Item, Link, Select, Skeleton, Switch, Tag, Tooltip, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

deploy template; clone template; template deploy page; connect git provider; deploy from template; one click deploy; start from a template; implantar template; clonar template; conectar git; deploy uploaded project; deploy imported repository; implantar projeto enviado; import from git form; import from git; importar do git; where it runs; select a service; choose service to deploy to; install integration template; integration template; add integration to service; origin proxy template; instalar integração

A focused page, outside the console shell, where the user turns a template into a running project. They chose a template in the Creation Center and now need to see what it clones, connect a Git provider if they have none, name the repository it creates, fill the settings the template requires and deploy. The same column then shows the build and the outcome, so the user never leaves the page.

## When to use

- Use deploy-template for the configure-and-deploy step once the source (repository, template or uploaded folder) is chosen.
- The user picked a template, a Git import or an upload from `create/create-hub`, and the next step is to deploy it.
- The flow creates a repository from a source in the user's Git account and deploys from it on every push.
- The template needs a few settings (tokens, a domain) before its first build can run.
- The project must first say which service it runs on (WhereItRuns), or the template is an integration that adds records and a rule to a service instead of cloning code (InstallIntegration).

## When not to use

- Choosing what to start from: use `create/create-hub`.
- A first-level resource created from a form with no source code: use `create/create-page`.
- Provisioning a resource and binding it to another: use `create/create-wizard` (CreateAndDeploy).

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `AppHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)
- B. Template and Git step — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button`, `Link` (required)
- C. Browse templates — `Button` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/deploy-template.md](blocks/create/deploy-template.md).

## Data

The block takes the template and the account through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `DeployTemplateProps` and `DeployTemplateTemplate` are exported from `deploy-template.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample template and account the block renders when a prop is left out. The variants are their own screens (the later steps of the flow) and keep their own records.

Prop: `template`, `account`, `providersHref`.

Event: `back`, `account`, `connect`, `skip-git`, `browse`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/deploy-template.md](blocks/create/deploy-template.md).

## Do

- Keep the template preview card at the top of the column through every phase, so the user always sees what is being deployed.
- Ask for Git first; show the form only once a provider is connected.
- Let Deploy check the form: show each missing required value under its field and open the collapsed group that holds it. Disable Deploy only while the settings load, or on an upload until a Root (/) is picked.
- Keep build and variable settings in their collapsible groups, prefilled with defaults, so a template that needs nothing more deploys in one press.
- Mark a secret variable with the locked Secret checkbox and mask its value, with a show control beside it.
- Hand the same column to the create-flow card of `detail/deployment-logs` (InCreateFlow) on Deploy, then to `create/deploy-success`.
- Trim the form to the repository fields for Import from Git, and to the uploaded files for Upload a Project.

## Don't

- Don't open this flow inside the console shell or a drawer; it is a page with its own header.
- Don't ask for settings the template does not use, or move a required setting out of view.
- Don't create the repository before Deploy is pressed.
- Don't replace the page with a new route for the build; the column changes, the page stays.
- Don't put a Cancel next to Deploy; the back control and Browse templates already leave.

## Copy

- **Breadcrumb:** the entry point, then the template name, e.g. "Start from a template" then "Nuxt E-commerce".
- **Back control:** `aria-label` names the destination, e.g. "Back to Creation Center".
- **Git step:** title states the task, e.g. "Connect a Git provider"; description one sentence saying what happens, e.g. "Nuxt E-commerce is cloned into a repository in your account, then deployed from it on every push."
- **Provider buttons:** verb first, e.g. "Continue with GitHub"; the link names the place, e.g. "Manage connected providers".
- **Form heading:** e.g. "Deploy your project"; settings labels 1 to 3 words with the constraint in the description, e.g. "You can find this token in the API credentials of your store."
- **Groups:** "Build and output settings", "Environment variables"; rows "Key", "Value", "Secret"; the reveal control "Show value" or "Hide value".
- **Errors:** "<label> is required.", e.g. "Root directory is required."
- **Upload:** breadcrumb "Upload a project"; "Project files"; "Root (/)" with "Select a file".
- **Import:** breadcrumb "Import from Git"; preview "Import and deploy the acme-web repository from GitHub."
- **Commit:** "Deploy", the same verb on the button and in the run that follows.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash in labels or `aria-label`s, no parentheses in labels.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark under the header; the step title is an `h2` and the settings group an `h3`.
- The back `IconButton`, the brand link and the account button each have an `aria-label`.
- The repository name has a visible `Field.Label` tied to its input by its `Field`; the privacy switch is labelled Public repository and announces its on or off state.
- Settings use `Field` labels and descriptions, so each input announces its name and constraint.
- Required fields carry the Required marker; a failed Deploy puts each error in a `Field.Error` (`role="alert"`) tied to its input.
- Each `Accordion` trigger is a button that announces its expanded state; the Value input is labelled by its Value label, the Key row by its Key label, and the show control is a toggle with `aria-pressed`.
- The uploaded files list is a `ul` named by the folder, inside a focusable scroll region (`role="region"`, `tabindex="0"`) so it scrolls from the keyboard; while settings load the region is `aria-busy` with one status line.
- The page enter animation stops under reduced motion.

## States

- WhereItRuns: the service chooser before the Git step, with search, Create Service and Continue without a service.
- InstallIntegration: the Origin Proxy integration on service-01; its settings, What gets added and Add to service-01, which shows the required origin message.

# ReleaseImpact (`create/release-impact`)

> The Review and deploy page of a release that carries several resources at once.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/release-impact/release-impact.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/release-impact")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Badge, Button, Card, Checkbox, ConfirmDialog, EmptyState, Field, Input, OverflowCount, PageHeader, SaveBar, Select, Skeleton, Spinner, Switch, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

release impact; review and deploy; release composer; what a deploy changes; dependency versions; deployment impact; impacto do release; revisar e implantar; impacto del despliegue

The Review and deploy page of a release that carries several resources at once: a service, the policy in front of it, its storage, its error page and every dependency they reference. The user is about to put all of it into traffic and needs to see, before deploying, which version of each resource goes out, which dependencies go with it, and every Deployment Setting, environment and project the release reaches. One Deploy release at the foot commits it, after one confirmation.

## When to use

- A release spans several resources that deploy together, each at its own version.
- The release reaches projects through shared Deployment Settings, and the user must see how far it goes before it goes.
- Dependencies are detected from the resources and may be shared between them.

## When not to use

- Deploying one service or project from its page: use `create/deploy-drawer`, which is the default way to deploy.
- Watching several Deployment Settings activate after a deploy started: use `create/deploy-progress-dialog`.
- Reading what a past deploy did: use `detail/deployment-logs`.
- Switching one resource back to an earlier version: use `detail/version-detail` (Revert).

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Outcome — `Alert`, `Button` (required after a run)
- C. Resource cards — `Card`, `Switch`, `Tag`, `Tooltip` (required)
- D. Resource and version — `Field`, `Input`, `Select`, `Tag` (required)
- E. Dependencies — `Badge`, `Accordion`, `Alert`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `Select` (required when a resource references others)
- F. Impact — `Card`, `ToggleGroup`, `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `Alert`, `Button` (required)
- G. Footer and commit — `SaveBar`, `Button`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- Before the review: choosing the Deployment Settings

What each part takes: [blocks/create/release-impact.md](blocks/create/release-impact.md).

## Data

The block takes the release and its impact through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing and runs no deploy of its own. `ReleaseImpactResource`, `ReleaseImpactSettings` and `ReleaseImpactProps` (with the version, dependency, environment and project types) are exported from `release-impact.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample resources and Deployment Settings the block renders when `resources` or `impact` is left out (the impact sample never renders while `loading` or `error` is set). The switches and version selects edit a local copy of `resources`; `deploy` carries the included resources at the versions picked.

Prop: `resources`, `impact`, `loading`, `error`, `truncated`, `deploying`, `deployed`, `deployError`.

Event: `deploy`, `retry`, `edit`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/release-impact.md](blocks/create/release-impact.md).

## Do

- Show every resource and dependency with the version that goes out, including the ones the user did not touch.
- Say what tracking the latest Ready version resolves to now.
- Block Deploy release only for something the user can fix here, and say what it is in the footer.
- Keep Deploy possible when the impact cannot be computed; say the impact is unknown.
- Report the outcome in the page `Alert` with Edit and Redeploy; the toast only announces it and dismisses itself.

## Don't

- Don't hide shared dependencies; changing one changes it everywhere in the release.
- Don't confirm twice: the page is the review, the `ConfirmDialog` is the only step before the run. Deploying one service or one project is `create/deploy-drawer`, which confirms nothing after Deploy; this page is only for a release of several resources.
- Don't keep the user on the page while it runs; the run reports wherever they are.
- Don't draw the Flow view with `FlowDiagram` until its list semantics pass axe.

## Copy

- **Title:** "Review and deploy". **Commit:** "Deploy release"; in progress "Deploying…".
- **Confirmation:** "Deploy this release?" and one sentence with the resources, versions and reach.
- **Selecting settings:** title "Select Deployment Settings"; search "Search 6 Deployment Settings"; "2 selected", "Select all", "Clear"; workloads "4 workloads affected" or "No workloads deploy with it yet"; no match "No Deployment Settings match" with "Clear search"; footer "Select at least one Deployment Setting to continue."
- **Versions:** "Track latest Ready", "resolves at deploy", "Pin a ready version", tag "Current".
- **Blockers:** "<name> has no Ready version, so the release cannot be deployed."
- **Outcome:** "Release deployed." / "The release wasn't deployed." with the cause and that nothing changed in traffic.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: Deploy, never publish; sentence case; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- Each resource card is a `section` named by its type and resource; the Resources heading takes focus on Edit.
- Every `Select` is labelled through its `Field` (visible for the resource, `sr-only` for dependencies).
- The include `Switch` has an `aria-label`; its `Tooltip` repeats it for pointer users.
- The Shared `Tag` sits in a focusable wrapper so its `Tooltip` opens from the keyboard.
- The Impact region is `aria-busy` while loading and announces it in a `role="status"` line.
- In ChooseSettings each group is a `role="group"` named by its heading, each choice card is a `label` around its `Checkbox`, the selected count is a polite live region, and a loading workloads count is read as text rather than a bare `Skeleton`.
- The `ConfirmDialog` traps focus and returns it to Deploy release.

## States

- ChooseSettings: the step before the review; grouped checkbox choice cards with search, Select all and Clear, a loading workloads count, an inactive setting with its activate link, and Continue disabled until one is selected.
- Ready: `resources` all have a version and `impact` is computed; Tree view.
- Loading: `loading` is set while the impact is computed.
- Unavailable: `error` says the impact could not be read; Retry emits `retry`, and a truncated answer sets `truncated`.
- MissingVersion: a resource in `resources` has no `versions`, which blocks the deploy.
- Error: `deployError` says the last run was refused; an error toast announces it, and Edit and Redeploy sit on the page `Alert`.

## Related

- `create/deploy-drawer` — deploying one service or project.
- `create/deploy-progress-dialog` — several Deployment Settings activating after the deploy.
- `state/async-submit` — the toast rule every deploy follows.
- `detail/version-detail` — one version, its history and revert.

## Variants

`Ready` (primary) · `ChooseSettings` · `Loading` · `Unavailable` · `MissingVersion` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/create/release-impact.md](blocks/create/release-impact.md), `get_block("create/release-impact", { variant })`.

<!-- blocks/create/resource-picker.md -->

# ResourcePicker (`create/resource-picker`)

> The card a create flow uses to bind one resource to another: a lead, a ToggleGroup choosing between an existing resource and a new one, then either a hint over a searchable list of the existing resources with a select…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/create/resource-picker/resource-picker.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("create/resource-picker")`
- Components: Button, Card, Field, `FieldError`, Input, Item, SettingsRow, Skeleton, Switch, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

resource picker; select existing or new; choose resource; bind resource; searchable picker; pick application; seletor de recurso; escolher recurso; existente ou novo; optional binding; opt-in binding; protect with firewall; bind firewall; vincular firewall

The band a create flow uses when the resource being created needs another resource that may already exist. The user either reuses one of theirs or makes a new one on the spot, and answers it in one place: an Existing / New choice, then a searchable, paged list of what exists or the few fields that create a new one. The chosen row is marked, every search and load is announced, and a missing answer is flagged above the list where it is seen first. When the binding itself is optional (a firewall in front of a project), the same band sits behind an opt-in switch row and unfolds in place when it is turned on.

## When to use

- Use resource-picker inside a create flow to bind one resource the user may reuse or create; it is a card, not a page.
- A create flow binds a whole resource that the user may reuse or create: the project a service serves, the deployment a release is cut against, the firewall that protects a workload.
- The candidates can run past seven, so the list needs search, paging and a no-match line.
- Creating the bound resource takes one or a few fields that fit in the same card.
- The binding is optional and off by default: wrap the band in the opt-in switch row (OptionalBinding).

## When not to use

- A single field that references an existing resource (a certificate, an environment, a function): use a select row inside the form, as `create/create-wizard` (CreateAndDeploy) does for Environment.
- Choosing where a resource runs as a step of its own, with module tags and an inline create row: use the chooser in `create/create-wizard` or `create/deploy-template` (WhereItRuns).
- Browsing or managing the resources themselves: use `view/table-view`.
- Creating the bound resource needs its own full form: New opens that form in a drawer over the page (`create/create-drawer`) instead of nesting it in the band. Only a create of several steps opens its page in a new tab.

## Building blocks

- A. Band card — `Card` (required)
- B. Existing / New choice — `ToggleGroup` (required when something exists)
- C. New resource fields — `Field`, `Input` (required in New)
- D. Search and required message — `Input`, `FieldError` (optional)
- E. Resource list — `Item`, `Skeleton` (required in Existing)
- F. Load more — `Button` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/create/resource-picker.md](blocks/create/resource-picker.md).

## Data

The block takes its resources through props, keeps the answer in `v-model`s and emits Load more; it fetches nothing. `ResourcePickerOption`, `ResourcePickerMode` and `ResourcePickerProps` are exported from `resource-picker.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample projects the block renders when `projects` is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop / model: `projects`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model`, `v-model:mode`, `v-model:name`.

Event: `load-more`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import. Set `error` when Next is pressed with nothing chosen and clear it once the user answers.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/create/resource-picker.md](blocks/create/resource-picker.md).

## Do

- Default to Existing when anything exists, and drop the toggle entirely when nothing does.
- Mark the chosen row three ways: background, trailing check and `aria-pressed`.
- Keep the required message above the rows, under the search, so it is read before the list is scanned.
- Offer the other mode in the no-match line, so an empty search leads to creating one.
- Keep the chosen value when the user switches to New and back.
- Keep an optional binding off by default, and prefill the new resource's name from the resource being created.
- Build the band once and pass the noun, icon and options; every flow that binds a resource reads the same (see `skills/webkit-create-surface`).

## Don't

- Don't use radio buttons or a select for a whole resource the user may also create; that is this band.
- Don't show the search for a list that fits in one batch.
- Don't validate the Name while it is being typed, or show required and invalid together.
- Don't render a loading spinner in place of the rows; show skeleton rows in the row shape and keep the visible ones.
- Don't put the create fields in a dialog or a second page; they belong in the same card.
- Don't hide a locked module or leave it looking editable; disable it, keep it on and say why in its row description, never only in a tooltip.

## Copy

- **Card title:** the bound noun, singular, e.g. "Project".
- **Lead:** one sentence on what the binding does, e.g. "What this service serves on each environment, so one service can serve different projects on Production and Preview."
- **Toggle options:** `Existing <noun>` and `New <noun>`, e.g. "Existing project", "New project".
- **Search:** placeholder and `aria-label` name the collection, e.g. "Search projects".
- **Load more:** the verb and the batch size, e.g. "Load 5 more".
- **No match:** the fact, then both ways out, e.g. "No project matches “api”. Create one instead, or clear the search."
- **Required:** what to do, as a sentence, e.g. "Select the project this service serves, or create a new one."
- **Name guidance:** the allowed characters, e.g. "Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens."
- **Opt-in row:** the action as the title, e.g. "Protect with a firewall", and what it does and that it is off by default as the description. A locked module's description ends with the fact, e.g. "Always on."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: "Select", never "Pick" or "Choose"; sentence case; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The `ToggleGroup` has an `aria-label` that states the question, e.g. "Where the project comes from".
- Each row is a native `button` with `aria-pressed` reflecting the selection; the check icon is `aria-hidden`.
- Search has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder.
- A `role="status"` region announces the count after every search, load and no-match, e.g. "5 of 19 projects".
- Skeleton rows are `aria-hidden`; the Load more `Button` carries `:loading` so its busy state is announced.
- The required message is tied to the search group by `data-field-invalid`, and focus stays where it was when it appears.
- The opt-in `Switch` and every module `Switch` carry an `aria-label` equal to their row title; the folded body is `inert`, so its controls leave the tab order while the switch is off; the reveal honours reduced motion.

## States

- Existing: `projects` holds resources; the toggle sits on Existing with the `v-model` row chosen in the first batch.
- New: `mode` is `new` (the user switched to New); the list gives way to the Name field with the allowed characters as helper text.
- Loading: `loading` is set after Load more; five skeleton rows follow the visible ones and the button spins.
- Required: `error` holds the required message after Next was pressed with nothing chosen; the required message sits under the search, above the list.
- Empty: `projects` is `[]`, nothing exists to bind; no toggle, one line saying a new project is created, and the Name field.
- OptionalBinding: the Protect with a firewall switch is on and New firewall is selected; the Name is prefilled from the project and the Firewall modules list has DDoS Protection locked on.

## Related

- `create/create-wizard` — its CreateAndDeploy variant binds its project with this band on the first step and reuses the list for the deployment.
- `create/create-wizard` — the step wizard whose Where it runs chooser follows the same list rules.
- `state/form-validation` — how required and invalid messages appear on submit.
- `Item` — the selectable row the list is built from; see `skills/webkit-form`.
- `ToggleGroup` — the Existing / New segment; see `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

## Variants

`Existing` (primary) · `New` · `Loading` · `Required` · `Empty` · `OptionalBinding`. Code: [blocks/create/resource-picker.md](blocks/create/resource-picker.md), `get_block("create/resource-picker", { variant })`.

# AlertsDashboard (`dashboard/alerts-dashboard`)

> An alerts dashboard: what is open, how severe it is, what kind it is and who is involved.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/alerts-dashboard/alerts-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/alerts-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, BarList, Card, Chart, ChartCard, DataTable, EmptyState, Hint, PageHeader, Select, SeverityTag, Skeleton, StatTile, `TableCellStatus`, Tag, `use-locale`

## Asked as

alerts dashboard; open alerts; alerts by severity; incident dashboard; false positive rate; alert triage; painel de alertas; alertas abertos; alertas por severidade; triage open alerts

The page a security or operations lead opens to triage: what is open, how severe it is, what kind of
alert it is and which entities are involved. It leads with the open counts, shows how many alerts were
raised each day by severity, and ends in the open alerts table, ordered from critical to info, where
the reader picks what to work on next. Severity reads on one scale everywhere: tiles, chart, tags
and tables.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use alerts-dashboard to triage open alerts by severity.
- Alerts carry a severity level and the reader has to decide which to handle first.
- The reader needs both the trend (are we raising more?) and the queue (what is open now?) on one page.
- Alerts name entities (hosts, users, accounts) whose accumulated risk is worth ranking.

## When not to use

- Every request and the rule that decided it, not only alerts: use
  `dashboard/security-dashboard` (ByActor).
- Service health with latency and error thresholds and a short alert rail: use
  `dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.
- Items waiting for a verdict from an analysis engine: use `dashboard/scan-results-dashboard`.
- Only the list of alerts with filters: use `view/table-view`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Period — `Select` (required)
- C. Summary tiles — `StatTile` (required)
- D. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)
- E. Alerts per day — `ChartCard` (required)
- F. Daily stack — `Chart` (required)
- G. Open by severity — `Card` (required)
- H. Loading rows — `Skeleton` (required)
- I. Severity — `SeverityTag` (required)
- J. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- K. Alerts by type — `BarList` (required)
- L. Highest risk and Open alerts — `DataTable` (required)
- M. Alert status — `TableCellStatus`, `Tag` (required)
- N. Load failure — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.md).

## Data

The block takes its figures and records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `AlertsDashboardProps` and the record types (`AlertsDashboardKpis`, `AlertsDashboardLevelCount`, `AlertsDashboardEntity`, `AlertsDashboardAlert`) are exported from `alerts-dashboard.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample period the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `kpis`, `labels`, `series`, `openByLevel`, `types`, `entities`, `alerts`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:period`.

Event: `retry`, `update:period`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Use one severity ramp for every severity on the page, in the same order.
- Sort the open queue by severity first, then by age.
- Mark every count where growth is bad as `inverse`.
- Give each region its own empty state that says why it is empty.

## Don't

- Don't color severity with categorical series tokens, and don't use the severity ramp for anything else.
- Don't show a donut for open by severity; the reader needs exact counts.
- Don't add a per-card period selector.
- Don't collapse the page into one empty state when only some regions are empty; each region speaks for itself.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Alerts`.
- **Description:** one sentence on the page's job. `What is open, how severe it is, what kind it is and who is involved.`
- **Tile labels:** sentence case, no parentheses. `Critical or high open`, `False positives`.
- **Hint:** one sentence definition ending with a period. `Alerts nobody has closed yet, at any severity.`
- **Empty states:** state the fact, then the next step. `No alerts in this period` / `Nothing was raised in the last 30 days. Select a longer period.`, with the chosen period named in the sentence
- **Severity labels:** the level only. `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info`.

## Accessibility

- The period `Select` has `aria-label="Period"`; the tile row is a region labelled `Summary`.
- Severity is always a word in the `SeverityTag`, never a color alone; the chart tooltip lists every level by name.
- Counts and shares use `tabular-nums`.
- The `BarList` carries an `aria-label` naming what it ranks.

## States

- Default: the populated page for the selected period (`v-model:period`).
- Loading: `loading` is set; tiles, chart, bar list and both tables render their own `Skeleton`; Open by severity holds Skeleton rows.
- Empty: a period with no alerts (`kpis` is `{}` and every list is `[]`); tiles show a dash with no delta, and every region keeps its box with an `EmptyState` that says why and what to do next.
- Error: the request for the period failed (`error` is set); tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry.

## Related

- `dashboard/security-dashboard` (ByActor) — every request and its outcome, not only alerts.
- `dashboard/security-dashboard` — blocked traffic and the rules that block it.
- `dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard` — threshold alerts beside service health.
- `SeverityTag` — the one severity scale the page shares.

## Variants

# AnalyticsDashboard (`dashboard/analytics-dashboard`)

> The analytics dashboard pattern: KPI tiles, charts and a table that all read the same period, so one change of range moves every region together: the Period Select in the PageHeader actions sets the comparison of ever…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/analytics-dashboard/analytics-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/analytics-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, Chart, ChartCard, DataTable, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, Dialog, `DialogTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Hint, IconButton, Input, Link, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelBody`, `PanelHeader`, Select, StatTile, StatTileGroup, Tabs, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, `use-locale`, `utils/clipboard`, `utils/csv`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

metrics; metric panel; kpi tiles; sparkline; real-time metrics; analytics dashboard; painel de métricas; indicadores; analytics; traffic analytics; requests over time; period comparison; painel analítico; análise de tráfego; real-time metrics per product; product metrics; metrics by product; period filter; métricas por produto; métricas en tiempo real; expand chart; chart dialog; export csv; copy query; metrics overview; metrics landing; sub-dashboards; status class filter; visão geral de métricas; data dashboard; metrics dashboard; kpi dashboard; stat tiles; data transferred; usage dashboard; usage per project; consumption; breakdown charts; métricas; painel de dados; painel de uso; traffic and usage dashboard

The page a developer or operator opens to see how much traffic their services handled and how well
they handled it: requests, data transferred, success rate and server errors for the period, then the
charts and the table that explain those totals. Every tile, chart and the table read the same period,
so one change of range moves every region together. It is the reference grammar for the other
dashboards: KPI row first, a 12-column grid of `ChartCard`s below, one shared card header.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use analytics-dashboard for KPI tiles, charts and a table over one shared period: Traffic (requests, status codes) by default, Usage for consumption per product or project.
- The reader monitors volume and quality of traffic (requests, bytes, status codes) over a period.
- Several metrics share one time window and one set of dimensions (host, country, status code).
- The reader needs to move from a total to the breakdown and then to the rows behind it.

## When not to use

- Latency percentiles and live service health with an alert rail: use
  `dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.
- Blocked and allowed requests and the rules behind them: use `dashboard/security-dashboard`.
- The reader arranges the cards themselves: use `dashboard/configurable-dashboard`.
- Money split by category over time: use `dashboard/breakdown-dashboard`.
- Real-user web vitals or one banded score: use `dashboard/health-score-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading and period — `PageHeader`, `Select` (required)
- B. KPI row — `StatTileGroup`, `StatTile` (required)
- C. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)
- D. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- E. Aggregation and variation — `Tag` (required)
- F. Line or Bar — `ToggleGroup` (optional)
- G. Control labels — `Tooltip` (required)
- H. Expand — `IconButton`, `Dialog`, `DialogContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `PanelBody` (optional)
- I. More options — `DropdownMenu`, `toast` (optional)
- J. Charts — `Chart` (required)
- K. Table search — `Input` (optional)
- L. Top hosts — `DataTable` (required)
- M. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- N. Product and period — `PageHeader` (optional)
- O. Sub-dashboards and breakdowns — `ToggleGroup`, `Input`, `DataTable`, `EmptyState` (optional)
- P. Overview landing — `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (optional)
- Q. Usage — `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `DataTable`, `Hint`, `Input`, `EmptyState` (optional)
- R. Failure — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.md).

## Data

The block takes its figures through props and emits its actions; it fetches nothing. `AnalyticsDashboardProps` and the record types (`AnalyticsDashboardKpis`, `AnalyticsDashboardCountry`, `AnalyticsDashboardHost`, `AnalyticsDashboardChanges`, `AnalyticsDashboardRange`) are exported from `analytics-dashboard.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample figures the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set). The tile labels, hints and formats, the card titles and the period options stay in the SFC.

Prop: `v-model:period`, `kpis`, `intervals`, `requestSeries`, `statusSeries`, `countries`, `hosts`, `changes`, `range`, `defaultExpanded`, `loading`, `error`, `refetching`.

Event: `update:period`, `retry`.

The queries the card menus copy run as-is against the Azion Real-Time Metrics API
(`POST /v4/metrics/graphql`). What the API expects, so a live page asks for the right shapes:

Card: Requests over time, Status codes, Requests by country, Top hosts.

- Every query takes `limit` and `filter: { tsRange: { begin, end } }`; an aggregate needs `groupBy`, and a ranked list orders by the aggregate (`sum_DESC`), never by the measured field (`requests_DESC` is rejected).
- Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC **without** the trailing `Z` (`2026-11-13T11:00:00`); the block strips a `Z` and milliseconds from `range` before it writes the query.
- `resample: { function: sum, points: 96 }` returns a fixed number of points for a time series, so a long period does not come back as thousands of rows.
- One query returns at most 10,000 rows (`limit: 10000`).
- Data transferred is `aggregate: { sum: bytesSent }`; the Functions product reads `functionsMetrics` (`sum: invocations`) and Edge DNS reads `idnsQueriesMetrics`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Keep the KPI row to the four numbers the reader checks first; put the rest in cards.
- Use one card header layout for every card, so the controls are in the same place.
- Let one period drive every region.
- Keep the period when the product tab changes, so the reader compares products over the same window.
- Give each product the same grammar: four tiles, then cards of two per row.
- Distinguish "nothing recorded" from "nothing matches the search" in the empty copy.

## Don't

- Don't give a card its own period selector.
- Don't offer Line or Bar on a ranked breakdown; bars are the only form there.
- Don't put more than one search on the page header; table search belongs to its table.
- Don't use status colors for categorical series such as countries or hosts.
- Don't sum a rate or a percentile in a legend total; Metrics turns totals off for those cards.
- Don't nest product tabs inside a card; the product is a page-level choice.
- Don't put a product's sub-dashboard switch inside a card; it sits under the product tabs and changes the whole page.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Analytics`. **Description:** `Requests, data transferred and errors your services handled in the period.`
- **Card titles:** noun phrase, sentence case. `Requests over time`, `Status codes`, `Top hosts`.
- **Tile labels:** the metric name only. `Data transferred`, never `Data transferred (GB)`; the unit belongs to the value.
- **Hint:** one sentence ending with a period. `Requests that ended in a server error. A rise is a regression.`
- **Menu items:** verb first. `Copy query`, `Export CSV`.
- **Overview:** footer links read `Open <Product> dashboard`; breakdown searches name what they match (`Search addresses, networks or countries`).
- **Toasts:** `Query copied.` / `Paste it into any GraphQL client that sends your token.`; `The query could not be copied.`; `CSV exported.` with the file name.
- **Metrics:** title `Real-time metrics`; tab labels are product names; aggregation tags name the math (`Sum`, `Median`, `Percentile`).
- **Usage:** title `Data usage`, description `What your projects consumed in the period, against the previous period.`; card titles say what is compared (`Data transferred, this period vs previous`); series `This period`, `Previous period`.
- **Empty state:** `No traffic yet` / `Metrics appear here once a service serves requests.`
- **No-match state:** `No matching rows` / `Change the search.`

## Accessibility

- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` that names its card, plus a `Tooltip`.
- The expanded `Dialog` traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus to the Expand button; its title and description name the card.
- The `ToggleGroup` is labelled with the card it controls.
- The search `Input` has an `aria-label` equal to its placeholder, since there is no visible label.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`; deltas carry a sign and a word, not color alone.
- The product strip is a tab list (`PageTabs`); the region under it is named after the product and the period (`Functions metrics, Last 24 hours`).
- Charts expose their table twin and keyboard model through `Chart`; do not replace them with a bare SVG.

## States

- Default: the populated dashboard for the period (`kpis`, `intervals`, `requestSeries`, `statusSeries`, `countries`, `hosts`, `changes`).
- Loading: `loading`; every tile, chart and the table hold their place with a `Skeleton`; the grid does not reflow.
- Refetching: `refetching`; the period reloads (a new period, a Refresh) over figures already shown: the tiles, charts and table keep their data and every chart holds its previous render at reduced opacity until the new figures arrive. Use `loading` only for the first response.
- Empty: `kpis` is `{}` and the series and rows are `[]`; no traffic in the period, tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and each card keeps its box with an `EmptyState`.
- Metrics: real-time metrics per product, a `PageTabs` strip of products and a `Period` `Select` in the header; each product shows four tiles and four area, line or stacked bar cards, and products with sub-dashboards switch them with a `ToggleGroup`, adding breakdown table cards.
- Expanded: `defaultExpanded="requests"`; the Requests over time card open in the large `Dialog`, with the Line or Bar choice and a 420px plot.
- MetricsOverview: six cross-product tiles and six highlight cards, each with a footer link to its product dashboard.
- Usage: the Data usage page, consumption per meter and per project against the previous period.
- Error: `error` holds the message; the request for the period failed, tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `dashboard/breakdown-dashboard` — when the total is money split by category.
- `dashboard/health-score-dashboard` — real-user web vitals and banded scores.
- `account/change-plan-drawer` — where usage limits are changed.
- `dashboard/configurable-dashboard` — when the reader arranges the cards.
- `dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard` — latency percentiles and an alert rail.
- `ChartCard` / `StatTile` — the card and tile every dashboard shares.
- `view/events-explorer` — the events behind these numbers, row by row.
- `edit/edit-resource` (DataStream) — where the streams counted under Data stream are set up.

# BreakdownDashboard (`dashboard/breakdown-dashboard`)

> A composition dashboard: how a total breaks down into its parts and how that mix moved over time, here the organization’s monthly spend by category.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/breakdown-dashboard/breakdown-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/breakdown-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Chart, ChartCard, DataTable, DonutChart, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Hint, IconButton, PageHeader, Progress, Select, StatTile, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, `use-locale`, `utils/csv`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

composition dashboard; spend breakdown; cost by category; donut chart dashboard; stacked area chart; top contributors; mix over time; painel de composição; gastos por categoria; custos por categoria; total by category over time; spend by category

The page that answers "what is this total made of, and how did the mix move?". The block's example is
the organization's monthly spend: the total and its three largest categories first, then the mix over
12 months, the current month's split, and the resources that drive it, ranked. The same shape fits any
total that breaks down into exclusive parts (storage by type, requests by product, seats by team).

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use breakdown-dashboard when a total breaks into categories over time.
- One total splits into a small number of exclusive categories (up to six, plus Other).
- The reader needs both the current split and how it changed over time.
- The reader has to find the individual items that drive the largest share.

## When not to use

- The parts are not exclusive or do not sum to the total: use a multi-series line in
  `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` instead of a stack or a donut.
- The reader tracks progress against targets: use `dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard`.
- Changing the plan that drives the spend: use `account/change-plan-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Period — `Select` (required)
- C. Export — `Button` (optional)
- D. Total and top categories — `StatTile` (required)
- E. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)
- F. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- G. Area or Bar — `ToggleGroup` (optional)
- H. More options — `DropdownMenu` (optional)
- I. More options trigger — `IconButton` (optional)
- J. Spend by category — `Chart` (required)
- K. Current split — `DonutChart` (required)
- L. Top contributors — `DataTable` (required)
- M. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- N. Category and change — `Tag` (required)
- O. Share of total — `Progress` (required)
- P. Load failure — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/breakdown-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/breakdown-dashboard.md).

## Data

The block takes its figures and records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `BreakdownDashboardProps` and the record types (`BreakdownDashboardKpis`, `BreakdownDashboardContributor`) are exported from `breakdown-dashboard.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample year the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `kpis`, `labels`, `series`, `split`, `contributors`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:period`.

Event: `retry`, `export`, `update:period`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/breakdown-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/breakdown-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Keep the category order and colors identical across tiles, stacked chart, donut and table.
- Put the total first in the tile row, then the parts.
- Show a percentage next to every share bar.
- Mark spend tiles as `inverse`.

## Don't

- Don't use a donut for more than six slices; fold the tail into Other.
- Don't stack series that overlap or do not sum to the total.
- Don't color categories with status tokens; a category is not a state.
- Don't drop the absolute amount and show only the share.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Cost breakdown`.
- **Description:** `How the organization’s spend splits across categories and the resources that drive it.`
- **Tile labels:** the category name only. `Total spend`, `Compute`, `Database`, `Storage`.
- **Card titles:** `Spend by category`, `Current split`, `Top contributors`.
- **Donut center label:** the period it shows. `This month`.
- **Empty state:** `No spend in this range` / `Nothing was billed to the organization in the selected period.`

## Accessibility

- The period `Select` has `aria-label="Period"`; icon-only controls name their card.
- The donut has an `aria-label` (`Current split`) and its legend lists every category with its value.
- Each `Progress` names its resource; the percentage is visible text, not only the bar.
- Amounts and shares use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: the populated breakdown for the period (`v-model:period`).
- Loading: `loading` is set; every tile, both charts and the table hold their place with a `Skeleton`.
- Empty: nothing billed in the period (`kpis` is `{}` and every list is `[]`); tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, the exports disable, and the stacked chart, donut and table each keep their box with an `EmptyState` that names the reason.
- Error: the request for the period failed (`error` is set); tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry.

## Related

- `dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard` — targets and trends instead of parts.
- `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — non-exclusive series as lines.
- `account/change-plan-drawer` — where a reader acts on the spend.
- `DonutChart` / `Chart` — share now, mix over time.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/dashboard/breakdown-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/breakdown-dashboard.md), `get_block("dashboard/breakdown-dashboard", { variant })`.

# ConfigurableDashboard (`dashboard/configurable-dashboard`)

> A configurable dashboard: the reader arranges the cards.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/configurable-dashboard/configurable-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/configurable-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, BarList, Button, Chart, ChartCard, DashboardGrid, DonutChart, Hint, PageHeader, Tag, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-layout`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

configurable dashboard; custom dashboard; drag and drop dashboard; resizable cards; edit layout; dashboard-grid; dashboard grid; dashboard builder; painel configurável; painel personalizado; reorganizar cards; rearrange cards; resize dashboard cards

A dashboard the reader arranges: they move cards, change how many columns a card spans and how tall it
is, and keep that layout. It serves readers who come back to the same page every day and care about
different cards than the default puts first. The page owns the layout (an array of id, span and
height, in order) and binds it to `DashboardGrid`, which moves, resizes, clamps and announces; the
`ChartCard` inside each `DashboardGrid.Item` provides the drag handle and the resize corner.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use configurable-dashboard only when each reader rearranges and resizes the cards.
- The same dashboard serves readers with different priorities, and each comes back often.
- The cards are independent: none depends on its position to make sense.
- The product has somewhere to store per-user preferences.

## When not to use

- A dashboard read once to answer one question, or one whose order tells a story: use a static
  dashboard such as `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` or
  `dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard`.
- The reader needs to add or remove widgets from a palette; this block only rearranges and resizes the
  cards it has.
- A single chart with editable settings: use `ChartCard` alone.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Edit layout, Done and Reset layout — `Button` (required)
- C. Grid — `DashboardGrid` (required)
- D. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- E. Card definitions — `Hint` (required)
- F. Span while editing — `Tag` (required in edit mode)
- G. Split cards — `DonutChart` (optional)
- H. Ranked cards — `BarList` (optional)
- I. Time series cards — `Chart` (optional)
- J. Load failure — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md).

## Data

The block takes its series through props and emits every change; it fetches nothing. `ConfigurableDashboardProps` and `ConfigurableDashboardSeries` are exported from `configurable-dashboard.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample period the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set). The layout is a model, so the page can save it per user.

Prop: `labels`, `series`, `sources`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:layout`, `v-model:editing`.

Event: `retry`, `update:layout`, `update:editing`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Keep the layout as data (id, span, height, order) owned by the page, bind it to `DashboardGrid`, and persist
  it wherever the product stores preferences.
- Give every `DashboardGrid.Item` the card title as its `label`; it is what moves and resizes announce.
- Announce a reset yourself in a polite live region (`Layout reset to the default.`); the board
  announces only what it did.
- Keep every card at its place and size in loading and empty states, so the reader can arrange it
  before data arrives.

## Don't

- Don't show handles outside edit mode; a dashboard that can be dragged by accident is worse than a static one.
- Don't let a card shrink below a span where its content stops reading (3 columns here).
- Don't put card menus, toggles or exports in the header; they conflict with the drag handle.
- Don't hide Reset layout behind a menu once the layout is customized.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Traffic overview`. **Description:** `Requests, regions, errors and response time for the period, in the layout you set.`
- **Mode button:** `Edit layout`, then `Done`. Never `Save`; changes apply as they happen.
- **Reset:** `Reset layout`.
- **Help line:** two short sentences on how, no layout positions. `Drag a card by its handle to move it, or by its corner to resize it. Focus a handle to use the arrow keys.`
- **Handle labels:** verb plus card title. `Move Requests over time`, `Resize Requests over time`.
- **Announcements:** full sentences with a period. `Layout reset to the default.`
- **Empty state:** `No requests yet` / `Metrics appear here once a service serves requests.`

## Accessibility

- The drag handle moves a card with the arrow keys; the resize corner changes span with Left and Right and height with Up and Down (`DashboardGrid` handles both and mirrors them under right-to-left).
- Focus returns to the moved card's handle after a reorder.
- `DashboardGrid` announces every move and resize in its own polite live region; the page announces the reset in an `aria-live="polite"` `sr-only` region.
- The board is a list named `Traffic overview cards`, one item per card.
- `Edit layout` exposes its mode with `aria-pressed`.
- Charts carry an `aria-label` equal to the card title.

## States

- Default: the arranged dashboard, read-only (`v-model:layout`).
- Editing: `v-model:editing` is `true`; handles and resize corners on every card, span tags in the headers, help line visible.
- Loading: `loading` is set; every chart renders its own `Skeleton` inside its card; the layout holds its shape.
- Empty: nothing recorded yet (`series` is `{}`, `sources` is `[]`); each card keeps its place and size and shows its empty state.
- Error: the request failed (`error` is set); every card keeps its place, size and header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load, carries the message and offers Retry.

## Related

- `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — the static version of the same cards.
- `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — a fixed dashboard when the order tells the story.
- `DashboardGrid` — the grid component: layout model, bounds, reorder, resize and announcements.
- `ChartCard` — the card inside each item, with the drag handle and resize corner.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Editing` · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md), `get_block("dashboard/configurable-dashboard", { variant })`.

# DashboardSwitcher (`dashboard/dashboard-switcher`)

> The dashboards hub: one page that switches between every dashboard of the account.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher/dashboard-switcher.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-switcher")`
- Components: Alert, BarList, Chart, ChartCard, FilterMenu, Hint, IconButton, PageHeader, Select, StatTile, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-navigation`

## Asked as

dashboards; dashboard switcher; dashboards hub; dashboard picker; choose a dashboard; observability dashboards; switch dashboard; shared period filter; painéis; seletor de painel; trocar de painel; tableros; selector de tablero

The dashboards hub. The reader comes here to look at one of several prepared views of the account (traffic, usage, edge health, threats, business figures, or a layout of their own) without hunting for each page in the navigation. One control picks the dashboard, one shared period scopes it, and the body under them is the chosen dashboard. Switching keeps the period, so comparing traffic and threats over the same 7 days is two clicks.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- An account has several dashboards that share one time scope, and the reader moves between them often.
- The set mixes platform, security and business views, so a grouped list beats a long navigation menu.
- Some dashboards report on their own calendar (a quarter, a billing cycle) and must say so instead of following the shared period.

## When not to use

- A single dashboard with its own page: use the dashboard block directly (`dashboard/analytics-dashboard`, `dashboard/security-dashboard`, and the rest of `dashboard`).
- A dashboard the reader arranges by hand: use `dashboard/configurable-dashboard` (it is the body of the Custom entry).
- An overview of the whole account with resources and recent activity: use `dashboard/home-dashboard`.

## Pick the dashboard by the shape of the data

| Data shape | Block |
| --- | --- |
| Traffic volume and quality over one period (requests, status codes, hosts) | `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` |
| Consumption per product or project against the previous period | `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` (Usage) |
| Blocked vs allowed requests, attack categories, source IPs | `dashboard/security-dashboard` |
| Each request of known actors with the rule that decided it | `dashboard/security-dashboard` (ByActor) |
| Open alerts to triage by severity | `dashboard/alerts-dashboard` |
| Items waiting for a verdict from an asynchronous analysis | `dashboard/scan-results-dashboard` |
| One total split into categories over time | `dashboard/breakdown-dashboard` |
| Many signals rolled up into one banded score | `dashboard/health-score-dashboard` |
| Real-user web vitals | `dashboard/health-score-dashboard` (RealUser) |
| Latency percentiles, error rates and live state per service | `dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard` |
| Cards each reader rearranges and resizes | `dashboard/configurable-dashboard` |
| The account's landing overview | `dashboard/home-dashboard` |
| A one-page roll-up of business KPIs for leadership | `dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard` |
| Several of these behind one picker and one shared period | `dashboard/dashboard-switcher` |

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Dashboard picker — `Select` (required)
- C. Shared period — `FilterMenu` (required)
- D. Own period — `ToggleGroup` (optional)
- E. Refresh — `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)
- F. Applied period — `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` (required)
- G. Dashboard body — `StatTile`, `Hint`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `BarList`, `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md).

## Data

The block takes its views and the selected view's data through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `DashboardSwitcherView`, `DashboardSwitcherFigure`, `DashboardSwitcherData`, `DashboardSwitcherFigureValue`, `DashboardSwitcherPeriod`, `DashboardSwitcherQuarter`, `DashboardSwitcherFormat`, `DashboardSwitcherMarkForm` and `DashboardSwitcherProps` are exported from `dashboard-switcher.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample views and a generator of their figures that the block renders when `views` or `data` is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop / model: `views`, `data`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:view`, `v-model:period`, `v-model:quarter`.

Event: `refresh`, `retry`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md).

## Do

- Keep the period when the reader switches dashboards; reset only the hover state.
- Load the body on a switch (Skeletons in the final boxes) and refetch it on a period change or Refresh (previous render held), so the controls never jump.
- Hide the shared period for a dashboard that owns its own, and show that dashboard's control in the same place.

## Don't

- Don't list the dashboards as tabs; twelve views in four groups need the grouped picker.
- Don't keep a Period chip that the body ignores.
- Don't put a second period control inside a card.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Dashboards`.
- **Description:** one sentence on what the views cover. `Traffic, security and business views across every workload, plus a layout of your own.`
- **Groups:** one word. `Platform`, `Security`, `Business`, `Yours`.
- **Dashboard names:** a noun phrase in sentence case. `Edge health`, `Funnel and cohorts`.
- **Chip:** the field, then its value. `Period: Last 7 days`.
- **Comparison:** `vs previous 24 hours`, `vs previous quarter`.

## Accessibility

- The picker trigger is named `Dashboard`; the controls sit in a section labelled `Dashboard controls`, the body in a section named after the dashboard, with `aria-busy` while it loads or refetches.
- The period lives in `FilterMenu`, which names its applied count on the Filter button and gives every row and chip its own name.
- Refresh is an icon-only button with `aria-label="Refresh"`.

## States

- Default: Traffic over the last 24 hours.
- OwnPeriod: `v-model:view` set to Executive summary; the shared filter and chip are hidden and the quarter `ToggleGroup` shows.
- Loading: `loading` with no `data`; tiles, chart and list render their Skeletons.
- Error: `error`; the tiles show dashes and each card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` and Retry, which emits `retry`.
- Empty: `data` with no series and no bars; the tiles show dashes, the chart and the ranked list show their empty state (`No data in this period`).
- Refetching: `loading` while `data` is shown, after a period change or Refresh; the chart holds the previous render at reduced opacity and Refresh shows its spinner.

## Related

- `dashboard/configurable-dashboard` — the Custom entry, laid out by the reader.
- `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` (Default and Usage), `dashboard/security-dashboard` — the Traffic, Usage and Threats bodies on their own pages.
- `dashboard/home-dashboard` — the account overview.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `OwnPeriod` · `Loading` · `Error` · `Empty`. Code: [blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md](blocks/dashboard/dashboard-switcher.md), `get_block("dashboard/dashboard-switcher", { variant })`.

# HealthScoreDashboard (`dashboard/health-score-dashboard`)

> A health score dashboard: how well something performs for the people who use it, read as one score out of 100 and its bands.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/health-score-dashboard/health-score-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/health-score-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, BarList, Card, Chart, ChartCard, EmptyState, Hint, Item, PageHeader, Select, Skeleton, StatTile, Tag, Tracker, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

health score; health dashboard; performance score; web vitals; score bands; quality score; pontuação de saúde; painel de saúde; nota de desempenho; real user monitoring; rum; core web vitals; page load time; monitoramento de usuário real; banded score

The page that answers "how well does this work for the people who use it, and where is it worst?".
Experience is reduced to one score out of 100 with three bands (Good at 80 or more, Fair from 50 to 79,
Poor under 50). The page shows the overall score and its trend, ranks applications and locations
lowest first with the top cause of poor samples, gives each application an hour-by-hour strip, and ends
in the open incidents that need someone's attention.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use health-score-dashboard when many signals roll up into one banded score (including real-user web vitals).
- Many raw signals (latency, packet loss, DNS time, Wi-Fi signal) are combined into one score the
  reader can act on.
- The score has fixed bands that mean the same thing everywhere on the page.
- The reader's job is to find the worst application or place and the cause behind it.

## When not to use

- The raw metrics themselves (p50, p95, error rate) matter more than a score: use
  `dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.
- A pass or fail verdict per item: use `dashboard/scan-results-dashboard`.
- Alerts triaged by severity: use `dashboard/alerts-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Period — `Select` (required)
- C. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- D. Definitions — `Hint` (required)
- E. Overall figure — `StatTile` (required)
- F. Band — `Tag` (required)
- G. Loading placeholders — `Skeleton` (required)
- H. Score per hour — `Chart` (required)
- I. Rankings — `BarList` (required)
- J. Hourly strips — `Tracker` (required)
- K. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- L. Open incidents — `Card` (required)
- M. Incident rows — `Item` (required)
- N. Real-user monitoring — `PageHeader`, `Select`, `StatTile`, `Hint` (optional)
- O. Load failure — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/health-score-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/health-score-dashboard.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `HealthScoreOverall`, `HealthScoreHourlyRow`, `HealthScoreIncident`, `HealthScoreBand`, `HealthScorePeriod` and `HealthScoreDashboardProps` are exported from `health-score-dashboard.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample score, rankings, hourly rows and incidents the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set). The RealUser variant is a separate page and keeps its own sample figures.

Prop / model: `overall`, `applications`, `locations`, `hourly`, `incidents`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:period`.

Event: `retry`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/health-score-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/health-score-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Use the same three bands, with the same thresholds and words, in every region.
- Sort rankings lowest first.
- Name the top cause next to every poor score, so the reader knows what to fix.
- State the band thresholds in the overall `Hint`.

## Don't

- Don't show a score without its band word.
- Don't use the status colors for anything other than the bands on this page.
- Don't average away the worst hour; the hourly strip exists to show it.
- Don't sort rankings best first.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Experience score`.
- **Band words:** one word each. `Good`, `Fair`, `Poor`.
- **Cause:** subject, a middle dot, the cause in lowercase. `CRM · slow DNS lookups`.
- **RealUser:** title `Real-user monitoring`, description `Real-user timings collected in the browser, for the selected period.`; tile labels are the timing in sentence case (`First input delay`); the aside of a trend tile is the period name (`Last 24 hours`).
- **Empty state:** name the period. `No open incidents in the last 24 hours` / `An incident opens when an application or a location stays poor for several samples in a row.`

## Accessibility

- Each `Tracker` has an `aria-label` naming its application, and each block a label with time, score and band.
- Bands are always words; the strip is never color alone.
- Rankings carry an `aria-label` (`Score per application`, `Score per location`).
- Loading regions set `aria-busy="true"`.
- Scores use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: the scored period.
- Loading: `loading`; the chart, rankings and trackers render their own `Skeleton`; incidents hold Skeleton rows.
- Empty: a period with no samples (`overall.score: null`, every list `[]`); the score shows a dash with no band, and every region keeps its box with an empty state that names the period and says what fills it.
- RealUser: the real-user monitoring page; the vitals and the trend tiles follow the Period select.
- Error: `error`; the score shows a dash, and every region keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard` — the raw latency and error metrics.
- `dashboard/alerts-dashboard` — when incidents are triaged as alerts by severity.
- `Tracker` — hour-by-hour status strips.

## Variants

## Asked as

home; home page; home dashboard; console home; usage overview; página inicial; início do console; first access; home empty state; new account home; welcome screen; first run; brand-new account; getting started home; primeiro acesso; tela de boas-vindas; home vazia; classic overview; overview dashboard; account summary; recent activity; monthly usage; visão geral; account landing overview

The Console's Home page: the first screen a signed-in user lands on. Its job
is to get them back to work fast. For an account that owns resources it shows a short usage band and
the resources they touch most (projects, resources, domains, recents), every row a link. For a
brand-new account it becomes the first-access screen: a greeting, the command prompt and three doors
to a first project, a first domain and a coding agent. It is not an analytics page; detail lives on
each resource's own dashboard.

The populated Home fits the screen at `xl` (each resource panel scrolls its own rows), so its root carries `data-layout-fill` and scrolls itself (`overflow-y-auto`): below `xl` the root scrolls as one page, its content centred while it fits (`justify-center-safe`). The first-access screen (Empty) is a centred page with nothing pinned; it does not fill, and the layout's `main` scrolls it (`h-dvh` on the populated root only sizes a standalone preview).

## When to use

- Use home-dashboard for the account's landing overview.
- The landing page after sign-in in the Console.
- The reader needs to resume work (open a recent resource) more than to analyse data.
- The same page must serve both a populated and a brand-new account.

## When not to use

- Analysing traffic or usage: use `dashboard/analytics-dashboard`
  (Traffic by default, Usage for consumption).
- The empty first page of one resource list: use `state/first-use`.
- Only the shell, with another page inside: use `shell/console`.
- A placeholder while Home loads: use the Overview and Onboarding wires of `state/page-skeleton`.

## Building blocks

- A. Control labels — `Tooltip` (required)
- B. Icon-only controls — `IconButton` (required)
- C. Usage band — `StatTileGroup`, `StatTile`, `Hint` (required)

- H. Loading — `Skeleton` (required)
- I. First access — `SearchTrigger`, `Card`, `Illustration`, `Button`, `Input`, `Popover`, `Spinner` (required)

The tile labels, units and hints and the panel headings stay in the SFC.
