What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/home-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/home-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Greet by first name in a muted heading; it is the only personal line on the page.
- Make every resource row a single link (`Item` with `href`) and keep row actions on the resource's page.
- Let the user dismiss the agent card for good.
- Show the first-access screen, not a grid of empty panels, when the account owns nothing.
- Open the layout's palette from the first-access prompt with `useConsoleLayout({ optional: true })` and `layout?.openSearch()` (the body also renders alone, in its preview and test, where the call returns `null`); never wrap `useConsoleLayout()` in `try` / `catch`, and never mount a second `Command`.
- Mark the populated page root with `data-layout-fill` and let it scroll, so the panels scroll their rows at `xl` and the page scrolls as one below it.

## Don't

- Don't add charts to Home; link to the dashboard that has them.
- Don't put more than four usage tiles in the band.
- Don't hand-build the band's card, grid or dividers around the tiles; `StatTileGroup` draws them.
- Don't pass figures as strings or flags as `'true'` / `'false'`: a tile's `value` and `delta` are
  numbers, and the string `'false'` is truthy.
- Don't nest the dismiss button inside the card's link.
- Don't show a second highlighted button next to `Agent`.

## Copy

- **Greeting:** time of day and first name. `Good morning, Alex`.
- **Tile labels:** the metric in sentence case. `Data transferred`, `Requests per second`.
- **Tile tooltips:** one sentence with a period. `Total bytes delivered across all your resources.`
- **Agent card:** imperative title plus one sentence. `Set up your coding agent` / `Give your editor a prompt that teaches it to build and deploy here.`
- **Empty panel:** `No <things> yet` with one sentence (`Domains you create show up here.`); Recents: `Nothing opened yet`.
- **Failure:** `Couldn't load <thing>. Check your connection and retry.` with Retry.
- **Prompt label:** `Search resources, pages and commands`.
- **Summary:** section headings `Metrics`, `Resources`, `Recent activity`; card titles `Monthly usage`, `Marketplace trends`; footer links `View all <thing>` in sentence case (`View all DNS zones`).

## Accessibility

- The usage band is labelled `Usage` and the panels `Resources`; the layout owns the header, the rail and the one `main`.
- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` and a `Tooltip`.
- Every resource row is one link in the tab order; its focus ring is the row's.
- On a new account the prompt opens the layout's command palette, which also opens with ⌘K / Ctrl K.
- Entrance animations and the card's dismiss transition honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- Default: populated Home for an account that owns resources (`metrics`, `projects`, `resources`, `domains`, `recents`): usage band, agent card, resource panels.
- Error: `error` holds the message; Home's data could not load, and the usage band and every panel show a danger `Alert` with Retry.
- Empty: `projects`, `resources`, `domains` and `recents` are all `[]`; a brand-new account gets the first-access screen with the greeting, the command prompt that opens the palette, and the three doors (create a project, add a domain with an availability check, set up an agent).
- Summary: the classic overview; metric tiles with the window caption, the resources and recent activity tables, and the aside with monthly usage and a featured marketplace template.

## Related

- `shell/console` — the shell Home renders inside.
- `state/page-skeleton` — the Overview and Onboarding wires that hold Home while it loads.
- `state/first-use` — the first-use state of one resource list.
- `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — where usage detail lives.

# ServiceMonitoringDashboard (`dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`)

> The service monitoring dashboard pattern: a PageHeader with the one window ToggleGroup, status tiles with sparklines, multi-series charts and an alert rail.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, Chart, ChartCard, EmptyState, Hint, Item, PageHeader, Skeleton, StatTile, StatusIndicator, Tag, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

service monitoring; monitoring dashboard; latency p95; error rate; uptime; service health; observability; monitoramento; painel de monitoramento; latência; latency percentiles; error rate per service

The page an on-call engineer keeps open: is every service up, how fast is it answering, how many
requests fail, and which alerts are open right now. One tile per service states its p95 latency and
its state in words; latency percentiles and error rates sit in two charts read over one window; the
open alerts live in a rail on the right that scrolls on its own, so the alerts stay in view while the
reader studies a chart.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shell/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`. Its root carries `data-layout-fill`, so the layout's `main` stops scrolling and the root fills it: from `xl` the charts column and the alerts rail scroll on their own; below `xl` the root itself scrolls, so the page still scrolls as one (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview).

## When to use

- Use service-monitoring-dashboard for latency percentiles, error rates and live state per service.
- The reader watches a known set of services for state changes and threshold breaches.
- Latency percentiles and error rates matter more than volume.
- Open alerts need to stay visible next to the evidence.

## When not to use

- Volume and status codes over a longer period: use `dashboard/analytics-dashboard`.
- Alert triage by severity with a full queue and trends: use `dashboard/alerts-dashboard`.
- One experience score with bands: use `dashboard/health-score-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading and window — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Service tiles — `StatTile` (required)
- C. Service state — `StatusIndicator` (required)
- D. Charts — `ChartCard` (required)
- E. Definitions — `Hint` (required)
- F. Window — `ToggleGroup` (required)
- G. Latency and error rate — `Chart` (required)
- H. Alert level — `Tag` (required)
- I. Loading placeholders — `Skeleton` (required)
- J. Alert rail — `Item` (required)
- K. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- L. Load failure — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md).

## Data

The block takes its records through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `ServiceMonitoringService`, `ServiceMonitoringSeriesData`, `ServiceMonitoringAlert`, `ServiceMonitoringWindow` and `ServiceMonitoringDashboardProps` are exported from `service-monitoring-dashboard.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample services, series and alerts the block renders when a data prop is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop / model: `services`, `latency`, `errorRate`, `alerts`, `loading`, `error`, `v-model:window`.

Event: `retry`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Write the service state in words in every tile.
- Keep alerts in a rail that stays in view; fold it below the charts on narrow screens.
- Title an alert with the threshold that tripped, not with a generic name.
- Drive every tile and chart from the one window in the page heading.
- Mark the page root with `data-layout-fill` and let it scroll (`overflow-y-auto`), so the panes scroll on their own at `xl` and the page scrolls as one below it.

## Don't

- Don't average latency into one line; show the percentiles.
- Don't use the status colors for percentile series.
- Don't make the rail scroll the page with it at wide screens.
- Don't give a chart a window of its own.
- Don't hide the rail when there are no alerts; say `No open alerts`.

## Copy

- **Service state:** one word. `Operational`, `Degraded`, `Down`.
- **Delta label:** what is compared. `p95 latency vs previous 24 hours`.
- **Alert title:** metric, comparison, threshold with unit. `p95 latency above 800 ms`.
- **Alert time:** relative. `12 minutes ago`.
- **Empty rail:** `No open alerts` / `Alerts appear here when a service crosses a threshold.`

## Accessibility

- The window `ToggleGroup` is named `Window`; the page has one `h1` from `PageHeader`, and `Open alerts` is an `h2` under it.
- The rail's `Item.Group` has `aria-label="Open alerts"`. An independently scrolling region must be reachable by keyboard.
- The rail's scroll container is a `region` labelled by the `Open alerts` heading with `tabindex="0"`, so a keyboard user can scroll it in every browser.
- State and level are words (`StatusIndicator`, `Tag`), never color alone.
- Latency figures use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: services reporting, both charts populated, open alerts in the rail.
- Loading: `loading`; every tile, both charts and the rail hold Skeletons; the window switch stays usable.
- Empty: no traffic yet (`latency: null` per service, no series, `alerts: []`); tiles show a dash, both charts say metrics appear once a service serves requests, and the rail reads `No open alerts`.
- Error: `error`; tiles show a dash, and both charts and the alert rail show a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `dashboard/alerts-dashboard` — the full alert queue with severity trends.
- `dashboard/health-score-dashboard` — the same services as one experience score.
- `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — volume and status codes over a longer period.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Error`. Code: [blocks/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md](blocks/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md), `get_block("dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard", { variant })`.

# DeploymentLogs (`detail/deployment-logs`)

> The deploy logs of a build or deploy run with known steps, wherever it is shown: `LogViewer.Steps` lists the pipeline as an Accordion of steps, each with its status glyph and the status in words for assistive technolo…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/detail/deployment-logs/deployment-logs.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("detail/deployment-logs")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Avatar, Button, Card, CopyButton, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, IconButton, LogViewer, StatusIndicator, Tag, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

deployment logs; deploy logs; build logs; pipeline steps; log viewer; phased logs; logs do deploy; logs de build; etapas do pipeline; deployment progress; creation progress; deployment status; build pipeline; deploy failed; status da implantação; deploy flow; fluxo de deploy; first deploy; primeiro deploy; deployment detail; deployment failed; deployment queued; deployment page; página da implantação; implantação na fila

The user started a deployment and wants to know where it is, whether it went live and, when it did not, exactly which step failed and why. This block shows the pipeline as ordered steps, each with its status, its one-line outcome, its time and its own log output, so the user can follow the run as it streams, then read the full output once it settles. It is the one deploy-log block: the same steps sit in the deploy card of a create flow and on a deployment's own page.

## When to use

- Use deployment-logs wherever a build or deploy run with known steps is shown, in a create flow (InCreateFlow) or on a deployment page.
- Inside the deploy card of a create flow (a template deploy, an import from Git, a provisioning run), from the moment Deploy is pressed until the run finishes or fails.
- On a deployment's own page, under its status banner and Deployment details card (DeploymentDetail, DeploymentError, DeploymentQueued).
- Any build or deploy pipeline with a fixed, known list of steps whose output the user needs to read.

## When not to use

- A run of half a minute or more the user is expected to leave and come back to: use `state/async-submit`, which reports the outcome where the user returns (its logs card composes the same `LogViewer.Steps`).
- The outcome once a create flow's run has finished: hand the column to `create/deploy-success`; do not keep the finished card as the last screen.
- A dropped folder being uploaded before anything is built: use the Initializing overlay in `state/project-intake`.
- The overview of the resource the deployment belongs to: use `detail/resource-detail`.
- One function run with its request path and trace: use `detail/invocations`.
- Events or logs explored over time with filters and a chart: use `view/events-explorer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Steps — `LogViewer.Steps` (required)
- B. Toolbar row — `LogViewer.Steps` header slot, `Tag` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/detail/deployment-logs.md](blocks/detail/deployment-logs.md).

## Create-flow card (InCreateFlow, InCreateFlowError)

`Card :padded="false"` at the full width of the flow's column, titled Deployment (Provisioning when the flow provisions rather than deploys). Its header carries the run status opposite the title: a loading `StatusIndicator` with `severity="info"`, Cloning during the splash, then Building (or Creating). The content opens on the cloning splash, which fades in: a small source tile (the Git provider glyph), a dashed connector whose dashes march toward the destination (`animate-flow-dash`, still under `motion-reduce`) and a large destination tile, with one polite live line naming the repository and the scope. Once the first step starts, the content becomes the steps with their controls moved up to the card header: after a failure the header swaps the indicator for the Phased or Complete `ToggleGroup` bound to `v-model:view` (`:view-switch="false"` on the steps) and the footer holds Edit (outlined, back to the form with the values kept) and Redeploy (primary, with its loading state and a Redeploying indicator). Every deploy surface ends a failure with the same two actions (`create/deploy-drawer`, `create/deploy-progress-dialog`, `state/async-submit`, `create/release-impact`).

## Deployment page (DeploymentDetail, DeploymentError, DeploymentQueued)

A page body for `ConsoleLayout`, with no tabs: a status banner (success; danger with Redeploy; info while queued), the Deployment details card with every fact and its Deployment Settings band, then the Deployment logs card. The logs card header carries the duration or the status and the Phased or Complete switch; the steps drop their own toolbar row and progress. Visit stays disabled until the deployment is live. A queued run shows a not-started `EmptyState` in place of the steps, with no switch.

## Data

The block takes the run through props; it fetches nothing and has no actions of its own. `DeploymentLogsStep` and `DeploymentLogsProps` are exported from `deployment-logs.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample runs (running, succeeded, failed) the block renders when `steps` is left out. Running or settled, the outcome, the counts, the open step and the step tags all follow from the step statuses.

Prop / model: `steps`, `duration`, `v-model:view`, `v-model:open-step`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/detail/deployment-logs.md](blocks/detail/deployment-logs.md).

## Do

- Show a step's time only once it has run (done, running, failed); a pending or skipped step shows none.
- Open the failed step automatically and mark every step after it Skipped.
- Show copy buttons only once the run has settled.
- In a create flow, open on the cloning splash the moment Deploy is pressed, so the column never goes blank between the form and the first log line, and hand over to `create/deploy-success` a beat after the last line prints.
- Inside a card, move the toolbar controls up to the card header.

## Don't

- Don't hand-build the step list from `Accordion`, `LogViewer` and status glyphs; compose `LogViewer.Steps`.
- Don't open several steps at once or auto-expand every step after a success.
- Don't print lines for steps that never ran in the Complete view.
- Don't summarize the error in a vague sentence; the failed step shows the reason in full.
- Don't put the run status in a toast while the user watches it; it belongs in the toolbar row or the card header.
- Don't auto-advance to the success screen after a failure, or add a Cancel to the card while the run goes.

## Copy

- **Header:** "Deployment logs"; inside a card, "Logs" under a card titled "Deployment" or "Provisioning".
- **Running status:** count and step, e.g. "3/8 steps", "Build"; the card indicator a progressive word, e.g. "Cloning", "Building".
- **Outcome tags:** a past-tense word, or the failure and its step, e.g. "Completed", "Failed on Routing Rules".
- **Run time:** past tense with the duration, e.g. "Deployed in 42s", "Failed after 42s".
- **Step titles:** a short noun phrase in sentence case, keeping a product name as written, e.g. "Access token", "Install dependencies", "Routing Rules"; descriptions state the outcome without a period, e.g. "478 packages installed".
- **Skipped step:** two sentences, never a dash, e.g. "Never ran. The deployment stopped at Routing Rules."
- **Splash line:** names source and destination in fragments, e.g. "Cloning acme/web-app to acme".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy` and `skills/webkit-errors`: say what failed and why, no "please", no exclamation in console copy.

## Accessibility

- Each step is an accordion trigger, a button that announces expanded or collapsed and is reachable by keyboard in run order; opening a step does not move focus.
- Status glyphs are `aria-hidden`; `LogViewer.Steps` gives each step trigger its status as screen-reader text, and the outcome tag carries the run's, so it never depends on color.
- While the run goes, the step count and step in flight sit in one `role="status"` region, so a screen reader hears each step as it starts; new log lines do not announce one by one.
- The progress bar and the view switch carry the accessible names `LogViewer.Steps` gives them; copy buttons announce what they copy.
- The splash tiles and connector are one `aria-hidden` group; its meaning is the visually hidden live line.
- Shimmer, spinner and connector animations stop under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- Running: the run is in flight (a step is `running` or `pending`); the toolbar shows 3/8 steps and Build, Build is open with the spinner and the progress bar runs along the bottom.
- Success: every step checked (every `steps` status is `success`, `duration` set), the last one open, a Completed tag with Deployed in 42s and the view switch, copy on every step log.
- Error: a step has status `error`; the Routing Rules step is open on its error output with a Failed tag, the steps after it read Skipped and the toolbar names the failed step.
- ContinuousLog: a finished run in the Complete view (`view` is `complete`), every line as one `LogViewer` with its copy button.
- ContinuousLogError: the failed run in the Complete view (`view` is `complete`), the lines up to the error and nothing from the skipped steps.
- InCreateFlow: Deploy was just pressed in a create flow; the Deployment card with a Cloning indicator on the cloning splash.
- InCreateFlowError: the create-flow card after a failure, the switch in the header, the failed step open and Edit and Redeploy in the footer.
- DeploymentDetail: a deployment that went live, the success banner, the Deployment details card and the Deployment logs card.
- DeploymentError: a deployment the rules rejected, the danger banner with Redeploy, Visit disabled and the logs open on the failed step.
- DeploymentQueued: a deployment waiting for a runner, the info banner, Visit disabled, Queued in the details and the logs header, and a not-started `EmptyState` in the logs card.

## Related

- `create/deploy-template` — the template flow that streams the create-flow card after Deploy.
- `create/deploy-success` — where a create flow lands once the run goes live.
- `state/async-submit` — a long run the user leaves and comes back to, with the same steps in its logs card.
- `detail/resource-detail` — the overview of the resource a deployment belongs to; its Deployments tab links here.
- `LogViewer` — `LogViewer.Steps` draws the steps; see `skills/webkit-ui-states` for the running and failed states.

## Variants

`Running` (primary) · `Success` · `Error` · `ContinuousLog` · `ContinuousLogError` · `InCreateFlow` · `InCreateFlowError` · `DeploymentDetail` · `DeploymentError` · `DeploymentQueued`. Code: [blocks/detail/deployment-logs.md](blocks/detail/deployment-logs.md), `get_block("detail/deployment-logs", { variant })`.

# DnsZoneDetail (`detail/dns-zone-detail`)

> A DNS zone detail page, opened from its index: a full-bleed tab bar with Main settings and Records over a scrolling tab panel.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/detail/dns-zone-detail/dns-zone-detail.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("detail/dns-zone-detail")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, CopyButton, DataTable, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem`, EmptyState, Field, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, FileDropzone, IconButton, Input, `InputGroupRoot`, `ItemList`, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PropertyFilter, SaveBar, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, Switch, `TableCellActions`, `TableCellId`, `TableCellLink`, Tabs, Tag, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-navigation`

## Asked as

dns zone; dns records; record table; zone detail; nameservers; dnssec; records list; zona dns; registros dns; tabela de registros; import zone file; zone file; bind import; import dns records; importar arquivo de zona; importar registros dns

The detail page of a resource that owns a long list of records, here a DNS zone. The user arrives from the zones index to do one of two jobs: adjust the zone itself (name, nameservers, DNSSEC, status) and save, or find, add, edit and delete the records the zone answers with. A tab bar splits the two jobs so the settings form and the records table never share a scroll. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

## When to use

- A resource has its own settings and also owns many child records that need search, filters, sorting and paging (DNS records, firewall entries, list items).
- Users copy values out of the resource into another system (nameservers, DNSSEC digests) and need a copy control next to each value.
- Child records are added from inside the resource, so the action reads `Add <Module>`.

## When not to use

- The child list is short and needs no search or filters: use `detail/domains-card` inside a settings section.
- A first-level list reached from the sidebar: use `view/table-view`.
- A resource whose detail page is an overview with several tabs and no dominant record list: use `detail/resource-detail`.
- Settings only, with no child records: use `edit/edit-resource`.

## Building blocks

- A. Tab bar — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)
- B. Settings sections — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `ItemList`, `SettingsRow`, `Input`, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError` (required)
- C. Copyable values — `InputGroupRoot`, `Input`, `CopyButton` (required)
- D. Toggles — `Switch` (required)
- E. Save bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)
- F. Records heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- G. Controls row — `PropertyFilter`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- H. Records table — `Card`, `DataTable`, `TableCellId`, `TableCellLink`, `TableCellActions`, `Tag` (required)
- I. Empty and no-match — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- J. Row actions — `TableCellActions`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem` (required)
- K. Load failure — `Alert` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/detail/dns-zone-detail.md](blocks/detail/dns-zone-detail.md).

## Data

The page takes the zone, its records and both requests' state through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing and fakes no save or refresh. `DnsZoneDetailZone`, `DnsZoneDetailRecord`, `DnsZoneDetailSettings` and `DnsZoneDetailProps` are exported from `dns-zone-detail.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample zone and record the page renders when `zone` or `records` is left out (the records never while `loading` or `error` is set). The settings form keeps its own draft; `zone` is the baseline Discard returns to, and a new `zone` resets the form to it.

Prop: `zone`, `records`, `loading`, `error`, `saving`, `importable`, `v-model:tab`.

Event: `submit`, `discard`, `create`, `import`, `refresh`, `retry`, `row-action`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/detail/dns-zone-detail.md](blocks/detail/dns-zone-detail.md).

## Do

- Keep settings and records on separate tabs, each with its own scroll.
- Show required errors only after a failed save, and clear each one when its field changes.
- Make every copyable value read-only and pair it with a `CopyButton` whose label names the value.
- Raise the save bar only when something changed, and keep it until Save lands or Discard restores the record.
- Reuse the table view controls row and table recipe in the Records tab so filters, search and columns behave the same as on index pages.
- Rewind pagination to the first page when the filter changes.
- Tell an empty zone (Add Record, Import zone file) apart from a filter that matches nothing (Clear filters).
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't put a primary or large Create button in the Records heading; it is `Add Record`, outlined.
- Don't validate on first render or on blur; the form is quiet until Save.
- Don't make nameservers or digests editable text the user could change by accident.
- Don't save Main settings from a button inside each section; one save bar covers the whole form.
- Don't let the records table scroll the page sideways.

## Copy

- **Tabs:** short nouns, e.g. "Main settings", "Records".
- **Section titles:** a noun or a short instruction, e.g. "General", "Configure your nameserver".
- **Row descriptions:** one sentence that ends with a period, e.g. "Give a unique and descriptive name to identify your zone."
- **Required error:** "This field is required."
- **Save bar:** the label states the fact, e.g. "You have unsaved changes."; buttons "Discard" and "Save".
- **Records heading:** title "Records", description one sentence, e.g. "The authoritative records this zone answers with."; actions "Documentation" and "Add Record".
- **Copy buttons:** name the value, e.g. "Copy nameserver 1", "Copy record value".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The form is labeled "Zone settings" and its fieldset has a visually hidden legend with the same words.
- Each `Input` has an `aria-label` matching its row title; an `Input` with an error points to its `FieldError` through `aria-describedby`.
- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` and a `Tooltip` with the same words; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The property filter has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder, "Filter records".
- Focus order follows reading order: tabs, form fields, save bar; or heading actions, the property filter, toolbar, table, pagination.
- Tab panel entrances respect reduced motion.

## States

- MainSettings: the default `tab`, the Main settings tab with General, nameservers, DNSSEC and Status from `zone`; the save bar appears on the first edit and Save spins while `saving`.
- Records: `tab="records"`, the Records tab with the zone's one A record from `records`, the ID column hidden by default; `loading` spins Refresh and loads the table, `error` swaps the table for a danger `Alert` with Retry, and `[]` shows No records yet.
- ImportZoneFile: `importable` puts Import zone file beside Add Record; the page listens to `import` and opens a large `Drawer`. The file comes from a `FileDropzone` (one `.zone`, `.txt` or `.db` file; a rejected or empty file shows an invalid `FieldError` under it) or is pasted into a `Textarea`. Every line is previewed in a `DataTable` paginated at ten lines: line number, name relative to the origin, type, value and a Ready, Skipped or Error `Tag`, with the reason under the value. The counts sit in a polite status line, errors add a danger `Alert` above the preview, and Import N records (disabled at zero) adds only the ready lines, then a toast says how many were imported and how many lines were left out.

## Importing a zone file

- Parse on the client shortly after the text stops changing (a 250 ms pause; a dropped file parses at once) and preview every line, ten per page, before anything is written; never import on drop.
- Name the line number on every row, so the user can fix the file.
- Skip with a reason what the zone manages itself (SOA, apex NS) and types it does not support; mark as errors only values that are wrong.
- Import what is ready even when some lines fail, and say in the toast how many were left out.

## Related

- `view/table-view` — the index this page is opened from, and the source of the controls row recipe.
- `edit/edit-resource` — the settings form and save bar pattern used by Main settings.
- `detail/domains-card` — a short related list inside a settings section.
- `edit/delete-dialog` — the dialog behind the row menu's Delete.
- `SaveBar` — the unsaved-changes band; see `skills/webkit-form`.

## Variants

`MainSettings` (primary) · `Records` · `ImportZoneFile`. Code: [blocks/detail/dns-zone-detail.md](blocks/detail/dns-zone-detail.md), `get_block("detail/dns-zone-detail", { variant })`.

# DomainsCard (`detail/domains-card`)

> The domains card of a resource settings tab: a borderless data-driven table of the addresses the resource answers on, each with its environment as the row's one medium rounded tag, its deployment policy as text, its c…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/detail/domains-card/domains-card.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`

## Asked as

domains section; domains card; domains table; resource domains; domain list in settings; hostnames; seção de domínios; domínios do recurso; lista de domínios; attached resources; related resources table; recursos vinculados

A short list of the things one resource is attached to, shown in place inside its Settings tab. Here they are its domains: the user sees every address the resource answers on, which environment, deployment policy and certificate each one uses, and can edit, delete or add one without leaving the settings page.

## When to use

- Use domains-card inside a section of a resource's Settings tab for a short list of the records it owns; it is a section, not a page.
- A section of a resource's Settings tab lists related records owned by that resource (domains, attached origins, bound certificates) and the list is short enough to read without search or paging.
- Each related record has two to four attributes worth scanning side by side, and one or two row actions.
- The user adds a related record from inside the resource, so the action reads `Add <Module>`.

## When not to use

- The related records are many and need search, filters or columns: use the list of `view/table-view`, scoped to the resource.
- A first-level list of one resource type reached from the sidebar: use `view/table-view`.
- Pairs of keys and values the user types in place: use `edit/variables`.
- Choosing one existing resource inside a form: use `create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Container — `Card` (required)
- B. Attached table — `DataTable` (required)
- C. Environment chip — `Tag` (optional)
- D. Row actions — `TableCellActions`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuItem` (required)
- E. Footer — `Button` (required)
- F. Load failure — `Alert` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/detail/domains-card.md](blocks/detail/domains-card.md).

## Data

The card takes its domains and the request's state through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `DomainsCardDomain` and `DomainsCardProps` are exported from `domains-card.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample domains the card renders when `domains` is left out (and never while `loading` or `error` is set).

Prop: `domains`, `loading`, `error`.

Event: `create`, `retry`, `row-action`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/detail/domains-card.md](blocks/detail/domains-card.md).

## Do

- Keep the card unpadded and the table borderless, so there is one border around the whole list.
- Keep one chip per row: the Environment `Tag` (secondary, medium, rounded); every other attribute is plain text, with a glyph where it helps.
- Leave a cell empty when the attribute does not apply to that record.
- Hide the row menu on records the user cannot change, rather than showing disabled options.
- Count the records in the footer with the right singular or plural noun.
- Follow `skills/webkit-tables` for column kinds and the action column.

## Don't

- Don't add search, filters or pagination; switch to the `view/table-view` list when the list needs them.
- Don't use a primary or large button for Add; the page's Save belongs to the settings form.
- Don't put Delete in the same group as Edit, or use a destructive color in the menu trigger.
- Don't write a dash or "None" in cells that do not apply.
- Don't wrap the table in a second card or give it its own border.

## Copy

- **Column headers:** short nouns without punctuation, e.g. "Domain", "Environment", "Policy", "Certificate".
- **Add action:** `Add <Module>` with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Add Domain"; never "Create" inside a resource.
- **Count:** a number and the noun, singular or plural, e.g. "1 domain", "3 domains".
- **Row menu:** single verbs, e.g. "Edit", "Delete"; the trigger tooltip reads "Row actions".
- **Attribute values:** the value as the product names it, e.g. "Production", "Managed".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The row menu trigger's `aria-label` names the record, e.g. "Actions for shop.example.com", so a screen reader user knows which row it acts on.
- Menu option icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the option label is the accessible name.
- The action column has no visible header; its cells hold only the labeled trigger.
- The menu is reachable by keyboard, opens on Enter or Space and returns focus to its trigger on close.
- The count is plain text, read after the table, before the Add button.

## States

- Default: three domains from `domains`, one generated by the platform with no row menu, two the user added with Edit and Delete, and the footer counting them beside Add Domain; `loading` shows the table's loading state and `error` the danger `Alert` with Retry.

## Related

- `edit/edit-resource` — the Settings tab whose Domains section renders this card.
- `view/table-view` — the full list, with filters and pages, for longer related lists.
- `edit/delete-dialog` — the dialog behind the row menu's Delete.
- `DataTable` — the table this card wraps; see `skills/webkit-tables`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary). Code: [blocks/detail/domains-card.md](blocks/detail/domains-card.md), `get_block("detail/domains-card", { variant })`.

# GetStarted (`detail/get-started`)

> The onboarding block for a resource made from the CLI: a section heading with a toggle between the CLI and GitHub Actions paths, then three numbered step cards, each with a code block for its commands.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/detail/get-started/get-started.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("detail/get-started")`
- Components: Card, CodeBlock, SectionHeader, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

get started; cli setup steps; github actions setup; onboarding steps; deploy with cli; numbered steps with code; primeiros passos; como começar; passos de configuração

The first thing a user reads about a resource they created from the CLI and have not deployed yet. They need the exact commands to build and ship it, in order, for the path they work with: the CLI on their own machine or a GitHub Actions workflow. The block names the two paths, lets them pick one and walks them through three numbered steps, each with commands they can copy.

## When to use

- Use get-started inside a resource's Overview tab or a deploy success screen to list the next commands; it is a card, not a page.
- Under the summary card on the Overview tab of a resource made from the CLI that has no deployment yet.
- At the end of a create wizard, on the deploy success screen, when the next move happens in a terminal.
- Any onboarding that comes down to three ordered steps with commands per step.

## When not to use

- A resource that already serves traffic: show the summary and its deployments in `detail/resource-detail` instead.
- A list of gates to pass before going to production (domain, policy, error pages): use `detail/production-checklist`.
- A module the account has never used: use `state/first-use`, which explains the module before any resource exists.
- Connecting a repository or editing build commands: that is the Build tab of `detail/resource-detail`.

## Building blocks

- A. Section heading — `SectionHeader` (required)
- B. Path switch — `ToggleGroup` (required)
- C. Step cards — `Card` (required)
- D. Commands — `CodeBlock` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/detail/get-started.md](blocks/detail/get-started.md).

## Data

The block fetches nothing; the steps are its copy. `GetStartedProps` and `GetStartedPath` are exported from `get-started.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample resource name the link command fills in when `resourceName` is left out.

Prop: `resourceName`, `v-model`.

Event: `update:modelValue`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/detail/get-started.md](blocks/detail/get-started.md).

## Do

- Keep exactly three steps per path, in the order the user runs them: install or authenticate, connect, deploy.
- Make every command copyable and runnable as shown, with the resource name already filled in.
- Keep the two paths parallel: same number of steps, same card shape, same last step that ends in a live deployment.
- Point to the docs from the description, not from a separate button.

## Don't

- Don't add a primary button to the block; the action happens in the terminal or the repository.
- Don't put secrets or real tokens in a command; refer to the repository secret by name.
- Don't nest cards or put more than one `CodeBlock` in a step.
- Don't let a long command push the page sideways; the code block scrolls inside its card.

## Copy

- **Section title:** "Get started".
- **Description:** one sentence that names the choice, then the docs link, e.g. "Two ways to build and deploy this resource. Select one and follow the steps, or read the CLI docs."
- **Path options:** the tool names as their makers write them, e.g. "CLI", "GitHub Actions".
- **Step titles:** verb first, sentence case, no period, e.g. "Install the CLI", "Link your project", "Push to deploy".
- **Step descriptions:** one or two sentences that say what the step does and why, e.g. "Authenticate, then link the local project to this resource so every deploy lands on it."
- **Copy button label:** names the step, e.g. "Copy the commands for Install the CLI".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The section title is a heading below the page `h1`; each step title is an `h3`.
- The toggle group carries `aria-label="Deploy with"`, so the switch reads as a choice of path.
- The step number is visible text, so the order is announced; the dashed connector is `aria-hidden`.
- Each copy button names its step, so several copy buttons on the page stay distinguishable.
- The docs link opens in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and keeps a visible focus ring.

## States

- Cli: the default `v-model` (`cli`), install the CLI, link the project named by `resourceName`, then deploy and sync.
- Ci: `model-value="actions"`, the GitHub Actions path: store a personal token as a repository secret, add the deploy workflow, then push to the production branch.

## Related

- `detail/resource-detail` — the resource Overview tab this block sits on, under the summary card.
- `create/deploy-success` — the end of a create flow that can show these steps.
- `detail/production-checklist` — the next set of tasks once the resource is live.
- `CodeBlock` — tabs, file name and copy for each step's commands.

## Variants

`Cli` (primary) · `Ci`. Code: [blocks/detail/get-started.md](blocks/detail/get-started.md), `get_block("detail/get-started", { variant })`.

# Invocations (`detail/invocations`)

> The Invocation page of one function run, as a page body for ConsoleLayout: one run end to end.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/detail/invocations/invocations.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("detail/invocations")`
- Components: Button, Card, CopyButton, DropdownMenu, FlowDiagram, IconButton, Link, `LogViewerContent`, LogViewer, PageHeader, SectionHeader, StatusIndicator, Tag, Tooltip, Trace, `use-locale`
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-data-viz`

## Asked as

function invocations; invocation detail; function run; request path; trace waterfall; function logs; replay invocation; invocações da função; detalhe da invocação; execução da função; caminho da requisição; rastreamento; one invocation; invocation summary; function invocation; invocação de função

The page a user opens to understand one run of a function: did it work, how long did it take, where did the time go, and what did the code print. It reads top to bottom from the answer to the evidence: the invocation summary, the path the request travelled, the trace that measured each step, and the logs on the same clock. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the layout owns the rail, the header with the breadcrumb (Functions › the function › Invocations) and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use invocations for one function run end to end (summary, trace, logs).
- A function has run and the user needs one invocation end to end: its status, duration, request and outcome.
- The user arrives from a function's list of runs, from an alert, or from a failed request in an event log.
- Several services touch the request and the user must see which hop spent the time or failed.

## When not to use

- Testing code you are still editing: use the TestRun variant of `edit/function-editor`.
- Searching many requests or events across products: use an event log table, e.g. `view/table-view`.
- The overview of the function itself, its versions or deployments: use `detail/resource-detail`.
- Following a deployment as it builds: use `detail/deployment-logs`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Invocation summary — `Card`, `Link`, `Tooltip`, `CopyButton`, `StatusIndicator`, `Button`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton` (required)
- C. Request path — `SectionHeader`, `FlowDiagram`, `Tag` (required)
- D. Trace — `Trace` (required)
- E. Logs — `SectionHeader`, `StatusIndicator`, `LogViewer`, `LogViewerContent` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/detail/invocations.md](blocks/detail/invocations.md).

## Data

The block takes the function and its recent invocations through props, owns the open invocation and the selected span as models, and emits its actions; it fetches nothing. `InvocationsFunction`, `InvocationsInvocation`, `InvocationsLog` and `InvocationsProps` are exported from `invocations.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample function and runs the block renders when they are left out.

Prop / model: `edgeFunction`, `invocations`, `v-model:invocation`, `v-model:span`.

Event: `replay`, `invocation-action`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/detail/invocations.md](blocks/detail/invocations.md).

## Do

- Lead with the outcome: the status and the outcome line come before any chart.
- Keep one clock for the trace and the logs, so a line and a span can be read against each other.
- Let a request path node jump to its span; never make the user search the waterfall for it.
- Keep the run switcher in the summary, so the user moves between invocations without leaving the page.
- Disable Replay while a run is still going; Replay emits `replay` and the page reports it through `toast`.

## Don't

- Don't color the outcome without words; the status and the outcome sentence carry the meaning.
- Don't put Replay or the run switcher in the page heading.
- Don't scroll smoothly when the user prefers reduced motion.
- Don't show raw stack traces in the summary; they belong in the failing span and the logs.

## Copy

- **Heading:** "Invocation", with "One run of this function, end to end: the path the request took and what each step cost."
- **Facts:** "Started", "Completed" ("Not yet" while running), "Duration", "Location".
- **Durations:** milliseconds under a second ("412 ms"), seconds with two decimals above ("1.24 s"); log times relative ("+16 ms").
- **Outcome:** the status code and one sentence, e.g. "502, the origin did not answer within the 1 s budget."
- **Node actions:** "Show <name> in the trace".
- **Menu:** "Open in Real-Time Events", "Function settings"; switcher "Recent", group "Recent invocations".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The body renders no landmark of its own; the Request path, Trace and Logs are sections named by their headings.
- The invocation ID and the request each have a `CopyButton` with an `aria-label` that names what is copied.
- Status uses `StatusIndicator` and `Tag` with words, never color alone; decorative glyphs are `aria-hidden`.
- The request path node facts are a description list; each jump `IconButton` has an `aria-label` and a matching `Tooltip`.
- The trace is the `Trace` grid, named "Trace of <id>", operable with the keyboard; selecting from the path moves its selection, and the scroll respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- Completed: the open invocation (`invocation`, the first by default) is a run that served its response, every node tagged Active or Answered, the trace with no error and the logs ending on a success line.
- Error: the open invocation (`invocation="inv_7d41be02"`, `span="response"`) is a run the origin timed out, the danger status and outcome, the function and origin nodes failed, the origin-response span selected with its message, and warning lines in the logs.
- Running: the open invocation (`invocation="inv_6a90c3f7"`) is a run in progress, the loading status, Replay disabled, Completed reading Not yet, running spans, and the lines printed so far with a Streaming indicator in the Logs header.

## Related

- `edit/function-editor` — its TestRun variant runs the function before it ships, with the same trace and logs.
- `detail/resource-detail` — the overview of the function; this page owns the invocation summary card.
- `detail/deployment-logs` — the step logs of a deployment.
- `shell/console` — the `ConsoleLayout` this page body renders in; see `skills/webkit-layout`.

## Variants

`Completed` (primary) · `Error` · `Running`. Code: [blocks/detail/invocations.md](blocks/detail/invocations.md), `get_block("detail/invocations", { variant })`.

# ProductionChecklist (`detail/production-checklist`)

> A production checklist on a resource overview: a card that names the gates between the generated hostname and production, counts how many are done and lists each as a row, with an expand button (named by a `Tooltip`)…

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/detail/production-checklist/production-checklist.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("detail/production-checklist")`
- Components: Button, Card, `DrawerContent`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, IconButton, Item, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Tag, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

production checklist; go-live checklist; checklist; setup progress; launch steps; onboarding checklist; checklist de produção; lista de verificação; passos para produção

A service that is live on its generated hostname is not yet ready for real traffic. This card tells the user what stands between the service and production (a custom domain, a security policy, custom error pages), how many of those gates are done and which one to take next. It expands into a drawer where each gate explains itself and offers its action, and it shrinks to a single line once every gate is done.

## When to use

- Use production-checklist inside a resource's Overview tab for the few setup gates left before production traffic; it is a card, not a page.
- On the Overview tab of a service or resource that is deployed but still has setup gates before it should take production traffic.
- When the gates are few (three to five), independent and each completed by one action elsewhere in the console.

## When not to use

- Commands to build and deploy a resource for the first time: use `detail/get-started`.
- Ordered steps the user must complete before the resource exists: use `create/create-wizard`.
- A list of resources already bound to this one: use `detail/domains-card`.
- A module the account has never used: use `state/first-use`.

## Building blocks

- A. Checklist card — `Card` (required)
- B. Progress tag — `Tag` (required)
- C. Expand button — `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)
- D. Gate rows — `Item` (required)
- E. Checklist drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/detail/production-checklist.md](blocks/detail/production-checklist.md).

## Data

The block takes its gates through props and emits every action; it fetches nothing. `ProductionChecklistStep` and `ProductionChecklistProps` are exported from `production-checklist.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample gates the block renders when `steps` is left out.

Prop: `steps`, `defaultOpen`.

Event: `step-action`, `done`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/detail/production-checklist.md](blocks/detail/production-checklist.md).

## Do

- Order the gates by how much they matter for production; domain first.
- Count done gates in the tag and keep the count in step with the rows.
- In the drawer, give each open gate one outlined action named for what it adds, and replace it once done with a Done `Tag` and a muted sentence naming what it now serves.
- Collapse the card when every gate is done; keep the title, the success tag and the expand button.

## Don't

- Don't block the rest of the page or nag with an alert banner; the checklist is guidance, not an error.
- Don't put the gate actions on the card rows; the card only lists, the drawer explains and acts.
- Don't show a percentage or a progress bar next to the count.
- Don't remove the card once complete; the success tag confirms the service is ready.

## Copy

- **Title:** "Ship to production".
- **Progress:** "<done> of <total>", e.g. "1 of 3"; when complete, "Ready for production".
- **Gate titles:** verb first, sentence case, no period, e.g. "Add a custom domain", "Enable a security policy".
- **Gate descriptions (drawer):** one or two sentences on what the gate gives the service, e.g. "Answer 4xx and 5xx with your own page instead of the default response."
- **Gate actions (drawer):** `Add <Module>` or a verb and noun, three words or fewer, e.g. "Add Domain", "Attach Policy", "Add Error Page".
- **Done note:** a muted sentence beside the Done tag naming what the gate now serves, ending with a period, e.g. "Serving shop.example.com."; the tag itself reads "Done".
- **Drawer description:** one plain sentence on where the service stands, e.g. "This service is live on a generated hostname. These steps take it to production."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The card title is an `h2` under the page `h1`; the drawer has its own title.
- The expand button has an `aria-label` that names what it expands.
- Gate icons and the done check are `aria-hidden`; each row announces "Done" or "Not started" in visually hidden text, so status never relies on color.
- Rows are real buttons, reachable by keyboard in reading order.
- The drawer returns focus to the expand button when it closes.

## States

- Card: `steps` with some gates done; the card lists every gate with the count in its tag, and the expand button and every row open the drawer.
- Success: `steps` with every gate done; the tag reads Ready for production and the rows are gone.
- DrawerDetail: `defaultOpen`, as when the expand button opened the right-side drawer with every step, its description and its action or its Done tag and note, over a Done footer; a card row opens the same drawer.

## Related

- `detail/resource-detail` — the service Overview tab that renders this card under the summary.
- `detail/get-started` — onboarding before the first deployment, for a resource made from the CLI.
- `detail/domains-card` — where an attached policy or error page shows up once added.
- `Item` — the row primitive for each gate; see `skills/webkit-ui-states` for the done and empty states.

## Variants

# ResourceDetail (`detail/resource-detail`)

> The Overview tab of a resource detail page: the full-bleed tab bar, sticky while the layout scrolls, then the column that opens on the resource summary card.

- Surface: app
- Source: `blocks/detail/resource-detail/resource-detail.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_block("detail/resource-detail")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Avatar, Button, Card, CodeBlock, ConfirmDialog, ConsoleLayout, CopyButton, DataTable, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, Drawer, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, IconButton, Input, `InputGroupRoot`, Item, Link, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelBody`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Popover, SaveBar, SectionHeader, Select, SettingsRow, SettingsSection, StatusIndicator, Tabs, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, TopologyDiagram, `use-locale`, `use-unsaved-changes`
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

overview page; resource overview; detail page; summary page; application overview; página de visão geral; detalhe do recurso; página de resumo; details page with tabs; versions tab; build tab; detalhe com abas; resource summary; summary card; overview card; resource facts; status card; resumo do recurso; cartão de resumo; visão geral; details page; resource details; página de detalhes; application detail; application tabs; topology tab; deployment topology; detalhe da aplicação; topologia; first deploy; not deployed; connected repository; primeiro deploy; resource overview tabs; service details; policy details

The second-level page of one resource. The user arrives from a list row or a deploy flow to answer three questions about it: where it lives and whether it is serving, what it is made of, and what to do next. The page names the resource in the breadcrumb, splits its concerns into tabs, and opens the Overview tab on one summary card of facts, followed by whatever the resource needs next: Get started for a resource made from the CLI, the production checklist and topology for a service. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

## When to use

- Use resource-detail for the tabbed overview of one resource, service, policy or application.
- A user opens one resource, service, policy or application from its list or from a deploy flow.
- The resource has more than one concern (overview, versions, build, deployments) that each deserve a tab.
- The user needs the live address, the status and the latest deployment of a resource at a glance, with Visit and the resource actions one click away.

## When not to use

- Many resources of one type to compare and filter: use `view/table-view`.
- Editing one version's settings, source or rules: use `detail/version-detail`.
- Changing a resource's settings in a form: use `edit/edit-resource` or `settings/settings-form`.
- One deployment, as it streams in a create flow or on its own page (live, failed, queued): use `detail/deployment-logs`.
- One function run end to end (summary, trace, logs): use `detail/invocations`.
- A key and value list that belongs to the resource: use `detail/dns-zone-detail`.

## Building blocks

- A. Tab bar — `PageTabs`, `Tabs`, `EmptyState` (required)
- B. Summary subject band — `Card`, `Tooltip`, `Button`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton` (required)
- C. Summary facts band — `Link`, `Tag`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `Tooltip` (required)
- D. Summary state band — `Button` (optional)
- E. Get started — `SectionHeader`, `ToggleGroup`, `Card`, `CodeBlock` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/detail/resource-detail.md](blocks/detail/resource-detail.md).

## Breadcrumb and environment

- The trail is in the layout's header: `breadcrumbs` from the route meta (`module › resource name`, e.g. Resources › analytics-app), or the page's own `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`. A page body never renders `Breadcrumb`, `AppHeader` or a `<main>`.
- A service ends the trail on its environment. That crumb is a control, so the page sets the trail itself: `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb` with the module and the service as `items` and, in its default slot, a `Select` with `variant="ghost"` and `size="small"` (no `w-full`: it sizes to its value like a crumb), labelled `Switch environment`, with a search `Input`, each environment tagged with its deployment policy and Add Environment at its foot. The environment is part of the route, so picking one navigates and the page reads it. ServiceOverview and `shell/console` (DetailPage) show it.
- The layout hides its breadcrumbs while compact, so below md the service summary's Deployment Settings band carries its own environment menu.

## Topology tab

- Use `TopologyDiagram` for the path a request takes to the resource (Application and ServiceOverview both do). A pick from a node's bind menu is pending on the node until its Apply control confirms it (Cancel or Escape drops it); only the confirmed `bind`, a change or a removal is staged on the node, counted beside Deploy and listed in the deploy `Drawer`; the run ends in the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy. A production-checklist step that binds a slot (Bind Policy, Bind Error Page) scrolls to the topology and expands that node instead of opening a separate form.
- Bind, create and remove act on staged state only. Nothing reaches Production until Deploy, and the deploy drawer lists every staged change before it runs.
- Show the staged count on the tab row next to Deploy, so it stays visible from every tab.
- Report the deploy through the async-submit toast (Edit and Redeploy) and clear the staged marks once it succeeds.
- A node that collects many resources adds to itself through the diagram's `actions` slot: the Domains node of ServiceOverview carries an outlined small `IconButton` (`az az-plus`) named Add domain inside a `Tooltip`, picked by `node.key === 'domains'`. Never hand-draw a node card to get the `+`.

## Data

The primary (ResourceOverview) takes the resource through a prop, owns the open tab as a model and emits its actions; it fetches nothing. `ResourceDetailResource`, `ResourceDetailTab` and `ResourceDetailProps` are exported from `resource-detail.vue`, and `sample.ts` holds the sample resource the block renders when `resource` is left out. The other variants are whole screens of their own (a service, a policy, an application with working tabs) and keep their own records.

Prop / model: `resource`, `v-model:tab`.

Event: `resource-action`, `connect-repository`.

Then delete `sample.ts` and its import.

What each prop and event does, and the go-live code: [blocks/detail/resource-detail.md](blocks/detail/resource-detail.md).

## Do

- Keep the content in `layout-column` with its boundary inset, and let the tab bar run full-bleed above it.
- Open the Overview tab on the summary card; every other section of the tab comes after it.
- Name the resource in the breadcrumb, not in a `PageHeader` title above the card.
- Put the one primary page action (Deploy) on the tab row, medium and outlined; keep Visit in the summary.
- Give Versions and Deployments the same table shape as `view/table-view`, scoped to this resource, with a small section heading, pages of 10 and an `EmptyState` for none yet.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shell/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't put the tab name in the breadcrumb, or repeat the resource name as a large heading.
- Don't add a second primary button to the tab row or the summary card.
- Don't spread the facts across several cards; one summary card holds them in bands.
- Don't hide the live address behind the actions menu; it is the card's primary link.
- Don't render empty facts as blank space; show the action that fills them, e.g. Connect Git repository under Source, or a muted word (None, Not deployed) when nothing can fill them yet.
- Don't show Visit for a resource that has no address yet.

## Copy

- **Breadcrumb:** module, then the resource name as created, e.g. "Resources" › "analytics-app".
- **Tabs:** one or two nouns, e.g. "Overview", "Versions", "Build", "Deployments".
- **Fact labels:** a short noun, sentence case, no colon, e.g. "Deployment", "Domains", "Status", "Created", "Source", "Framework".
- **Created:** relative time and author, e.g. "2 weeks ago by John Smith".
- **Actions:** a verb, e.g. "Visit", "Deploy", "Redeploy"; menu options "Copy URL", "Settings".
- **Link tooltips:** say where the link goes, e.g. "Open analytics-app-z1x2c3.example.com in a new tab".
- **State band:** one sentence on the next step, e.g. "To deploy to Production, drop your project anywhere on this page, connect Git, or run platform deploy via the CLI."
- **Failure banner:** what failed and what still serves, without an em dash, e.g. "A rule with the same behavior is already bound to this service, so the manifest was refused."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The body renders no landmark of its own: the layout's single `main` holds the tab bar and the tab content, and the rail and header are the layout's.
- The tab bar is a tablist; arrow keys move between tabs and the active tab is announced.
- Links that open a new tab add "(opens in a new tab)" in visually hidden text; decorative icons are `aria-hidden`.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label` and a `Tooltip` with the same words, e.g. "Resource actions", "Add domain".
- Status uses a `StatusIndicator` with a text label, never color alone.

## States

Grouped by the resource type the page shows. A deployment's own page is `detail/deployment-logs` (DeploymentDetail, DeploymentError, DeploymentQueued) and one function invocation is `detail/invocations`.

### Resource

- ResourceOverview: the Overview tab of a resource made from the CLI (`resource`, `tab` is `overview`), the summary card followed by Get started; any other `tab` shows the Open link to its own route.
- Resource: the summary card alone, in its resource shape.
- FirstDeploy: the summary cards before and during the first deploy. A resource never deployed shows Not deployed yet in place of the address, None, Not deployed and Not yet as muted values, Connect Git repository and Project upload under Source, and no Visit; a service on its first deploy reads Deploying · Build with a loading `StatusIndicator`, and one that serves nothing reads Inactive.
- ResourceVersions: the Versions tab, a small Versions heading with Add Version over the controls row and the versions table.
- ResourceBuild: the Build tab, the Git repository, Build configuration and Deployment bands, with a save bar once a command changes.
- ResourceBuildConnected: the Build tab of a resource with a connected repository, its link and a danger Disconnect, the Production branch and Preview branch rows, the Build configuration and Deployment bands, and the save bar once a value changes.

### Service

- Service: the service summary with its domains, environment menu, ID and the Deployment Settings band.
- ServiceOverview: a service (its environment crumb is the page's `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`), Deploy on the tab row, the production checklist and the deployment topology on `TopologyDiagram` (policy, error page and origin slots staged until Deploy).

### Policy

- Policy: the policy summary with the resource it protects, a Rules shortcut, its status, environment, rule count and modules.

### Application

- Application: a whole application page body, with working tabs. Overview is the summary card; Versions and Deployments are a small `SectionHeader` over a flush `DataTable`; Topology draws the request path with `TopologyDiagram` (domain, workload, firewall, application, function instance). Binding or removing the firewall or the function only stages the change: the node turns dashed with a Staged status, a polite status line names it, and the tab row shows the count as a warning `Tag` beside Deploy. Deploy opens a `Drawer` that lists each staged change as from and to, then runs on its own: a loading toast, then the async-submit toast with **Edit** (back to the Topology tab) and **Redeploy**, never View deployments.
- ApplicationBuild: an application page body with Overview, Versions, Build and Deployments. Dragging files over the page raises the dashed drop target of `state/project-intake`; dropping them or Deploy opens a deploy `Drawer` naming the source, and the run reports through the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy. Leaving the Build tab with unsaved changes asks first in a `ConfirmDialog`.

## Related

- `view/table-view` — the list a row of which leads here.
- `detail/get-started` — the section that follows the summary for a resource made from the CLI.
- `detail/production-checklist` — the card on a service overview.
- `detail/deployment-logs` — a deployment's own page, and the steps a create flow streams.
- `detail/version-detail` — where a row of the Versions tab leads.
- `create/deploy-drawer` — the drawer the Deploy action opens.
- `state/project-intake` — the drop target an application page raises while files hover over it.
- `detail/invocations` — the page an invocation summary opens, with its request path, trace and logs; it owns the invocation summary card.
- `edit/edit-resource` — the service Settings tab.
- `shell/console` — the `ConsoleLayout` this page body renders in; see `skills/webkit-navigation` and `skills/webkit-layout`.

`ResourceOverview` (primary) · `Resource` · `Service` · `Policy` · `ResourceVersions` · `ResourceBuild` · `ServiceOverview` · `Application` · `FirstDeploy` · `ResourceBuildConnected` · `ApplicationBuild`.
