<!-- components/browser-frame.md -->

# Browser Frame

> A browser window that renders live webkit components inside a viewport of its own, so a page or story can show a real screen at a real device size — desktop, tablet or mobile — and resize it by hand. The default slot is teleported into an internal `iframe`, which gives the content a true width × height viewport: CSS breakpoints fire against the frame's simulated width, viewport units resolve against its simulated height, and content taller than the viewport scrolls inside it like a page. When the simulated width is wider than the space available, the frame scales the whole viewport down to fit instead of clamping it. The chrome's window dots, address and size readout are decoration; its one control is a copy button inside the address bar, and the frame's other controls are the resize handles on its right edge, bottom edge and bottom-right corner.

- Import: `import BrowserFrame from '@aziontech/webkit/browser-frame'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use BrowserFrame to run real components inside a resizable device viewport (docs, stories); for a screenshot or clip in documentation use DocFrame, for third-party iframe content use Embed.
- Showing a real screen — a site band, a console page, a template — built from webkit components, at a device size you choose.
- Letting a reader drag a layout from desktop to tablet to mobile to see how it responds, on a documentation page.
- Pinning a composed example to a device size (`v-model:width` + `v-model:height`) so a story or page always shows the tablet or mobile layout.
- Showing that a result lives at a URL — a deployed site, a preview link — by setting `address`.

## Do

- Compose the default slot exactly as the screen would be composed in an app — the frame mirrors the page's stylesheets and theme into its viewport, so no extra wiring or classes are needed.
- Pin the device the example is about with `v-model:width` and `v-model:height` (`375 × 812` mobile, `768 × 1024` tablet, `1280 × 800` desktop); leave `width` unset to fill the container.
- Give the frame an `ariaLabel` that names what is shown (`Pricing page at tablet size`); it becomes the viewport's accessible name.
- Viewport-height units (`h-screen`, `min-h-dvh`) in slot content resolve against the simulated height, so a full-height shell renders as it would on the device.
- Do not add controls to the chrome — the address's copy button and the resize handles are the frame's only controls. Interactive content belongs in the default slot.

## Don’t

- For a static screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.
- For third-party content loaded from another origin → use `embed`.
- For a mock of the Azion console's own shell on a marketing band → use the console shell mockup the page composes; it draws the console chrome and staggers its parts.
- For content whose layout depends on an overlay (`dialog`, `drawer`, a dropdown panel) or a JS breakpoint composable — those still read the outer page (see States), so the frame cannot show them at the simulated size.
- For a framed page section or grid cell → use `registration-frame`.

## Related

- `doc-frame` — the documentation figure frame for stills and clips; no live viewport.
- `embed` — a titled `iframe` for another origin's document; `browser-frame` renders our own components.
- `registration-frame` — the page's registration frame (hairlines + corner marks), not a window.
- `copy-button` — the clipboard control the address bar composes; reach for it directly to copy any other value.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | `string` | `''` | false | Read-only URL shown in the chrome's address bar; the address bar is not rendered when empty. |
| `minWidth` | `number` | `320` | false | Smallest viewport width the resize handles can reach, in pixels. |
| `maxWidth` | `number` | `1920` | false | Largest viewport width the resize handles can reach, in pixels; widths wider than the container are scaled down to fit. |
| `minHeight` | `number` | `320` | false | Smallest viewport height the resize handles can reach, in pixels. |
| `maxHeight` | `number` | `1440` | false | Largest viewport height the resize handles can reach, in pixels. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the viewport; when empty it falls back to `address`, then to `Preview`. |
| `copyAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the address bar's copy button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy address`). |
| `widthHandleAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the right-edge width handle. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Resize preview width`). |
| `heightHandleAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the bottom-edge height handle. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Resize preview height`). |
| `width` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:width`). |
| `height` | `number` | `800` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:height`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The live content, teleported into the frame's viewport `iframe` once it is ready. Renders client-side only. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:width` | `number` | `undefined` | `update:width` | Simulated viewport width in pixels via `defineModel('width')`. Undefined fills the container; the width and corner handles write a number, clamped to `minWidth`…`maxWidth`, on every resize step. Works controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `v-model:height` | `number` | `800` | `update:height` | Simulated viewport height in pixels via `defineModel('height', { default: 800 })`. The height and corner handles write a number, clamped to `minHeight`…`maxHeight`, on every resize step. Works controlled or uncontrolled. |

## States

The frame is static apart from its resize handles.

- **Viewport.** The root renders an `iframe` (blank document). Once it loads, the frame mirrors the host page's stylesheets (every `style` and stylesheet `link` in `head`, kept in sync as they change so HMR still applies) and the theme attributes of the host's root element (`data-theme`, `class`) into it, then teleports the default slot into its `body`. The content is the same Vue app — props, reactivity, provide/inject and events behave as if it were rendered in place.
- **Breakpoints.** CSS media queries and viewport units in the content resolve against the viewport's width and height. JS breakpoint reads (`matchMedia` in a composable) and overlays that teleport to the document `body` still resolve against the host page — a documented limit, not a bug.
- **Size.** The viewport renders at the effective width (`width` when set, otherwise the container's width) and at `height`. Content taller or wider than the viewport scrolls inside the `iframe`'s own document, exactly as a page scrolls in a browser.
- **Scale.** When the effective width exceeds the container, the viewport is scaled down by `container / effective` on both axes, and the frame's on-page height is `height × scale`. A frame narrower than its container is centered in it.
- **Resizing.** Three handles resize the viewport:
  - the **width handle** on the right edge writes `width`;
  - the **height handle** on the bottom edge writes `height`;
  - the **corner handle** at the bottom-right writes both at once.
    Pointer drags use pointer capture. A width drag moves the right edge under the pointer (the frame is centered, so the width changes by twice the pointer's travel) and is clamped to `minWidth` and the container width; a height drag follows the pointer's travel divided by the current scale and is clamped to `minHeight`…`maxHeight`. The keyboard reaches up to `maxWidth` / `maxHeight`. While any handle is dragged the root sets `data-resizing` and the content ignores the pointer.
- **Size readout.** While any handle is dragged or focused, the chrome shows the viewport size (`768 × 1024`) at its trailing end; it is hidden otherwise.
- **Scaled.** The root sets `data-scaled` while the viewport is scaled below 1.
- **Address.** Rendered only when `address` is non-empty, centered in the chrome as a compact, fully rounded pill up to `--container-xs` wide and exactly as tall as the small copy button (28px), which sits flush at its trailing end, never overlapping the window dots or the readout. The pill is filled with the skeleton placeholder fill (static — no sweep) and edged with a muted hairline. Its text is set in the monospace code label and centered in the space left of the copy button; long addresses truncate in the middle: a leading part ellipsizes and the last 12 characters always stay visible.
- **Copy.** The address bar's trailing end composes the package's `CopyButton` (`variant="ghost"`, `size="small"`) with `value` = the full `address`; its copied feedback is the `CopyButton`'s own.
- **Test ids.** Root fallback `browser-frame` (consumer override wins); `${testId}__address`, `${testId}__viewport` (the `iframe`), `${testId}__copy`, `${testId}__width-handle`, `${testId}__height-handle`, `${testId}__corner-handle`.
- **Composable.** The document mirroring and teleport target live in a co-located lifecycle composable, `composables/use-frame-document.ts`, that disconnects every observer on scope dispose.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the width and height handles show `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`; focusable content inside the viewport keeps its own ring.
- Keyboard map:
  - width handle — `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` change the width by 10px, `Shift` + arrow by 100px, `Home` jumps to `minWidth`, `End` to `maxWidth`;
  - height handle — `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` change the height by 10px, `Shift` + arrow by 100px, `Home` jumps to `minHeight`, `End` to `maxHeight`;
  - the corner handle is pointer-only and not focusable — both of its axes are already reachable through the two keyboard handles;
  - the copy button is a normal tab stop before the handles and keeps `CopyButton`'s own keyboard behavior (`Enter` / `Space` copy);
  - the viewport's content is reached with `Tab` as part of the page's normal order.
- ARIA:
  - width handle — focusable `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation="vertical"`, `aria-valuenow` (effective width), `aria-valuemin` (`minWidth`), `aria-valuemax` (`maxWidth`), `aria-valuetext` (`768 pixels wide`), `aria-controls` (the viewport id, from `useId()`), `aria-label` from `widthHandleAriaLabel`;
  - height handle — focusable `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation="horizontal"`, `aria-valuenow` (`height`), `aria-valuemin` (`minHeight`), `aria-valuemax` (`maxHeight`), `aria-valuetext` (`1024 pixels tall`), `aria-controls` (the viewport id), `aria-label` from `heightHandleAriaLabel`;
  - the corner handle, the window dots, the address text and the size readout are `aria-hidden="true"`; the chrome bar itself is not hidden, so the copy button stays reachable, named by `copyAriaLabel`;
  - the `iframe` carries `title` from `ariaLabel` → `address` → `Preview`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-placeholder)` over `var(--bg-surface)` for the address and on `var(--bg-surface)` for the readout; the handle grips at rest `var(--border-strong)` meet 3:1 against `var(--bg-canvas)` as non-text controls.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the handles' color transition; nothing else moves.
- Touch target: the edge handles' hit areas are 24px deep and run the frame's full width or height, and the corner handle is 24×24 — a justified deviation from 40×40: a deeper strip would cover more of the content's edge, and 24px meets WCAG 2.5.8.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BrowserFrame from '@aziontech/webkit/browser-frame'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import CallToAction from '@aziontech/webkit/call-to-action'
  import CardGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/card-grid'
  import FeatureItem from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-item'
  import RegistrationFrame from '@aziontech/webkit/registration-frame'
  import SectionContainer from '@aziontech/webkit/section-container'
  import SectionGap from '@aziontech/webkit/section-gap'
  import SectionModule from '@aziontech/webkit/section-module'
  import SectionTitle from '@aziontech/webkit/section-title'
</script>

<template>
  <BrowserFrame
    address="https://www.azion.com"
    aria-label="Azion platform page"
  >
    <SectionContainer max-width="site">
      <SectionGap
        size="small"
        hatch
      />
      <SectionModule
        :divided="false"
        :padded="false"
      >
        <template #header>
          <SectionTitle
```

<!-- components/card.md -->

# Card

> Use Card for one bordered box of related content in product UI; for a collection of records shown as cards use CardList, for a catalog tile use IntegrationCard, and for the frame of a dashboard chart use ChartCard. A bordered surface that groups related content under a title, with a header, a body and an optional footer the consumer composes. It holds a settings block, a summary or a form section.

- Import: `import Card from '@aziontech/webkit/card'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Group related console content into one bordered surface with a title header, a body and an optional footer, such as a settings block, a summary or a form section.
- Host a divided list edge to edge: set `:padded="false"` and put an `Item` list in the body.
- A centered single-card screen (sign-up, onboarding, a success page) that needs header, body and footer regions.

## Do

- Put the body in the default slot.
- Use `title` for a plain heading (rendered as an `h2`). Use the `header` slot only when the header needs another layout: it replaces both the title and `header-actions`.
- `header-actions` content stays hidden until the header is hovered or focused, so keep it to secondary actions and never make it the only way to reach a control.
- Set `:padded="false"` only when the content draws its own inset or needs flush dividers.
- The footer renders only when the `footer` slot has content; don't pass an empty template to reserve space.

## Don’t

- The surface sits above the page as a modal or a side sheet → use `dialog` or `drawer`.
- It is one tier of a pricing comparison → use `pricing-card`.
- It is a framed cell or band of a marketing page → use `registration-frame` or `card-grid`.
- It is a single row of title, description, media and actions → use `item`.
- It is one record of a resource list shown as cards, with selection and fields → use `card-list` (with `useCollection`).
- It is a catalog tile for an integration, an extension or a plugin (logo, vendor, badges, installed state) → use `integration-card`.

## Related

- `item` — rows inside the card; with `padded` set to false, an `Item` list runs its dividers to the card edges.
- `integration-card` — the catalog tile, split out of Card in 6.0.
- `pricing-card` — pricing tier card with its own price hierarchy and action.
- `card-grid` — responsive grid of cells for marketing pages.
- `panel` — the layered shell behind overlays, not an in-page card.
- `empty-state` — goes in the default slot when the card has no data yet.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading rendered in the header when the `header` slot is empty. |
| `padded` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Pads the content region. Set `false` for flush, edge-to-edge content such as an `ItemList` with full-width dividers. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | — | Replaces the default header layout (title + header-actions). |
| `header-actions` | — | Actions aligned to the end of the default header; visible on header hover. |
| `default` | — | Main card body: children passed without a slot name. |
| `footer` | — | Footer actions or metadata; omitted when empty. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- Responsive: the content region is the `@container/card`, so `KeyValueList`, `Field orientation="responsive"` and any `@sm:`/`@md:` utility inside follow the card, not the window. A card used as a shrink-to-fit flex item must get an explicit width (`flex-1`, `w-full`, a grid track): inline-size containment gives the content no intrinsic width.
- Hover-free devices: the `header-actions` slot stays visible where the pointer cannot hover (`@media (hover: none)`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Card from '@aziontech/webkit/card'
</script>

<template>
  <Card
    title="Card Title"
    class="w-full max-w-[512px]"
  >
    <template #default>
      <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
        Card body content. Place forms, tables, or any markup in the content slot.
      </p>
    </template>
  </Card>
</template>
```

# Console Mockup

> Draws one of the **official console widgets**: a scaled, inert mock of an Azion Console screen or fragment, built from real webkit components inside an internal `ConsoleMockupShell` frame (not exported), that marketing bands use to show the product. `name` selects the widget from a closed registry of 70 drawings, loaded on demand, so a page can only render mocks that already exist and the same screen is the same drawing on every page that shows it. The remaining props pass through to the widget that declares them, and a widget that does not declare one keeps its own value.

- Import: `import ConsoleMockup from '@aziontech/webkit/console-mockup'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ConsoleMockup to show an official console screen on a marketing band.
- A product band (hero, media split, feature tab, widget grid cell) needs to show a console screen or a fragment of one.
- The same console screen appears on more than one page and must be the same drawing on each.
- Several widgets share one slot (tabs), and only the one showing should play: drive `active` from the host.
- A grid cell plays its fragment's beat while the pointer is over it: drive `hovered` from the host.

## Do

- Give the host a size (a height or an aspect ratio). A widget fills its host and scales its design width to fit.
- Host a framed widget (a full screen) in a wide panel, and a fragment in a grid cell with its own padding. A bare fragment floats on the cell's surface and a framed one fades its window into it, so set `--console-mockup-fade-color` on the cell when it is not `--bg-canvas`. The cell clips on both axes (`overflow-clip`, as a media split's media cell does): a fragment's collaborator cursor and shadows float onto the cell's padding, and at a large root font size (200% zoom) its mock text outgrows the drawing; clipping them at the cell's border keeps the page from scrolling sideways. Never frame a fragment with `overflow-x-visible`.
- Leave `variant`, `chrome`, `width`, `tab` and `autoplayInterval` unset unless the host needs a different value: unset keeps the widget's own.
- Leave a fragment's plating to the registry. Each fragment has its own default: a form or a list that reads as a console screen is framed in a console window titled with its module, and a fragment that draws its own card, terminal or code panel is bare, because a window around it would be a window in a window. Set `variant` only when the host needs the other plating, and `chrome` to drop the window's console bar. `width` and `fade` re-plate only the workload screens listed under Props; a fragment keeps its own design width and fade, and the root warns in development when a prop is set on a widget that does not read it.
- Turn `cursor` off when the widget stands for a screen the reader uses alone. Fragments act their beat with a named collaborator cursor; that is right in a feature grid that plays on hover, and a fake second person in a product band that reads as a screenshot.
- Keep the copy beside the widget saying what it shows. Every widget but `function-code` and the coding-agent switch of `functions-start` is hidden from assistive technology.

## Don’t

- The screen you need is not in the registry → add it to the registry inside WebKit (drawn in the internal `ConsoleMockupShell` frame). Do not approximate it at the call site.
- A live, working screen at a device size → use `browser-frame`.
- A static product concept drawing → use `illustration`.
- A screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.

## Related

- `illustration` — the same closed-registry pattern for static scenes.
- `texture` — the texture a full-screen widget grounds itself with through `texture`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `'ai-inference-function' \| 'ai-inference-model' \| 'ai-inference-template' \| 'application-accelerator-cookie' \| 'application-accelerator-method' \| 'application-accelerator-query-string' \| 'application-cache' \| 'application-function' \| 'application-rule' \| 'application-version' \| 'applications-create-method' \| 'applications-device-group' \| 'applications-rule-phases' \| 'bot-manager-metrics' \| 'bot-manager-rule' \| 'bot-manager-traffic' \| 'cli-terminal-deploy' \| 'cli-terminal-start' \| 'data-stream-connector' \| 'data-stream-sampling' \| 'data-stream-source' \| 'ddos-firewall-modules' \| 'ddos-http-events' \| 'ddos-requests-metric' \| 'edge-dns-dnssec' \| 'edge-dns-nameserver' \| 'edge-dns-record' \| 'firewall-function' \| 'firewall-modules' \| 'firewall-rules-order' \| 'function-code' \| 'functions-start' \| 'image-processor-events' \| 'image-processor-module' \| 'image-processor-rule' \| 'kv-store-function' \| 'kv-store-key' \| 'kv-store-security-list' \| 'load-balancer-address' \| 'load-balancer-method' \| 'load-balancer-origins' \| 'network-shield-ip-list' \| 'network-shield-lists' \| 'network-shield-rule' \| 'object-storage-access' \| 'object-storage-browser' \| 'object-storage-buckets' \| 'real-time-events-filter' \| 'real-time-events-log' \| 'real-time-events-volume' \| 'real-time-metrics-dashboard' \| 'real-time-metrics-filter' \| 'real-time-metrics-panel' \| 'sql-database-query' \| 'sql-database-row' \| 'sql-database-table' \| 'waf-allowed-rule' \| 'waf-firewall-rule' \| 'waf-threat' \| 'workload-deploy' \| 'workload-deploy-logs' \| 'workload-deployments' \| 'workload-domain' \| 'workload-domains' \| 'workload-overview' \| 'workload-rollout-rows' \| 'workload-topology-chain' \| 'workload-topology' \| 'workload-topology-flow' \| 'workloads-list'` | `—` | true | Name of the console widget to draw. |
| `active` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Whether this widget is the one showing; it replays its entrance each time it becomes active. |
| `hovered` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Whether the pointer is over the host; a fragment plays its beat while it is. |
| `variant` | `'window' \| 'bare'` | `undefined` | false | How the widget is plated (window or bare): a workload screen re-plates its own frame, a fragment is drawn bare or framed in a console window, and unset keeps the widget's own plating. |
| `chrome` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Draws the console bar on a workload screen or on the window a framed fragment is drawn in; unset keeps the widget's own bar, and a bare fragment ignores it. |
| `width` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Design width of a workload screen from md up; fragments keep their own width, and unset keeps the widget's own. |
| `fade` | `'none' \| 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'y'` | `'none'` | false | Edge a workload screen, workload-overview or application-version fades out along; fragments keep their own fade. |
| `texture` | `'dots' \| 'grid' \| 'lines' \| 'dither' \| 'pixelate' \| 'none'` | `'none'` | false | Texture a full-screen widget is grounded with. |
| `tab` | `'agents' \| 'console' \| 'cli' \| 'overview' \| 'topology' \| 'deploy' \| 'main-settings' \| 'cache-settings' \| 'device-groups' \| 'functions' \| 'rules-engine'` | `undefined` | false | Tab a tabbed widget plays (`workload-overview`, `application-version`, `functions-start`); other widgets ignore it, and unset plays the first tab. |
| `cursor` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draws the named collaborator cursor a fragment acts its beat with; turn it off for a still console picture. Widgets without a cursor ignore it. |
| `autoplayInterval` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Milliseconds between revealed log lines in the deploy logs widget; unset keeps its own pace. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` only. A widget is decorative: no hover, `focus-visible`, `disabled` or `loading` state of its own. `hovered` and `active` are triggers the host drives, not states the root renders.
- Every widget is drawn in an inert `ConsoleMockupShell`, except `function-code`, whose frame is `interactive` so the viewer can switch its file tabs and copy its code. `functions-start` draws `function-code` on its `console` tab, and on its `agents` tab a `toggle-group` above its inert frame that switches the coding agent.
- `cli-terminal-start` and `cli-terminal-deploy` play a recorded Azion CLI session (init to curl, or link and deploy); `workload-topology-flow` draws domains, a workload and its bindings joined by `flow-diagram` connectors, with the workload ringed in the primary glow.
- `data-name` mirrors `name` on the root, and `data-variant` mirrors a fragment's plating (`window` or `bare`, the registry default when `variant` is unset); a workload screen leaves `data-variant` off the root. The window around a framed fragment carries `data-testid="<root testid>__frame"` and its body `<root testid>__frame-body`.
- Loading: the widget's code is loaded on demand, and the plating registry with the window part beside it. The root keeps its size while it loads and draws nothing until the widget (and its window) arrives, so a framed fragment is never drawn bare first. A `name` change clears the current widget at once, so the root never shows the earlier widget under the new `data-name`, whether the new load is still in flight or has failed.
- A `name` outside the registry (from untyped code), or a widget chunk that fails to load, warns in development only (`import.meta.env.DEV`) and leaves the root empty; it never throws.
- A plating prop the loaded widget does not read warns in development only, once per load, and changes nothing.
- `cursor` off: no collaborator cursor or name tag is drawn; the fragment's controls still open, highlight and settle on their beat.
- Each widget owns its entrance (a `ConsoleMockupShell` replay when `active` turns on) and, for fragments, its beat while `hovered` is set or the device cannot hover. Under reduced motion every widget is drawn in its settled state.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none in an inert widget, where nothing takes focus. In `function-code` the code block's file tabs and copy button keep their own focus rings, and the coding-agent switch of `functions-start` keeps the segmented button's.
- Keyboard map: none in an inert widget. In `function-code`, `Tab` reaches the code block's file tabs and copy button, which keep their own keyboard behaviour. In `functions-start` on its `agents` tab, `Tab` reaches the coding-agent switch, which keeps the segmented button's arrow-key behaviour.
- ARIA: the root is a plain `div`; the widget inside is a `figure` with `aria-hidden="true"` and `inert` (except `function-code`), and so is the window around a framed fragment, so assistive technology skips the picture. The coding-agent switch of `functions-start` sits outside that figure, named `Coding agent`. The band's own copy carries what it shows.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): widgets use the console's own text and surface pairs (`var(--text-default)` / `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-canvas)` / `var(--bg-surface)`).
- Every motion class inside a widget pairs with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target: not applicable in an inert widget; `function-code` keeps the code block's own targets, and `functions-start` the segmented button's.
- Reflow: the workload-topology node header wraps (`flex-wrap`), so a status tag moves under the node name in a narrow frame instead of overflowing it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ConsoleMockup from '@aziontech/webkit/console-mockup'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="h-96 w-full">
    <ConsoleMockup name="workloads-list" />
  </div>
</template>
```

# Copy Text

> CopyText shows one code value (a CSS custom property, a utility class, a CNAME, a key ID, a one-line command) in monospace inside a quiet bordered box, with an always-visible `CopyButton` at its inline end that copies the value. It composes `CopyButton` for the clipboard write, the copied confirmation, the live announcement and the manual-copy fallback, so it re-implements none of them. Unlike `CopyButton` (icon only, no visible value) and `TableCellId` (an identifier laid out for a table cell), CopyText is the inline "show this value and let me copy it" pattern for prose, key/value lists, token tables and cards.

- Import: `import CopyText from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-text'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Show a short code value the reader will paste elsewhere, next to its label: a design token (`--spacing-2xl`), a class (`p-(--spacing-2xl)`), a CNAME, an API key ID, a one-line CLI command.
- Token tables, key/value rows, setup steps and cards outside a data table.

## Do

- Pass the exact text in `value`; CopyText shows and copies the same string.
- Keep values to one line. A long value truncates with an ellipsis; the full value stays in the `title`, in the accessible name of the copy button and in the clipboard.
- Pass `ariaLabel` when the value alone does not say what it is (`Copy CNAME`); the default reads `Copy {value}`.
- Listen to `copy` for analytics or a toast; it fires only after the clipboard write succeeds.
- Use `size="small"` in dense tables and lists.

## Don’t

- The value is not shown, only copied → use `copy-button`.
- An identifier inside a data table cell → use `table-cell-id`.
- A multi-line snippet or a block of code → use `code-block`.
- A keyboard shortcut → use `kbd`.
- A secret that must stay masked until revealed → use `password-input` (`readonly`) with a `copy-button`.

## Related

- `copy-button` — the control CopyText composes; use it alone when the value is not displayed.
- `table-cell-id` — the same idea laid out for a table cell (fills the cell, outline button).
- `code-block` — multi-line code with its own copy control.
- `kbd` — keycaps for shortcuts, not copyable values.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `—` | true | The code value shown and copied to the clipboard. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the copy button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy {value}`). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; sets the code typography and the size of the copy button (28 px or 32 px). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `(event: MouseEvent, value: string)` | Re-emitted from the composed `CopyButton` after a successful write; `value` is the copied text. |

## States

- Visual states: `idle`, `copied` (owned by the composed `CopyButton`: check glyph, tooltip and `role="status"` announcement for 2 s), `focus-visible` on the copy button.
- `data-size` mirrors `size` on the root.
- The composed `CopyButton` carries `data-state` (`idle` | `copied`).
- Clipboard blocked: the composed `CopyButton` opens its manual-copy popover (see `.specs/copy-button.md`); CopyText adds nothing.
- Empty `value`: the box renders empty and the copy click is a no-op (CopyButton ignores an empty value).
- `loading`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `open`/`closed`: not states of this component — it is a static value with one action.

## Accessibility

- Pattern: static text plus a native `button` (WAI-ARIA APG Button pattern, provided by `CopyButton`). The value is plain text, readable and selectable; only the copy button is interactive, so there is one tab stop.
- Visible focus: inherited from `IconButton` (`focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the copy button; `Enter` / `Space` copies; `Esc` closes the manual-copy popover when the clipboard is blocked (owned by `CopyButton`).
- ARIA: the copy button's name is `ariaLabel` or `Copy {value}` (it carries the full value even when the visible text truncates); `Copied` replaces it for 2 s and is announced through CopyButton's `role="status"` region. The value has `title` set to the full value.
- Attributes: consumer `class`, `id` and listeners land on the root `span` (`inheritAttrs: false` + `v-bind="$attrs"`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the value (`--text-default` on `--bg-surface`) and ≥3:1 for the copy glyph.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every motion (inherited).
- Touch target: the copy button is 28 px (`small`) or 32 px (`medium`), above the 24 px minimum, with IconButton's 44 px hit area on `pointer: coarse`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CopyText from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-text'
</script>

<template>
  <CopyText value="--spacing-2xl" />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/copy-text.md](components/copy-text.md).

# Currency Amount

> Use CurrencyAmount to typeset one money amount anywhere; a money metric with a delta and a sparkline is a StatTile. Typesets one monetary amount as three separately-styled parts — the currency symbol, the figure, and a trailing period or unit — so money reads the same everywhere in the product instead of being a formatted string each screen spells its own way. The suffix carries the code typeface (`text-label-code-*`), which keeps the unit visually subordinate to the figure and aligns the whole set with the way the system typesets metered values. The size ladder is the house one (`small` / `medium` / `large`) and each step is a different reading distance: `small` is an amount inside a table row or a list cell, `medium` an amount stated as a fact on a card, `large` the headline figure of a pricing card. `large` bottom-aligns the suffix against the figure rather than centring it, because a 56px numeral centred against a 14px unit reads as two unrelated pieces of text.

- Import: `import CurrencyAmount from '@aziontech/webkit/currency-amount'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Any monetary amount in the product: a price in a table row or list cell (`small`), an amount stated on a card (`medium`), the headline figure of a pricing card (`large`).
- An amount followed by a period or unit (`/ mon`, `/ GB`) that should read as secondary to the figure.

## Do

- Pass `value` already formatted as a string (`'1,250.00'`). The component does no number or locale formatting.
- `prefix` defaults to `'$'`; set `prefix=""` to drop the symbol. The suffix renders only when `suffix` is set.
- Pick `size` by reading distance, not by available space: `small` in tables and lists, `medium` (the default) on cards, `large` only for a headline price.
- Don't restyle the parts with classes; each size takes its typography from the `text-amount-*` and `text-label-code-*` tokens.

## Don’t

- You need a full pricing tier with plan name, caveat and action → use `pricing-card`.
- The headline figures are not money (throughput, uptime, points of presence) → use `stats`.

## Related

- `pricing-card` — composes CurrencyAmount for its price, `medium` or `large` depending on `slotPosition`.
- `stats` — display-scale figures for metrics that aren't money.
- `stats-section` — page section of big figures with their own prefix and unit.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `''` | false | value. |
| `prefix` | `string` | `'$'` | false | prefix. |
| `suffix` | `string` | `''` | false | suffix. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects typography and the gap between the figure and the suffix. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CurrencyAmount from '@aziontech/webkit/currency-amount'
</script>

<template>
  <CurrencyAmount
    value="20"
    prefix="$"
    suffix="per month"
    size="small"
  />
</template>
```

# Eyebrow

> Overline is the short uppercase label set above a headline to name the section, panel or group it opens (the "eyebrow"). It renders its default slot in `.text-overline-md` in the brand orange (`--text-brand`: the logo orange `#F3652B` in light and dark), optionally behind a preset code-style prefix (`//`, `<>`, `</>`) and followed by a blinking terminal-style cursor. It is purely presentational text with no interaction; the marketing headers (`section-title`, `hero-title`, `call-to-action`, `media-split`, `marquee`) and several page sections render their eyebrow (the `eyebrow` prop, or `label` on `marquee`) through it.

- Import: `import Eyebrow from '@aziontech/webkit/eyebrow'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Name a section, panel or column group with one or two words set above its headline.
- Build a custom marketing header that must match the eyebrow treatment of `section-title` and `hero-title` (the `//` prefix and the blinking cursor).
- Label a band inside a page section (a comparison group, a closing panel) with the same uppercase code-style mark.

## Do

- Keep the label to one or two words: it is set uppercase and, with the default `single-line`, stays on one line whenever it fits its container.
- Turn `single-line` off only when the label can be longer than its container (narrow columns, translated copy); the label then wraps under `text-pretty`, which avoids a lone word on the last line.
- Use a `prefix` from the preset set only (`//`, `<>`, `</>`); the prefix is decorative and hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden="true"`), so never put meaning in it.
- Use `cursor` for one eyebrow per view at most; the blink stops under reduced motion.
- Keep the semantic heading in the element after the Eyebrow; the Eyebrow itself carries no heading role.

## Don’t

- The header has a headline, description and actions → use `section-title` (or `hero-title` for the hero), which already renders its `eyebrow` through Eyebrow.
- The text is a status, count or category attached to an item → use `tag` or `badge`.
- The text is the heading itself → use a real heading element; Eyebrow renders a `div` and is not a heading.
- The text is a keyboard shortcut → use `kbd`.
- The text is a field label → use `Field.Label`.

## Related

- `section-title` — the framed section header; renders its `eyebrow` as an Eyebrow with `prefix="//"` and `cursor`.
- `hero-title` — the hero copy block; renders its `eyebrow` as an Eyebrow closed by the cursor, with `single-line` turned off.
- `tag` — a compact label attached to an item, not a heading companion.
- `badge` — a compact count or status indicator.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `singleLine` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Keeps the prefix unbroken and the label on one line while it fits; a longer label wraps instead of overflowing. |
| `cursor` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a blinking terminal-style cursor after the label. |
| `prefix` | `'' \| '//' \| '<>' \| '</>'` | `''` | false | Preset prefix rendered before the label; empty renders no prefix. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The label text, rendered uppercase in the brand primary color. |

## States

- Static: no hover, focus, active or disabled states; the root is a non-interactive `div`.
- Prefix: a `span` before the label is rendered only when `prefix` is not empty; it carries `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Cursor: a decorative, `aria-hidden` `span` after the label is rendered only when `cursor` is set; the root carries `data-cursor` and drops its end padding (`data-[cursor]:pe-0`) while the cursor is shown.
- Wrapping: with `singleLine` (default) the root carries `data-single-line` and the prefix turns `whitespace-nowrap` and the label sits on one line because the root is `w-fit`; it wraps (with `text-pretty`) only when the container is narrower than the label. With it off the prefix may wrap too.
- Attributes (including `class`) are forwarded to the root `div` (`inheritAttrs: false` + `v-bind="$attrs"`).
- Test ids: root `eyebrow` (consumer `data-testid` wins); the label `<root>__label`.
- Reflow: the root is capped at the width of its container, and a label that does not fit wraps instead of overflowing at any width, at 200% zoom and with translated copy (no viewport breakpoint involved).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — the component renders no focusable element.
- Keyboard map: none; the component is not interactive.
- ARIA: no role; the root is a plain `div` and the label is read as text. The prefix `span` is decorative and carries `aria-hidden="true"`, so only the label is announced; the cursor `span` is empty and contributes no text.
- Contrast: the prefix uses `var(--text-default)` (≥4.5:1). The label uses `var(--text-brand)`, the logo orange `primary-500` in both themes: 5.5:1 or more on every dark surface, but about 2.9–3.1:1 on the light surfaces, under WCAG 2 AA 4.5:1 and APCA Lc 60. This is an owner-accepted brand exception (the eyebrow matches the logo orange; owner decision 2026-11-16), recorded in `rules/webkit-tokens.md` § "Contrast: APCA and WCAG 2"; the automated axe checks skip `color-contrast` on the `<root>__label` part in light only.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the cursor's `animate-blink`.
- Touch target: not applicable (non-interactive).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Eyebrow from '@aziontech/webkit/eyebrow'
</script>

<template>
  <Eyebrow>OVERLINE TEXT</Eyebrow>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/eyebrow.md](components/eyebrow.md).

# File Preview

> The preview of one stored file in a storage or object browser: a header with the file's glyph, name, type and size, a Download action, and a body that shows the file the way it can be read. An image renders as the image, text as wrapped monospace text, JSON pretty-printed, and any other type a no-preview state that points at Download. Long text is cut at `maxLength` characters with a note that says so. It renders what the app hands it (an image URL, the text it fetched); it fetches nothing.

- Import: `import FilePreview from '@aziontech/webkit/file-preview'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The detail pane or drawer of a file browser when a row is opened (`view/file-browser`, an Edge Storage bucket, a KV value).
- Showing an uploaded object before it is published or replaced.
- Any screen that shows one file and needs a type-aware fallback for files it cannot draw.

## Do

- Pass `mimeType` from the object's `Content-Type`; leave it empty and the file name's extension decides.
- Fetch only the first part of a large text file (a ranged request) and pass `bytes` with the full size, so the header shows the real size while the body shows the first part.
- Handle `download` with the app's own signed or authorized URL; the component never builds one.
- Pass an object URL (`URL.createObjectURL`) or a short-lived signed URL as `src`; revoke an object URL when the preview closes.

## Don’t

- Editing a file — use `CodeEditor`.
- Highlighted source code with tabs and copy — use `CodeBlock`.
- A list of files with upload progress — use `FileTokenGroup` or `UploadProgress`.
- A log stream — use `LogViewer`.

## Related

- `CodeBlock` — syntax-highlighted code; heavier, for a code sample rather than a stored object.
- `EmptyState` — the no-preview and error states inside this component.
- `Skeleton` — the loading placeholder inside this component.
- `DataTable` — the file list a preview opens from.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fileName` | `string` | `—` | true | Name of the file, shown in the header and used as the image's alternative text. |
| `mimeType` | `string` | `''` | false | Media type of the file (`image/png`, `application/json`). Empty reads the type from the file extension. |
| `bytes` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Size of the whole file in bytes, shown beside the type. Unset hides the size. |
| `src` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of an image file to draw. An image with no `src` shows the no-preview state. |
| `content` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of a text or JSON file. JSON that parses is pretty-printed; JSON that does not shows as text. |
| `maxLength` | `number` | `20000` | false | Characters of text shown before the rest is cut, with a note that says how much is shown. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a placeholder in the body while the app fetches the file; the header stays. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Why the preview could not load. Set, the body shows the error state with this text. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `download` | `MouseEvent` | The Download button was pressed; the app starts the download. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | — | More actions in the header, before Download (copy link, delete). |

## States

- `data-type`: `image` | `text` | `json` | `unknown`, the way the body draws the file (derived from `mimeType`, then the extension).
- `data-loading` mirrors `loading`; the body is a `Skeleton` in a `role="status"` region and `aria-busy` is set.
- `error` set: the body is an `EmptyState` with the error text; Download stays available.
- An image that fails to load falls back to the no-preview state.
- Text over `maxLength` sets `data-truncated` and shows the truncation note.
- A text or JSON file with no content shows the empty-file line.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `section` named by the file name (`aria-labelledby`).
- The image's `alt` is the file name.
- The text body is a focusable, scrollable region (`tabindex="0"`, `role="region"`, named `Contents of <file>`) so a keyboard user can scroll it.
- Loading is a `role="status"` region named `Loading preview`; the root has `aria-busy`.
- Download is a real `Button` with a visible label; the glyph is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Keyboard: `Tab` reaches the `actions` slot, Download and the text body; arrow keys scroll the text body.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the name, the meta line and the text.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
  import FilePreview from '@aziontech/webkit/file-preview'

  const settings = JSON.stringify({
    name: 'acme-store',
    domains: ['www.example.com', 'shop.example.com'],
    cache: { ttl: 3600, browser: true },
    origin: { host: 'origin.example.com', protocol: 'https' }
  })

  const onDownload = (event: MouseEvent) => {
    event.preventDefault()
  }
</script>

<template>
  <FilePreview
    class="max-w-(--container-md)"
    file-name="settings.json"
    mime-type="application/json"
    :bytes="182"
    :content="settings"
    @download="onDownload"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/file-preview.md](components/file-preview.md).

# Help Panel

> The content of a help side region: a topic's title, a few sections of short guidance, and the "Learn more" links that leave for the documentation. Guided tutorials belong to `tutorial-panel`. It is the thing that goes **inside** a side region, not the region itself: the consumer places it in a `Drawer` or in the page's side rail, and that host owns opening, closing and the close button. It owns no open state, so it has no `Trigger` / `Content` and no `data-state="open|closed"`. Its anatomy is the anatomy of a help page — `Header`, `Section`, `Links` — composed by hand, so a topic can omit the links or carry one section or five.

- Import: `import HelpPanelRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import HelpPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use HelpPanel for static page help (title, guidance, Learn more links) in the app layout's tools region.
- A Console screen needs contextual help beside the work: what this page is for, what a field means, where the docs are.
- The help content is loaded asynchronously and the region must reserve its space while it arrives (`loading`).

## Do

- One topic per panel. When the reader moves to another part of the page, swap the panel's content — do not stack two headers.
- Keep each `Section` to a short paragraph or a short list. If the reader has to scroll a section, the content belongs in the docs and the panel should link to it.
- Title sections with the question the reader is asking (`What is a workload?`), not with a noun (`Overview`).
- Put links to the documentation in `HelpPanel.Footer`, at the end, not inline in every section.
- Close affordances belong to the host. Do not put a close button in `HelpPanel.Header`; the `Drawer` or side rail already has one.

## Don’t

- A one-line hint attached to a single control → use `tooltip` or `hint`, or the field's `field-description`.
- A guided tutorial with tasks, progress and hotspots on the real controls → use `tutorial-panel`.
- The region itself (overlay, slide-in, close button, focus trap) → use `drawer`; put `help-panel` inside it.
- Ordered steps the reader navigates between, with the step's form filling the column beside it → use `stepper`.
- Numbered instructions inside a documentation page, read all at once → use `doc-steps` (`DocSteps.Step`).
- A page with nothing configured yet, which needs one call to action → use `empty-state`.

## Related

- `drawer` — the host that opens, closes and traps focus around a help panel shown as an overlay.
- `tutorial-panel` — guided tutorials, drawn with these parts plus its own task list.
- `link` — the standalone link each `HelpPanel.Footer` row is composed from.
- `skeleton` — what the panel renders in place of its content while `loading`.
- `doc-prose` — long-form documentation prose; a help section is a few short paragraphs, not an article.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the complementary landmark the panel renders. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Help`). |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders skeleton lines in place of the content while the help topic loads; sets aria-busy. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The panel's parts — `HelpPanel.Header`, `HelpPanel.Group`, `HelpPanel.Footer` — in reading order. Not rendered while `loading`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-footer`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: an `index.ts` (beside `help-panel.vue`) attaches every sub-component
to the root so `<HelpPanel.Header>`, `<HelpPanel.Group>` and `<HelpPanel.Footer>` resolve from one
import; the standalone imports remain the tree-shaking path. The panel has no open/closed state, so
there is no `Trigger` / `Content` — every member is named after a part of a help page. 6.0 removed the
tutorial mode (`HelpPanel.Tutorial`, `HelpPanel.Task`): `TutorialPanel` owns tutorials.

- `help-panel-header/help-panel-header.vue` — The topic's title and an optional one-line description.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — the topic's name, rendered as the panel's heading), `description?: string` (default `''` — one line under the title saying what the topic covers; not rendered when empty).
  - Slot: `default` — optional extra content under the description (a `Tag` naming the product state, for example).
  - `data-testid` fallback: `help-panel-header`.
- `help-panel-group/help-panel-group.vue` — One block of guidance with its own heading.
  - Props: `label?: string` (default `''` — the question this section answers; the section renders no heading when empty).
  - Slot: `default` — the section's prose: paragraphs, short lists, inline `text-link` anchors.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `help-panel-group`.
- `help-panel-footer/help-panel-footer.vue` — The "Learn more" footer: a heading over a column of `Link` items the consumer composes.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `undefined` — the heading over the links; absent uses the locale catalog, `Learn more` in English, and an empty string renders no heading).
  - Slot: `default` — `Link` items, one per destination.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `help-panel-footer`.
    Resulting layout (no per-component `package.json`; the root `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`
    resolves every path, and `.d.ts` is generated at publish time):

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/help-panel/
├── help-panel.vue                         (root; aside landmark, loading state)
├── help-panel.test.ts
├── index.ts                               (compound: attaches the three parts to the root)
├── help-panel-header/
│   └── help-panel-header.vue
├── help-panel-group/
│   └── help-panel-group.vue
└── help-panel-footer/
    └── help-panel-footer.vue
```

Exports to add to `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` (flat public names; category lives in the
folder only):

```jsonc
"./help-panel": "./src/components/content/help-panel/index.ts",
"./help-panel-root": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel.vue",
"./help-panel-header": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-header/help-panel-header.vue",
"./help-panel-group": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-group/help-panel-group.vue",
"./help-panel-footer": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-footer/help-panel-footer.vue"
```

Composed DS components (all present in `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`, imported by relative path
inside the package): `skeleton` (root, `loading`), `divider` (`Links`).
`link` is composed by the consumer through slots, never imported by the panel.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading`
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors the `loading` prop
- No `data-state` — the panel has no open/closed state (the host owns it)
- No `data-disabled` — nothing in the panel is interactive on its own; interactive content (`Link`, `Button`) is composed by the consumer and carries its own states

The root, while `loading`: the default slot is not rendered; in its place the root renders a title
line and three body lines with `Skeleton` (`variant="rectangle"`; title `width="60%"` `height="1.25rem"`, body
lines `width="100%"`, `width="100%"`, `width="75%"`, each `height="0.875rem"`), and sets
`aria-busy="true"`. The loading lines carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the landmark keeps its accessible
name.

- Responsive: the root is the `@container/help-panel`, so the content in the side panel adapts to the panel width.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the panel itself is not focusable; focus rings belong to the composed `Link` / `Button` controls, which already carry `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the composed links and action buttons in reading order. The panel adds no key handling of its own — no roving tabindex, no arrow navigation. `Esc` and focus trap / restore are owned by the host (`Drawer`), not by the panel.
- ARIA: the root is an `<aside>` (complementary landmark) named by `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`; `aria-busy="true"` while `loading`. Headings form an outline — `HelpPanel.Header` is `<h2>`, `Section` / `Links` titles are `<h3>` — and each `<section>` is `aria-labelledby` its heading via `useId()`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons)
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable to the panel's own markup (nothing in it is interactive); the composed `Link` / `Button` controls meet it

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import HelpPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <HelpPanel aria-label="Help: Cache settings">
      <HelpPanel.Header
        title="Cache settings"
        description="How long content stays at the edge before it is fetched again."
      />
      <HelpPanel.Group label="What does the cache TTL control?">
        <p>
          The TTL sets how many seconds an object is served from the edge before the origin is asked
          for a fresh copy.
        </p>
      </HelpPanel.Group>
      <HelpPanel.Group label="When should I bypass the cache?">
        <p>Bypass it for responses that change per user, such as carts and account pages.</p>
      </HelpPanel.Group>
      <HelpPanel.Footer>
        <Link
          label="Cache settings documentation"
          href="https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/"
          target="_blank"
        />
        <Link
          label="Purging cached content"
          href="https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/"
          target="_blank"
        />
      </HelpPanel.Footer>
    </HelpPanel>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/hotspot.md -->

# Hotspot

> Marks a real control as a step of a tutorial. It wraps the control and, while a tutorial that names its `hotspotId` runs, draws a small marker beside it. The current step's marker pulses and opens the step in a popover: the step's title, `Step n of N` with the task's name, the instructions, and Previous / Next (Finish on the last step). Outside a running tutorial, or outside a `TutorialPanel.Provider`, it renders only the wrapped control, so hotspots can stay on a page for good.

- Import: `import Hotspot from '@aziontech/webkit/hotspot'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A tutorial step is about one control on the page, and the reader should see where it is.
- The page runs inside a `TutorialPanel.Provider` and offers guided tutorials from its help region.

## Do

- Wrap exactly the control the step is about; keep the marker beside it, not inside a long row.
- Use `side="start"` when the control sits at the end of a row and the marker would overflow.
- One `hotspotId` per control and per page. The same id on two elements opens two popovers.
- Keep step content short: the popover is a small surface over the real UI.

## Don’t

- A permanent tip on a control → use `hint` or `popover`.
- A new feature announcement with no tutorial behind it → use `popover` or an `alert`.
- Help text for a form field → use the field's `field-description`.

## Related

- `tutorial-panel` — the provider holds the steps a hotspot shows; the panel lists and runs the tutorials.
- `popover` — the overlay the current step opens in.
- `help-panel` — static help without a guided run.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hotspotId` | `string` | `—` | true | Matches the `hotspotId` of a tutorial step; the marker shows while that step's tutorial runs. |
| `side` | `'start' \| 'end'` | `'end'` | false | Which side of the wrapped control the marker sits on, in reading direction. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The real control the step is about. |

## States

- Visual states: `idle` (no marker), `marked` (static marker: the step belongs to the running tutorial), `active` (the current step: marker filled and pulsing, popover open), `dismissed` (active step closed by the reader: marker filled, no pulse, popover closed)
- `data-marker` on the root when the marker shows; `data-active` on the root and on the marker for the current step (the step you are on)
- `data-side` mirrors `side`
- The popover's `data-state` is `open` | `closed` (owned by `Popover`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the marker.
- Keyboard map: the marker is a `button` in the tab order after the wrapped control (before it with `side="start"`); `Enter` / `Space` opens its step (and makes it current). Inside the popover `Tab` cycles Close, Previous and Next (the `Popover` loop); `Esc` closes the step and returns focus to the marker. Next, Previous and the marker move focus into the new step's popover; Finish moves focus to the panel's completion heading.
- ARIA: the marker is named `Tutorial step: <title>` and carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` (from `Popover.Trigger`). The popover is a non-modal `dialog` labelled by the step title and described by `Step n of N`. The pulse ring and dot are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast: the marker's `--primary` against the canvas ≥3:1 (non-text) in both themes.
- Touch target: the visible marker is 24 px; a `before:` pseudo-element extends the hit area by 8 px on each side (40 px). While the marker shows, the root reserves those 8 px on the marker's outer side (`--spacing-xs` padding), so a hotspot flush with the end of a narrow row does not scroll the page sideways.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Hotspot from '@aziontech/webkit/hotspot'
  import TutorialPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const tutorials = [
    {
      id: 'publish',
      title: 'Publish a change',
      tasks: [
        {
          title: 'Review and deploy',
          steps: [
            {
              title: 'Preview the change',
              content: 'Open the preview to check the change before anyone else sees it.',
              hotspotId: 'preview'
            },
            {
              title: 'Deploy',
              content: 'Select Deploy to send the change to production.',
              hotspotId: 'deploy'
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]

  const active = ref('publish')
  const step = ref(0)
</script>

<template>
  <TutorialPanel.Provider
    v-model:active-key="active"
    v-model:step="step"
    :tutorials="tutorials"
  >
    <div class="flex min-h-(--container-3xs) flex-wrap items-start gap-(--spacing-sm)">
      <Hotspot hotspot-id="preview">
        <Button
          label="Preview"
          variant="outline"
          size="medium"
        />
      </Hotspot>
      <Hotspot hotspot-id="deploy">
        <Button
          label="Deploy"
          variant="primary"
          size="medium"
        />
      </Hotspot>
    </div>
  </TutorialPanel.Provider>
</template>
```

<!-- components/illustration.md -->

# Illustration

> Renders an **official product illustration** — one of the scenes drawn in the Assets library in Figma and exported as an SVG that ships with this package. `name` selects a scene from a closed registry; there is no way to assemble artwork out of markup, so a page can only render illustrations design has actually signed off, and a scene can never drift between the screens that use it. The library is drawn once, in dark mode. The scene is drawn into the page as inline SVG and every colour it carries is repainted from the `illustration` theme foundation of `@aziontech/theme` — `--illustration-*` roles that alias the global tokens — so the one export follows light and dark like the rest of the page.

- Import: `import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Illustration for a static official scene.
- An empty state, error page, onboarding step, or marketing tile needs a diagrammatic illustration of a product concept (a deploy, a request path, a connected service).
- The same concept appears on more than one screen and must be the same drawing every time.
- The artwork must scale to its container without rasterizing or re-exporting.

## Do

- Leave the illustration decorative (no `ariaLabel`) unless it carries information the surrounding copy does not. A decorative illustration is hidden from assistive tech, which keeps screen readers out of a graphic that adds nothing.
- Size the illustration from the call site with a class. The root is `w-full` at the canvas aspect ratio, so a narrower column simply gets a smaller scene.
- Pick the scene that draws the claim next to it, not the one whose filename matches the page title.
- Find the names in `llms/foundations/illustrations.md` (installed under `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/`), the MCP tool `list_assets` (`kind: "illustration"`) or the Assets example. Never guess a name from a file name or a page title: an unknown name renders the placeholder.
- To add a scene, export the frame from the Figma assets library (592×300 for a scene, the tile's own size for a tile or crop), drop the `.svg` into `src/assets/illustrations/`, and register it in `registry.ts`. The test fails while a drawing in the folder is unregistered. Never hand-draw one.
- Leave `<Illustration />` unnamed where a scene is still being drawn: the placeholder frame reserves the space and reads as unfinished on the screen, which is louder than a gap nobody notices.

## Don’t

- A single glyph is enough → use an icon from `@aziontech/icons` (`<i class="az az-…">`).
- The artwork is a brand mark (a client logo, a framework mark) → those are brand assets, not illustrations.
- The whole component is "no data here, with a title and an action" → use `empty-state`, which already owns that layout and may embed an `Illustration`.
- The graphic is a live data visualization → that is a chart, not an illustration.
- The scene you need is not in the registry → it has to be drawn in Figma and exported first. Do not approximate it in markup.

## Related

- `empty-state` — the surrounding layout (illustration + title + description + actions); reach for it first and put an `Illustration` inside it.
- `flow-diagram` — a real interactive node/edge diagram driven by data; `Illustration` is decorative and static by comparison.
- `skeleton` — the loading placeholder; an illustration is never a loading state.
- `svg/azion/*` — drawn brand marks, for artwork that is not part of the illustration library.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | no | Name of an official scene in the illustration asset library. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | no | Accessible name; empty keeps the illustration decorative and hidden from assistive tech. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.

## States

- Visual states: `default` — an illustration is decorative and has no `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`, `loading`, or `active` state, and is never interactive.
- Most scenes are drawn on the one 592×300 canvas, so they line up with each other in a grid; a few tiles and crops (`ai-gateway`, `azion-highlight`, `azion-rest-api`, `branches`, `ddos-protection`, `distributed-apis-tile`, `personal-tokens`, `real-time-metrics-error-rate`, `real-time-metrics-status-codes`, `usage-chart`) keep the canvas they were drawn on. The root declares 592×300 as its intrinsic `width`/`height` until the SVG loads, which reserves the box, then the scene's own canvas, and renders at its container's width at that aspect ratio. A call site that wants it smaller caps it with a class.
- A `name` that resolves to no scene — empty, or not in the registry — renders the **placeholder**: a tinted frame reading `PLACE DESIGN ASSET`, marked `data-placeholder`, on the 592×300 canvas. An unregistered `name` also warns in the console, naming where the valid names are listed; neither case throws, and neither collapses the layout. The placeholder is always decorative, `ariaLabel` or not: it draws no scene, so announcing a description of the missing artwork would describe something that is not on the page.
- While a registered scene's SVG is still resolving, the frame already on screen stays — the placeholder never flashes in front of a scene that is about to arrive.
- Theme: each colour of the export palette maps to one `--illustration-*` role (see § Tokens), resolved where the scene renders, so a scene inside a `[data-theme]` subtree follows that subtree. A translucent ground colour is a drop shadow and stays as drawn; colours that read the same in both themes (window controls, framework marks, the dot map) stay as drawn too. Masks, clip paths and filters are never repainted.
- Every instance scopes the SVG's internal ids, so two scenes — or two copies of one — on the same page never resolve each other's gradients, masks or filters.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: _not applicable_ — an illustration is never focusable or interactive, so it declares no focus ring.
- Keyboard map: _none_ — no interactive elements, nothing in the tab order.
- ARIA: the root is an inline `<svg>`. With no `ariaLabel` it carries `aria-hidden="true"` and no role, so assistive tech skips a purely decorative graphic; with an `ariaLabel` it carries `role="img"` and the label as its `aria-label`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the component declares no text and no colour. An exported scene is decorative shape, not information — no meaning is conveyed by the artwork alone, so the copy beside it must carry the claim.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: _not applicable_ — nothing here is a target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'
</script>

<template>
  <Illustration name="modern-frontends" />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/illustration.md](components/illustration.md).

# Integration Card

> Use IntegrationCard for one tile of a catalog of integrations, extensions or plugins; for a bordered box of related content use Card, and for a collection of resource records shown as cards use CardList. A catalog tile laid out from props: a logo mark, the item name, its vendor, a short description, badges, the installed state and one action. The name is the tile's single target: a link when `href` is set, otherwise a button that emits `select`, stretched over the whole tile. `featured` gives the centred, raised layout used for a short row of picks above the full catalog. It was the `integration` variant of `Card` until 6.0, split out because a tile shares neither the header nor the footer of a content card.

- Import: `import IntegrationCard from '@aziontech/webkit/integration-card'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A catalog tile for an integration, an extension or a plugin: the logo, the name, the vendor, a short description, badges, the installed state and one action.
- A short row of highlighted integrations above the full catalog (Featured): add `featured` for the centred, raised layout with the badges in the corner.
- A starter template or next-step tile that carries a mark, a name and a short description and links somewhere.

## Do

- The tile is laid out from props: `title`, `logo` (or the `logo` slot), `vendor`, `description`, `badges` and `installed`. The title becomes a link when `href` is set, otherwise a button that emits `select`, and it stretches over the whole tile so the tile is one target. Put a single action (Install, Configure) in the `actions` slot; it sits above the stretched target and stays reachable on its own.
- Keep the description to one or two sentences; the tile clamps it to three lines.
- Show at most two badges (category, context, plan). The installed state is a prop, not a badge, so it reads the same everywhere.
- Tiles sit under a section heading, so their title is an `h3`.
- `featured` centres the mark, the name, the vendor and the description on a raised surface with a primary glow at the top, and moves the badges to the top end corner, where a badge without `severity` is `primary`. Use it for a row of at most three or four picks above the full catalog, never for every tile; the full catalog keeps the plain tile.

## Don’t

- A bordered box of related content with a title, a body and a footer → use `card`.
- One record of a resource list shown as cards, with selection and fields → use `card-list` (with `useCollection`).
- One tier of a pricing comparison → use `pricing-card`.
- A single row of title, description, media and actions → use `item`.

## Related

- `card` — the content box this tile was split from; shares its surface tokens.
- `tag` — renders the badges and the Installed state.
- `card-list` — the resource list in card form, with selection.
- `view/marketplace` — the block that lays these tiles out in a filtered grid.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The item name; the tile's single target. |
| `logo` | `string` | `''` | false | Icon class for the logo mark. The `logo` slot takes an image instead. |
| `vendor` | `string` | `''` | false | Who publishes the item, shown as "by {vendor}". |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One or two sentences on what the item does. |
| `badges` | `IntegrationCardBadge[]` | `[]` | false | Small tags such as the category or the context (`{ label, variant?, severity? }`, `variant` a `TagVariant` and `severity` a `TagSeverity` (`IntegrationCardBadgeVariant` and `IntegrationCardBadgeSeverity`); a badge with neither is `info`, a featured badge with neither is the `primary` variant). |
| `installed` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the Installed tag. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | The title links here; without it the title is a button that emits `select`. |
| `featured` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The featured layout, centred on a raised surface with a primary glow at the top and the badges in the top end corner. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `event: MouseEvent` | Without `href`: the title (the whole tile) was activated. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Extra content under the description. |
| `logo` | — | Replaces the logo mark, for an `img` with an empty `alt`. |
| `actions` | — | One action at the end of the tile, above the stretched title target. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`
- `hover` shades the surface, `focus-visible` rings the whole tile (the ring sits on the stretched title target), `installed` adds the success Installed tag.
- Featured (`featured`): the surface is raised; `hover` strengthens the border and brightens the top glow instead of shading the surface; the layout is centred and the badges sit in the top end corner. `data-featured` on the root drives the styles.
- Test ids: `integration-card` on the root, with `__logo`, `__title`, `__vendor`, `__installed`, `__actions`, and `__glow` and `__badges` when featured.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the stretched title target draws an inset `focus-visible:after:ring-2 focus-visible:after:ring-(--ring-color)` around the whole tile, so `overflow-clip` on the tile never cuts it.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the title (a link or a button) and then the action; `Enter` activates the title (`Space` too when it is a button).
- ARIA: the root is a `section`; the title is an `h3` holding the link or the button; the logo mark is `aria-hidden`; the featured glow is `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the hover and glow transitions.
- Touch target: the whole tile is the title's target; the action is a regular `Button`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import IntegrationCard from '@aziontech/webkit/integration-card'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const opened = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-[400px] flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <IntegrationCard
      title="Request Signer"
      vendor="Acme Inc."
      logo="az az-key"
      description="Sign every request at the edge with a rotating key, so the origin only answers traffic that passed through."
      :badges="[{ label: 'Firewall' }]"
      @select="opened = 'Request Signer'"
    >
      <template #actions>
        <Button
          label="Install"
          variant="outline"
          size="small"
        />
      </template>
    </IntegrationCard>
    <p
      class="m-0 text-body-xs text-(--text-muted)"
      role="status"
    >
      {{ opened ? `Opened ${opened}` : '' }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```
