# Item

> Use Item rows for a short list of mixed rows (title, description, actions) that do not share columns; read-only label/value facts about one resource are KeyValueList, records compared across columns are a Table, and what a plan includes is a PlanFeatureList. Versatile flex row for title, description, media, and actions. Mirrors the shadcn-vue Item anatomy so consumers can reorder or omit regions. Compose with `ItemGroup` for gapped off-card lists, `ItemList` for divided in-card lists (inside a `Card`), and `ItemSeparator` between rows. Reference: https://www.shadcn-vue.com/docs/components/item (adapted to Webkit tokens and naming).

- Import: `import ItemRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/item-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Item from '@aziontech/webkit/item'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A row that pairs a title and description with leading media (icon, avatar, image) and trailing actions — settings entries, team members, next steps, notifications.
- A list of such rows: `Item.Group` for gapped rows off a card, `Item.List` for divided rows inside a `card`.
- A whole row that is one link or button — set `href` and the row renders as an anchor, or set `clickable` and bind `@click` and it renders as a native button.
- A compact option in a chooser list (a workload, a host, an application picked under a search field): `variant="option"` with `clickable`, so the row is a native button. The row is 38 px — `--spacing-xs` block padding, `--spacing-sm` inline padding and gap, the title at `text-body-md` — and paints `var(--bg-selected)` when the row is `aria-pressed="true"` or `aria-selected="true"`.

## Do

- Use `Item.Group` off-card and `Item.List` inside a `card` with `:padded="false"`; both force their child items' `variant` (`inline` in a group, `default` in a list), so do not set `variant` on rows inside them.
- `Item.List` draws its own dividers — do not add `Item.Separator` inside it.
- With `href` or `clickable` the whole row is one focusable control with the row's hover, active and focus ring, so do not also put buttons or links inside that row.
- Set `Item.Media` `type="icon"` for a glyph and `type="image"` for a picture; the frame sizes and clips the content.
- Use `size="small"` for dense lists; `medium` is the default.
- For the rows of a picker under a search field use `variant="option"` (not `size="small"` plus your own padding): it sets its own density and the selected fill from `aria-pressed` / `aria-selected`, so `size` does not change it. Keep option rows in a plain column, not in `Item.List` or `Item.Group`, which force their own variant.

## Don’t

- Records that share columns and need sorting, selection or paging → use `table`.
- Hierarchical navigation rows in a sidebar → use `sidebar-menu`.
- A grid of selectable option cards → use `radio-group` with `variant="card"`.
- A single surface that frames arbitrary content → use `card`.

## Related

- `card` — the surface an `Item.List` sits in (with `:padded="false"`).
- `table` — columnar data; below `sm`, `listing-table-section` swaps its table rows for `item` rows.
- `sidebar-menu` — navigation rows with nesting and drill levels.
- `avatar` — the usual leading media for people rows inside `Item.Media`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'outline' \| 'muted' \| 'inline' \| 'option'` | `'default'` | false | Item root surface variant. `inline` removes the row's outer padding (transparent surface) for inline placement and divided in-card lists. `option` is a compact chooser row (38 px, title at body-md) that fills when its element is pressed or selected. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Item root density (padding and gap). |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | When set, the whole row renders as an anchor link to this URL. |
| `clickable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the whole row as a button; bind the click handler on the Item. Ignored when href is set. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Every sub-component exposes `default` for its region. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/item-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-list`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-separator`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-media`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-actions`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-footer`

## Sub-components

- `item.vue` — Root row container (`variant`, `size`).
- `item-group.vue` — Vertical list wrapper (`role="list"`) with a gap between rows; for off-card lists.
- `item-list.vue` — Vertical list wrapper (`role="list"`) that draws full-width dividers between rows and no gap; for in-card lists (inside a `Card` with `padded=false`).
- `item-separator.vue` — Horizontal divider between rows in a group.
- `item-media.vue` — Leading media slot (`type` for icon/image frames).
- `item-content.vue` — Main text column (title + description).
- `item-title.vue` — Primary label line.
- `item-description.vue` — Secondary muted line.
- `item-actions.vue` — Trailing actions cluster.
- `item-header.vue` — Optional top band (e.g.
- `item-footer.vue` — Optional bottom band.

## States

- Visual states on Item shell: `default` only, **except with `href` or `clickable`**, where the root is the whole-row anchor or button and gains row-level `hover`, `active`, and `focus-visible`
- With `href` or `clickable`, the row paints `var(--bg-selected)` while it carries `aria-pressed="true"` or `aria-selected="true"`, whatever its `variant`: a pressed chooser row binds `:aria-pressed` on the Item and adds no fill class of its own
- Without `href` or `clickable`, the root is a `div` and slotted controls (`Button`, `a`, etc.) own hover, active, and `focus-visible`
- `data-variant` on Item root: `default` | `outline` | `muted` | `inline` | `option` (an Item inside `ItemGroup` is forced to `inline`; inside `ItemList` to `default`)
- `variant="option"`: `--spacing-xs` block padding, `--spacing-sm` inline padding and gap whatever the `size`, `Item.Title` at `text-body-md`, and `var(--bg-selected)` on the row while it carries `aria-pressed="true"` or `aria-selected="true"`
- `data-size` on Item root: `small` | `medium`
- `data-type` on ItemMedia: `default` | `icon` | `image`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: on slotted links and buttons. The Item shell draws no focus ring on its own, except with `href` or `clickable`, where the row itself (an anchor or a native button) receives the `focus-visible` ring (`focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`) and hover/active feedback.
- Keyboard map: slotted links and buttons supply Tab order; with `href` the row is one link (`Enter` follows it), with `clickable` one native button (`Enter` and `Space` activate it).
- ARIA: `ItemGroup` and `ItemList` use `role="list"` and tell their direct Items, through context, that they are list members; the consumer wires nothing. A member Item renders `role="listitem"` on its root. A member Item with `href` or `clickable` renders a `role="listitem"` wrapper (`data-slot="item-listitem"`) around its anchor or button root, so a link row stays a link. An Item outside a list, or nested inside another Item, gets no list role. `ItemSeparator` uses `role="separator"`, and `role="none"` when it sits directly inside a list, where a separator is not an allowed child.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for title and description text.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on color transitions.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on slotted actions (owned by children).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Item from '@aziontech/webkit/item'
</script>

<template>
  <Item>
    <Item.Content>
      <Item.Title>Basic Item</Item.Title>
      <Item.Description>A simple item with title and description.</Item.Description>
    </Item.Content>
    <Item.Actions>
      <Button
        label="Action"
        variant="outline"
        size="small"
      />
    </Item.Actions>
  </Item>
</template>
```

<!-- components/kbd.md -->

# Kbd

> Kbd renders keyboard input — a single key or a shortcut combination — as a compact, non-interactive keycap. It reads like a real key: a bordered surface with a thicker bottom edge for depth. Modifier keys are passed as boolean props (`meta`, `shift`, `alt`, `ctrl`) and rendered with the correct OS-aware glyph (⌘ on macOS, the catalog's `Ctrl` elsewhere), and named keys (`keyName`) print their localized name, so consumers never hardcode platform symbols or English key names. The platform is read once mounted: the server and the first client render print the non-Mac names, then a Mac swaps in its glyphs, so hydration never mismatches. Use it for shortcut hints in prose, menus, and control suffixes (e.g. the ⌘K hint in `command`). A sequence can also be passed as a `keys` list (`['meta', 'shift', 'p']`, `['arrow-up', 'arrow-down']`), drawn either as one keycap (`variant="combined"`, the default) or as one keycap per key (`variant="separate"`, each a nested `<kbd>` as HTML specifies for key combinations). Arrow keys and the Return glyph (`↵`) are named keys like `escape`.

- Import: `import Kbd from '@aziontech/webkit/kbd'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Show a keyboard shortcut or a single key inline (a ⌘K hint on a search button, an `Esc` hint in a dialog, `/` to focus search).
- Present a modifier combination whose glyph should adapt to the user's OS.

## Do

- Keep the default slot to a single key or glyph (`K`, `7`, `Enter`, `Esc`, `/`); avoid lowercase words or sentences.
- Pass modifiers as boolean props rather than hardcoding `⌘`/`⇧` so the glyph adapts to the OS.
- Name a key with `key-name` (`<Kbd key-name="escape" />`) instead of typing `Esc` or `Enter`: the text comes from the locale catalog (`kbd.*`), so it follows `WebkitProvider` (`Espaço` in pt-BR, `Intro` in es) and a consumer renames it with `messages` (`{ kbd: { ctrl: 'Strg' } }`). The macOS symbols `⌘`, `⌃`, `⌥` and `⇧` are never translated.
- Place surrounding punctuation outside the element, not inside the keycap.
- Use `keys` when the shortcut comes from data (a command list, a settings table); use the boolean props when you write it by hand. Pick `variant="separate"` for a sequence pressed key by key or for arrow pairs (`↑` `↓` to navigate), `combined` for a chord pressed at once.
- Name the Return key `return` (`↵`) in compact hints (a footer "↵ to select"); keep `enter` (`Enter`) where the word reads better.

## Don’t

- The token is a status/category label, not a key → use `tag` or `badge`.
- You need an interactive control that fires on click → use `button` / `icon-button`; Kbd is a presentational hint only.

## Related

- `command` — consumes Kbd for its per-item shortcut hints and its ⌘K trigger affordance.
- `badge` — compact non-interactive indicator for counts/status; Kbd is specifically for keyboard keys.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `meta` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the meta/command modifier glyph (⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). |
| `ctrl` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Control modifier glyph (⌃ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). |
| `shift` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Shift modifier glyph (⇧). |
| `alt` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Alt/Option modifier glyph (⌥ on macOS, Alt elsewhere). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `small` is a denser keycap for menus, command bars, and table cells. |
| `keyName` | `'' \| 'ctrl' \| 'alt' \| 'shift' \| 'escape' \| 'enter' \| 'space' \| 'tab' \| 'backspace' \| 'delete' \| 'return' \| 'arrowUp' \| 'arrowDown' \| 'arrowLeft' \| 'arrowRight'` | `''` | false | Named key printed from the locale catalog (`escape` → `Esc`, `enter` → `Enter`); the slot still renders after it. |
| `keys` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | A key sequence drawn after the modifier props and `keyName`: `meta`/`ctrl`/`alt`/`shift` print their OS-aware glyph, a named key prints from the catalog (matched without case or hyphens, so `arrowUp`, `arrow-up` and the DOM's `ArrowUp` are one key), a single character is upper-cased, anything else prints as written. |
| `variant` | `'combined' \| 'separate'` | `'combined'` | false | Visual variant: one keycap holding every key, or one keycap per key. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The single key or glyph rendered after any modifier glyphs (`K`, `Enter`, `Esc`). |

## States

Kbd is non-interactive: it has no hover, focus, active, or disabled states and emits no events. Variants are exposed as `data-*` attributes on the root for Tailwind variant styling and for test/Code-Connect hooks:

- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop (`small` | `medium`).
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop (`combined` | `separate`). With `separate` the root drops its keycap chrome (border, surface, shadow, padding) and each key renders as a nested `<kbd>` keycap with the same size tokens, separated by `--spacing-2xs`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — Kbd is non-interactive (no focus, no keyboard, no tab stop).
- Keyboard map: none — Kbd is a presentational hint and exposes no interactive affordance.
- ARIA: the root is the native `<kbd>` element so assistive tech announces it as keyboard input; modifier glyphs render as text so a combination like ⌘K is announced in reading order.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface)` is theme-guaranteed in both light and dark.
- `motion-reduce:*`: not applicable — Kbd is static (no motion).
- Touch target: not applicable — Kbd is non-interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Kbd from '@aziontech/webkit/kbd'
</script>

<template>
  <Kbd meta>K</Kbd>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/kbd.md](components/kbd.md).

# Key Value List

> Use KeyValueList to show read-only label/value facts about one resource, including its tags; rows with their own actions are Item rows. A grid of labelled facts about one subject: each pair is a key (the term) and its value, which may be plain text or a composed component such as a `Link`, `Tag`, `CopyButton` or `StatusIndicator`. It renders a native description list laid out in 1 to 4 responsive columns, optionally split into titled groups, and owns its loading and empty-value surfaces. It replaces the hand-rolled label/value grids the resource detail templates (`ResourceSummary`, the detail Overview tabs) draw today.

- Import: `import KeyValueListRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import KeyValueList from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- The facts band of a resource detail or Overview page: ID, status, region, created at, domain.
- A read-only summary of settings before a confirm step (review step, deploy summary).
- Any set of named attributes of a single subject where the reader scans keys to find a value.
- Facts that fall into named clusters (General, Networking, Source) shown side by side as titled columns.
- The rows of a summary card, label on the left and value on the right (a subscription plan: Plan Price, Billing Period, Next Invoice): `variant="split"`.

## Do

- Keep keys short nouns in sentence case ("Created", "Region"), never sentences or trailing colons.
- Order pairs by what the reader looks for first: identity, status, then the rest.
- Pick `variant` by the box: `stacked` (label over value) for a facts band that spans a page; `split` (label at the start, value at the end of one row) for a narrow summary card where each row reads as a line of a receipt. Do not hand-write a `<dl>` with `justify-between` for it.
- Use `columns` for width, not for grouping; use `KeyValueList.Group` when the facts form named clusters, one group per column.
- Do not mix bare Items and Groups at the same level; pick one shape per instance.
- Leave the value slot out (or render nothing in it) when a value is absent; the component shows the em dash and its accessible "Not set". Do not type your own "-", "N/A" or "None".
- Put a `CopyButton` after an ID or key, never in place of the visible value.
- Use the `info` slot for a short `Hint` that explains the key; long explanations belong in the page, not in a tooltip.
- Drive `loading` from the data request so the labels stay in place and only the values shimmer.

## Don’t

- Rows of many subjects compared attribute by attribute → use `table`.
- Editable fields → use the form field components (`field` with `input`, `select`, …); this component is read-only.
- A single headline figure with a trend → use `stat-tile`.
- A list of items with no key/value relation → use a plain list or `item`.

## Related

- `table` — many subjects, one row each; KeyValueList describes one subject.
- `card` — the surface a KeyValueList usually sits in; KeyValueList brings no surface of its own.
- `copy-button` — the trailing copy affordance for IDs and keys inside a value.
- `status-indicator`, `tag` — status and category values.
- `link` — a value that navigates (a domain, a linked resource).
- `hint` — the info glyph composed into an Item's `info` slot.
- `skeleton` — rendered in place of each value while the root is `loading`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'stacked' \| 'split'` | `'stacked'` | false | How each pair is laid out: `stacked` puts the label over the value, `split` puts the label at the start and the value at the end of one row. |
| `columns` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4` | `1` | false | Columns at full width; fewer columns when a cell would get narrower than `--container-3xs`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Replaces every value with a skeleton while the data loads; labels stay visible. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list when no visible heading names it. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | `KeyValueList.Item` children, or `KeyValueList.Group` children — one shape per instance. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list-group`

## Sub-components

The root `key-value-list.vue` renders a `<dl>` that is the grid. It provides a context (`injection-key.ts` + `composables/use-key-value-list-context.ts`) holding the root test id and the `loading` state, read-only. Every part throws a clear error when used outside `<KeyValueList>`.

Markup is valid HTML in both shapes: an Item is a `<div>` wrapping one `<dt>` and one `<dd>` (allowed as a direct child of `<dl>`). A Group is also a `<div>` child of the root `<dl>`: its title is the `<dt>`, and its `<dd>` holds a nested `<dl>` with the group's Items — a term whose description is a list of pairs. A heading element is not used for the group title because `<dt>` does not allow heading content.

- `key-value-list.vue` — the root: the `<dl>` grid, the `columns` layout, `aria-label`, `aria-busy`, the context.
- `key-value-list-item/key-value-list-item.vue` — one pair: `<div>` → `<dt>` (label + `info`) + `<dd>` (value).
  - Props: `label: string` (required — the key, rendered in the `<dt>`).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the value (text or composed components); fallback is the empty-value marker (`<span aria-hidden="true">—</span><span class="sr-only">Not set</span>`), shown when the slot is omitted or renders nothing. `info` — optional affordance after the label text inside the `<dt>`, such as a `Hint`.
  - While the root is `loading`, the `<dd>` renders a `Skeleton` in place of the value; the label stays visible.
  - `data-testid` fallback `${rootTestId}__item`; a consumer `data-testid` on the Item wins.
- `key-value-list-group/key-value-list-group.vue` — a titled column: `<div>` → `<dt>` (label) + `<dd>` → nested `<dl>` stacking its Items in one column.
  - Props: `label: string` (required — the group's term, shown above its Items).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the group's `KeyValueList.Item` children.
  - Occupies one cell of the root grid, so `columns` sets how many groups sit side by side.
  - `data-testid` fallback `${rootTestId}__group`; a consumer `data-testid` on the Group wins.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading`, empty value (per Item)
- `data-variant` on the root and on each Item mirrors `variant`; `split` turns each Item into one row (label start, value end, wrapping under the label only when the value does not fit)
- `data-columns` on the root mirrors `columns` and drives the grid template through `data-[columns=n]:` variants
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors `loading`; `aria-busy="true"` while loading
- Empty value: the Item's `<dd>` shows `—` (`aria-hidden`) plus a visually hidden "Not set"
- Responsive columns follow the list's own box, not the viewport: the grid is `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(100%, max(--container-3xs, share)), 1fr))`, where the share is the box divided by `columns`. It shows `columns` columns when every cell gets at least `--container-3xs` (256 px), fewer otherwise, and one column in a narrow box; a list in a drawer or split view lays out for that box.

- No `disabled`, `invalid`, `readonly`, `error`, `open` states: the component is read-only and fetches nothing. An error loading the facts is the page's surface (e.g. `message`), not this component's.

## Accessibility

- Native description list: root `<dl>`, each Item `<div>` → `<dt>` + `<dd>`; each Group `<div>` → `<dt>` + `<dd>` → nested `<dl>`. Screen readers announce term/definition pairs with no ARIA roles added.
- `ariaLabel` is applied as `aria-label` on the root `<dl>` only when non-empty; when a visible heading precedes the list, the consumer names it with `aria-labelledby` through `$attrs` instead.
- Loading: `aria-busy="true"` on the root; each `Skeleton` is decorative (`aria-hidden`), so assistive tech reads the labels and waits for the values.
- Empty value: `—` is `aria-hidden="true"`; a `sr-only` "Not set" gives the `<dd>` an announced value.
- Keyboard map: the component itself has no tab stop. Focus moves only through interactive values and `info` affordances (`Link`, `CopyButton`, `Hint`) in reading order, each with its own focus ring and key handling.
- Reading order follows source order: row by row across the grid, top to bottom inside a group.
- Contrast: `var(--text-muted)` keys and `var(--text-default)` values at ≥4.5:1 on `var(--bg-surface)` and `var(--bg-canvas)` in both themes.
- No motion of its own; the composed `Skeleton` carries `motion-reduce:animate-none`.
- Touch targets belong to the composed interactive values; the component adds none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'
  import KeyValueList from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
  import StatusIndicator from '@aziontech/webkit/status-indicator'
</script>

<template>
  <KeyValueList aria-label="Workload details">
    <KeyValueList.Item label="Workload ID">
      <span>1752167890</span>
      <CopyButton
        value="1752167890"
        aria-label="Copy workload ID"
        size="small"
      />
    </KeyValueList.Item>
    <KeyValueList.Item label="Status">
      <StatusIndicator
        severity="success"
        label="Active"
      />
    </KeyValueList.Item>
    <KeyValueList.Item label="Created">Nov 10, 2026, 14:32</KeyValueList.Item>
    <KeyValueList.Item label="Region">US East (Virginia)</KeyValueList.Item>
    <KeyValueList.Item label="Domain">
      <Link
        label="shop.example.com"
        href="https://shop.example.com"
        size="small"
      />
    </KeyValueList.Item>
  </KeyValueList>
</template>
```

# Line Figure

> An isometric line-art figure that answers the pointer: one per product (cache TTL, load balancer, DNS lookup, firewall, a 404 page and 20 more), drawn by a small engine into one SVG with the illustration tokens, so it follows the theme. Each figure loads on demand. The pointer, or focus with arrow keys, moves the figure through its answer; `play` walks it through on its own until a person arrives; under reduced motion it holds a still frame. From the design sample's `shared/ui/line-figure` (engine MIT, kept with its `LICENSE`). The figures are marketing assets, listed in the marketing inventory.

- Import: `import LineFigure from '@aziontech/webkit/line-figure'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use LineFigure for an interactive isometric product figure.
- The art beside a product's copy on a landing or a docs home.
- An empty state or a not-found page (`azion-404`).

## Do

- One figure per view; two figures answering the pointer compete.
- Pass `aria-label` when the page says something more specific than the figure's own description.
- Use `play` only where nothing else moves.
- Take the name from `llms/foundations/line-figures.md` or `list_assets({ kind: "lineFigures" })`; an unknown name draws nothing.
- In a container that sizes to its content (the `EmptyState` `icon` slot, a centred flex column) the figure takes its natural 400×320 size, capped by the space available. Put it in a sized wrapper (`<div class="w-60 max-w-full">`) when the art should be smaller.

## Don’t

- For static, non-interactive art — use `Illustration`.
- For data — use the charts.
- Inside dense application screens.

## Related

- `Illustration` — static art from the registry.
- `ConsoleMockup` — product scenes.
- `EmptyState` — can carry a figure in its art slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `LineFigureName \| ''` | `''` | false | Registered figure to draw; an unknown or empty name draws nothing. |
| `intensity` | `number` | `0.5` | false | How strongly the figure answers the pointer, from 0 (subtle) to 1 (strong). |
| `play` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Walks the figure through its answer on its own until a pointer or focus arrives; a still frame under reduced motion. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name; falls back to the figure's own English description. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read` | `caption: string` | The figure's current reading each time it changes (the first reading on mount). |

## Assets

- Line figures: every valid name is in line-figures.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "lineFigures" })`). An unknown or empty name draws nothing.

## States

- `data-name` mirrors `name`; `data-play` is present while `play` is on.
- Empty: no role and an empty SVG for an unknown name.

## Accessibility

- `role="img"` named by `ariaLabel` or the figure description; the SVG is `aria-hidden`.
- The figure is not a control: it never takes focus on its own, and the page stays operable without it.
- Readings go out through `read`; a page that shows them should put them in a polite live region (see the Play example).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import LineFigure from '@aziontech/webkit/line-figure'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="max-w-(--container-sm)">
    <LineFigure name="cache-ttl" />
  </div>
</template>
```

# Logo

> A third-party mark (a client, a competitor, an analyst firm, a standard or certification, a coding agent) drawn right on both themes. The asset registries already hold the files (`@aziontech/webkit/assets/client-registry`, `@aziontech/webkit/assets/competitor-registry` and the `@aziontech/webkit/assets/<file>.svg` exports); every surface that drew one repeated the same theme rule by hand (two `img` tags revealed per `[data-theme]`, a `brightness-0` silhouette, a CSS mask in `currentColor`) and none had every route. `Logo` holds the rule once: a light/dark pair of files, or one file inverted on the theme where it would vanish, or one ink (the theme's black or white, the surrounding `currentColor`, or black pinned for a coloured fill), and the company's name as a typographic wordmark when there is no file yet. It replaces the design sample's `AgentMark` and `ClientMark`. It is a renderer: it takes the file URLs from a registry entry and imports no registry itself, so a page pays only for the marks it shows.

- Import: `import Logo from '@aziontech/webkit/logo'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Logo for any other company's mark (client, competitor, agent, certification).
- A logo wall, a trust strip, a client story card, a quote attribution, a comparison column head: any place that shows another company's mark.
- The coding agents a prompt works with (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor), drawn in the ink of the surface they sit on.
- A list of standards or analyst firms (SOC, PCI DSS, Gartner, Forrester).

## Do

- Pass a registry entry as it stands: `name`, `src` from `logo`, `src-light` from `logoLight`, `artwork` from `artwork`. The registry knows which theme each file is drawn for.
- Set the height with `size`: `small` (16 px) beside a label or in a table cell, `medium` (24 px, the default) in a card or a list, `large` (32 px) in a logo wall or a quote attribution. The width follows each file's own aspect ratio. Cap wide wordmarks with `max-w-*`.
- In a list of many clients, use `variant="monochrome"`: per-brand colour reads as noise next to twenty others.
- On a coloured fill (white, `--primary`), use `variant="knockout"`: a fill does not follow the theme, so the ink must not either.
- On a surface that is dark in both themes, or among drawn diagram parts, use `variant="current"` so the mark takes the surface's own ink.
- When the text beside the mark already names the company, set `decorative`.

## Don’t

- The Azion logo → use `Brand`.
- A card network beside a payment method → use `PaymentBrand`.
- A person or an account → use `Avatar`.
- A product icon or a UI glyph → use an icon from `@aziontech/icons`.
- A grid of client marks → use `LogoWall`; it renders each mark and can render `Logo` in its `mark` slot.

## Related

- `brand` — the Azion lockup; `Logo` is everyone else's.
- `payment-brand` — card-network plates, drawn in tokens.
- `logo-wall` — the grid that lays marks out; `Logo` draws one mark.
- `avatar` — a person's or an organization's picture with initials.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `—` | true | The company or product the mark belongs to; the accessible name, and the typographic wordmark drawn when no file is set. |
| `src` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of the mark; on its own it serves both themes, and with `srcLight` it is the dark-theme file. Empty draws the wordmark. |
| `srcLight` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of the light-theme file; with `src` both files render and the theme reveals one. |
| `artwork` | `'color' \| 'light' \| 'dark'` | `'color'` | false | The ink a single file is drawn in: `light` art (for dark surfaces) is inverted on the light theme, `dark` art is inverted on the dark theme, `color` is kept as is. Ignored when `srcLight` is set or `variant` is not `color`. |
| `variant` | `'color' \| 'monochrome' \| 'current' \| 'knockout'` | `'color'` | false | Ink: `color` keeps the vendor's colours, `monochrome` paints one silhouette black on light and white on dark, `current` paints it in the surrounding text colour, `knockout` pins it black for a mark on a coloured fill. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when it should differ from `name`. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Height of the mark: `small` 16 px, `medium` 24 px, `large` 32 px; the width follows the file's aspect ratio. |
| `decorative` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Hides the mark from assistive technology when the text beside it already names the company. |

## States

- `data-variant` on the root: `color` | `monochrome` | `current` | `knockout`.
- `data-route` on the root: `pair` (both files in the DOM, the theme reveals one), `single` (one file, filtered by `artwork` or the ink of `variant`), `wordmark` (no file: the name in type).
- `data-artwork` on the root mirrors `artwork`.
- `data-size` on the root mirrors `size`: `small` is `h-4`, `medium` is `h-6`, `large` is `h-8`.
- `data-sized` on the root when the caller's class sets a height (`h-*` or `size-*`, with or without a breakpoint); it then wins over `size`.
- Not applicable: `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `open`/`closed` (a static mark).

## Accessibility

- Pattern: an image (`role="img"` on the root) named by `ariaLabel`, else `name`. The files inside have empty `alt` and are `aria-hidden`, so a light/dark pair is announced once.
- With `decorative` the root is `aria-hidden="true"` and has no role.
- Not focusable; no keyboard map (a static mark).
- Contrast: marks are logos (WCAG 1.4.3 exempts logotypes); the `monochrome` route makes a mark pure black or white against the page, and `knockout` pure black on a light fill.
- Forced colors: the `current` route paints `currentColor`, so it follows `CanvasText`.
- No motion.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import { CLIENTS } from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/client-registry'
  import Logo from '@aziontech/webkit/logo'

  const client = CLIENTS.find((entry) => entry.name === 'Agibank')
</script>

<template>
  <Logo
    :name="client.name"
    :src="client.logo"
    :src-light="client.logoLight"
    :artwork="client.artwork"
    size="large"
    class="max-w-40"
  />
</template>
```

# Network Map

> A decorative, full-bleed layer that paints the dotted world map with Azion's PoPs lit in the brand accent. It is a material — it takes no content and claims no space — but unlike a static illustration it is tuned by the consumer (region, PoP density, landmass opacity, static or animated) to sit behind a band's copy.

- Import: `import NetworkMap from '@aziontech/webkit/network-map'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use NetworkMap as a decorative world-map backdrop; for data by location use MapChart.
- As the backdrop of a band whose subject is the network (reach, data centers, latency, resilience), composed as a sibling under the band's copy inside a positioned, clipping ancestor.
- When a band is about one part of the network, so only that region's PoPs should light (`region`) while the whole world stays drawn.
- When the same artwork has to read with more or fewer PoPs lit, or with none at all (`density="none"`), from one component instead of separate exports.

## Do

- Give the layer a positioned ancestor (`relative overflow-hidden`); it fills that box and nothing else.
- Never offset or resize the layer with utilities (`left-*`, `w-*`, `inset-*`). It always fills its positioned ancestor, and `position` + `fade` place the map inside that box — so a fade measures from the band's own edges. An offset box moves the fade's edges off the band's and makes the two placements fight.
- To make the map smaller or larger inside its box, set `scale` instead of resizing the layer. The map shrinks toward its `position` corner, so there is no hard edge and the fade keeps measuring from the band's edges.
- Keep `opacity` low (the default `0.4`) when copy sits over the landmass; the PoPs keep full strength so the network still reads.
- For copy on one side of a band, park the map on the other side with `position` and fade it toward the copy (`position="right"` + `fade="left"`); the default stops need no consumer class.
- Tune where a fade holds and ends with `--network-map-fade-start` / `--network-map-fade-end` only when the default stops do not fit, instead of adding masks.
- Leave `animated` off by default; turn it on for the one band per page whose subject is the network.
- To nudge the map or let it run off the band, set `offsetX` / `offsetY` (for example `:offset-x="0.15"` to bleed right, `:offset-y="-0.1"` to bleed up) instead of offsetting the layer.
- The landmass is the design's pixel map cell for cell (4,987 cells on a 10-unit grid), and the default `medium` density lights the design's PoP field exactly: 172 cells, each metro a capital with up to two satellites, pulsing in the design's three phases. `low` lights the capitals alone (71); `high` adds 31 outlying PoPs.
- `asia` and `oceania` hold no PoPs — the artwork carries no accent field there — so either region lights none and the map reads as landmass alone.

## Don’t

- For a real node/edge diagram driven by data → use `flow-diagram`.
- As a wrapper around content. The layer is absolutely positioned and paints only itself; content is a sibling above it.

## Related

- `registration-frame` — the ruled box a network band usually sits in; it supplies the positioned, clipping ancestor.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `region` | `'world' \| 'atlantic' \| 'americas' \| 'north-america' \| 'south-america' \| 'europe' \| 'africa' \| 'asia' \| 'oceania'` | `'world'` | false | Which part of the world has its PoPs lit; the map always frames the whole world. |
| `density` | `'none' \| 'low' \| 'medium' \| 'high'` | `'medium'` | false | How many PoPs are lit, from `none` to `high`. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Pulses the PoPs in three staggered waves; static when false. |
| `opacity` | `number` | `0.4` | false | Opacity of the landmass dots, from 0 to 1; the PoPs stay at full strength. |
| `position` | `'center' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'top-left' \| 'top-right' \| 'bottom-left' \| 'bottom-right'` | `'center'` | false | Where the map parks in the space the box leaves over. |
| `scale` | `number` | `0.85` | false | Size of the map relative to the box; 1 fits it, below 1 shrinks it toward its position, above 1 enlarges it. |
| `offsetX` | `number` | `0` | false | Horizontal shift as a fraction of the map width; negative moves it left, positive right, past the box edge if large enough. |
| `offsetY` | `number` | `0` | false | Vertical shift as a fraction of the map height; negative moves it up, positive down, past the box edge if large enough. |
| `fade` | `'none' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'edges' \| 'vignette'` | `'none'` | false | Fades the map out along an axis so it meets content without a hard edge. |
| `traffic` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Draws traffic between lit PoPs: faint links and, while `animated`, packets that cross them; the links alone under reduced motion. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-region`, `data-density` and `data-fade` on the root mirror their props; `data-fade` drives the mask that fades the layer out
- `density="none"` draws the landmass alone, with no hole where a PoP would be — every PoP cell is also a landmass cell
- `density` levels are cumulative: `low` (65 PoPs) ⊂ `medium` (186) ⊂ `high` (275); `core` carries a PoP on every main Brazilian capital, so they light at every density
- Each PoP path carries `data-animated` (present only when `animated` is set) and `data-phase` (`0` / `1` / `2`), which select the pulse and its wave delay
- The map always frames the whole world; `region` only chooses which PoPs light — a PoP renders when its cell falls inside the region's bounds, and a phase with no PoP left renders no path
- `scale` sizes the map around the `position` anchor, so it renders at that fraction of its fitted size while the anchored edge stays put; a value of 0 or below falls back to `1`
- `offsetX` / `offsetY` translate the map after `position` and `scale` place it, by that fraction of the map's own width / height; the sign is the direction (negative left / up, positive right / down), so each axis moves independently of the anchor
- The default `scale` of `0.85` leaves room on both axes, so every `position` moves the map in any box shape. At `1` the fitted map fills one axis edge to edge, so `position` acts only on the other axis: `top` / `center` / `bottom` render alike in a wide box, and `left` / `center` / `right` in a tall one
- `top` / `bottom` / `left` / `right` fade the map out toward that edge: full ink from the opposite edge up to `--network-map-fade-start`, zero at `--network-map-fade-end`, both measured from the opposite edge. `top` / `bottom` default to 16% / 55%; `left` / `right` default to 50% / 80%, which clears a copy column on that side of a band
- Custom properties tune the fade in place, set from the consumer's class: `--network-map-fade-start` / `--network-map-fade-end` (where the fade holds full ink and where it reaches zero)

## Accessibility

- Decorative: the root is `aria-hidden="true"` and `pointer-events-none`; the network's claims are carried by the band's copy, never by the artwork
- Keyboard map: none — the layer is not focusable and has no interactive parts
- Visible focus: not applicable (nothing receives focus)
- Contrast: not applicable to the artwork (decorative); the copy above it keeps its own ≥4.5:1 against the band, which the low default `opacity` protects
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` stops the pulse under reduced motion
- Touch target: not applicable (no interactive parts)

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import NetworkMap from '@aziontech/webkit/network-map'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="relative h-80 w-full overflow-hidden bg-(--bg-canvas)">
    <NetworkMap
      region="world"
      density="medium"
      :opacity="0.4"
      position="center"
      :scale="0.85"
      fade="none"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/overflow-count.md -->

# Overflow Count

> Use OverflowCount for the '+N' that opens the hidden items of a truncated list; a plain number attached to something else is a Badge. A small `+N` chip that stands for the items a slot cannot show, and opens a popover with the whole list. It replaces the design sample's `DomainOverflowPopover`, the overflow badge of `TagListCell` and `WorkloadCell`, and the Console Kit's `OverflowCountButton`. The popover follows the overflow rule of `webkit-ux-heuristics`: a summary line (`12 domains`, `10 of 34 domains` while paged), a search box once the list holds more than 7 items, a scrolling list, a **Load N more** footer while items remain, a no-match line quoting the query, and a polite status region that announces the summary. Closing it clears the query and the paging.

- Import: `import OverflowCount from '@aziontech/webkit/overflow-count'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A table cell or a detail row shows the first value of a list and the rest hide behind a count: the domains of a workload, the tags of a row, the workloads a rule applies to.
- A card or a header names one item of many and the reader may want the full list without leaving the screen.

## Do

- Show the first item (or as many as fit) beside the chip; the chip counts only the hidden ones, and `items` passes only those.
- Name the items with `noun` (`{ one: 'domain', other: 'domains' }`) so the summary reads `12 domains`, not `12 items`.
- Give an item an `href` only when it opens something; an item without one renders as plain text.
- Use the `item` slot for a router link or a richer entry; keep every entry to one truncating line.

## Don’t

- The list is the content of the page → render it as a `Table` or an `Item` list.
- The reader picks from the list → use `Select`, `Combobox` or `MultiSelect`.
- A single count without a list behind it → use `Badge`.

## Related

- `table` — `TableCellTags` and `TableCellLink` put this chip after the values they fit.
- `tag` — the chip is a small secondary `Tag`.
- `popover` — the list opens in a `Popover`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Array<string \| { label: string; href?: string }>` | `[]` | false | The hidden items. The chip reads a plus sign and the count; an item with `href` opens in a new tab. |
| `noun` | `string \| { one: string; other: string }` | `''` | false | What the items are, for the summary and the trigger's name. Empty uses the catalog (`item` / `items`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` |  | One list entry; replaces the built-in text or link. |

## States

- `data-state` on the trigger: `open` | `closed` (from `Popover`).
- Search shows when `items` holds more than 7 entries; Load more shows while entries beyond the loaded batches (10 per batch) match.
- Empty `items` renders nothing.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a button named `Show all <count> <noun>` (the visible `+N` alone does not say what it counts); `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` come from `Popover`.
- Keyboard: `Enter`/`Space` opens, `Esc` closes and returns focus to the chip, `Tab` moves through the search box, the links and Load more.
- A polite `role="status"` region announces the summary after a search or Load more.
- A link that opens a new tab carries a visually hidden `(opens in a new tab)`.
- The trigger stops its click from bubbling, so opening the list inside a clickable table row does not fire the row's `row-click`; the wrapper itself is not interactive and lets other clicks through.
- Contrast: the secondary `Tag` and the muted summary meet 4.5:1 in both themes.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import OverflowCount from '@aziontech/webkit/overflow-count'

  const domains = ['shop.example.com', 'api.example.com', 'img.example.com', 'docs.example.com']
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-xs) min-w-0 items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
    <a
      :href="`https://${domains[0]}`"
      target="_blank"
      rel="noopener noreferrer"
      class="min-w-0 truncate text-body-sm text-(--text-default) underline-offset-2 hover:underline"
      >{{ domains[0] }}</a
    >
    <OverflowCount
      :items="domains.slice(1).map((label) => ({ label, href: `https://${label}` }))"
      :noun="{ one: 'domain', other: 'domains' }"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

# Payment Brand

> The card-brand plate shown beside a payment card: a small bordered plate with the network's mark (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Diners Club, JCB, Discover, Elo, Hipercard, UnionPay) drawn in one colour in theme tokens, so it reads in light, dark and forced colors without a raster image or a brand hex. It replaces the design sample's `CardBrandMark` (a Visa plate on a hard-coded blue fill), the Console Kit's card flag block (six colored SVG logos) and the inline Visa SVG the account blocks repeated. A brand it does not draw (Maestro, Hiper, or any unknown value) shows a generic card glyph and keeps the brand's name for assistive technology.

- Import: `import PaymentBrand from '@aziontech/webkit/payment-brand'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use PaymentBrand for the card network plate next to a payment card.
- A payment method row, a checkout summary or a billing table names the card on file: the plate sits before `Ending in 4242` or `Visa •••• 4242`.
- A list of saved cards where the brand helps the reader tell them apart.

## Do

- Pass the brand as the payment API returns it; the plate normalizes `American Express`, `american_express`, `Diners Club` and casing.
- When the row text already says the brand (`Visa •••• 4242`), set `decorative` so the name is not read twice; when the text says only `Ending in 4242`, leave the plate named.
- Keep the plate at `medium` in rows and forms, `small` inside dense tables.

## Don’t

- The Azion logo → use `Brand`.
- A partner or integration logo (Git providers, clouds) → use the product's logo asset or an `Avatar`.
- A status or category of the card (expired, default) → use `Tag` beside the plate.

## Related

- `brand` — the same idea for the Azion lockup: an inline mark, sized by token.
- `tag` — put `Default` or `Expired` next to the plate, not inside it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brand` | `string` | `''` | false | The card network as the payment API names it (`visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`, `American Express`, `diners`, `jcb`, `discover`, `elo`, `hipercard`, `unionpay`…). Unknown values draw the generic card glyph. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Plate size: `small` 20 × 32 px for dense tables, `medium` 28 × 40 px for rows and forms. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name. Empty uses the brand's name (`Visa`), or the catalog's `Card` for an unknown brand. |
| `decorative` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Hide the plate from assistive technology when the text next to it already names the brand. |

## States

- `data-brand` on the root: `visa` | `mastercard` | `amex` | `diners` | `jcb` | `discover` | `elo` | `hipercard` | `unionpay` | `unknown`.
- `data-size`: `small` | `medium`.
- `data-glyph`: `mark` when the brand has a drawn mark, `generic` otherwise.

## Accessibility

- The root is `role="img"` named by `ariaLabel` (the consumer writes `aria-label`) or the brand's name; with `decorative` it is `aria-hidden="true"` and has no role.
- The SVG inside is `aria-hidden` and not focusable; the plate takes no focus.
- Contrast: the mark is `--text-default` on `--bg-surface` (above 4.5:1 in both themes); forced colors draw it in `CanvasText` because it uses `currentColor`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PaymentBrand from '@aziontech/webkit/payment-brand'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <PaymentBrand brand="visa" />
    <span class="text-label-md text-(--text-default)">Ending in 4242</span>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Plan Feature List

> Use PlanFeatureList only for what a plan includes; any other list of rows is Item rows, and facts about one resource are KeyValueList. The features a plan, product or upgrade includes, each behind a check mark, in one or two columns. It is the "what you get" list of a plan card, an upgrade card or a change-plan drawer: short labels, an optional one-line description under each, and a check that says "included", never "done". It replaces the hand-written `ul` with a `az az-check` per row that the billing pages and the change-plan drawer drew with different icon colours.

- Import: `import PlanFeatureList from '@aziontech/webkit/plan-feature-list'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The perks of an upgrade card (Upgrade to Pro: Unlimited Applications, Unlimited Workloads, Custom Domains).
- The features a plan includes in a change-plan or upgrade drawer, each with a short description.
- Any short list of included capabilities where the check is the only marker.

## Do

- Keep each label to a few words in title case or sentence case, one capability per row; put the detail in `description`, not in the label.
- Use `columns: 2` for six or more short labels in a wide card; it falls back to one column in a narrow box on its own.
- Name the list with `ariaLabel` (for example "Pro plan features") when no visible heading right above it says what the features belong to.
- Do not hand-write the list with your own check icons: the check colour and spacing are part of the component.

## Don’t

- Steps or tasks with a done/not-done state (a production checklist, a setup guide) → use `outcome-icon` per row, or the `stepper`.
- A comparison of features across plans → use `plan-comparison-section` or `table`.
- Label and value facts → use `key-value-list`.
- Rows that navigate or carry actions → use `item`.
- Marketing pricing cards on the site → use `pricing-card` / `pricing-plans-section`, which carry their own feature lists.

## Related

- `key-value-list` — the plan facts that sit next to the feature list in a billing card.
- `card` — the surface the list sits in; PlanFeatureList brings no surface of its own.
- `outcome-icon` — the mark for a step that finished, which this check is not.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `PlanFeatureListItem[]` | `[]` | false | The features, in order; each item is `{ label: string; description?: string }`. |
| `columns` | `1 \| 2` | `1` | false | Columns when the list's own box is at least the md container; a narrower box always shows one column. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list when no visible heading names it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-columns` on the list mirrors `columns`
- Empty: with no `items` the component renders nothing (no empty list, no placeholder); the card around it decides what to say
- No `loading`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `readonly`, `error` or `open` states: the list is static, read-only text

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none; the list has no interactive part.
- Keyboard map: no tab stop.
- ARIA: a native `ul` with `role="list"` (so the list semantics survive `list-style: none` in Safari); each feature is an `li`; the check glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`; `ariaLabel` is set as `aria-label` on the `ul` only when non-empty.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the label and the muted description, ≥3:1 for the check glyph, on `var(--bg-surface)` in both themes.
- No motion.
- No touch target: nothing is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PlanFeatureList from '@aziontech/webkit/plan-feature-list'

  const features = [
    { label: 'Unlimited Applications' },
    { label: 'Unlimited Workloads' },
    { label: 'Custom Domains' },
    { label: 'Priority Support' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <PlanFeatureList
    :items="features"
    aria-label="Pro plan features"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/pricing-card.md -->

# Pricing Card

> One tier of a pricing table: what it is called, what it costs, what that price includes, and the one action that moves the account onto it. The card owns the typographic hierarchy of a price — an overline plan name, the amount as the headline figure, and the billing caveat under it in muted body copy — so a row of tiers reads as a comparison rather than as three differently-typeset cards. `actionsPosition` is the axis that decides which of the two compositions the card is. **`bottom`** is the compact tier: the name, a `medium` amount and the caveat stack at the top, the action follows, and the slot sits under it — a card sized by its own content, for a row of tiers a reader scans. **`middle`** is the full tier: the amount becomes the `large` headline figure, the caveat moves up to `body-md`, the slot grows to fill the card, and the action is pinned to the bottom edge so a row of `middle` cards has its buttons on one line whatever each tier's feature list holds. `variant` decides only whether the card draws its own surface (`contained`) or sits on the one behind it (`ghost`); it never changes the composition. The name, the amount and the caveat are **one column**, capped at `--container-xs` (348px) rather than at the card's full width: the caveat is a sentence about the price directly above it, so it wraps on the price's measure. The cap shipped as `--container-3xs` (256px) — two rungs down the ladder, and too narrow for the copy it holds. 256px sets `body-md` at roughly 33 characters, under the 45–75 a prose measure wants, and all three billing caveats on the sample pricing page (66, 69 and 84 characters) ran to three lines there. At 348px the measure is ~46 characters and the same three set in two, while the card's own content box at 1440 is 413px — so the caveat is still held to the price's column instead of the card's. The card carries **one** prose region — the pricing caveat, below the amount. It used to carry a second paragraph above the amount as well, and with `equalHeight` reserving a band for each, a row of tiers showed two two-line muted blocks around every price doing the same visual job. The Figma component (`3605:2260`) has a single prose region, `Pricing Details`, positioned below the amount, so that is the one the card keeps; a tier's positioning sentence belongs to whatever the consumer puts in the slot. `equalHeight` makes a ROW of cards read as one comparison. Every region is content-sized by default, which is right for a single card and wrong for three side by side — a tier with a two-line caveat and a tier with none put their feature lists on different lines, and the reader has to re-find the row in every column. It reserves **three** lines for the caveat, in `lh` so the reservation follows the type token rather than a hard-coded height. Three is the design's 64px band expressed in whole lines of the region's own token (`body-md` is a 22px line box, so `3lh` is 66px; `2lh` is 44px and twenty short) — it shipped as `2lh`, and the shortfall stayed invisible until a tier's caveat ran to three lines at the region's then-256px measure, overflowed the band, and pushed that column's feature list 22px below the other two. Opt-in, because reserving empty lines is wrong for a lone card; set it on every card in the row. A caveat past three lines still pushes the row down, like any overflow. The plan title is an **overline** (`.text-overline-md` on an `<h3>`): the token carries the display face, the uppercase transform and the widest tracking step, so the tier reads as a label on the card rather than as a title competing with the price beneath it. It stays an `<h3>` for the document outline — the tier is the section heading — while looking like an overline. There is no built-in plan name: set `title` on every card.

- Import: `import PricingCard from '@aziontech/webkit/pricing-card'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- One tier in a row of plans: plan name, price, billing caveat, one action and the tier's feature list.
- A compact tier sized by its content (`actions-position="bottom"`), or a full tier whose action is pinned to the bottom so a row's buttons line up (`actions-position="middle"`).
- A tier set on the surface behind it (`variant="ghost"`) inside a section that already draws the frame.

## Do

- In a row of tiers, set `equalHeight` on every card so each caveat reserves the same band and the feature lists start on one line.
- Keep `pricing-details` to the billing caveat. A tier's positioning sentence goes in the default slot with the feature list.
- The card emits no events, and the built-in button has no handler. To act on the click, fill the `actions` slot with your own `Button`.
- Hide the symbol or the period with `:show-prefix="false"` / `:show-suffix="false"` (for example on a custom-quote tier) instead of clearing `prefix` / `suffix`.
- Mark at most one card in a row with `show-tag` and `tag-label`.

## Don’t

- You need the whole plans band of a pricing page, with the billing-period toggle and the framed row → use `pricing-plans-section`.
- You need a feature-by-feature comparison across plans → use `plan-comparison-section`.
- You only need to show an amount, in a table cell or a summary → use `currency-amount`.
- The card holds general content rather than a price → use `card`.

## Related

- `currency-amount` — typesets the amount inside the card; use it directly for prices outside a tier card.
- `pricing-plans-section` — the page section that lays out a row of plan cards with the billing toggle.
- `plan-comparison-section` — the matrix that sits under the plan cards.
- `card` — generic bordered card with header, content and footer regions.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Plan name shown as the card heading. |
| `pricingDetails` | `string` | `''` | false | Caveat under the price, such as the billing terms. |
| `showPricingDetails` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the pricing details line. |
| `showTag` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the tag beside the plan name. |
| `tagLabel` | `string` | `'Popular'` | false | Text of the tag beside the plan name. |
| `equalHeight` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Reserves the caveat's band so a row of cards aligns row-for-row. Set it on every card in the row. |
| `actionsPosition` | `'bottom' \| 'middle'` | `'bottom'` | false | Composition of the card: `bottom` stacks the actions under the price, `middle` puts the price and actions between the header and the default slot. |
| `variant` | `'contained' \| 'ghost'` | `'contained'` | false | Whether the card draws its own surface: `contained` has a border and a surface, `ghost` sits on the page. |
| `value` | `string` | `'20'` | false | Price amount, already formatted, without the currency symbol. |
| `prefix` | `string` | `'$'` | false | Text before the amount, usually the currency symbol. |
| `suffix` | `string` | `'/ mon'` | false | Text after the amount, usually the billing period. |
| `showPrefix` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the prefix. |
| `showSuffix` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the suffix. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | `'Label'` | false | Label of the default action button. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Fades the old price out and the new one in when the price changes, such as on a billing-period switch. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | — | Named slot. |
| `default` | — | Main content. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- Animated: with `animated`, a change of `value`, `prefix` or `suffix` fades the old price out and the new one in (`data-animated` on the root); without it the price swaps in place

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states; the `animated` price fade pairs each class with `motion-reduce:animate-none`, so the price swaps in place under reduced motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PricingCard from '@aziontech/webkit/pricing-card'
</script>

<template>
  <PricingCard
    title="Pro"
    pricing-details="Billed annually or $25/mo billed monthly."
    actions-position="bottom"
    variant="contained"
    value="20"
    prefix="$"
    suffix="/ mon"
    action-label="Label"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/qr-code.md -->

# Qr Code

> A QR code drawn as SVG from a string, with no image request and no dependency: WebKit's own encoder (byte mode, UTF-8, versions 1–40, error correction L/M/Q/H) turns the value into modules, and the component draws them as one path. It is for setup flows that hand a URI to a phone, first the `otpauth://` URI of an authenticator app in `auth#MfaSetup`, where it replaces the image the API returned and the framed placeholder of the demo. The code is always dark on a light plate (the plate pins the light theme), because several authenticator scanners do not read an inverted code.

- Import: `import QrCode from '@aziontech/webkit/qr-code'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A phone has to pick up a value the screen shows: an authenticator `otpauth://` URI, a pairing link, a short download URL.
- Next to a typed alternative: the same value (or its secret) as text with a `CopyButton`, for people who cannot scan.

## Do

- Always give the code a typed alternative next to it: the setup key or the link as text.
- Name the code after what it does (`QR code to add jane.doe@example.com to an authenticator app`), not `QR code`.
- Keep the default `M` error correction; raise it only when the code is printed or shown small.

## Don’t

- The value is only for reading or copying on the same device → show it as text with `CopyButton`.
- A brand or partner logo → use `Brand` or the partner's asset.
- A long payload (over a few hundred characters) → link to it; a dense code is hard to scan from a screen.

## Related

- `copy-button` — the typed alternative beside the code.
- `otp-input` — the 6-digit code the app shows after the scan.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `—` | true | The text the code carries (a URI, a key), encoded as UTF-8 bytes. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the image. Empty uses the catalog's `QR code`; name it after what the scan does. |
| `errorCorrection` | `'L' \| 'M' \| 'Q' \| 'H'` | `'M'` | false | Error-correction level: `L` 7 %, `M` 15 %, `Q` 25 %, `H` 30 % of the code can be lost and still read. Higher levels make denser codes. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Rendered width: `small` 128 px, `medium` 160 px, `large` 224 px, quiet zone included. |

## States

- `data-size`: `small` | `medium` | `large`.
- `data-version` on the root: the QR version the encoder picked (1–40); `data-modules`: the module count per side.
- An empty value draws no code: the plate keeps its size and `data-version` is absent. A value too long for version 40 at the chosen level draws no code either and logs one warning.

## Accessibility

- The root is `role="img"` named by `ariaLabel` (the consumer writes `aria-label`; catalog `QR code` when empty); the SVG inside is `aria-hidden` and not focusable; the code takes no focus.
- The code is never the only way: the page puts the value or its secret beside it as text.
- Contrast: dark modules on a light plate in both themes (the plate sets `data-theme="light"`); `forced-color-adjust: none` keeps the code dark on light in forced colors, so a scanner still reads it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'
  import QrCode from '@aziontech/webkit/qr-code'

  const account = 'jane.doe@example.com'
  const secret = 'JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP'
  const uri = `otpauth://totp/Azion:${encodeURIComponent(account)}?secret=${secret}&issuer=Azion`
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-col items-start gap-(--spacing-md)">
    <QrCode
      :value="uri"
      :aria-label="`QR code to add ${account} to an authenticator app`"
    />
    <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-2xs)">
      <p class="text-label-sm text-(--text-default)">Can't scan the code?</p>
      <div class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
        <code
          class="text-label-code text-(--text-default)"
          dir="ltr"
          >{{ secret.match(/.{1,4}/g).join(' ') }}</code
        >
        <CopyButton
          :value="secret"
          aria-label="Copy setup key"
          copied-label="Setup key copied"
          size="small"
        />
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/qr-code.md](components/qr-code.md).

<!-- components/severity-tag.md -->

# Severity Tag

> Use SeverityTag only for a level on the critical → info scale of findings and alerts; the state of a resource is a StatusIndicator, and any other category word is a Tag. SeverityTag labels an item with its place on an ordered severity scale: critical, high, medium, low or info. The level reads from a four-bar glyph, where the filled bars count the level, and from the label, so two levels never depend on colour alone to differ. It differs from `tag`, whose `severity` prop is a colour tone (success, warning, danger) with no order between values.

- Import: `import SeverityTag from '@aziontech/webkit/severity-tag'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Show how severe an alert, finding, detection, incident or vulnerability is, in a table cell, a list row or a detail header.
- Rank items on a fixed five-step scale where critical and high must stay visibly distinct.

## Do

- Keep the default label (the level name from the locale catalog, translated under `WebkitProvider`) so the text always names the level; override `label` only when the product glossary names the level differently.
- Use one SeverityTag per row, in its own column, so the glyphs line up and the scale reads down the column.
- Do not pair the tag with a toned `tag` for the same level; the glyph and the ramp already carry it.

## Don’t

- The value is an outcome or a status with no order (allowed, blocked, healthy) → use `tag`.
- The value is a count or a one-word indicator on an icon or avatar → use `badge`.
- The user can select or remove the value (a severity filter) → use `chip`.

## Related

- `tag` — a toned status or category label; use it for outcomes and states, not for an ordered level.
- `badge` — a dense count or short-label indicator.
- `chip` — an interactive or removable token, for severity filters.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | `'critical' \| 'high' \| 'medium' \| 'low' \| 'info'` | `'info'` | false | Severity level on the findings scale (exported as `SeverityTagSeverity`, distinct from the shared status `Severity`); sets how many glyph bars fill, their colour and the default label. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the tag. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info`). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Replaces the label text. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (static, non-interactive)
- `data-severity` mirrors the `severity` prop: `critical` | `high` | `medium` | `low` | `info`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop: `small` | `medium`
- Filled bars per level: critical 4, high 3, medium 2, low 1, info 0

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not focusable; the tag is static text and takes no `tabindex`.
- Keyboard map: none; the tag has no interaction.
- ARIA: the glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`; the visible text names the level, so the tag needs no `role` or `aria-label`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the label (`var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-canvas)`) and ≥3:1 for every filled bar on `var(--bg-canvas)` in both themes.
- No motion, so no `motion-reduce:*` fallback is needed.
- Touch target: not applicable; the tag is not interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SeverityTag from '@aziontech/webkit/severity-tag'
</script>

<template>
  <SeverityTag
    severity="info"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/status-code.md -->

# Status Code

> Use StatusCode only for an HTTP status code or method (200, 404, GET); for resource state use StatusIndicator, and for any other word use Tag. StatusCode shows the HTTP status of a request, optionally preceded by its method, as one compact monospace pill whose colour comes from the status class: informational, success and redirect responses (1xx, 2xx, 3xx) stay neutral, client errors (4xx) take the warning colour and server errors (5xx) the danger colour, so failures stand out in a long request log without every successful row competing for attention. Anything that is not a status from 100 to 599 renders muted, as written. It composes `Tag` for the surface, so its sizes, shape and colours are the tag's; the component owns only the mapping from status to colour and the method plus code layout that every logs table would otherwise repeat.

- Import: `import StatusCode from '@aziontech/webkit/status-code'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A request log, an invocation list or a trace detail shows the HTTP status of each request (`GET 200`, `POST 503`).
- A detail panel summarizes the response of one request next to its timing and size.

## Do

- Pass the status as it comes from the log (`404` or `'404'`); the component derives the colour, so do not pick a colour per row.
- Pass `method` only when the list mixes methods; a list of `GET` requests reads better with the code alone.
- Keep the column narrow: the pill never wraps and is at most `GET` plus three digits wide for real traffic.

## Don’t

- The status is a resource lifecycle (`Active`, `Pending`, `Failed`) → use `tag` or `TableCellStatus`.
- The value is a security or incident level → use `severity-tag`.
- A dot that says whether a service is up → use `status-indicator`.

## Related

- `tag` — the surface StatusCode composes; use it directly for statuses that are not HTTP codes.
- `table` — place StatusCode inside a `#cell-<id>` slot of a request log.
- `severity-tag` — ordered severity levels with a bar glyph.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `number \| string` | `''` | false | HTTP status, as a number or a string (`404`, `'404'`). 1xx to 3xx render neutral, 4xx warning, 5xx danger; anything else renders muted as written, empty a dash. |
| `method` | `string` | `''` | false | Request method shown before the code (`GET`, `POST`), upper-cased. Empty shows the code alone. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token forwarded to `Tag`; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px. |

## States

- `data-status-class` on the root: `informational` (1xx), `success` (2xx), `redirect` (3xx), `client-error` (4xx), `server-error` (5xx) or `invalid` (anything else, including empty).
- `data-size` mirrors `size` (set by `Tag`).
- The `Tag` severity follows the class: `neutral` for 1xx to 3xx and `invalid`, `warning` for 4xx, `danger` for 5xx.
- `invalid` mutes the text; an empty `code` shows a dash, any other invalid value shows as written.
- Non-interactive: no hover, focus, active or disabled state.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — StatusCode is non-interactive.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: plain text inside a `span`; the status number carries the meaning, so the colour is never the only cue (WCAG 1.4.1). Screen readers read `POST 503`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1: the `Tag` severity pairs (`--warning` / `--warning-foreground`, `--danger` / `--danger-foreground`, `--text-default` on `--bg-canvas`) and `--text-muted` on `--bg-canvas` are theme-guaranteed in light and dark.
- `motion-reduce:*`: not applicable — no motion.
- Touch target: not applicable — non-interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import StatusCode from '@aziontech/webkit/status-code'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <StatusCode
      :code="101"
      method="GET"
    />
    <StatusCode
      :code="200"
      method="GET"
    />
    <StatusCode
      :code="301"
      method="GET"
    />
    <StatusCode
      :code="404"
      method="POST"
    />
    <StatusCode
      :code="503"
      method="PUT"
    />
    <StatusCode :code="201" />
    <StatusCode code="n/a" />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/tag.md -->

# Tag

> Use Tag for a read-only category or outcome word on an item (Production, Beta, Allowed) that is not a lifecycle state. The state of a resource is a StatusIndicator, a number is a Badge, a removable or selectable token is a Chip, and a level on the critical → info scale is a SeverityTag. A compact, read-only word on an item, colored by its brand look `variant` or its status colour `severity` so the category or outcome reads at a glance (Production in `variant="primary"`, Blocked in `severity="danger"`). It takes an optional leading icon, a pill shape with `rounded`, and two sizes; it is never interactive and never counts.

- Import: `import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'`
- Category: content · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Label or categorize an item with a short descriptive text, optionally with a leading icon or pill shape.
- Show a status with its colour via `severity` (`neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`), or a category with a brand look via `variant` (`primary`, `accent`, `contrast`, `highlight`); `severity` wins when both are set.
- Mark the one value a list highlights (the Owner role in a users table) with `variant="highlight"`: the brand orange as a tint, orange text on `--primary-mask`, like the success, info and warning tints.

## Do

- Colour comes from `variant` or `severity`; the optional icon is decorative — keep it `aria-hidden`.
- Pick the severity by meaning: `success` Active, `warning` Pending, `neutral` Inactive or a neutral category (Developer, Viewer), `info` a second role (Admin), `variant="highlight"` the one value to single out (Owner), `primary` a solid brand label. Do not use `danger` for a state that is only off (Inactive): it reads as an error.
- Do not restyle a Tag with colour classes to get a tint; every tint is a `variant` or a `severity`.
- Use `rounded` for the pill shape rather than a custom radius.

## Don’t

- It is purely a count or one-glance status label → use `badge`.
- The user can select or remove it (filters, multi-select values) → use `chip`.

## Related

- `badge` — denser count/short-label indicator with no icon affordance.
- `chip` — interactive/removable token.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback text when the default slot is empty. |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'accent' \| 'contrast' \| 'highlight'` | `'primary'` | false | Brand look of the tag surface and label, used when `severity` is not set: `primary` (solid brand orange), `accent`, `highlight` (the brand orange as a tint) and `contrast` (`var(--bg-contrast)` / `var(--text-contrast)`). |
| `severity` | `'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `—` | false | Status colour of the tag surface and label, the shared `Severity` scale exported from this component; wins over `variant` when set. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px. |
| `rounded` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Pill shape when true. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class for the leading icon. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Main content. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`. A tag is static text: it takes no focus and has no hover or active state.
- `data-severity` mirrors `severity` when it is set; otherwise `data-variant` mirrors `variant`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none; the tag is not focusable. A focusable control that holds a tag draws its own ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'
</script>

<template>
  <Tag
    label="Label"
    variant="primary"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```
