# Date Picker

> DatePicker picks **one date**, optionally with a time, in a form field. A trigger button opens a popover that holds a month grid, a typed date field (and a time field with `showTime`), an optional footer and an Apply action. The selection is staged in a draft inside the popover and committed to `v-model` only on Apply (or immediately when `show-apply` is false). Date math uses the native `Date` API only — no date library; the trigger formats the value with `Intl` in `v-model:time-zone` (the local zone when empty). Before 6.0 this component was `Calendar` and also picked ranges, periods and presets; every range — relative or absolute, with or without times — now belongs to `date-range-picker`, which reuses this component's month grid and fields as internal parts. The name follows Cloudscape DatePicker and the shadcn "Date Picker".

- Import: `import DatePickerRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/date-picker-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import DatePicker from '@aziontech/webkit/date-picker'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use DatePicker to pick one date (optionally with a time) in a form field. For any start–end range use DateRangePicker; to display a moment in time use Timestamp.
- A due date, a start date, an expiry date, a birthday.
- A date and a time of day together (`show-time`): a scheduled maintenance window start, a release time.

## Do

- `modelValue` is committed only on Apply; read the final value from `update:modelValue` or the second argument of `apply`, and set `:show-apply="false"` when every edit should commit at once.
- Bind a `Date` or `null`.
- Bound the selectable days with `min` and `max` instead of validating after commit.
- Send `toISOString()` (or the ISO date `2026-11-15`) to the server, never the printed label.

## Don’t

- A start and an end, whole days or with times, relative or absolute → use `date-range-picker`.
- Displaying a date the person does not edit → use `timestamp`.
- A duration or count (retention days, TTL) rather than a date → use `number-input`.

## Related

- `date-range-picker` — every range: relative windows (`last 15 minutes`) kept relative, absolute ranges down to the minute, and whole days with `:show-time="false"`. It is built on this component's grid, fields and time zone selector.
- `timestamp` — shows a moment in time in the app's time zone.
- `field` — inside a `Field`, the trigger takes the field's label (`for` points at it), description, `invalid` and `disabled`.
- `input` — the trigger and the date field share its heights, hover, and disabled treatment, so they align side by side.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects the trigger, day-cell hit-area, and typography. |
| `min` | `Date \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Earliest selectable date; earlier days render disabled. |
| `max` | `Date \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Latest selectable date; later days render disabled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger, grid, and all controls, applying disabled tokens. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the trigger invalid: sets `aria-invalid` and the danger border. An enclosing `Field`'s `invalid` sets it too. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Trigger text shown when there is no selection. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Select a date`). |
| `showFields` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the date field (and the time field with `showTime`) in the panel. Set false when the grid is the whole interaction and typing a date is not offered. |
| `showTime` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a time field beside the date field, so the value carries a time of day. |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | false | Places the fields and Apply column below the calendar (vertical) or beside it (horizontal). |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the trigger; the current value is appended (`Due date: Nov 15, 2026`). Empty leaves the name to the Field label or the trigger text. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a clear control on the trigger that empties the committed selection. |
| `showApply` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Stages edits in a draft and requires Apply to commit; when false, every edit commits immediately. |
| `split` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the trigger as a split control with a separate chevron affordance. |
| `modelValue` | `DatePickerValue` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |
| `timeZone` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:timeZone`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `month-change` | `DatePickerMonth` | Emitted when the first visible month changes via navigation or keyboard paging. Payload is `{ year, month }` (month is 0-indexed). |
| `apply` | `(event: Event, value: Date \| null)` | Emitted when the draft selection is committed via Apply; `event` is the activating click or key event, `value` the committed date. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | { open, value, displayValue } | Replaces the default trigger button; scope exposes the open state, raw value, and formatted label. |
| `footer` | — | Custom footer/action-bar content (e.g. `<DatePicker.Clear>`) alongside Apply. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/date-picker-clear`

## Sub-components

- `date-picker-clear/date-picker-clear.vue` — context-aware button that clears the draft selection through injected context; disabled when there is no selection.

Internal parts, not exported, shared with `date-range-picker`, in `parts/`: `parts/date-picker-grid.vue` (the month grid), `parts/date-picker-fields.vue` (the date and time fields, a Start/End pair for a range), `parts/date-picker-timezone.vue` (the time zone selector `date-range-picker` shows). A private part lives in `parts/`, so it is not mistaken for a public `date-picker-<part>`.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `Date \| null` | `null` | `update:modelValue` | The committed date via `defineModel`; `null` on clear. Only updated on Apply (or immediately when `showApply` is false). Uncontrolled when unbound. |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state of the popover via `defineModel`. Fires when the popover opens or closes. Unbound, the popover keeps its own state and starts at `defaultOpen`. |
| `v-model:time-zone` | `string` | `''` | `update:timeZone` | IANA time zone the trigger formats the value in, via `defineModel('timeZone')`. Empty resolves to the local zone. Same name as on `date-range-picker`. |

**Booleans that default to true.** `showFields` and `showApply` default to `true`: they switch off parts of the default panel. Inverting them (`hideFields`, `instant`) would break every consumer, so they are recorded here as the exceptions to props.md's default-false rule.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `disabled`, `today`, `outside` (adjacent-month), popover `open` / `closed`
- **Field contract parity.** Every field-shaped surface — the trigger and the date + time fields — follows the shared `inputs` field contract used by `input`, `number-input`, `select-trigger` and `textarea`, so a DatePicker reads identically to a text field placed beside it: heights are `small=28px` / `medium=32px` / `large=40px`, the value renders at `.text-label-sm`, and `disabled` applies `var(--bg-disabled)` + `var(--text-disabled)` + `cursor-not-allowed` rather than an opacity wash.
- **Hover is identical to `input`.** The whole trigger is one field with one border, so hover raises **only** that border to `var(--border-strong)` — no background wash on any segment. It is suppressed while the control is focused and while `disabled`, via the same selector `input` uses: `[&:not(:focus-within):not([data-disabled])]:hover:border-(--border-strong)`. Hovering any segment — the date, clear, or split — raises the single shared border.
- `data-state` on the root and trigger mirrors the popover open state (`open` | `closed`)
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop on the root, trigger, and each day cell (`small` | `medium` | `large`)
- `data-selected` mirrors the selected day cell
- `data-band` on each day cell is `single` on the selected day and `none` elsewhere (the `start` / `middle` / `end` bands are `date-range-picker`'s)
- `data-today` marks the current date, taken from the nearest `WebkitProvider` `now` when set (so a server render and the hydrating client agree), else the current time; the grid also opens on that month when there is no value; `data-outside` marks an adjacent-month day cell
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on the root, unselectable day cells, and the clear control when there is no selection
- `data-invalid` mirrors `invalid` (own prop or the enclosing `Field`'s) on the root and the trigger shell, with `aria-invalid` on the trigger and the danger border
- Reflow: the root is capped at the width of its container (`max-w-full`), so the trigger never overflows a 320 px box.
- `data-side` (`bottom` | `top`) and `data-align` (`start`) on the calendar panel mirror where it landed after flipping; `start` follows the text direction, so under `rtl` the panel lines up with the field's right edge

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the trigger and `focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-surface-raised)` inside the popover. The date and time fields reuse `input`, whose ring offset resolves `var(--input-ring-offset, var(--bg-canvas))`; the fields container declares `--input-ring-offset: var(--bg-surface-raised)` once and it inherits to every field.
- Field labels: the visible Date label is a `<label for>` bound to its date field through `useId()`; the time field beside it carries its own `aria-label` (`Time`), so every field has a programmatic accessible name.
- Keyboard map: the trigger toggles the popover with `Enter`/`Space` and exposes `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`; `Escape` and click-outside close it and return focus to the trigger; focus is trapped in the open popover. In the grid, `Tab` enters at the focused day, `Arrow` keys move focus (paging the visible month when crossing its first/last day), `Enter`/`Space` selects, `Home`/`End` move to the first/last day of the week (the grid starts on Sunday; logical, so the same under `dir="rtl"`), `PageUp`/`PageDown` change month, `Shift+PageUp`/`Shift+PageDown` change year. Tests: `date-picker.test.ts` › Home and End, Shift+PageDown and Shift+PageUp. Apply, Clear and the fields are all reachable by `Tab`.
- ARIA: the month grid uses `role="grid"` with `role="row"` and `role="gridcell"` descendants; the selected cell sets `aria-selected="true"`; the current date sets `aria-current="date"`; navigation buttons carry `aria-label`; the popover is a `dialog` named by the catalog (`Choose date`); decorative icons are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the popover and `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px (or justified deviation): day cells use a 32×32 px (`small`), 36×36 px (`medium`), or 40×40 px (`large`) hit area; `small`/`medium` are a justified deviation for dense month-grid layouts, `large` meets the 40 px target.

```vue
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const date = ref(null)

    aria-label="Start date"
  />
```

# Date Range Picker

> A time range for queries over time: logs, events, traces and metrics. After the Console Kit date-time range (quick ranges, absolute range with times, previous and next) and Cloudscape's date range picker. The value is either **relative** (`{ type: 'relative', amount: 15, unit: 'minute' }`, read as "the last 15 minutes" and re-resolved against the clock on every query, so a live view keeps moving) or **absolute** (`{ type: 'absolute', start, end }`, two ISO 8601 instants). The trigger prints `Last 15 minutes` or the absolute range in the selected time zone with its UTC offset. The panel switches between Relative range (the quick ranges and a custom duration) and Absolute range (the `DatePicker` month grid, start and end date and time fields — the times hidden with `showTime` off — and the time zone selector) and commits only on Apply; Cancel and Escape drop the draft. Absolute boundaries are typed as wall-clock time in the selected zone and stored as instants, so the same value reads correctly in every zone. With `showStep`, Previous and Next move the range by its own length. Date math uses `Intl` and the native `Date` only.

- Import: `import DateRangePicker from '@aziontech/webkit/date-range-picker'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use DateRangePicker for any start–end range: relative ('last 24 hours') or absolute, with or without times; turn times off for whole-day reports and billing periods. For one date use DatePicker; to display a moment in time use Timestamp.
- Filtering events, logs, traces or metrics by time, where "the last N minutes" must stay relative.
- Any range that needs times of day and a time zone, not only dates.
- Investigations that page through time window by window (`show-step`).
- Whole-day ranges for a report or a billing period: `range-selector-mode="absolute-only"` with `:show-time="false"`.

## Do

- Keep relative values relative: resolve them to instants when the query runs (`now - amount × unit` to `now`), never when the user picks them. `useTimeRange(value)` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-time-range` returns `from` and `to` and holds the window until `refresh()`; its `TIME_RANGE_PRESETS` (last hour, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days) go in `relative-options`.
- Fix the reference clock in tests, demos and server-rendered pages so labels and step limits are deterministic: `now` on the app's `WebkitProvider` covers every picker below it; the `now` prop overrides it for one picker.
- Bind `v-model:time-zone` to the user's saved preference, and show times elsewhere on the page in the same zone.
- Set `max` (usually now) and `min` (the retention limit) instead of validating after Apply.
- Name the picker after what it filters (`aria-label="Events time range"`).

## Don’t

- A single date or a date and time → use `date-picker`.
- A fixed list of named intervals and nothing custom → use `select` or `toggle-group`.

## Related

- `date-picker` — the month grid, the date and time fields and the time zone selector come from its internal parts, so both pickers look and behave the same. Split: DatePicker picks one date (optionally with a time); DateRangePicker owns every range and keeps a relative window relative.
- `timestamp` — displays a moment in time; both read the `WebkitProvider` `timeZone`.
- `webkit-provider` — its `timeZone` is the zone the picker formats in while `v-model:time-zone` is unbound.
- `field` — inside a `Field`, the trigger takes the field's label (`for` points at it), description, `invalid` and `disabled`.
- `property-filter` — the query bar it sits next to in an events toolbar.
- `chart` — the histogram whose brush usually writes an absolute range back into this picker.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `relativeOptions` | `RelativeOption[]` | `5m, 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d` | false | Quick ranges listed on the Relative tab. |
| `timeZones` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Zones offered by the selector. Empty falls back to the zones `Intl` supports. |
| `showTimeZone` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the time zone selector in the panel. |
| `showTime` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the start and end time fields of an absolute range. Off, a range covers whole days (a report or billing period). |
| `showStep` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows Previous and Next buttons that move the range back or forward by its own length. |
| `rangeSelectorMode` | `'default' \| 'relative-only' \| 'absolute-only'` | `'default'` | false | Which kinds of range the panel offers. |
| `min` | `Date` | `undefined` | false | Earliest instant an absolute range may start at. |
| `max` | `Date` | `undefined` | false | Latest instant an absolute range may end at. |
| `now` | `Date` | `undefined` | false | Reference clock for relative ranges and stepping. Unset uses the nearest `WebkitProvider`'s `now`, then the real clock. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Trigger text with no range. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the trigger. Empty uses the Field label inside a `Field`, else the locale catalog. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger and the step buttons. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the trigger invalid: sets `aria-invalid` and the danger border. An enclosing `Field`'s `invalid` sets it too. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token of the trigger and the panel controls. |
| `modelValue` | `DateRangeValue \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `timeZone` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:timeZone`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `DateRangeValue \| null` | `null` | `update:modelValue` | The committed range: relative (last N units, re-resolved against now) or absolute (ISO instants). Set on Apply with a valid draft, or by Previous / Next (always an absolute range). |
| `v-model:timeZone` | `string` | `''` | `update:timeZone` | IANA time zone the absolute range is typed and shown in; empty uses the local zone. Set on Apply after the zone changed in the panel. |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state of the panel via `defineModel('open')`: the trigger, Apply, Cancel, `Esc` and an outside click update it. Unbound, the picker keeps it itself and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `open`, `disabled`; the panel shows an inline error after an Apply that the draft cannot satisfy.
- `data-state="open|closed"` on the root and the panel; `data-size`; `data-disabled`; `data-invalid` on the root and the trigger shell (own `invalid` or the enclosing `Field`'s, with `aria-invalid` on the trigger and the danger border); `data-empty` on the trigger with no value; `data-selected` on the chosen quick range.
- The Next button is disabled while the range is relative (it already ends now) or when the step would pass `max` (or now); Previous is disabled when the step would pass `min`.
- `data-side` (`bottom` | `top`) and `data-align` (`start`) on the calendar panel mirror where it landed after flipping; `start` follows the text direction, so under `rtl` the panel lines up with the field's right edge

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: a 2 px `--ring-color` ring inset on each trigger segment; the quick ranges ring their row when the radio inside has focus.
- Keyboard map: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens the panel and the focus trap moves into it; `Tab` cycles inside the panel; the range type is a `ToggleGroup` (arrow keys); the quick ranges are native radios (`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` move and select); the grid keeps the `date-picker` keyboard map; `Escape` closes without committing and returns focus to the trigger.
- ARIA: the trigger has `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and a name that starts with the picker's label and contains the visible range (inside a `Field` with no `ariaLabel`, the Field label names it and the trigger also carries the Field's `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`); the panel is a named `dialog`; the quick ranges are a `fieldset` with a `legend`; the custom duration and unit have visible labels; the error is `role="alert"` and described from the duration field; Previous and Next are named buttons.
- Targets: options are 32 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

```vue
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const range = ref({ type: 'relative', amount: 15, unit: 'minute', key: 'last-15-minutes' })
</script>

<template>
  <DateRangePicker
    v-model="range"
    aria-label="Events time range"
  />
</template>
```

# Field

> One composable form field that wraps **any** control — `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `NumberInput`, `PasswordInput`, `PhoneInput`, `InputGroup`, `Combobox`, `DatePicker`, `DateRangePicker`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `Slider` — with its label, description and error. The root `Field` owns the field state (`invalid`, `disabled`, `required`) and the ids, and shares them through `provide`/`inject`: the control picks up its `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `disabled` and `required` from the Field, `Field.Label` points its `for` at the control and shows the Required marker, and `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` register themselves so the control is described by them. Grouping parts (`Field.Set`, `Field.Legend`, `Field.Group`, `Field.Content`, `Field.Title`, `Field.Separator`) build fieldsets, choice cards and settings rows. One anatomy serves every control, so there is no per-control field wrapper.

- Import: `import FieldRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/field-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Field (Field.Label, Field.Description, Field.Error) around every form control; it wires the id, the required marker and the error for you. Field.Description and Field.Error also work alone, under a control that is not inside a Field; for a one-sentence explanation beside a label use Hint.
- Any labelled form control: a text input, a select, a textarea, a password, a phone number, a slider.
- A checkbox, radio or switch with its label beside it (`orientation="horizontal"`).
- A selectable checkbox or switch card: `Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field` (replaces the v5 `*-block` variants). For one choice among cards use `RadioGroup variant="card"`, never a radio inside a `Field.Label`.
- A group of related controls under one caption (`Field.Set` + `Field.Legend`), or a form section (`Field.Group`).

## Do

- Put the state on the `Field`, not on the control: `<Field invalid>` sets `aria-invalid` on the control and the invalid tone on `Field.Description`.
- Let the Field own the ids. Pass an explicit `id` on the control and `for` on `Field.Label` only when another part of the page needs the id (focusing the first invalid field, an error summary link).
- Render `Field.Description` for guidance and `Field.Error` for a validation message; both are announced through `aria-describedby`. `Field.Error` has `role="alert"`, so render it only when there is an error.
- Choice cards: `<Field.Label><Field orientation="horizontal">control + Field.Content</Field></Field.Label>`. Never nest a choice card inside another `Field`; group cards with `Field.Set`.
- Use `orientation="responsive"` for settings rows that stack in a narrow container and sit side by side in a wide one; it follows the nearest container (a `Field.Group`, a Card, a dialog or drawer body).

## Don’t

- A control with no visible label inside a toolbar or a table cell → render the control alone with an `aria-label`.
- A group of mutually exclusive cards with icons → use `radio-group` with `type="card"`.
- A static key/value read-out → use `key-value-list`.

## Related

- `input-group` — wraps an input with addons; put it inside a `Field` and use `InputGroup.Input` as the control.
- `phone-input`, `password-requirements` — a phone number control and the live password rules row, each placed inside a `Field`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'responsive'` | `'vertical'` | false | Layout axis: label above the control, beside it, or beside it once the enclosing container (a FieldGroup, Card, drawer or dialog body) is wide enough. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field invalid: the control sets aria-invalid and FieldDescription switches to the invalid tone. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the wrapped control and dims the field. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the Required marker on FieldLabel and sets required on the wrapped control. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | `Field.Label`, the control, `Field.Description`, `Field.Error` (or `Field.Content` beside the control in a horizontal field). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/field-label`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-error`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-set`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-legend`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-separator`

## Sub-components

The root `Field` provides `FieldInjectionKey` (`injection-key.ts`): a generated `controlId`, the reactive `invalid` / `disabled` / `required` flags, `describedBy` (the ids of the mounted `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` parts), `labelledBy` (the ids of the mounted `Field.Title` parts) and `register`. Controls read it through the shared `useFieldControl` composable (`src/composables/use-field-control`); an explicit prop or attribute on the control always wins over the Field, except `aria-describedby`: the control's own ids are joined with the Field's description and error ids (deduplicated), so a consumer description never hides the Field's error. Composite controls (`Select`, `MultiSelect`, `PhoneInput`) consume the context on their root and provide `null` below it, so their inner search inputs never take the field id. Every part works outside a `Field` too (it then reads no state). Member names mirror the anatomy; there is no `Trigger`/`Content` pair because the field has no open/closed state.

- `field-label/field-label.vue` — `<label>` whose `for` defaults to the Field's `controlId`; appends the Required marker (`*` + "(Required)") when the Field is `required` or its own `required` prop is set (for a label s…
  - Props: `hint` (`string`, default `''`) — short explanation revealed by a `Hint` glyph.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — label text, or a horizontal `Field` for a choice card.
- `field-description/field-description.vue` — guidance line in the label-sm text style; registers its id with the Field.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-error/field-error.vue` — validation message in the danger tone with `role="alert"`; registers its id with the Field, and while it is mounted the Field counts as invalid (the control gets `aria-invalid`) even wh…
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-group/field-group.vue` — vertical stack of fields; it is a `@container/field-group`, one of the containers `orientation="responsive"` can follow.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-set/field-set.vue` — native `<fieldset>` without browser chrome, for a group of related fields or choices.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-legend/field-legend.vue` — native `<legend>` captioning a `Field.Set`.
  - Props: `type` (`'legend' \| 'label'`, default `'legend'`) — `legend` titles a section, `label` matches a `Field.Label` for a group of choices.
  - Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-content/field-content.vue` — column that holds the label/title and descriptions beside a control in a horizontal Field.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.

- `field-separator/field-separator.vue` — horizontal rule between fields, with optional centred text.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `required`
- `data-orientation`: `vertical` | `horizontal` | `responsive`
- `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-required` mirror the props on the root; `data-invalid` is also set while a `Field.Error` is mounted
- `data-slot` identifies every part (`field`, `field-label`, `field-description`, `field-error`, `field-group`, `field-set`, `field-legend`, `field-content`, `field-title`, `field-separator`)
- Responsive: `orientation="responsive"` queries the nearest container (`@md:`), not only `Field.Group`: inside a Card, a drawer or dialog body (`@container/panel`), a settings section or a `Field.Group` it stacks the label above the control in a narrow box and puts them side by side from `@md`. With no container ancestor it stays vertical.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the control keeps its own ring; a choice card shows `has-[:focus-visible]:ring-2 ring-(--ring-color) ring-offset-1 ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` around the whole card.
- Keyboard map: the Field adds no keys; `Tab` reaches the control, and clicking `Field.Label` focuses or toggles it.
- ARIA: root `role="group"`; `Field.Label` `for` → control `id`; control `aria-describedby` → every mounted `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` id; control `aria-invalid` when the Field is `invalid` or a `Field.Error` is mounted; `required` / `aria-required` when it is `required`; `Field.Error` `role="alert"`; `Field.Set` is a native `fieldset` named by its `legend`; the Required marker's `*` is `aria-hidden` and the word "(Required)" is read.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for label, description and error text in every tone, including disabled.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the choice card transition.
- Touch target: the whole choice card is the target; a horizontal Field's label extends the control's target.

# File Dropzone

> A FileDropzone is the target a user drags files from the operating system onto. It owns the drag lifecycle (only drags carrying `Files` count), the `accept` / `multiple` filtering, and the idle/active look, and it hands the result back as two activation events: `drop` with the accepted files, `reject` with the files it filtered out. It holds no value and renders no file list. The list, upload progress and validation messages belong to the consumer (typically a `Field` around this component, whose `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` carry the messages). `variant` covers the two places a drop target lives: - **`inline`**: a dashed region that is always visible (icon, title, description, plus a default slot for the "Browse files" action the consumer composes). It switches to the active look while files are dragged over it. This is the Cloudscape FileDropzone / Cloudflare Pages "Upload assets" shape. - **`overlay`**: invisible at rest. When files are dragged into the window it fades in over its nearest positioned ancestor (`absolute inset-0`), and it fades out on window drag-leave, drop or `Escape`. This is the Vercel "drag and drop a folder to deploy" shape, and it replaces the sample app's page-level `ProjectDropZone` and the drop target in the project intake block (`Blocks/State/ProjectIntake`). The drop target itself is pointer-only. It is never a keyboard control. The keyboard (and screen-reader) path to the same outcome is a real button the consumer puts in the default slot (`inline`), or elsewhere on the page (`overlay`).

- Import: `import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A form or settings surface accepts one or more files and should also accept them by drag (`variant="inline"` with a Browse button in the slot).
- A whole page or card should accept a project, folder contents or assets dropped anywhere on it, with no permanent drop region taking up space (`variant="overlay"` inside a `relative` container).
- The consumer needs the accepted and rejected files separated by an `accept` filter before it uploads anything.

## Do

- Always give the user a non-drag path. In `inline`, put a `Button` in the default slot that opens a native `<input type="file">`. In `overlay`, keep an upload button somewhere on the page. The drop target is pointer-only by design.
- Pass the same `accept` string to the dropzone and to the native input behind your Browse button, so both paths filter the same way.
- Handle `reject`. Tell the user which files were skipped and why (e.g. a `toast` naming the files and the accepted types). A silent rejection reads as a broken drop.
- Announce the outcome of a drop yourself (a toast, or a live region on your file list). The dropzone does not announce drag states (see Accessibility).
- Render one `overlay` dropzone per positioned container, and make the container `relative`. Without a positioned ancestor the overlay covers the nearest positioned element up the tree, which may be the whole page.
- Place the `overlay` dropzone as the last child of its container, so it paints above the container's other positioned content (see Theme gaps).
- When the consumer's own flow is busy (an upload in progress), set `disabled` and disable the Browse button too.
- Put the accepted types and limits in `description` ("PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB"). The title is the instruction, the description is the constraint.

## Don’t

- Picking files by keyboard or click only, with no drag affordance → a `button` that opens a native file input is enough.
- Showing the chosen files, their progress or their errors → render them yourself with `progress`, `message` or `field-error`. The dropzone renders none of these.
- Dragging items inside the page (reordering rows, moving cards) → this component only reacts to OS drags that carry `Files`. In-page drag and drop is out of scope.
- A static "nothing here yet" panel with no drop behavior → use `empty-state`.

## Related

- `button`: the "Browse files" action composed into the default slot. It is the keyboard path to the same outcome as a drop.
- `empty-state`: a no-data panel. Compose a FileDropzone inside or beside it when the empty state's call to action is "upload".
- `progress`: the consumer renders per-file progress after `drop`. The dropzone does not track uploads.
- `toast`: confirms the result of a drop or reports rejected files to everyone, including users who never see the drag.
- `card`: a positioned container (`class="relative"`) that hosts an `overlay` dropzone.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'inline' \| 'overlay'` | `'inline'` | false | Placement. Inline is an always-visible dashed region; overlay stays hidden until files are dragged over the window, then covers its nearest positioned ancestor. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Instruction shown under the icon. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Drop files to upload`). |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Secondary line under the title, typically the accepted types and limits. Not rendered when empty. |
| `accept` | `string` | `''` | false | Comma-separated file filter using the native input accept syntax (extensions, MIME types, type wildcards). Files that do not match are rejected. Empty accepts every file. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When false, only the first accepted file of a drop is accepted and the rest are rejected. `true` by default (recorded exception to the default-false rule; inverting it would break consumers). |
| `directories` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Accepts dropped folders: walks every dropped folder and emits the files inside, each with its `webkitRelativePath` (`assets/img/logo.svg`). The events fire after the walk. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Ignores drags and drops: no active state, no events. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Paints the inline region with the danger border so a wrapping field can show a validation error. Drops still work. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Azion icon class for the glyph above the title. Empty draws the cloud-upload glyph (`az az-cloud-upload`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `drop` | `(event: DragEvent, files: File[])` | Activation event. Fires when files are dropped on the target (the inline root, or the visible overlay) and at least one passes `accept` / `multiple`. `files` holds only the accepted files, in `dataTransfer.files` order, and is never empty. Not emitted when `disabled`. Declaring `drop` means a consumer `@drop` listener binds to this event, never to the native DOM `drop` on the root. |
| `reject` | `(event: DragEvent, files: File[])` | Activation event. Fires on the same drop when one or more files were filtered out, because they do not match `accept` or exceed `multiple="false"`. `files` holds only the rejected files and is never empty. When a drop has both variants of file, `drop` fires first, then `reject`, with the same `event`. Not emitted when `disabled`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Actions or extra content under the description, typically a "Browse files" `Button`. Rendered only in `variant="inline"`. The overlay is `aria-hidden` decoration, so interactive content there would be unreachable and is not rendered. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `idle`, `active` (files dragged over the target), `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `idle` | `active`
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop (`inline` | `overlay`)
- `data-disabled` is present when the `disabled` prop is true. A disabled dropzone is always `data-state="idle"`.
- `data-invalid` is present when the `invalid` prop is true.
- **Inline / invalid**: the dashed border turns `--danger-border` while idle; the active state still wins while files are dragged over it. Overlay ignores `invalid`.
- **Inline / idle**: dashed `--border-strong` border on a `--bg-surface` fill. Icon, title, description and slot are centered.
- **Inline / active**: the border turns `--border-selected` and the fill `--bg-selected`. Layout does not move (same border width in both states).
- **Inline / disabled**: `--border-default` dashed border, `--bg-disabled` fill, icon, title and description in `--text-disabled`, `cursor-not-allowed`. The slot still renders, and the consumer disables its own Browse button.
- **Overlay / idle**: not displayed (`v-show`). The root stays in the DOM so `data-testid` and `$attrs` are always present.
- **Overlay / active**: `absolute inset-0` over the nearest positioned ancestor. 2px dashed `--border-selected` border on a `--bg-canvas` fill, `--shape-card` radius. The content column sits in a `sticky top-0` wrapper capped at the viewport height (`h-dvh max-h-full`), so the prompt stays centered in the viewport even when the ancestor is taller than the screen (the page-level case). It receives pointer events while active so the drop lands on it, and `data-[state=idle]:pointer-events-none` keeps the fade-out from swallowing clicks.
- No `loading`, `empty` or `error` state: the dropzone does not upload, validate or list anything. `invalid` only paints the border; the message and the file list belong to the consumer (compose it inside a `Field`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the dropzone root is **not focusable** and has no focus ring. Focus belongs to the controls in the default slot, which carry their own `focus-visible` ring (e.g. `Button`).
- Keyboard map: none on the dropzone. Drag and drop from the OS is a pointer gesture with no keyboard equivalent on the target. The keyboard path is the consumer's Browse button, which opens a native file input and reaches the same outcome. `Escape` during a drag hides the overlay (window `keydown` fallback; browsers also cancel the drag natively).
- No `@click` on the root: clicking the region does nothing, so there is no click-without-key handler. The Browse button is the click target.
- ARIA, inline: the root is a `<div role="group">` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title and `aria-describedby` pointing at the description (only when `description` is non-empty), both ids from `useId()`. A screen reader therefore reads the slotted Browse button in context ("Drop files to upload, group, PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB each, Browse files, button"). The title is a `<p>`, not a heading: the page owns its heading outline. When `disabled`, the group carries `aria-disabled="true"`, so the dimmed title and description are announced as part of a disabled control and fall under the WCAG 1.4.3 exemption for inactive components.
- Inside a `Field` (inline): the group reads the field through `useFieldControl` — it takes the field's `id`, prepends `Field.Title` to `aria-labelledby`, appends `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` to `aria-describedby`, sets `aria-invalid` from the field's (or its own) `invalid`, and the field's `disabled` disables it (`aria-disabled`, drops ignored).
- ARIA, overlay: the root is `aria-hidden="true"`. It is a pointer-only duplicate of an affordance that must exist elsewhere on the page, and it renders no interactive content.
- No `aria-live` in the component. Announcing every drag that crosses the window is noise, and the outcome that matters (files accepted or skipped) is the consumer's to announce from `drop` / `reject` (a `toast`, or a live region on its file list). `aria-dropeffect` / `aria-grabbed` are deprecated in WAI-ARIA 1.1 and are not used.
- The icon is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`.
- `data-disabled` has no ARIA mirror because the root is not a control. The slotted button carries its own `disabled` / `aria-disabled`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title and description in both themes, including `--text-muted` on `--bg-selected` (inline active) and on `--bg-canvas` (overlay). The `webkit-ui-verifier` must confirm the active state in both themes, since the unit suite has no CSS. The dashed border (`--border-strong` idle, `--border-selected` active) must meet 3:1 non-text contrast against the surrounding surface.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on both overlay fades, `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the inline colour transition.
- Touch target: not applicable. The region is not a control (touch devices cannot drag OS files into a page), and the slotted Button carries its own ≥40×40 px target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const inputEl = ref(null)
  const browse = () => inputEl.value?.click()
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <FileDropzone description="Or browse for files on your computer.">
      <Button
        label="Browse files"
        variant="secondary"
        size="medium"
        @click="browse"
      />
    </FileDropzone>
    <input
      ref="inputEl"
      type="file"
      multiple
      class="hidden"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

# File Token Group

> Use FileTokenGroup for the files picked in a form field, before and during upload; a transfer that runs in the background while the person keeps working is an UploadProgress. The files a person picked for upload, shown as removable tokens before or while they upload: each token names the file with a glyph for its type, its size and, when asked, its last-modified date, carries a progress bar while it uploads and its own error or warning line when it cannot be sent. It pairs with `file-dropzone` (which receives the files) and with a Browse files button: the product keeps the list, the group renders it and reports which token was removed. Taken from Cloudscape's file token group; the Console Kit and the design sample list files by hand.

- Import: `import FileTokenGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/file-token-group'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Under a `FileDropzone` or a Browse files button in a form, to show what will be uploaded and let the person drop a file before submitting.
- In an upload dialog, to show each file's progress and the files that were refused (too large, wrong type) with the reason.
- Read-only, in a review step, to list the attachments that will be sent.

## Do

- Keep the refused files in the list with their error, so the person sees why and can remove them; do not drop them silently.
- Write each error as the reason and the limit (`Larger than 300 MB`), not as a code.
- Use `limit` when more than five files are common, so the form below stays in view.
- Remove the file from your list on `remove`; the group moves focus to the next token for you.

## Don’t

- A running transfer that should follow the person around the console → use `upload-progress`.
- Files already stored in a bucket or a repository → use `table` (the file browser block).
- Free-text tags or labels → use `tag-editor` or `chip`.

## Related

- `file-dropzone` — receives dropped files; the group lists them.
- `upload-progress` — the floating card for transfers that keep running after the dialog closes. Split: FileTokenGroup lists the files picked in a form, before and while they are sent, and dies with the form; UploadProgress tracks transfers that outlive the dialog, with Cancel and Retry. Both draw a file row with a progress bar; when a transfer must survive navigation, hand it to UploadProgress instead of keeping the token.
- `chip` — a removable label without file details.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `FileTokenGroupItem[]` | `[]` | false | The files, in order; each with its optional upload state, error and warning. |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | false | Vertical stacks full-width tokens; horizontal wraps compact tokens in rows. Same name as `field`'s axis. |
| `limit` | `number` | `0` | false | Shows this many tokens and a Show more toggle for the rest. 0 shows them all. |
| `showFileSize` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the size beside the name, formatted for the locale. |
| `showFileLastModified` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the last-modified date, formatted for the locale. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Hides the remove buttons; the list is for reading only. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Files`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remove` | `(event: MouseEvent, payload: { index: number; item: FileTokenGroupItem })` | The remove button of the token at `index` was pressed. The parent removes it from `items`. Same name as Chip and AttributeEditor. |

## States

- Root `data-orientation`: `vertical` | `horizontal`; `data-readonly` when read-only.
- Token `data-status`: `idle` | `loading` | `warning` | `error` (error wins over warning, both over loading).
- Show more toggle: `aria-expanded` `true` | `false`.
- A file with a `webkitRelativePath` (picked with a folder picker or dropped as a folder on `FileDropzone directories`) is named by that path (`site/css/main.css`) in the token, its title, the remove button and the progress bar; otherwise by `name`.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `ul` (`role="list"`) named by `ariaLabel` or the catalog; each token is a `li`.
- Each remove button is an `IconButton` named `Remove <file name>`; its `aria-describedby` points at the token's error or warning line, so the reason is read with it.
- Keyboard map: Tab reaches each remove button and the Show more toggle in order; Enter or Space removes. After a removal focus moves to the remove button now at the same index, else the previous one, else the list itself (`tabindex="-1"`).
- An error or warning is shown as text with an icon, never by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1); the uploading bar is a `progressbar` named `Uploading <file name>`.
- Contrast: name and meta ≥ 4.5:1 on `--bg-surface` in both themes; the danger border ≥ 3:1.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'
  import FileTokenGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/file-token-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const LIMIT = 300 * 1024 * 1024

  const inputEl = ref(null)
  const items = ref([
    { file: { name: 'logo.svg', size: 4210, type: 'image/svg+xml' } },
    { file: { name: 'index.html', size: 18432, type: 'text/html' } },
    { file: { name: 'site-backup.tar', size: 412_000_000 }, error: 'Larger than 300 MB' },
    { file: { name: 'notes.txt', size: 0, type: 'text/plain' }, warning: 'This file is empty' }
  ])

  const toItem = (file) => ({
    file,
    error: file.size > LIMIT ? 'Larger than 300 MB' : undefined,
    warning: file.size === 0 ? 'This file is empty' : undefined
  })

  const add = (files) => {
    items.value = [...items.value, ...Array.from(files).map(toItem)]
  }

  const onPick = (event) => {
    add(event.target.files ?? [])
    event.target.value = ''
  }

  const remove = (index) => {
    items.value = items.value.filter((_, position) => position !== index)
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-md) flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <FileDropzone
      description="Up to 300 MB per file."
      @drop="(event, files) => add(files)"
    >
      <Button
        label="Browse files"
        variant="secondary"
        size="medium"
        @click="inputEl?.click()"
      />
    </FileDropzone>
    <input
      ref="inputEl"
      type="file"
      multiple
      class="hidden"
      aria-hidden="true"
      tabindex="-1"
      @change="onPick"
    />
    <FileTokenGroup
      :items="items"
      @remove="(_event, { index }) => remove(index)"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/file-token-group.md](components/file-token-group.md).

<!-- components/hint.md -->

# Hint

> Small info affordance — a muted `az az-circle-info` glyph on a focusable button — that reveals one short explanation on hover or focus, through `Tooltip`. It is the standard way to attach a "why does this matter?" note to a field name without spending a line of vertical space on it, and it is what `Field.Label`'s `hint` prop renders.

- Import: `import Hint from '@aziontech/webkit/hint'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Hint for the info glyph beside a field label or column header that explains it in one sentence. Guidance that must stay visible goes in Field.Description (inside Field) or FieldDescription.
- A field, switch or setting whose name is clear but whose consequence is not (what "Sensitive" does to a stored value).
- A short, self-contained sentence — one that reads fine in a tooltip and is not needed to complete the field.
- Beside a label, a section heading, or a table column header, where a permanent line of helper text would add noise.

## Do

- One sentence, ending in a period. If it needs two, it belongs in `field-description` or a `popover`.
- Never hide required information behind a hint — hover is not discoverable on touch, so treat it as an enhancement.
- The `content` doubles as the button's accessible name, so write it as prose a screen reader can read verbatim.
- Place it immediately after the thing it explains, not at the end of a row.

## Don’t

- Guidance the user needs while typing, or any validation message → use `field-error` (it stays on screen and is wired with `aria-describedby`).
- More than a sentence, links, or formatted content → use `popover`, which is dismissible and can hold real content.
- A plain description of an action already labelled by a control → use `tooltip` directly on that control.

## Related

- `tooltip` — the overlay `Hint` composes; reach for it when the trigger is an existing control rather than a standalone info glyph.
- `field-description` — persistent guidance under a field; the right choice when the text must always be visible.
- `Field.Label` — renders `Hint` from its own `hint` prop, so a field name and its note stay one component.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `string` | `''` | true | Guidance text revealed on hover or focus; also the trigger's accessible name. |
| `side` | `'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'start' \| 'end' \| 'auto'` | `'top'` | false | Side of the glyph the tooltip opens on, flipped when it does not fit; `'auto'` picks the side with the most room. `start` and `end` follow the text direction. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`
- `data-state` values (on the root, owned by `Tooltip`): `open` | `closed`
- `data-side` (on the root, owned by `Tooltip`): `top` | `bottom` | `start` | `end`, the side the tooltip landed on

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a native `<button type="button">`, so it is in the tab order and the tooltip opens on `focus` as well as hover (`Tooltip` opens on `focusin`).
- The glyph is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`); the button's accessible name is the `content` prop, so the hint is reachable by screen readers that never see the tooltip.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves focus to the glyph and opens the tooltip; `Escape` closes it (owned by `Tooltip`); the button has no activation behaviour.
- The button's default action is prevented on click, so a `Hint` rendered inside a `<label>` never toggles the labelled control.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 between `var(--text-muted)` and `var(--bg-canvas)`; the focus ring uses `var(--ring-color)` at 2px with an offset.
- Touch target: the glyph is drawn at 20×20 px inline with 12 px label text; a `[data-slot=touch-target]` span extends the hit area to 24×24 px (WCAG 2.5.8), and to 44×44 px on a coarse pointer. It is an enhancement, never the only path to the information.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Hint from '@aziontech/webkit/hint'
</script>

<template>
  <Hint content="Values are encrypted at rest and never displayed again after saving." />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/hint.md](components/hint.md).

<!-- components/input.md -->

# Input

> Single-line text input for forms and inline editing. Renders a bordered field with optional leading/trailing icon slots. Visual states (hover, focus, filled) are driven by native CSS pseudo-classes, not props. The component is the field only — labels, helper text, and error messages live in the wrapping form-field layer. Aligned with Figma frame `562:6774` (Webkit / Input).

- Import: `import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Capture a single line of free-form text (names, titles, search terms).
- Use Input with a search icon to filter a list in place; to open the ⌘K palette use SearchTrigger.

## Do

- Wrap it in `Field` when you need a label, helper text, or validation message.
- Set an appropriate `type`/`inputmode` for the content (email, url, …).
- Set `monospace` on a field whose value is code-like: a CLI command, an ID, a token, a hash, a path. Pair it with `:spellcheck="false"`.
- A read-only command or ID the user copies: `readonly` + `monospace` inside an `InputGroup` with a `CopyButton`, and a description saying why it cannot change.
- Do not set `monospace` on prose values (names, titles, e-mails, domains typed by the user).
- Do not restyle a read-only field (dashed border, transparent fill): it is the same filled field, made non-editable; the reason belongs in the field's description.

## Don’t

- The value spans multiple lines → use `textarea`.
- The value is strictly numeric → use `number-input`.
- The user must choose from a fixed set → use `select` / `multi-select`.

## Related

- `textarea` — multi-line free text.
- `number-input` — numeric input with stepper semantics.
- `field` — wraps this input with label, description and error; the input reads its id, `aria-describedby` and state from it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder shown when the field is empty. |
| `type` | `'text' \| 'email' \| 'number'` | `'text'` | false | Native input type. Restricted to single-line variants the field treats identically. |
| `maxLength` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `maxlength` — maximum number of characters allowed. |
| `autocomplete` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `autocomplete` token on the `<input>` (e.g. `email`, `username`, `off`). Omitted when unset. |
| `spellcheck` | `boolean \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `spellcheck` on the `<input>`. Set `false` for slugs, IDs and domains. Omitted when unset: the default is an explicit `undefined`, because Vue would otherwise cast an absent boolean to `false` and render `spellcheck="false"` on every field. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects height only — padding and typography are constant. Heights: small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only: value is visible, focusable and copyable but not editable. Keeps the filled field (surface and solid border) with no hover border and a default cursor (`data-readonly`); distinct from the disabled field. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; sets native `required` and `aria-required`. Visual indicator (asterisk) is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid`. |
| `monospace` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Sets the value and placeholder in the monospace code face (`.text-label-code-sm`) for CLI commands, IDs, tokens and hashes (`data-monospace`). |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` |  | Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). Logical: it sits on the right under `dir="rtl"`. |
| `trailing` |  | Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The field value via `defineModel`; updates on every native `input` event. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`
- Password managers: the `<input>` carries `data-1p-ignore`, `data-lpignore`, `data-bwignore` and `data-form-type="other"` unless it is a credential or identity field — `autocomplete` set to any token but `off`, or `type="email"`. A read-only field always carries them. This keeps 1Password, LastPass, Bitwarden and Dashlane from offering a sign-in on ordinary fields (names, IDs, searches) while login fields stay fillable. A consumer attr (e.g. `data-1p-ignore="false"`) wins.
- `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop: a read-only field keeps the editable field's fill (`var(--bg-surface)`) and solid `var(--border-default)` border, as the design sample draws it; it only drops the hover border and takes a default cursor. The value keeps `var(--text-default)` (readable and copyable, unlike `disabled`) and the field stays focusable. Why the value cannot change is said by the field's description, not by a different chrome.
- `data-monospace` mirrors the `monospace` prop: the value and the placeholder render in `.text-label-code-sm` instead of `.text-label-sm`.
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop; drives the warning-border treatment
- `data-leading` / `data-trailing` mirror slot presence (driven by `$slots.leading` / `$slots.trailing`), read at render time: an icon slot passed behind a `v-if` adds or removes its icon box when the condition changes, never leaving an empty box behind
- `filled` is detected via the native `:not(:placeholder-shown)` selector — no JS state

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2`, with the offset color resolving `var(--input-ring-offset, var(--bg-canvas))` — applied via `focus-within` on the field wrapper so the ring covers the whole control including icon slots. A host that places the field on a surface other than the canvas (a raised popover, a drawer) declares `--input-ring-offset` on any ancestor; custom properties inherit, so one declaration retunes the ring gap of every field inside it (this is how `date-picker`'s fields panel matches its raised popover).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the input; standard text-editing keys apply.
- Direction: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"` so a value typed in another script keeps its own direction inside right-to-left UI; a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: `aria-invalid` is bound to the `invalid` prop; `aria-required` to the `required` prop; icon slots are `aria-hidden="true"` (decorative).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition-bearing class.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on `size="large"`; smaller sizes are intended for dense layouts where the wrapping label area extends the hit zone.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <Input
    v-model="value"
    placeholder="Type something"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/input-group.md -->

# Input Group

> Composition container that joins an input primitive with any number of adjacent controls (buttons, selects, static addons) into a single visual field (an input group, as other UI kits call it). The root only orchestrates: it draws the outer border, the `focus-within` ring, and applies inline Tailwind child-selectors so the first child rounds only on the left, the last only on the right, and internal borders collapse between siblings. Everything else is a **child**: the middle input is a raw `<input>` in the root's `default` slot; sibling controls (`<Button>`, `<Select>`, `<Input>`, or an `<InputGroup.Addon>` for static text like `https://` / `.com` / `$`) are dropped in directly alongside it. This is a breaking change from v3: the `#left` and `#right` named slots are gone — their static-text role moves to `<InputGroup.Addon>`, and their interactive role is served by placing the real component (`Button`, `Select`) as a direct child. Consumers therefore never wrap `Button`/`Select` in an inner `<div>` — the root's child selectors do that job.

- Import: `import InputGroupRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import InputGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A text input that needs static prefix or suffix content inside the same border (`https://`, `.com`, a currency symbol).
- An input joined to a control: a search field with a trailing `button`, an amount with a leading currency `select`.

## Do

- Put static text and icons in `InputGroup.Addon`; place real controls (`button`, `select`) as direct children with no wrapper `div`.
- Set the same `size` on the group and on its child controls so heights line up.
- `disabled` and `invalid` on the group reach every field control inside (`InputGroup.Input`, `Input`, `Select` and the other controls that read the Field context); a `Button` or `IconButton` in the group needs its own `disabled`. `required` styles the group only; set it on the input or on the enclosing `Field`. Inside a `Field`, the Field's state reaches the root and the controls the same way.
- Use `InputGroup.Input` for the middle input: it is borderless, picks up the enclosing `Field`'s wiring, and spares the long raw-`<input>` class string.
- The root is `role="group"`; label the inner input itself, or give the group an `aria-label`.

## Don’t

- A phone number with a dial code → use `phone-input`.
- A single input with only a decorative icon → use `input` and its `iconLeft` / `iconRight` slots.

## Related

- `field` — wrap the group in a `Field` for a label and description/error; `InputGroup.Input` takes the field's id, `aria-describedby` and state, and the root takes `invalid` / `disabled` / `required` from it.
- `phone-input` — input group with a dial-code select and a per-country mask.
- `input` — the single-field primitive with icon slots.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects the root's height and inner addon padding. Heights: small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px. Matches the sibling input primitives (`Input`, `Select`) — set the same `size` on child controls to keep them visually aligned. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the error border and marks the field controls inside invalid (`aria-invalid` on the input, never on the `role="group"` root, where ARIA does not allow it). |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the required (warning) border. `aria-required` is not allowed on `role="group"`, so the required state belongs on the input (`InputGroup.Input` reads it from the Field). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the disabled visual, sets `aria-disabled="true"` on the root and disables the field controls inside (`InputGroup.Input`, `Input`, `Select`, …) through the Field context. A `Button` or `IconButton` inside needs its own `disabled`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | On the **root**: the full row of children in visual order — any mix of `<InputGroup.Addon>`, `<Button>`, `<Select>`, `<Input>`, raw `<input>`. Order in the template is the order rendered left-to-right. On **`<InputGroup.Addon>`**: the addon content — text (`https://`, `.com`, `$`), an Azion icon `<i>`, or any small inline node; kept short by convention (long content breaks the fixed row height). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-addon`
- `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-input`

## Sub-components

Folder layout:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/input/input-group/
├── input-group.vue                      # root
├── input-group-addon/
│   └── input-group-addon.vue            # <InputGroup.Addon>
├── input-group-input/
│   └── input-group-input.vue            # <InputGroup.Input>
└── index.ts                             # compound wire-up (Object.assign)
```

Public members of the compound:

| Member | Attached name | Standalone export | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Root | — (the compound itself) | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-root` | The container. Orchestrates borders, seams, focus ring, and states. |
| `<InputGroup.Addon>` | `Addon` | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-addon` | Static-content island (icon, text like `https://`, `.com`, `$`) rendered with the darker `--bg-canvas` fill and muted text. |
| `<InputGroup.Input>` | `Input` | `@aziontech/webkit/input-group-input` | Borderless middle `<input>`, with the same inline padding as `Input` (`--spacing-sm`). Props: `modelValue` (`''`), `type` (`'text' | 'email' | 'number' | 'password'`, default `'text'`: the restricted set of `Input`, plus `password`to mask a secret value that a reveal control in an addon toggles back to`text`), `placeholder` (`''`), `autocomplete`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `required`, `invalid`(all`false`); emits `update:modelValue`. Reads `id`, `aria-describedby`, `invalid`, `disabled`and`required`from an enclosing`Field` (an explicit prop/attribute wins). |

The root reads `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` from an enclosing `Field` too, OR-ed with its own props, so a `Field`'s state styles the whole group. The root then provides the Field context to its children with `invalid` and `disabled` OR-ed with the group's own (the parent Field's id, description, title and `required` pass through), so the group's state reaches the controls inside.

## States

- Visual states on root: `default`, `hover`, `focus-within`, `invalid`, `required`, `disabled`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop and drives the root height (`small`=`h-7`, `medium`=`h-8`, `large`=`h-10`)
- Only one focus indicator is visible when a descendant is focused: the group draws the single `focus-within` ring on its root, and the inner input primitives' own focus rings are suppressed via `[&_*]:focus-visible:!ring-0 [&_*]:focus-within:!ring-0` so `Button`, `Select.Trigger`, `Input` wrappers, and raw `<input>` share the group's ring instead of stacking their own on top
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop; `aria-invalid` lands on the controls inside, not on the root
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop (no `aria-required` on the group root)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop; sets `aria-disabled="true"`
- Border semantics mirror `input` (independent, not compound):
  - `data-invalid` → `var(--danger-border)`
  - `data-required` → `var(--warning-border)`
- Hover (only when not focus-within, not invalid, not required, not disabled): `border-(--border-strong)`
- Focus-within: 2-ring at `var(--ring-color)` with `var(--bg-canvas)` offset (suppressed when `data-disabled`)
- Disabled: `bg-(--bg-disabled)`, `text-(--text-disabled)`, `cursor-not-allowed`, hover ignored, focus-within ring suppressed
- Child seams (applied by the root via Tailwind child selectors):
  - `[&>*:first-child]:rounded-l-(--shape-control)` and `[&>*:not(:first-child)]:rounded-l-none`
  - `[&>*:last-child]:rounded-r-(--shape-control)` and `[&>*:not(:last-child)]:rounded-r-none`
  - `[&>*:not(:last-child)]:border-r-(color:--border-default) [&>*:not(:last-child)]:border-r` — a single vertical seam between adjacent children, drawn on the left child so child components keep their own left border intact
  - Child components' own outer borders remain — the root's outer border sits on top, so double lines are avoided by the child selector removing the _inner-facing_ border only

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the root shows a `focus-within` ring (`ring-2 ring-(--ring-color) ring-offset-2 ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`) whenever any descendant (any child control or the middle input) has focus. The middle input renders `focus:ring-0 outline-none` so the group's ring is the only visible focus indicator. Suppressed when `data-disabled` is present. Child components (`Button`, `Select`) retain their own focus behavior internally but the group's ring is visually authoritative.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the children in DOM order. No custom keybindings on the group.
- ARIA: root uses `role="group"` with `aria-disabled`; `aria-invalid` is set on the controls inside (ARIA 1.2 does not allow it on `group`); `required` is styling only on the root. Each child keeps its own `aria-*` — the group does not duplicate.
- `<InputGroup.Addon>` is decorative-by-default; when its content is not conveyed elsewhere the consumer should annotate it (`aria-hidden="true"` for pure decoration, or a visible-only label the middle input references via `aria-describedby`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for addon text against `var(--bg-canvas)`; ≥3:1 for the border in every state.
- Motion: color transitions on state changes are `duration-150 ease-out` and pair with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target ≥32×32 px for interactive children (matches root height `h-8`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import InputGroupRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/input-group-root'
</script>

<template>
  <InputGroupRoot>
    <input
      placeholder="domain"
      class="flex-1 min-w-0 h-full bg-(--bg-surface) border-0 outline-none focus:ring-0 px-(--spacing-md) text-label-sm text-(--text-default) placeholder:text-(--text-muted)"
    />
  </InputGroupRoot>
</template>
```
