<!-- components/multi-select.md -->

# Multi Select

> Select control specialised for choosing many options from a list. The trigger field mirrors `Input`'s visual API (size, hover/focus/filled/disabled/invalid/required states) so a MultiSelect sits next to other form fields without visual drift. The dropdown panel is teleported to `body` and anchored to the trigger by the shared `usePlacement` composable — no `@floating-ui` runtime. Every option row carries a checkbox indicator (the `Checkbox` webkit component), optionally a leading slot/icon and a trailing tag. Search and "Create new" footer are exposed as slots on `<MultiSelectContent>`. Since spec v4 the trigger can also show the selection as removable chips (`variant="chips"`, capped by `chipLimit` with a `+N more` chip), take typed text to filter the options in place (`searchable`), offer an `Add "…"` row for a typed value that matches no option (`allowCustom`, emits `create`), and render its own loading, error and empty list states (`loading`, `error`, `emptyTitle`) — the same vocabulary as `combobox`. MultiSelect is the one multi-pick field (`Select` picks exactly one): `modelValue` is always an array and the indicator is always a checkbox. Aligned with Figma frame `3899:29362` (options panel). The trigger reuses the `Input`/`Select` trigger visuals.

- Import: `import MultiSelectRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import MultiSelect from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use MultiSelect whenever the person picks several values from a list in a form field; the chosen ones show as a count or chips in the trigger. For two to five options that fit on screen use a Checkbox per option; to build a large subset with both sides visible use TransferList.
- Choosing several values from a long list (regions, tags, permissions) in a compact field.
- A filter whose selected values stay editable from the same dropdown.
- Grouped options with icons or trailing tags, optionally with search.
- Tagging a record with labels people pick or type (`variant="chips"` + `searchable` + `allowCustom`).
- Options fetched from a server as the person types (`searchable`, `:filter="false"`, `@search`, `loading`, `error`).

## Do

- `modelValue` is always an array; start it as `[]`, never `null`.
- Pass `displayValue` to summarise long selections (e.g. "3 regions") instead of a list that overflows the trigger.
- Keep each option's `value` stable and unique; selection is matched by value.
- Put a search input in the `search` slot and a create action in the `footer` slot of `MultiSelect.Content` — or set `searchable` (and `allowCustom`) to type in the trigger itself; do not combine the two.
- With `variant="chips"`, set `chipLimit` when the field sits in a dense row; leave it `0` in a form so every chip wraps and stays removable.
- `create` only reports the typed value: add the new option to your list and its value to the model in the handler.
- For a server-side search, set `:filter="false"`, fetch on `search`, and drive `loading` and `error` from the request.

## Don’t

- Only one value may be chosen → use `select`.
- A labelled form field with helper/error text → put it inside a `field`.
- A handful of options that fit on screen → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.
- The user builds a subset and needs the chosen and remaining items side by side → use `transfer-list`.
- Free-form tags with no list of options to pick from → use `tag-editor`.

## Related

- `select` — single-choice counterpart.
- `field` — wraps this control with its label, description and error; it hands the trigger its id and state.
- `transfer-list` — dual-list transfer for building larger subsets.
- `checkbox` — the indicator every option row renders.
- `combobox` — single-value field with typed text; `searchable`, `allowCustom`, `filter`, `loading` and `emptyTitle` share its meaning.
- `chip` — each selected value in `variant="chips"`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Trigger placeholder shown when no option is selected. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects trigger height (small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px) matching `Input`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger and prevents opening; applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only; the current selection is visible but the dropdown cannot open. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; sets `aria-required` on the trigger. Visual indicator (asterisk) is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid` on the trigger. |
| `displayValue` | `(value: TValue[]) => string` | `undefined` | false | Custom formatter used by the trigger to render the selected labels; receives the current `modelValue` array. |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | false | Form field name. Set, the root renders one hidden input per selected value so a native `form` and `FormData` submit every selection under that name; `required` then adds a hidden required proxy that blocks an empty submit, and `disabled` leaves the values out. |
| `variant` | `'summary' \| 'chips'` | `'summary'` | false | How the trigger shows the selection: `summary` joins the labels (or `displayValue`), `chips` renders one removable chip per value. |
| `chipLimit` | `number` | `0` | false | With `variant="chips"`, the most chips shown before a `+N more` chip; `0` shows every chip and wraps. |
| `searchable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Types in the trigger: the text filters the options, `Backspace` in an empty field removes the last value. |
| `filter` | `boolean` | `true` | false | With `searchable`, hides the options whose label does not contain the typed text. Turn off when the server filters on `search`. |
| `allowCustom` | `boolean` | `false` | false | With `searchable`, offers typed text that matches no option as an `Add "…"` row that emits `create`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the loading row in place of the options while they are fetched. |
| `error` | `string` | `''` | false | Message shown in place of the options when they failed to load; empty shows the options. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the list when no option is visible. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `modelValue` | `TValue[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | `string` | The typed text, on each keystroke (`searchable`), and `''` when the panel closes and the text is cleared. Value event: no DOM event. |
| `create` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: string)` | The `Add "…"` row was activated (`allowCustom`), by click or by `Enter` in the field or on the row; `value` is the trimmed typed text. The typed text is cleared; the consumer adds the option and the value. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Composition slot; receives `<MultiSelectTrigger>` and `<MultiSelectContent>` (and the option tree inside it). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-item`

## Sub-components

- `multi-select-trigger/multi-select-trigger.vue` — With the default `variant="summary"` and no `searchable`, a bordered trigger button; otherwise a bordered field (`min-h` of the size, wrapping) that holds the chips (`…
- `multi-select-content/multi-select-content.vue` — Popover panel teleported to `body` and anchored with `usePlacement`; exposes `default` (the options), `#search` and `#footer` slots, typed with `defineSlots`, and scro…
- `multi-select-group/multi-select-group.vue` — Section wrapper for a labelled group of options; hidden while the typed filter hides every one of its options; renders a `text-label-sm` heading in `--text-muted` when `la…
- `multi-select-item/multi-select-item.vue` — Selectable option row; hidden (`v-show`) while `searchable` + `filter` and its label text does not contain the typed text (case and accent insensitive, in the active locale)…

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `TValue[]` | `[]` | `update:modelValue` | The selection via `defineModel`. Always an array; each item is the `value` of a selected `<MultiSelectItem>`. Fires when an option is toggled with the next selection array. Uncontrolled when unbound. |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state of the dropdown via `defineModel`. Fires when the dropdown opens or closes. Unbound, the dropdown keeps its own state, seeded by `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `opened`
- `data-state` on the root and trigger: `open` | `closed`
- `data-size` on the trigger mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-required`, `data-readonly`, `data-filled` mirror the matching props (or the selection state for `data-filled`)
- `data-selected` on `<MultiSelectItem>` when the option's value is part of the current selection
- `data-variant` on the root and trigger mirrors `variant`; `data-searchable` on the trigger mirrors `searchable`
- `loading`: `aria-busy` on the listbox and the loading row; `error`: the message row; `empty`: the empty row — each in place of the options, in the panel
- `data-variant="create"` on the `Add "…"` row
- Typed filter: while the typed text is not empty, every chunk is mounted so the filter sees every option.
- Long lists: above 300 options the list mounts in chunks of 100 as they scroll near view (unmounted chunks keep their height, 32 px per option), so opening a 1,000-option list stays within its runtime budget. The first arrow, `Home` or `End` key in the list mounts every option before moving focus, so keyboard navigation always reaches every option.
- `data-side` (`bottom` | `top`) and `data-align` (`start`) on the listbox panel mirror where it landed after flipping; `start` follows the text direction, so under `rtl` the panel lines up with the field's right edge

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on trigger and on every option row.
- Keyboard map (trigger): `Tab` focuses; `Space`/`Enter`/`ArrowDown` opens the panel; `Escape` closes it.
- Keyboard map (closed trigger): `Enter`, `Space`, `ArrowDown` and `ArrowUp` open the list (focus lands as described below); `Home` opens it on the first enabled option and `End` on the last; typing a printable character opens it on the first enabled option whose label starts with that character (with a search field, focus goes to the search field instead). Clicking the trigger while the list is open closes it. Tests: `multi-select.test.ts` › Select keyboard and naming (APG select-only combobox).
- Keyboard map (`searchable` field): typing filters and opens the panel; `ArrowDown` opens and focuses the first visible option, `ArrowUp` the last; `Enter` activates the `Add "…"` row when it is offered, else opens the panel; `Backspace` in an empty field removes the last selected value; `Escape` closes the panel, then clears the text; `Tab` closes and moves on. From the list, `Escape`, `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` return focus to the field instead of a trigger button.
- Chips: each chip's remove button is in the tab order and named `Remove <label>` (from `Chip`); removing one never opens the panel. The `+N more` chip is plain text.
- Keyboard map (open panel): opening focuses the search field when there is one, else the first selected option, else the first enabled option; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move between enabled options and wrap; `Home`/`End` jump to first/last enabled; `Enter`/`Space` toggles the focused option and keeps the panel open; typing a printable character moves focus to the next enabled option whose label starts with the typed text (characters typed within 500 ms add up; ignored while the search field has focus); `Escape` closes and returns focus to the trigger; `Tab` closes and moves focus to the control after the trigger; `Shift+Tab` closes and returns focus to the trigger. Tests: `multi-select.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: trigger uses `role="combobox"` with `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded` bound to open state, `aria-controls` pointing to the list. The teleported content is a plain panel holding the optional search field, the list and the optional footer; the list (not the panel) carries `role="listbox"`, so the search field sits outside it, and is named by the root's `aria-label`, else by the root's `aria-labelledby`, else by the enclosing `Field` label, else by the trigger (which always has an `id`). The list uses `role="listbox"` with `aria-multiselectable="true"`. Each option uses `role="option"` with `aria-selected` mirroring its selection. Decorative icons (`az az-chevron-down`, `az-heart`, etc.) are `aria-hidden="true"`. The checkbox indicator is decorative for screen readers (the `role="option"` + `aria-selected` carries the semantic); the inner `Checkbox` sits in an `inert`, `aria-hidden="true"` wrapper, so the option has no focusable descendant.
- Nested overlays: the open list joins the shared overlay layer stack (`useOverlayLayer`), so inside a `Popover`, `Dialog` or `Drawer` an option click or `Escape` in the list closes only the list; the host overlay stays open.
- `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` on the trigger mirror the matching props.
- With `variant="chips"` or `searchable`, the `combobox` role, `id`, name and `aria-*` move from the field to its control (the `input` gets `aria-autocomplete="list"`); the field itself is a plain container.
- List states sit in `role="presentation"` rows; a visually hidden `role="status"` region announces `Loading options`, the error message, the empty text, or `{count} options` after typing.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons + borders), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:animate-none` on every transition/animation-bearing class.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on `size="large"`; smaller sizes are documented as dense-layout-only (consistent with `Input`).
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="listbox"` content binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import MultiSelectContent from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-content'
  import MultiSelectItem from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-item'
  import MultiSelectRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-root'
  import MultiSelectTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/multi-select-trigger'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref(['opt-1'])
  const options = [
    { value: 'opt-1', label: 'Option 1' },
    { value: 'opt-2', label: 'Option 2' },
    { value: 'opt-3', label: 'Option 3' },
    { value: 'opt-4', label: 'Option 4' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <div style="width: 280px">
    <MultiSelectRoot
      aria-label="Options"
      v-model="value"
      placeholder="Select options"
    >
      <MultiSelectTrigger />
      <MultiSelectContent>
        <MultiSelectItem
          v-for="o in options"
          :key="o.value"
          :value="o.value"
          >{{ o.label }}</MultiSelectItem
        >
      </MultiSelectContent>
    </MultiSelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Number Input

> Numeric input field with optional increment/decrement spinner buttons. Use when the value is strictly numeric (counts, quantities, ports, thresholds, currency without formatting). Distinct from `input` because it enforces numeric type, supports `min`/`max`/`step`, and renders chevron-up/chevron-down controls on the trailing edge.

- Import: `import NumberInput from '@aziontech/webkit/number-input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Capture a strictly numeric value (counts, quantities, ports, prices).

## Do

- Set `min` / `max` / `step` to constrain input rather than validating after the fact.
- Use `inputmode="numeric"` semantics for mobile keyboards.
- Set `nullable` on an optional field (a port, a limit) so a cleared field stays unset (`null`) instead of falling back to `min ?? 0`.

## Don’t

- The value is free text → use `input`.
- The user picks from a fixed set of numbers → use `select`.

## Related

- `input` — free-text sibling with the same field API.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Text shown when the input is empty. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects height, padding, and typography. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as read-only; spinner buttons are inert. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border/ring tokens. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required for assistive tech. |
| `min` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Minimum allowed value; spinner stops at this bound. |
| `max` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Maximum allowed value; spinner stops at this bound. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | false | Increment used by the spinner buttons and arrow keys. |
| `showButtons` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Renders the chevron-up/chevron-down spinner controls. |
| `nullable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lets a cleared field emit null instead of falling back to min or 0. |
| `modelValue` | `NumberInputValue<TNullable>` | `0 as NumberInputValue<TNullable>` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `change` | `number` | Emitted when the user commits the value (blur or Enter). With `nullable` the payload is `null` when the field is committed empty. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` | — | Content rendered before the input (e.g. `$`). |
| `trailing` | — | Content rendered after the input, before the spinner buttons (e.g. `%`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `number` (`number \| null` with `nullable`) | `0` | `update:modelValue` | The value via `defineModel`, clamped to `min`/`max`; updates on typing and on the spinner. A cleared field falls back to `min ?? 0`; with `nullable` it emits `null` and shows the placeholder, and the spinner on a `null` value starts at `min ?? 0` (clamped). The component is generic over `nullable`, so the model and `change` are typed `number` unless `nullable` is set. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `filled`, `empty` (a `nullable` field whose value is `null` shows the placeholder)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the input; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` increment/decrement by `step`; `Home`/`End` jump to `min`/`max` when defined; `Enter` commits and emits `change`.
- Direction: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"` (digits resolve to left-to-right inside right-to-left UI); a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: `role="spinbutton"` on the input (native `<input type="number">` provides this); `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` mirror the props; `aria-invalid` mirrors `invalid`; `aria-required` mirrors `required`; spinner buttons have `aria-label` ("Increment" / "Decrement") and `tabindex="-1"` so keyboard users use arrow keys.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated state changes.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the large size; spinner buttons remain ≥24×24 px on `small`/`medium` per Figma — justified because arrow keys provide the primary interaction.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import NumberInput from '@aziontech/webkit/number-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref(1)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-[20rem]">
    <NumberInput
      v-model="value"
      :min="0"
      :max="100"
      :step="1"
      placeholder="Quantity"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

# Otp Input

> The field for a one-time code: the six digits an authenticator app shows, or a code sent by email or SMS. It looks like a row of boxes, one character each, but it is **one real text input** laid over the boxes, so the browser's one-time-code autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`), password managers, paste and screen readers all see a single field. Typing fills the next box (auto-advance), Backspace empties the last one, and a pasted code (`123 456`, `123-456`, with a line break) keeps only its valid characters and fills every box. When the last box fills it emits `complete`, so the screen can submit without a button press. It replaces six hand-wired text inputs with focus moves between them; the `account/mfa-settings` block uses it to set up and confirm an authenticator.

- Import: `import OtpInput from '@aziontech/webkit/otp-input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Multi-factor authentication: set-up confirmation and sign-in challenge.
- Verifying an email address or a phone number with a short code.
- Any short, fixed-length code the user copies from somewhere else.

## Do

- Label it with what the code is and where it comes from: `Authentication code`, and a description `The 6-digit code from your authenticator app.`
- Submit on `complete` only when the code is the last thing to fill; keep a Verify button for keyboard users and for a failed attempt.
- After a rejected code, mark it `invalid`, clear it, and keep focus in it.
- Use `group="3"` for codes people read aloud or copy from a phone; it draws a separator between groups and does not change the value.

## Don’t

- A password or a secret of free length → use `PasswordInput`.
- A long token or API key → use `Input` with a copy affordance.
- A number with a range → use `NumberInput`.

## Related

- `field` — wrap it in a `Field` for the label, the description and the error; the label names the input.
- `password-input` — the other credential input of the auth screens.
- `input` — the plain text field it shares tokens with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `length` | `number` | `6` | false | How many characters the code has; one box each. |
| `mode` | `'numeric' \| 'alphanumeric'` | `'numeric'` | false | `numeric` keeps digits and opens the number keypad; `alphanumeric` keeps letters and digits, upper case. |
| `group` | `number` | `0` | false | Draw a separator after every `group` boxes (`3` gives `123 – 456`). `0` draws none. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the field while a code is being checked. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Danger borders on every box and `aria-invalid`; set after a rejected code. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Native `required` and `aria-required`. |
| `autofocus` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Focus the field on mount, for a screen whose only task is the code. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `complete` | `string` |  |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The code typed so far, via `defineModel`, already filtered by `mode` and cut to `length`. |

## States

- `data-state` on each box: `empty` | `filled`; `data-active` on the box the next character goes to while the field has focus (the last box when the code is full).
- `data-invalid`, `data-disabled` on the root.
- Separators render between groups when `group` > 0.

## Accessibility

- One `input` carries the value, the name (from the `Field` label, an `aria-label`, or the catalog's `One-time code` when nothing else names it), `aria-describedby` from the `Field`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`, `maxlength`, `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, `inputmode` (`numeric` or `text`) and `enterkeyhint="done"`. The boxes and separators are `aria-hidden`; a screen reader reads the input's value as typed.
- Keyboard: type to fill, Backspace to clear the last character, Tab leaves the field in one stop; the caret stays at the end, so Arrow and Home keys do not move it into the middle of the code.
- Focus: the active box takes the focus ring; the whole field takes one focus stop.
- Contrast: characters `--text-default` on `--bg-surface`, borders `--border-default` (3:1 non-text) in both themes.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import OtpInput from '@aziontech/webkit/otp-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const code = ref('')
  const entered = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <Field>
      <Field.Label>Authentication code</Field.Label>
      <OtpInput
        v-model="code"
        name="code"
        @complete="(value) => (entered = value)"
      />
      <Field.Description>The 6-digit code from your authenticator app.</Field.Description>
    </Field>
    <p
      class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
      role="status"
    >
      {{ entered ? `Code ${entered} entered.` : '' }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Password Input

> Single-line password input for forms. Renders a bordered field with a built-in visibility toggle button on the trailing edge that flips the native `type` between `password` and `text`. Shares the visual language of `Input` (same heights, borders, focus ring, disabled treatment). The component is the field only — labels, helper text, and strength meters live in the wrapping form-field layer. Aligned with Figma frame `3714:10788` (Webkit / PasswordInput). The token mapping was originally inferred from the `input` sibling because the Figma MCP was unreachable during spec authoring; it has since been **reconciled against the frame** as rendered inside the password field frame (`2027:3212`), which corrected the trailing padding to `var(--spacing-xs)` and the visibility toggle to the 28 px (`small`) `IconButton`. One frame value is deliberately not adopted: the border width stays at the shared 1 px rather than the frame's `var(--border-width-default)` (0.8 px), because this component's contract is to share `Input`'s borders and `Input` is still on 1 px — moving one without the other would break that stated invariant. Adopting it is a coordinated follow-up across every bordered input.

- Import: `import PasswordInput from '@aziontech/webkit/password-input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A bare password field whose label and errors are laid out separately (an inline re-authentication prompt, a custom form row).
- Any secret the user may need to check while typing (passwords, tokens); the built-in toggle reveals it as plain text.

## Do

- Set `autocomplete="new-password"` on sign-up and password-change forms; keep the default `current-password` on login.
- Leave `toggleable` on; turn it off only when you need the `trailing` slot, which is ignored while the toggle is shown.
- The field is a fixed 40px tall with no `size` prop; align it with `size="large"` siblings in the same row.
- Give it an accessible name: a `label` whose `for` matches an `id` passed to the input, or `aria-label`.
- Set `monospace` on a secret that is code-like: an API token, a client secret, a signing key. Pair it with `autocomplete="off"` and `:spellcheck="false"`, so a revealed token reads character by character (`0`/`O`, `l`/`1`).
- Do not set `monospace` on a person's own password: they typed it and never read it back character by character.

## Don’t

- A password field with a label, helper or error text, or a requirements row → wrap it in a `field` (with `password-requirements` for the rules row).
- The value is not secret → use `input`.

## Related

- `field` — wraps this input with its label and description; it hands the input its id, `aria-describedby` and state.
- `password-requirements` — the live checklist of password rules rendered under this input.
- `input` — plain-text field with the same borders, focus ring, and disabled treatment.
- `input` — plain single-line text input.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder shown when the field is empty. |
| `maxLength` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Native `maxlength` — maximum number of characters allowed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. The toggle button inherits the disabled state. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only; value is visible but not editable. Toggle button stays operable. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; sets native `required` and `aria-required`. Visual indicator (asterisk) is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid`. |
| `toggleable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, renders the visibility toggle button on the trailing edge of the field. When false, the field behaves as a plain password input with no toggle and the `trailing` slot becomes available. |
| `autocomplete` | `'current-password' \| 'new-password' \| 'off'` | `'current-password'` | false | Native `autocomplete` hint for password managers. Use `new-password` for sign-up and password-change flows. |
| `monospace` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Sets the value and placeholder in the monospace code face (`.text-label-code-sm`) for API tokens, client secrets and keys (`data-monospace`). Same prop as on `Input`. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` | — | Leading adornment at the inline start of the field. Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). Same name as on `input` and `number-input`. |
| `trailing` | — | Trailing adornment at the inline end. **Only honored when `toggleable=false`** — the visibility toggle sits there when enabled. Hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden="true"`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The field value via `defineModel`; updates on every native `input` event. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `invalid`
- Single fixed height: 40px (large only)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop; drives the warning-border treatment
- `data-leading` mirrors `$slots.leading` presence
- `data-trailing` mirrors `$slots.trailing` presence (only relevant when `toggleable=false`)
- `data-toggleable` mirrors the `toggleable` prop
- `data-monospace` mirrors the `monospace` prop: the value (masked or revealed) and the placeholder render in `.text-label-code-sm` instead of `.text-label-sm`.
- `data-revealed` on the root mirrors the internal visibility state (`true` when the password is revealed as plain text)
- `filled` is detected via the native `:not(:placeholder-shown)` selector — no JS state

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` — applied via `focus-within` on the field wrapper so the ring covers the whole control including icon slots and the visibility toggle.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the input, then the visibility toggle button (when `toggleable=true`); `Enter` / `Space` on the toggle flips visibility; standard text-editing keys apply to the input.
- Direction: the `<input>` renders `dir="auto"` so a value typed in another script keeps its own direction inside right-to-left UI; a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: the visibility toggle is a `<button type="button">` with `aria-pressed` reflecting the current visible state and an `aria-label` that switches between "Show password" and "Hide password"; `aria-invalid` is bound to the `invalid` prop; `aria-required` to the `required` prop; decorative icon slots and the eye glyph are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition-bearing class.
- Touch target: the input fills the field's single fixed 40 px height. The visibility toggle is the 28×28 px `small` `IconButton` the Figma frame specifies — above WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) at 24×24 px, and centred in the 40 px row so the practical vertical reach is the full field height. It is below the 44×44 px of SC 2.5.5 (AAA), which this AA-scoped spec does not claim.
- The toggle button never submits the surrounding form (`type="button"`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PasswordInput from '@aziontech/webkit/password-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const password = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <PasswordInput
    v-model="password"
    placeholder="Enter your password"
    autocomplete="current-password"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/password-requirements.md -->

# Password Requirements

> Live checklist of password rules shown under a `PasswordInput`: a caption followed by one chip per rule, each chip turning to the success tone with a check as the typed value satisfies it. Put it in the same `Field` as the `PasswordInput`, under it; the entry also exports `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS` and the `PasswordRequirementsRule` type so a form validates with the same rules it shows. `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS` is typed `PasswordPatternRequirement[]` (exported too): every built-in rule has a `key` and a `RegExp` `test`, so `rule.test.test(value)` type-checks without narrowing; a custom rule list stays `PasswordRequirementsRule[]`, whose `test` may be a predicate.

- Import: `import PasswordRequirements from '@aziontech/webkit/password-requirements'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A new-password field (sign-up, reset, change password) where the user must meet explicit rules.

## Do

- Bind `value` to the same ref as the `PasswordInput` `v-model`.
- Validate on submit with `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS` (or your own array) so the error and the chips never disagree.
- Pass `requirements` to replace the rule set and `title` to localize the caption.

## Don’t

- A sign-in password field → render `password-input` alone; the rules do not apply to an existing password.
- A free-form strength meter → not provided; compose your own.

## Related

- `password-input` — the control whose value this checklist evaluates.
- `field` — place both inside one `Field` so the label and description stay together.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `requirements` | `PasswordRequirementsRule[]` | `DEFAULT_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENTS` | false | Rules rendered as chips, one per entry. Defaults to the built-in rule set; an empty array renders only the caption. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Caption that opens the row and names the group for assistive tech. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Must contain:`). |
| `value` | `string` | `''` | false | Password every rule is evaluated against; pass the PasswordInput value. |

## States

- Each chip carries `data-validated` when its rule passes.
- The row animates its height as chips wrap.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not focusable; the checklist is read-only.
- Keyboard map: _none_.
- ARIA: root `role="group"` named by the caption through `aria-labelledby`; the check icons are `aria-hidden`, so each chip ends with visually hidden state text from the locale catalog (`passwordRequirements.met` / `passwordRequirements.unmet`: `met` / `not met`) and the state is never conveyed by colour and icon alone.
- Direction: the check icon slides in from the inline start (`-translate-x-1`, mirrored under `rtl:`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for chip text in both tones.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import PasswordInput from '@aziontech/webkit/password-input'
  import PasswordRequirements from '@aziontech/webkit/password-requirements'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const password = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <Field
    required
    class="max-w-(--container-xs)"
  >
    <Field.Label>Password</Field.Label>
    <PasswordInput
      v-model="password"
      autocomplete="new-password"
    />
    <PasswordRequirements :value="password" />
  </Field>
</template>
```

<!-- components/phone-input.md -->

# Phone Input

> International phone-number control: an `InputGroup` with a searchable dial-code `Select` on the left and a `type="tel"` input on the right that applies the selected country's mask as the user types and accepts exactly the lengths that country allows. Two v-models (`v-model` for the national digits, `v-model:country` for the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code) carry the editable state; the one-way `phone-change` event hands the form the full E.164 number and whether it is complete. It carries no label or helper text: wrap it in a `Field` (`Field.Label` + `PhoneInput` + `Field.Description`), and it picks up `id`, `aria-describedby`, `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` from the Field.

- Import: `import PhoneInput from '@aziontech/webkit/phone-input'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- International phone entry where the user picks a country and types the national number with that country's mask.
- Forms that need the full E.164 number and whether it is complete, without per-country length rules in the form.

## Do

- Put it in a `Field` with a `Field.Label`; the label targets the tel input.
- `v-model` holds the national digits only; read `number` from the `phone-change` payload when you need the E.164 value.
- Use `complete` from `phone-change` to decide `invalid` and the `Field.Error` on submit; the control shows no incomplete-number message of its own.
- `v-model:country` defaults to `'US'`; seed it with the user's country when you know it.
- `searchPlaceholder` and `searchEmptyLabel` default to English; pass translated copy in localized UIs.

## Don’t

- The value may include characters the masks reject (extensions, free-form notes) → use `input`.
- The input needs addons other than the dial code → use `input-group` and compose it yourself.

## Related

- `field` — wraps the control with its label, description and error.
- `input-group` — the container this control renders around the dial-code select and the input.
- `select` — the dial-code picker inside the group.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `countries` | `PhoneInputCountry[]` | `(built-in list — see Notes)` | false | Countries offered by the dial-code Select. When omitted, uses the built-in curated list. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the tel input. Falls back to the selected country's mask when empty. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size forwarded to the InputGroup and the dial-code Select trigger. Heights: small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables both the dial-code Select and the internal input. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the internal input read-only; dial-code Select is also disabled while readonly. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the required border on the InputGroup and sets required on the input. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border on the InputGroup and sets aria-invalid on the input. |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | false | Form field name. Set, a hidden input submits the full E.164 number (dial code followed by the digits, empty while there are none) under this name; the visible input carries no name, so a native `form` never posts a national number without its country. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the search box that filters the dial-code list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Search country`). |
| `searchEmptyLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Shown in the dial-code list when no country matches the search. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No country found.`). |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `country` | `string` | `'US'` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:country`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `phone-change` | `[value: PhoneInputValue]` | One-way snapshot of the number, emitted once on mount and again whenever the digits or the country change. `PhoneInputValue` (exported from the component) is `{ country: string; dialCode: string; digits: string; number: string; complete: boolean }`: `number` is the full E.164 number (`dialCode + digits`, e.g. `'+14155550100'`; `''` while empty) and `complete` is true when the digit count is one the selected country allows. Not a v-model — the field never reads it back. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | National number as **digits only**, without dial code and without mask characters (e.g. `'4155550100'`). Updates on input when the digits change, and when a country switch truncates digits beyond the new country's capacity. Via `defineModel`, so the field also works unbound. |
| `v-model:country` | `string` | `'US'` | `update:country` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the selected country (e.g. `'US'`, `'GB'`, `'BR'`). Drives the dial code shown in the `Select` and the masks applied to the input. Via `defineModel`, so picking a country works even when the consumer binds only `v-model`. |

## States

- Visual states delegated to `InputGroup`: `default`, `hover`, `focus-within`, `invalid`, `required`, `disabled`.
- `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` combine the prop with the enclosing `Field`.
- The dial-code `Select` is disabled whenever the control is `disabled` **or** `readonly`.
- Completeness is reported through `phone-change`, never rendered.
- The flag sprite (`country-flags.png`, about 80 KB) loads with a dynamic `import()` the first time the dial-code list opens; until it arrives each option keeps its flag box blank. The closed field never fetches it.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the `InputGroup` focus-within ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves from the dial-code `Select` to the tel input; inside the `Select`, arrows navigate, typing filters, `Enter` picks and returns focus to the input, `Esc` closes.
- ARIA: the tel input has `type="tel"`, `inputmode="tel"`, `autocomplete="tel-national"`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`, and the `id` / `aria-describedby` of the enclosing `Field`; the dial-code trigger has `aria-label="PhoneInputCountry dial code"`. The control provides an empty Field context below it so the inner search input never takes the field id.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for input and dial-code text.
- Touch target follows the `size` (40px at `large`).
- Direction: the tel input, each option's dial code and the closed trigger's dial code (`SelectTrigger` `value-dir="ltr"`, a `<bdi dir="ltr">`) render left-to-right, so a number and its `+` keep their order on a right-to-left page; the typed number still aligns to the inline start of the page (`rtl:text-end`, which resolves against the input's own `ltr` direction).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import PhoneInput from '@aziontech/webkit/phone-input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const digits = ref('')
  const country = ref('US')
  const phone = ref(null)
</script>

<template>
  <Field
    required
    class="max-w-(--container-xs)"
  >
    <Field.Label>Phone</Field.Label>
    <PhoneInput
      v-model="digits"
      v-model:country="country"
      name="phone"
      @phone-change="phone = $event"
    />
    <Field.Description>We'll use this to send the verification code.</Field.Description>
  </Field>
</template>
```

<!-- components/radio-group.md -->

# Radio Group

> RadioGroup is the one "pick one of a few" component: it picks exactly one value from a short list of labelled options shown at once. The root is a `radiogroup` that owns the value (`v-model`), the shared form `name`, the group `disabled` / `required` / `invalid` state, the layout axis and the option look (`variant`), and hands them to every `RadioGroup.Item` through `provide`/`inject`; each item draws a radio circle beside its label, or, with `variant="card"`, a bordered card with an optional icon, description and trailing tag (Radix and shadcn style card radios the same way). The options are composed as `RadioGroup.Item`s, or passed as data through `options`. Because the items are native radios that share one `name`, the group is a single tab stop and the arrow keys move the selection, as the APG radio group pattern asks, with no wiring by the consumer. Before 6.0 the bare circle was `RadioButton` and the card look was `RadioCards`; both are folded in here.

- Import: `import RadioGroupRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-group-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import RadioGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-group'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use RadioGroup to pick exactly one of two to seven options shown at once in a form; set `variant="card"` when each option needs an icon, a description or card weight (plans, roles). For more options use Select; to switch a view or mode in place use ToggleGroup; for the theme in app chrome use ThemeSwitcher.
- A required choice of one option among two to seven, where every option should stay visible (billing cycle, region, notification channel).
- A settings form that posts with a native `form` or `FormData`: the selected value submits under `name`.
- A choice inside a `Field` that needs the group label, description and error wired to it.

## Do

- Name the group: put it in a `Field.Set` with a `Field.Legend`, give the `Field` a `Field.Title`, or set `aria-label` on the root.
- Keep labels short and parallel, and order options by likelihood or by a natural sequence.
- Preselect a sensible option when one exists; leave it empty only when the person must choose deliberately, and then set `required`.
- Use `orientation="horizontal"` only for two or three short options; longer lists read better stacked.
- Set `name` whenever the form posts natively; without it the radios share a generated name that is still submitted.
- Do not compose radios by hand (a `Field.Label` choice card around a bare radio): every radio is a `RadioGroup.Item` inside a `RadioGroup`.
- With `variant="card"`, give options a `description` rather than a longer label, and use the `tag` slot for a price or a "Recommended" tag. Use `orientation="horizontal"` for cards that share a row; they wrap at 12rem.
- Pass `options` when the list is data (a plan catalog, roles from an API); the `option` slot replaces an option's label, for a custom body such as an avatar.

## Don’t

- More than about seven options, or options loaded on demand → use `Select`.
- A single on/off setting → use `Switch` or `Checkbox`.
- Several options that may all be on at once → use `Checkbox` items in a `Field.Set`.
- A compact segmented control that switches a view → use `ToggleGroup`.

## Related

- `toggle-group` — a segmented button group for switching views or filters.
- `theme-switcher` — the system / light / dark choice in app chrome.
- `select` — one value from a longer list.
- `field` — wraps the group with its title, description and error; `Field.Set` with `Field.Legend` names it natively.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | false | Form field name shared by every radio; the selected value submits under it. Empty uses a generated name so the radios still group. |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `'vertical'` | false | Layout axis: options stacked, or in a wrapping row. Arrow keys move the selection on both axes either way. |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'card'` | `'default'` | false | Look of every option: a circle beside its label, or a bordered card for options with an icon, a description or card weight (plans, roles). `RadioGroupVariant`, exported. |
| `options` | `TOption[]` | `[]` | false | Options rendered as `RadioGroup.Item` rows, in place of composed items (`TOption extends RadioGroupOption`: `{ value, label, description?, icon?, ariaLabel?, disabled? }`, exported); extra fields reach the `option` and `tag` slots. Empty renders the default slot. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every option and applies the disabled tokens. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Requires a selection: sets `aria-required` on the group and `required` on the radios, so a native form blocks an empty submit. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the group invalid: sets `aria-invalid` on the group and on every radio. |
| `modelValue` | `TOption['value'] \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `RadioGroup.Item`s. Not rendered while `options` is set. |
| `option` | { option: TOption; selected: boolean } | Body of one data-driven option, in place of its label. |
| `tag` | { option: TOption; selected: boolean } | Trailing content of one data-driven option, such as a price or a tag. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/radio-group-item`

## Sub-components

- `radio-group-item/radio-group-item.vue` — one option: a `label` that wraps a native radio and the option text from its default slot.

Layout:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/input/radio-group/
├── radio-group.vue
├── index.ts
├── injection-key.ts
└── radio-group-item/
    └── radio-group-item.vue
```

`index.ts` attaches the item to the root as `RadioGroup.Item`. Exports: `./radio-group` → `index.ts`, `./radio-group-root` → `radio-group.vue`, `./radio-group-item` → `radio-group-item/radio-group-item.vue`.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `TOption['value'] \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Selected value via `defineModel` on the root. Unbound, the group keeps its own selection, starting empty. Emits the item's `value`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `checked`, `disabled`, `invalid`
- Root: `role="radiogroup"`; `data-orientation` (`vertical` | `horizontal`); `data-variant` (`default` | `card`); `data-disabled`, `data-required` and `data-invalid` mirror the group state (the `Field` state included).
- Item: `data-variant` mirrors the group's; `data-checked` while selected, `data-disabled` while the item or the group is disabled, `data-invalid` while the group is invalid. A card shows `var(--border-selected)` and `var(--primary-selected)` while checked, `var(--bg-hover)` on hover and the focus ring on the card itself.
- The circle: `var(--border-input)` ring on `var(--bg-surface)`, `var(--primary)` when checked with a `var(--primary-foreground)` dot, `var(--danger-border)` when invalid, disabled tokens at 50 % opacity.
- Not states of this component: `loading`, `empty`, `error` (the `Field.Error` carries the message) and `readonly` (a fixed choice is plain text, not a disabled group).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `ring-2 ring-(--ring-color) ring-offset-1` on the focused circle, or on the whole card with `variant="card"`.
- Keyboard map (APG radio group, native radios sharing one `name`): `Tab` enters the group on the checked radio, or the first one when none is checked, and the next `Tab` leaves it; `ArrowDown` / `ArrowRight` select the next enabled option and `ArrowUp` / `ArrowLeft` the previous one, wrapping at the ends and skipping disabled options; `Space` selects the focused option.
- ARIA: root `role="radiogroup"` with `aria-labelledby` (the `Field.Title` ids) or the consumer's `aria-label`, `aria-describedby` (the `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` ids), `aria-required` and `aria-invalid`; each option is a native `type="radio"` input named by its wrapping `label`. No `aria-checked` on the native radios: the checked state is native.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the label text, ≥3:1 for the circle, including the disabled state.
- Touch target: the whole label is clickable, and the native input extends to 44 × 44 px on a coarse pointer.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import RadioGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const cycle = ref('monthly')
</script>

<template>
  <RadioGroup
    v-model="cycle"
    name="billing-cycle"
    aria-label="Billing cycle"
  >
    <RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="yearly">Yearly, two months free</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item
      value="contract"
      disabled
    >
      Annual contract
    </RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/radio-group.md](components/radio-group.md).

<!-- components/schema-form.md -->

# Schema Form

> A form rendered from a JSON schema: each property of an object schema becomes a `Field` with its label, description, Required marker and control, and a nested object becomes a fieldset with its own legend. It edits one value object through `v-model`, seeds the schema's defaults, validates the supported draft-07 keywords with built-in messages (on leaving a field, or only after `validate()`), and shows server messages passed by field path. It also reads the OpenAPI request-body keywords a console generates its create and edit forms from: `oneOf` with a `discriminator`, `format`, `writeOnly` and string maps (`additionalProperties`). Through the `ui` map the app adds what a schema cannot say: fields shown only while a predicate holds (`when`), choices loaded from the app (`options`), arrays of objects edited as repeatable fieldsets (`widget: 'repeat'`) and sections, one of them folded under Advanced settings. It is for forms whose fields are data (a function's arguments, an integration's settings, a resource's request body), not for forms a designer lays out by hand.

- Import: `import SchemaForm from '@aziontech/webkit/schema-form'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A function, template or integration declares its own arguments as a JSON schema and the console must ask for them.
- The same settings form must follow a schema the server sends (fields added or removed without a release).
- A form of typed values (text, choices, numbers, switches, lists) with constraints that already live in a schema.
- A resource's create or edit drawer generated from its OpenAPI request schema, with choices read from other endpoints through a loader the app supplies.

## Do

- Give every property a `title` and a one-sentence `description`; the key is only the fallback label.
- Put limits in the schema (`minimum`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `enum`) so the form checks them; say the rule in the `description` when it is a `pattern`, since the built-in message cannot name it.
- Keep the default `validate-on="blur"` for short forms; use `submit` when the form sits in a drawer or dialog with one Save.
- Call `validate()` on submit and stop when it returns `valid: false`; it shows every message and focuses the first invalid field.
- Pass server rejections in `errors` keyed by path (`origin.host`): the field turns invalid with that message until the user edits it (the form-validation rule). Put a section-level failure in an `Alert` above the form, not in `errors`.
- Use a `field:<path>` slot for a control the schema cannot express (`RadioGroup` cards, a resource picker); the slot keeps the label, description and messages.
- Do not rely on unsupported keywords (`$ref`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `uniqueItems`, `multipleOf`, `patternProperties`, a `oneOf` without a `discriminator`): they are ignored, so validate them on the server. Express an `if`/`then` as `ui[path].when`.
- Define `ui` once in the script, not inline in the template: a new `ui` object rebuilds the fields and seeds defaults again.
- Keep a `when` predicate pure and cheap (it runs on every change); read the second argument (the object holding the field) inside a repeat item.
- An `options` loader receives the typed text (empty on first load) and resolves to `{ value, label?, description? }`; filter on the server, return a short list, and let it reject on failure (the field then says so). SchemaForm calls it; it never fetches on its own.
- Mark secrets `writeOnly`: the field starts empty, an empty field leaves the key out of the value, so a PATCH keeps the stored secret.
- Put rarely changed keys in a collapsed section (`ui[''].sections`), not in a second form.

## Don’t

- A form with a fixed, designed layout (settings sections, create pages) → compose `field`, `input`, `select` and `switch` by hand (`edit/edit-resource`, `create/create-page`).
- Rows of key/value pairs the user adds and removes → use `attribute-editor`.
- Editing the schema itself, or raw JSON → use `code-editor`.
- A single choice or value → use the control directly inside a `field`.

## Related

- `field` — the wrapper every generated field uses; SchemaForm adds no field chrome of its own.
- `input`, `select`, `switch`, `textarea`, `password-input` — the controls it renders per type and format.
- `combobox`, `multi-select` — the controls of a field whose choices come from `ui[path].options`.
- `accordion` — folds a collapsed section.
- `attribute-editor` — user-defined key/value rows; SchemaForm uses it for string maps and for the Add and Remove of a repeat.
- `code-editor` — the JSON view of the same value, when the user prefers to type it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `SchemaFormSchema` | `—` | true | JSON schema of an object (draft-07 subset); each property becomes a Field. |
| `errors` | `Record<string, string>` | `{}` | false | Server or external messages by field path; a field shows its message until it is edited. |
| `ui` | `Record<string, SchemaFormUi>` | `{}` | false | Presentation overrides by field path (`''` is the root, `*` a repeat item): widget, placeholder, hidden, order, when, options and sections. |
| `validateOn` | `'blur' \| 'submit'` | `'blur'` | false | When fields first show their validation message: on leaving the field, or only after `validate()`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every field. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows every value without letting it change. |
| `modelValue` | `SchemaFormValue` | `—` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `Record<string, unknown>` | `{}` | `update:modelValue` | The edited object. Each change emits a new object; an emptied field removes its key, and an emptied nested object is removed. Defaults are seeded on mount and on a schema change. |

## States

- Visual states per field come from `Field`: `default`, `invalid` (message under the control), `disabled`, read-only.
- `data-disabled` and `data-readonly` on the root mirror the props; each field carries `data-path` and `data-widget`.
- Validation timing: a field shows its own message after the user leaves it (`validate-on="blur"`), after `validate()` in both modes, and from then on updates as the user types. Opening a `Select` does not count as leaving its field.
- Server messages (`errors`) show at once, win over the field's own message and leave once that field is edited; a new `errors` object shows them again.
- Draft text: a number, list or JSON field keeps what the user typed while it does not parse; the value then holds no key for it, and the field reports "Enter a number." or "Enter valid JSON."
- Hidden (`when`): the field is not rendered, not validated and its key is removed from the value; a variant not chosen is hidden the same way.
- Loading options: the `Combobox` shows its spinner and loading row; a rejected loader shows "Couldn't load the options." in the list.
- Repeat: an empty array shows the editor's empty text; the item fieldsets carry `data-testid` `__item`; Add is disabled at `maxItems` and Remove is hidden at `minItems`.
- Map: a duplicate key marks its row invalid at once and fails `validate()` on the map's path.
- Sections: `data-widget="section"`; a collapsed section opens when `validate()` focuses a field inside it.

## Accessibility

- Every control is wrapped in a `Field` (`role="group"`): `Field.Label` targets the control by id, the description and the message join `aria-describedby`, `required` and `invalid` set `aria-required` and `aria-invalid`.
- A nested object is a real `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, so its fields are announced with the group name.
- Messages are text under the control, never colour alone; the message replaces the description while it shows, as the design sample does.
- `validate()` moves focus to the first invalid control, in reading order, so keyboard and screen-reader users land on the problem.
- Keyboard map: no keys of its own; Tab moves through the controls in schema order (or `ui` order, then sections); each control keeps its own keys (the `Combobox` arrows and Enter, the `Accordion` trigger's Enter and Space).
- A repeat and a map are `<fieldset>`s named by the property title; each repeat item is a `role="group"` named "Item 2" (or the item schema's `title` and number), its Remove button is named "Remove item 2", and Add and Remove are announced by `AttributeEditor`'s live region, which also moves focus to the new row.
- A collapsed section is an `Accordion` trigger with `aria-expanded`; a closed section's fields are still validated, and `validate()` opens it before moving focus.
- A field that appears or disappears through `when` is not announced; keep the controlling field just before it so the change happens where the user is.
- A `field:<path>` slot control must name itself (the scope gives `invalid`, `required`, `disabled`); WebKit inputs read the Field context and need nothing.
- Visible focus, contrast and touch targets come from the composed controls.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SchemaForm from '@aziontech/webkit/schema-form'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const schema = {
    type: 'object',
    required: ['greeting', 'region'],
    properties: {
      greeting: {
        type: 'string',
        title: 'Greeting',
        description: 'The text the function returns on every request.',
        default: 'Hello from the edge',
        maxLength: 80
      },
      region: {
        type: 'string',
        title: 'Region',
        description: 'Where the function reads its data from.',
        enum: ['sa-east', 'us-east', 'eu-west']
      },
      timeout: {
        type: 'integer',
        title: 'Timeout (ms)',
        description: 'How long the function waits for its origin.',
        minimum: 100,
        maximum: 30000,
        default: 3000
      },
      debug: {
        type: 'boolean',
        title: 'Debug headers',
        description: 'Adds timing headers to every response.',
        default: false
      },
      allowedPaths: {
        type: 'array',
        title: 'Allowed paths',
        description: 'Requests to other paths return 404.',
        items: { type: 'string', pattern: '^/' }
      }
    }
  }

  const args = ref({ greeting: 'Hello from the edge', timeout: 3000, debug: false })
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-sm) flex-col gap-(--spacing-lg)">
    <SchemaForm
      v-model="args"
      :schema="schema"
    />
    <pre
      class="m-0 overflow-auto rounded-(--shape-control) bg-(--bg-surface) p-(--spacing-sm) font-code text-body-xs text-(--text-muted)"
      >{{ JSON.stringify(args, null, 2) }}</pre>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Select

> Select control for choosing exactly one option from a list; several values are `multi-select`. The trigger field mirrors `Input`'s visual API (size, hover/focus/filled/disabled/invalid/required states) so a Select sits next to a TextInput without visual drift. The dropdown panel is teleported to `body` and anchored to the trigger by the shared `usePlacement` composable — no `@floating-ui` runtime. A selected option shows a trailing check (`az az-check`) (the shadcn pattern), optionally a leading slot/icon and a trailing tag. The trigger shows the selected option's label (each option records its text, as Radix `SelectValue` does), not its raw value. Search and "Create new" footer are exposed as slots on `<SelectContent>`. Aligned with Figma frames `3714:10801` (trigger states) and `3899:29361` (options panel).

- Import: `import SelectRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/select-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Select from '@aziontech/webkit/select'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Select to pick exactly one value from a list of more than about seven options. For several values use MultiSelect; when the person may type a value that is not in the list use Combobox; for two to seven options shown at once use RadioGroup.
- One value from a list too long to show inline (regions, runtimes, plans).
- Options grouped under headings, with icons or trailing tags.
- A list that needs a search box or a "Create new" action inside the panel.

## Do

- Render `Select.Trigger` and `Select.Content` inside the root; the parts read the root's context and throw outside it.
- Give each `Select.Item` a stable `value`; pass `displayValue` to control how the trigger renders the selection.
- Type an options list as `SelectOptionItem<string>[]` and render it with `v-for` into `Select.Item` (`:value`, `:icon`, `:disabled`, the `label` as the slot); bind a typed model so `displayValue` and `update:modelValue` take that type with no cast.
- Use `readonly` to show a fixed selection and `disabled` when the field is unavailable; neither opens the panel.
- A switcher inside a line of text, such as the environment that ends a resource's breadcrumb (`Workloads › workload_01 › Production ⌄`), is `variant="ghost"` with `size="small"` and an `aria-label` on `Select.Trigger`: no border or fill until hover, sized to its value. Never put a bordered field in the header, and never restyle the trigger with `!` overrides.
- Keep `variant="ghost"` out of forms: it draws no border, so it cannot show the `invalid` or `required` border; a form field is the default `outline` inside a `Field`.

## Don’t

- A select with a visible label and helper/error text in a form → put it inside a `field`; the trigger picks up the field's id, description and state.
- The field is always multi-pick → use `multi-select`.
- Two to seven options that fit on screen → use `radio-group` (`variant="card"` for cards).
- The list triggers actions or navigation instead of holding a value → use `dropdown-menu`.

## Related

- `field` — label, this select, and description/error, with the wiring done.
- `multi-select` — multi-only variant with checkbox rows and an array model.
- `dropdown-menu` — action menu that reports the chosen option as an event and holds no form value.
- `input-group` — joins a select to an input, such as currency plus amount.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Trigger placeholder shown when no option is selected. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects trigger height (small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px) matching `Input`. |
| `variant` | `'outline' \| 'ghost'` | `'outline'` | false | Trigger look: `outline` is the bordered field; `ghost` has no border or fill until hover, sized to its value, for a switcher inside a line of text such as the environment at the end of a breadcrumb. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger and prevents opening; applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only; the current selection is visible but the dropdown cannot open. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; applies the required (warning) border and sets `aria-required` on the trigger, matching `Input`. The label's Required tag is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid` on the trigger. |
| `displayValue` | `(value: TValue) => string` | `undefined` | false | Custom formatter used by the trigger to render the selection; receives the current `modelValue`, typed as the bound model. Unset, the trigger shows the selected options' labels. |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | false | Form field name. Set, the root renders one hidden input per selected value (`String(value)`, objects as JSON) so a native `form` and `FormData` submit the selection; `required` then adds a hidden required proxy that blocks an empty submit, and `disabled` leaves the value out, as a native control does. |
| `modelValue` | `TValue` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Composition slot; receives `<SelectTrigger>` and `<SelectContent>` (and the option tree inside it). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/select-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/select-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/select-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/select-item`

## Sub-components

- `select-trigger/select-trigger.vue` — Bordered trigger field with an optional `#leading` slot (typed with `defineSlots`), selected-value label, and chevron-down.
- `select-content/select-content.vue` — Popover panel teleported to `body` and anchored with `usePlacement`; exposes `default` (the options), `#search` and `#footer` slots, typed with `defineSlots`, and scrolls its opti…
- `select-group/select-group.vue` — Section wrapper for a labelled group of options; renders a `text-label-sm` heading in `--text-muted` when `label` is set.
- `select-item/select-item.vue` — Selectable option row with a trailing check when selected, an optional `icon` (an Azion icon class, default `''`), an optional leading `#leading` slot, the option label, and an optional…
- `select-group/select-group.vue` `label` defaults to `''` (no heading, no `aria-label`).

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `TValue` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | The selection via `defineModel`: the one picked value. Its type flows to `displayValue` and `update:modelValue`. Fires when an option is selected. Uncontrolled when unbound. |

**Empty value.** `undefined` and `null` mean no selection: the trigger shows the placeholder. `''` is a selection when an option has `value=""` (an `Auto` or `Any` choice): the trigger shows that option's label (or `displayValue('')`), `data-filled` is set and a named field submits `''`. With no such option, `''` means no selection, so a model seeded with `ref('')` still shows the placeholder.
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state of the dropdown via `defineModel`. Fires when the dropdown opens or closes. Unbound, the dropdown keeps its own state, seeded by `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `required`, `opened`
- `data-state` on the root and trigger: `open` | `closed`
- `data-size` on the trigger mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-variant` on the root, the trigger and the panel mirrors `variant` (`outline` | `ghost`)
- `variant="ghost"`: the trigger and root size to the value (`w-auto`, capped at the container), no border, no fill, `--spacing-xs` inline padding, `.text-label-md` like a breadcrumb crumb, `--bg-mask` on hover and while open; the panel stops matching the trigger's width and takes at least `--container-3xs`
- `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-required`, `data-readonly`, `data-filled` mirror the matching props (or the selection state for `data-filled`)
- `data-selected` on `<SelectItem>` when the option's value is part of the current selection
- Long lists: above 300 options the list mounts in chunks of 100 as they scroll near view (unmounted chunks keep their height, 32 px per option), so opening a 1,000-option list stays within its runtime budget. The first arrow, `Home` or `End` key in the list mounts every option before moving focus, so keyboard navigation always reaches every option.
- `data-side` (`bottom` | `top`) and `data-align` (`start`) on the listbox panel mirror where it landed after flipping; `start` follows the text direction, so under `rtl` the panel lines up with the field's right edge

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on trigger and on every option row.
- Keyboard map (trigger): `Tab` focuses; `Space`/`Enter`/`ArrowDown` opens the panel; `Escape` closes it.
- Keyboard map (closed trigger): `Enter`, `Space`, `ArrowDown` and `ArrowUp` open the list (focus lands as described below); `Home` opens it on the first enabled option and `End` on the last; typing a printable character opens it on the first enabled option whose label starts with that character (with a search field, focus goes to the search field instead). Clicking the trigger while the list is open closes it. Tests: `select.test.ts` › Select keyboard and naming (APG select-only combobox).
- Keyboard map (open panel): opening focuses the search field when there is one, else the selected option, else the first enabled option; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the active option and wrap; `Home`/`End` jump to first/last; `Enter`/`Space` select, close and return focus to the trigger; typing a printable character moves focus to the next enabled option whose label starts with the typed text (characters typed within 500 ms add up; ignored while the search field has focus); `Escape` closes and returns focus to the trigger; `Tab` closes and moves focus to the control after the trigger; `Shift+Tab` closes and returns focus to the trigger. Tests: `select.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: trigger uses `role="combobox"` with `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded` bound to open state, `aria-controls` pointing to the list. The teleported content is a plain panel holding the optional search field, the list and the optional footer; the list (not the panel) carries `role="listbox"`, so the search field sits outside it, and is named by the root's `aria-label`, else by the root's `aria-labelledby`, else by the enclosing `Field` label, else by the trigger (which always has an `id`). The list uses `role="listbox"` (single-select, no `aria-multiselectable`). Each option uses `role="option"` with `aria-selected` mirroring its selection. Decorative icons (`az az-chevron-down`, `az-heart`, etc.) are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Nested overlays: the open list joins the shared overlay layer stack (`useOverlayLayer`), so inside a `Popover`, `Dialog` or `Drawer` an option click or `Escape` in the list closes only the list; the host overlay stays open.
- `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` on the trigger mirror the matching props.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons + borders), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:animate-none` on every transition/animation-bearing class.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on `size="large"`; smaller sizes are documented as dense-layout-only (consistent with `Input`).
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="listbox"` content binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Select from '@aziontech/webkit/select'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref('')
  const options = [
    { value: 'opt-1', label: 'Option 1' },
    { value: 'opt-2', label: 'Option 2' },
    { value: 'opt-3', label: 'Option 3' },
    { value: 'opt-4', label: 'Option 4' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    aria-label="Option"
    v-model="value"
    size="large"
    placeholder="Select an option"
  >
    <Select.Trigger />
    <Select.Content>
      <Select.Item
        v-for="o in options"
        :key="o.value"
        :value="o.value"
        >{{ o.label }}</Select.Item
      >
    </Select.Content>
  </Select>
</template>
```
