# Slider

> Bare range control `Slider`: one thumb on a horizontal track that picks a single number between `min` and `max` in `step` increments, with the portion from `min` to the value filled. It is built on a native `<input type="range">`, so the keyboard model, the `slider` role and the value announcements come from the platform; the component only styles the track, fill and thumb with tokens and adds optional tick marks and labelled reference values under the track. It renders no label, value readout or helper text — a field composes it with `Field.Label` and `Field.Description`, the same way `switch` and `number-input` are composed.

- Import: `import Slider from '@aziontech/webkit/slider'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Picking an approximate value inside a known, bounded range where the position matters more than the exact digit (a spend or usage limit, a percentage threshold, a sampling rate).
- A plan or capacity selector whose stops are evenly spaced and few enough to read as tick marks.
- A bounded value the user adjusts by feel and then commits (listen to `change` to persist on release instead of on every drag frame).

## Do

- Always give the slider an accessible name: `aria-label`, or a `Field.Label` whose `for` matches the slider's `id`.
- Keep the value inside `[min, max]` and on a `step` multiple; the component clamps the displayed fill but never rewrites the bound value on its own.
- Turn on `ticks` only when every step is meaningful and the range has at most 21 positions; above that the ticks are not rendered.
- Use `referenceValues` for a few landmarks (`[0, 50, 100]`), not for every step — labels need horizontal room.
- Set `unit` when the number alone is ambiguous; it is appended verbatim to the reference labels and to the announced value, so include a leading space for word units (`' GB'`) and none for symbols (`'%'`).
- Listen to `change` for expensive side effects (saving a limit to the API); `v-model` updates on every movement.
- Use `readonly` to show a value the current user may not change but should still be able to focus and hear; use `disabled` when the control does not apply at all.

## Don’t

- The user must type an exact number, or the range is unbounded → use `number-input`.
- The choice is between a handful of named options (1h / 24h / 7d) → use `toggle-group`.
- An on/off setting → use `switch`.
- Showing progress or a read-only quantity the user cannot change → use `progress`.
- Selecting a range with two thumbs (from–to) — not supported by this component.

## Related

- `number-input` — exact numeric entry; pair it next to a slider when the user needs both coarse dragging and an exact value.
- `field` — `Field.Label` names the slider; point its `for` at the slider's `id` (the `id` attribute lands on the native input).
- `field-error` — description or error message under the slider in a field layout.
- `toggle-group` — a few discrete, named choices instead of a continuous range.
- `progress` — displays a fraction; it is not interactive.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | false | Lowest selectable value; the left end of the track. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | false | Highest selectable value; the right end of the track. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | false | Increment between selectable values, used by dragging and the arrow keys. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction, removes the control from the tab order and applies the disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Keeps the control focusable but prevents the value from changing. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the danger tokens and sets aria-invalid. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when no visible label is associated with the slider. |
| `ticks` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a tick mark at every step when the range has at most 21 positions. |
| `referenceValues` | `number[]` | `[]` | false | Values marked and labelled under the track; entries outside min and max are ignored. |
| `unit` | `string` | `''` | false | Text appended verbatim to the reference labels and to the announced value. |
| `modelValue` | `number` | `0` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `change` | `number` | Commit signal: emitted from the native `change` event — on pointer release after a drag, and after each keyboard step — with the committed value. Lets the consumer persist once per interaction instead of once per drag frame (`update:modelValue` fires continuously). A value event, so no DOM event in the payload (see `.claude/rules/event-payloads.md`). Not emitted while `disabled` or `readonly`. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `number` | `0` | `update:modelValue` | Current value via `defineModel<number>({ default: 0 })`. Emitted on every native `input` event (drag frame or key press) as `valueAsNumber`. Never emitted while `disabled` or `readonly`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active` (dragging), `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop; the native input is also `disabled`, so it leaves the tab order and ignores pointer and keys.
- `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop. A native range input ignores the HTML `readonly` attribute, so the component owns the behaviour: the input stays focusable, `aria-readonly="true"` is set, the navigation keys (arrows, `PageUp`/`PageDown`, `Home`/`End`) are prevented, pointer dragging is prevented, and any native `input` that still slips through writes the current model back to the element without emitting. Visual: fill and thumb border switch to the muted token and the cursor is `default`.
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop: the fill and the thumb border switch to the danger tokens; `aria-invalid="true"` is set on the input.
- Fill: the root sets the custom property `--slider-fill` (the clamped value as a percentage of `max - min`; `0%` when `max <= min`) through an inline `style` binding, the same way `tracker` and `chart` set their custom properties. The WebKit/Blink track paints the fill with a bracketed gradient (`[&::-webkit-slider-runnable-track]:bg-[linear-gradient(to_right,var(--accent)_var(--slider-fill),var(--bg-surface)_var(--slider-fill))]`); Firefox paints it natively with `[&::-moz-range-progress]:bg-(--accent)`. Expression values and custom-property declarations stay in brackets per `.claude/rules/styling.md`.
- Track and thumb are styled only through arbitrary pseudo-element variants on the native input (`appearance-none`, `[&::-webkit-slider-runnable-track]:…`, `[&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:appearance-none …`, `[&::-moz-range-track]:…`, `[&::-moz-range-thumb]:…`) — no extra track/thumb elements, no `<style>` block.
- Geometry: the native input is 40 px tall (`h-10`, the hit area) and full width; the track is 4 px tall and centred; the thumb is 16×16 px.
- Ticks (`ticks`) and reference marks (`referenceValues`) render in an `aria-hidden` row under the track. Each mark is positioned at the thumb-centre position for its value — `thumb/2 + (100% - thumb) × fraction` — so marks line up with the thumb at both ends; the fraction is passed per mark through an inline custom property. Every reference value also draws a tick. Reference labels read `{value}{unit}`; the first label is start-aligned, the last end-aligned, the rest centred on their mark.
- Attribute routing (as in `number-input`): consumer `class` merges onto the root wrapper; every other attribute (`id`, `name`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, …) is forwarded to the native input so a `Label for` and a `FieldDescription` association reach the focusable element. `data-testid` is read from attrs and applied to the root.
- `data-testid`: root fallback `slider`; native input `${testId}__input`; each reference label `${testId}__reference`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the ring is drawn on the thumb, not the 40 px input box — `focus-visible:outline-none` on the input plus `focus-visible:[&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:ring-2 focus-visible:[&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:[&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:[&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` and the same set for `[&::-moz-range-thumb]`.
- Keyboard map (native): `Tab` focuses; `ArrowRight`/`ArrowUp` +`step`; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowDown` −`step`; `PageUp`/`PageDown` move by a larger browser-defined increment; `Home` → `min`; `End` → `max`. Under `dir="rtl"` the track runs right to left, so `ArrowLeft` adds `step` and `ArrowRight` subtracts it (handled by the component through `useDirection`, so every browser agrees). When `readonly`, `Tab` still focuses and every value key is inert. When `disabled`, the control is skipped by `Tab`.
- ARIA: the native `<input type="range">` provides `role="slider"` and the implicit `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` / `aria-valuenow` from `min` / `max` / the value. `aria-label` comes from `ariaLabel` (omitted when empty, so an associated `Field.Label` wins). `aria-valuetext="{value}{unit}"` is set only when `unit` is non-empty. `aria-readonly="true"` when `readonly`; `aria-invalid="true"` when `invalid`. The ticks and reference-label row is `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast: thumb border and fill against the track ≥3:1 (non-text UI), reference labels ≥4.5:1, including the disabled state per the disabled tokens.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transitioned pseudo-element class.
- Touch target: the native input is 40 px tall and full width, so the whole track row is the hit area (≥40×40); the 16 px thumb is a visual, not the target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Slider from '@aziontech/webkit/slider'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref(40)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <Slider
      v-model="value"
      :min="0"
      :max="100"
      :step="1"
      aria-label="Alert threshold"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/slider.md](components/slider.md).

# Switch

> Control-only pill toggle `Switch` (36×20 px). Two visual types: `default` (plain handle) and `privacy` (handle carries a `az-lock` / `az-lock-open` icon mirroring the toggled state; both glyphs render and `group-data-[checked]:` shows the right one, so no class is chosen in script). No label or description — wrap it in a horizontal `Field` or a `Field.Label` choice card for labeled layouts, or place it bare where the label already exists outside the control (an ItemGroup row names the field with `Item.Title`). Because the bare form has no wrapper to defer to, the control owns its own `disabled` state.

- Import: `import Switch from '@aziontech/webkit/switch'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Switch for any on/off setting that applies at once — the answer for 'toggle'. For an on/off choice submitted with a form use Checkbox; to switch a view or mode in place use ToggleGroup.
- An on/off setting that takes effect as soon as it flips (enable a feature, turn a rule on).
- A row that already names the setting outside the control, such as an `item` row whose title is the label.
- A visibility or access toggle: `variant="privacy"` shows a closed lock when off and an open lock when on.

## Do

- The switch renders no text: give it an accessible name with `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at the visible label.
- Set `disabled` on the switch itself; it renders a native disabled button, so it leaves the tab order and ignores clicks and keys.
- Use `autofocus` to focus the switch when it mounts (a dialog whose first control it is).
- Keep `variant="default"` unless the setting is about visibility or access.

## Don’t

- The toggle needs its own label, description, or helper text in a form → wrap it in a horizontal `field` (`Field orientation="horizontal"` + `Field.Content`).
- The toggle should sit in a bordered card with a description → use a `field` choice card (`Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field`).
- A text value that only applies while a feature is on → compose a `Field` with an `InputGroup` (`InputGroup.Input` + an `InputGroup.Addon` holding the switch).
- The choice is submitted with a form instead of applied immediately → use `checkbox`.

## Related

- `field` — a horizontal `Field` gives the switch its label and description; a `Field.Label` wrapping it is a card-style option.
- `input-group` — a text input with a trailing switch addon that enables it, inside a `Field`.
- `checkbox` — boolean selection submitted with a form.
- `item` — list row whose title names a bare switch.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'privacy'` | `'default'` | false | Visual variant (`SwitchVariant`). `privacy` renders a lock icon inside the handle (closed when off, open when on). |
| `autofocus` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Moves focus to the switch once, when it mounts. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies the disabled tokens. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the control invalid: sets `aria-invalid` and the danger border (unchecked). An enclosing `Field`'s `invalid` sets it too. |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | false | Form field name. Set, a hidden input inside the button submits `on` under this name while the switch is on and nothing while it is off, as a native checkbox does; `disabled` leaves it out. |
| `modelValue` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:modelValue` | Toggled-on state via `defineModel`. Mirrors the Figma checked/on variant. Emitted when the user toggles the switch. Uncontrolled when unbound. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `checked`, `disabled`
- `data-checked` mirrors the `modelValue` prop (toggled-on state)
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop (`default` | `privacy`)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop; the root is also natively `<button disabled>`, so it leaves the tab order and neither click nor `Space`/`Enter` emits `update:modelValue`. The disabled treatment is the `--bg-disabled` track + `--text-disabled` handle + `cursor-not-allowed` — token surfaces, never an opacity wash. It wins over the checked tokens, so a disabled switch reads locked in both the off and on positions.
- `data-invalid` mirrors `invalid` (own prop or the enclosing `Field`); with `aria-invalid` on the control, it paints the danger border while unchecked
- Hover applies an inset `var(--bg-hover)` overlay on both off and on tracks; disabled suppresses that overlay (`data-[disabled]:hover:shadow-none`) while keeping the element hit-testable so `cursor-not-allowed` is what the pointer shows
- Touch: an invisible `::after` extends the hit area of the 36 × 20 px track to 24 px tall, and to 44 × 44 px on a coarse pointer.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Space` / `Enter` toggles. When `disabled`, the native `<button disabled>` root is skipped by `Tab` and both keys are inert.
- ARIA: `role="switch"` on the root; `aria-checked` mirrors `data-checked`; `aria-disabled` mirrors `data-disabled`. The lock icon in `variant="privacy"` is decorative — `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target: the control itself is 36×20 — the consumer is responsible for placing it inside a ≥40×40 hit area (typically a horizontal `Field`, whose label extends the target). The component still exposes a clickable root.
- Forced colors: the track border is `CanvasText` (`Highlight` when checked) and the handle opts out of forced colour adjustment (`forced-color-adjust: none`) to paint `CanvasText`, `Highlight` when checked and `GrayText` when disabled; without it the handle's background is forced to `Canvas` and disappears into the track. Tests: `src/test/forced-colors.test.ts`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Switch from '@aziontech/webkit/switch'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const modelValue = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <Switch
    v-model="modelValue"
    aria-label="Toggle setting"
  />
</template>
```

# Tag Editor

> Key and value tags of one resource, after Cloudscape's tag editor, built on `AttributeEditor`. It adds what tags need on top of the rows: key and value suggestions while typing, a tag limit (50 by default) that ignores tags marked for removal, the built-in key checks (required when the row has a value, unique, length, allowed characters, no key starting with a `reservedPrefix` the product reserves), and a removal that only marks a saved tag, with Undo, until the form is saved.

- Import: `import TagEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/tag-editor'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use TagEditor when the person adds, edits or removes key/value tags (labels) on a resource; it enforces tag limits and reserved prefixes. For a short list of same-field rows inside a form (environment variables, headers) use AttributeEditor; to edit many cells of many records in place use DataGrid.
- The Tags section of a create or settings form of any resource.
- Labels used for cost allocation, ownership or search, where keys repeat across resources and suggestions help keep them consistent.

## Do

- Mark saved tags with `existing: true`: their key is read-only, and Remove marks them `markedForRemoval` (Undo puts them back) so the save request knows what to delete.
- Call the exposed `validate()` on Save; it also flags empty keys, which are not flagged while typing.
- Feed `keySuggestions` with the keys already used in the account so tags stay consistent.
- Pass server errors per row through `errors`; they replace the built-in message of that cell.
- Keep the default `limit` unless the backend has another one.

## Don’t

- Environment variables, headers or any pairs without tag rules → use `attribute-editor`.
- Showing tags read-only → use `tag` (or `key-value-list`).
- Picking from a fixed list of labels → use `multi-select`.

## Related

- `attribute-editor` — the rows, Add, Remove, limit text, focus and announcements underneath.
- `input` — key and value controls; suggestions come from a native `datalist`.
- `tag` — how the saved tags read outside the editor.
- `state/form-validation` (SectionRejected) — the rule for server errors passed through `errors`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keySuggestions` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Keys offered while typing a key, for example the keys already used in the account. |
| `valueSuggestions` | `Record<string, string[]>` | `{}` | false | Values offered per key while typing a value. |
| `limit` | `number` | `50` | false | Most tags allowed; tags marked for removal do not count. |
| `keyMaxLength` | `number` | `128` | false | Longest key allowed, in characters. |
| `valueMaxLength` | `number` | `256` | false | Longest value allowed, in characters. |
| `reservedPrefix` | `string` | `''` | false | Prefix reserved for the platform (for example `acme:`); keys may not start with it. Empty allows every prefix. |
| `errors` | `TagEditorErrors` | `[]` | false | Server errors per row, aligned with `tags`; shown in place of the built-in checks. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every control. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of tags. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `tags` | `TagEditorTag[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:tags`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:tags` | `TagEditorTag[]` | `[]` | `update:tags` | Tags being edited, via `defineModel('tags')`. Saved tags carry `existing`; Remove marks them `markedForRemoval` until Undo. Unbound, the editor keeps its own tags. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `empty`, `at limit` (Add disabled), `invalid` (per cell), `marked for removal` (controls disabled, a muted note, Undo), `disabled`
- Saved tags (`existing`) render the key read-only.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every control keeps its own ring.
- Keyboard map: as `attribute-editor`; suggestions open with the browser's native `datalist` keys (ArrowDown, Enter, Escape).
- ARIA: rows, labels, errors and announcements come from `attribute-editor`; Undo is named "Undo removal of tag n"; a marked tag keeps a visible note ("This tag will be removed when you save.").
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.
- Touch target: Remove and Undo are 32 px buttons (`medium`).
- Inside a `Field`: the root is a `role="group"` that reads the field through `useFieldControl` — `id` from the field, `aria-labelledby` from `Field.Title`, `aria-describedby` from `Field.Description` / `Field.Error`, `aria-invalid` + `data-invalid` from the field's `invalid`, and the field's `disabled` disables every row. Each cell keeps its own inner field from `attribute-editor`, so the row inputs never take the outer field's id.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import TagEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/tag-editor'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const tags = ref([
    { key: 'team', value: 'payments', existing: true },
    { key: 'cost-center', value: 'cc-1042', existing: true },
    { key: 'environment', value: 'staging' }
  ])

  const keySuggestions = ['team', 'cost-center', 'environment', 'owner', 'project']
  const valueSuggestions = { environment: ['production', 'staging', 'preview'] }
</script>

<template>
  <TagEditor
    v-model:tags="tags"
    :key-suggestions="keySuggestions"
    :value-suggestions="valueSuggestions"
    aria-label="Resource tags"
  />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/tag-editor.md](components/tag-editor.md).

# Textarea

> Collects multi-line free-form text from the user. Sibling of `input` in the `input` category; renders a fixed-size (`large`) multi-line field with a minimum height of 80px. The resize axis is controlled by the `resize` prop (defaults to `vertical`). With `autoResize` the field instead grows with its content between `minRows` and `maxRows` lines. Native textarea attributes (`rows`, `maxlength`, `name`, etc.) flow through via attribute fallthrough.

- Import: `import Textarea from '@aziontech/webkit/textarea'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Capture multiple lines of free-form text (descriptions, comments, messages).

## Do

- Give it a sensible default size; avoid auto-growing beyond the viewport.
- Set `autoResize` on a field whose length varies a lot (a prompt, a comment, a commit message): it starts at `minRows` lines and grows as the person types. Always set `maxRows` with it, so a long paste scrolls inside the field instead of pushing the page down.
- `autoResize` turns the drag handle off; pick one or the other, never both.
- Wrap it in a `Field` for the label, description and error.
- Set `monospace` on a value that is code: a pasted zone file, a certificate, a JSON or YAML snippet, a list of IPs. Pair it with `:spellcheck="false"`. Prose (a description, a message) stays in the sans face.
- A value people edit as code with highlighting and line numbers belongs in `CodeEditor`; `monospace` is for a plain paste box.
- Do not restyle a read-only textarea (dashed border, transparent fill): it is the same filled field, made non-editable; the reason belongs in the field's description.

## Don’t

- The value is a single line → use `input`.
- The value is strictly numeric → use `number-input`.

## Related

- `input` — single-line sibling with the same field API.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder shown when the field is empty. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only: the value is visible, focusable and copyable but not editable. Keeps the filled field (surface and solid border) with no hover border and a default cursor (`data-readonly`), the same look as `Input`; distinct from the disabled field. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies invalid styling and sets `aria-invalid`. Combined with `required`, switches to warning border tone. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required and sets `aria-required`. |
| `resize` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both' \| 'none'` | `'vertical'` | false | Which axes the user can drag to resize the field, named after the CSS `resize` property (`TextareaResize`, exported). `none` locks the size; `vertical` keeps the default behavior. |
| `monospace` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Sets the value and placeholder in the monospace code face (`.text-body-code-sm`, which wraps) for pasted zone files, certificates, JSON and lists of IPs (`data-monospace`). Same prop as on `Input`. |
| `autoResize` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Grows the field with its content instead of a fixed height (`data-auto-resize`): CSS `field-sizing: content`, with a measured height where the browser lacks it. Turns the drag handle off. |
| `minRows` | `number` | `1` | false | Lines the field shows when empty while `autoResize` is on. Ignored without `autoResize`. |
| `maxRows` | `number` | `0` | false | Lines the field grows to before it scrolls while `autoResize` is on (`data-max-rows`); `0` sets no limit. Ignored without `autoResize`. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The field value via `defineModel`; updates on every native `input` event. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus`, `filled`, `disabled`, `required` (warning border), `invalid` (danger border), `readonly`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop
- `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop: a read-only textarea keeps the editable field's fill (`var(--bg-surface)`) and solid `var(--border-default)` border, as `Input` does and the design sample draws it; it only drops the hover border and takes a default cursor. The value keeps `var(--text-default)` and the textarea stays focusable. Why the value cannot change is said by the field's description, not by a different chrome.
- `data-monospace` mirrors the `monospace` prop: the value and the placeholder render in `.text-body-code-sm` instead of `.text-body-xs`.
- `data-filled` mirrors whether `modelValue` is non-empty
- `data-resize` on the native `<textarea>` mirrors the `resize` prop and drives the `resize-*` Tailwind variant; with `autoResize` it is `none`, since the content sets the height
- `data-auto-resize` mirrors the `autoResize` prop: the field takes `field-sizing: content` and a minimum height of `minRows` lines (`--textarea-min-rows`) in place of the fixed 80 px; in a browser without `field-sizing` the component sets the height from `scrollHeight` on mount and on every value change
- `data-max-rows` is set to `maxRows` when `autoResize` is on and `maxRows` is above 0: the field stops growing at that many lines (`--textarea-max-rows`) and scrolls its content

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: on `:focus`, a `ring-2` shadow in `var(--ring-color)` plus a `ring-offset-2` in `var(--bg-canvas)` render around the field; the color transition respects `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; typing inserts text; `Enter` inserts a newline; `Shift+Tab` moves focus to the previous element.
- Direction: the `<textarea>` renders `dir="auto"` so a value typed in another script keeps its own direction inside right-to-left UI; a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: root is a native `<textarea>`; `aria-invalid` mirrors `invalid`; `aria-required` mirrors `required`; `aria-disabled` mirrors `disabled` when applicable.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (border + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated state transitions.
- Touch target: field min-height ≥80px ensures adequate hit area; with `autoResize` and `minRows: 1` the field is one line plus padding (≥ 32 px), above the 24 px minimum.
- `autoResize` changes only the height: the field keeps its native role, and a capped field scrolls with the keyboard like any textarea.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Textarea from '@aziontech/webkit/textarea'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <Textarea
    v-model="value"
    placeholder="Write your message"
  />
</template>
```

# Theme Switcher

> A compact pill-shaped segmented control that lets the user pick the app color-theme mode — `system`, `dark`, or `light` — via three icon-only segments. It reflects and emits the selected mode through `v-model` and applies no global side effect itself (the app decides what each mode means). Unlike `switch` (a boolean toggle) or `tabs` (view navigation), it is a fixed three-way single-select over the theme modes.

- Import: `import ThemeSwitcher from '@aziontech/webkit/theme-switcher'`
- Category: input · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use ThemeSwitcher only for the system / light / dark choice in app chrome; for any other segmented choice use ToggleGroup, and for a choice in a form use RadioGroup.
- The app-wide color mode picker in a header, footer, account menu or settings page.

## Do

- Bind with `v-model` and apply the mode in the app (for example a `data-theme` attribute, resolving `system` from `prefers-color-scheme`); the component has no side effects.
- Persist the chosen mode on the app side so it survives a reload.
- Localize `ariaLabel`; the segment names (System, Dark, Light) are fixed in the component.

## Don’t

- A general on/off preference → use `switch`.
- Picking one of other mutually exclusive options → use `toggle-group`.
- Moving between views or panels → use `tabs`.

## Related

- `toggle-group` — the generic mutually exclusive option group, with labels and sizes.
- `switch` — boolean toggle for a single setting.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the whole control and applies disabled tokens. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the icon-only segmented group. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Theme`). |
| `modelValue` | `ThemeSwitcherValue` | `'system'` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `'system' \| 'dark' \| 'light'` | `'system'` | `update:modelValue` | Selected theme mode via `defineModel`. Emits when the user selects a different mode; the component applies no side effect itself. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on the root
- Selected segment carries `aria-checked="true"` and `data-state="active"`; unselected segments `aria-checked="false"` and `data-state="inactive"`
- A single `aria-hidden` indicator element renders the selection highlight (`var(--bg-selected)`) and slides to the active segment (position measured from the active segment's box); segments themselves stay transparent

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the focused segment.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves focus into the group (roving tabindex lands on the selected segment); `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` (and `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`) move selection between segments; `Space`/`Enter` selects the focused segment.
- ARIA: root is `role="radiogroup"` with `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`; each segment is `role="radio"` with `aria-checked` and its own `aria-label` (`System` / `Dark` / `Light`); the glyph is `aria-hidden`. `aria-disabled` mirrors `disabled`.
- Each segment is wrapped in `@aziontech/webkit/tooltip` (`side="bottom"`) surfacing its mode label (`System` / `Dark` / `Light`) on hover and keyboard focus; the tooltip owns its own `aria-describedby` wiring.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states.
- Touch target: segments follow the compact Figma sizing (28px pill height, 28×20px segments) and are below the 40×40 px target; justified deviation for a dense global control, consistent with the design.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ThemeSwitcher from '@aziontech/webkit/theme-switcher'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const theme = ref('system')
</script>

<template>
  <ThemeSwitcher v-model="theme" />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/theme-switcher.md](components/theme-switcher.md).

<!-- components/app-header.md -->

# App Header

> Application chrome for the top menubar: a fixed-height horizontal bar with three composable regions (start, center, end) and a dedicated brand slot for Azion logo variants. Matches the Webkit AppHeader (Figma node 4310:19617) — a Shell Core part with symmetric horizontal padding, a hairline bottom border, the menu trigger and brand grouped at the start, a growing nav region in the center, and trailing actions (Create, Copilot, Feedback, help, avatar) at the end. Consumers reorder or omit regions; logo and actions are not baked in. The bar has two placements, chosen with `variant`, and the only difference is where the inset is measured from. `content` is the default and the one every app shell wants: the bar runs full bleed across whatever zone holds it — a content zone beside a rail, or the whole window when nothing sits beside it — insetting its regions by the page boundary (`--layout-boundary-inline`) so the first region opens on the same vertical as the page content. It reads the token the page reads, so retuning the boundary moves both. A third placement, `app`, was removed in favour of that default. It insetted by a flat `--spacing-md` (16 at every width) on the theory that window-wide chrome above a navigation rail has no page column to answer to. Every shell that was placed deliberately chose `content` instead — including the bars that do span the whole window with no zone beside them — because a flat 16 disagrees with the page's 16-then-24 boundary at exactly the widths where nothing sits between the bar and the page, putting the brand on a different vertical from the title under it. Nothing selected `app` on purpose; the only bars on it had inherited it as the default. `site` is the marketing placement, for a page that is a FRAMED column rather than an app zone: the surface stays full bleed (the hairline and the fill run to the window edges, because a bar is chrome) while the regions are capped and centred, so the bar answers to the page under it at every width. It is one declaration, not a sub-component: `padding-inline: max(boundary, (100% - measure) / 2 + boundary)` — the cap and the boundary hand off to each other, so below the measure the boundary is the whole inset and the placement collapses to `content`. An uncapped bar over a capped page comes apart above the measure: the column stops growing and the bar does not, which on a 2560px window put the logo 684px to the left of the headline under it. The cap is the bar's OWN measure — `--layout-measure-site-header` (1620px), one rung wider than the page frame (`--layout-measure-site`, 1388px) that the hero, the sections and the footer share. A bar carries the brand at one end of the window and the account actions at the other, held apart by a navigation region in the middle: it wants the room a reading frame refuses, and held to the page's measure that middle region ran out of room on a laptop long before the page did. The two share one inset up to 1280 and part company only above the caps, by a fixed 92px from 1668 — half the 232px between the measures, less the boundary the bar keeps. It is the one band deliberately outside the frame, and the separate token is what keeps that exception reviewable in both directions.

- Import: `import AppHeaderRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/app-header-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import AppHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/app-header'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use AppHeader for the console's top bar; inside ConsoleLayout it is already rendered.
- The top bar of a console-style app: menu trigger and brand at the start, an optional nav or breadcrumb region, and trailing actions (create, help, account) at the end.
- A bar above a content zone that sits beside a navigation rail — `variant="content"` insets its regions by the page boundary so they line up with the page below.
- The bar of a framed marketing page — `variant="site"` keeps the surface full bleed but caps and centres the regions.

## Do

- Keep the default `variant="content"` for app shells; use `variant="site"` only on framed marketing pages.
- Group the menu trigger and the brand in `AppHeader.Container` so they stay together and never shrink.
- Make the logo the home link with `href` on `AppHeader.Brand` (`<AppHeader.Brand href="/" aria-label="Azion home">`) instead of wrapping it in a hand-made anchor: the brand owns the focus ring, the hover affordance and the hit area. Empty `aria-label` names the link from the locale catalog (`Azion home`).
- Set `aria-label` on the root (default `'Global header'`) when the page has more than one banner-style bar.
- Keep the regions free of layout overrides — the bar owns height, padding and the bottom hairline; put only controls in each region.
- Every header that navigates (console, demo, docs, site) carries `SearchTrigger` first in `AppHeader.End`, wired to a `Command` palette; wrap the header in an `@container` so it unfolds into the `Search … ⌘K` field. Never hand-roll the field or use a bare magnifier `IconButton` (lint `webkit/require-header-search`).

## Don’t

- The marketing site's complete navigation bar with mega-menus and a mobile sheet → use `site-header-section`, which composes this header.
- The navigation column at the side of the app → use `sidebar`.
- An action row above a list of records → use the `toolbar` slot of `table`.

## Related

- `site-header-section` — the marketing navigation band built on `app-header`, `brand` and `navigation-menu`.
- `navigation-menu` — the dropdown navigation that usually goes in `AppHeader.Center`.
- `brand` — the Azion lockup to place inside `AppHeader.Brand`.
- `console-layout` — the console layout template that composes the header with the sidebar and the page.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the header landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Global header`). |
| `variant` | `'content' \| 'site'` | `'content'` | false | Where the bar sits: `content` is the default — full bleed across whatever zone holds it, insetting its regions by the page boundary so the first region opens on the same vertical as the page content under or beside it; `site` keeps that full-bleed surface on a framed marketing page but caps the regions at the site header measure and centres them, so they land on the bar's own column, one rung wider than the page frame under it. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Root: compose `Container` (or `Start` + `Brand`), `Center`, and `End` sub-components. |
| `default` | — | Each sub-component (incl. `Container`) exposes `default` for region content. |
| `default` | — | `app-header-brand` exposes `default` for logo markup. |

## Sub-components

- `app-header-container.vue` — Start cluster wrapper; groups the menu trigger (`Start`) and `Brand` into one `shrink-0` flex unit, mirroring the Figma `Container` region.
- `app-header-start.vue` — `AppHeader.Start`.
- `app-header-center.vue` — `AppHeader.Center`.
- `app-header-end.vue` — `AppHeader.End`.

The regions are named start / center / end, not left / right, because the bar mirrors under
right-to-left: the start region is on the right there. 6.0 removed the physical names (`Left`,
`Middle`, `Nav`, `Right`). The parts derive `__start`, `__center` and `__end` testids from the root.

- `app-header-brand.vue` — `AppHeader.Brand`.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Placement: `data-variant="content" | "site"` on the root (from `variant`).
- No interactive states on the shell; children own focus/hover/disabled.
- `AppHeader.Brand` with `href`: `data-link` on its anchor; hover (opacity) and `focus-visible` (ring) are its only states.

## Accessibility

- Root renders as `<header role="banner">` with `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`.
- Keyboard map: none on the shell; interactive children supply Tab order.
- ARIA: landmark only on root. `AppHeader.Brand` with `href` is a native anchor named by `ariaLabel` (locale fallback `appHeader.home`), so the logo link always has an accessible name; without `href` it stays a non-interactive `div`.
- Keyboard (brand link): Tab reaches it, Enter follows it; the `focus-visible` ring uses `--ring-color`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for text and icons in slotted content.
- `motion-reduce:*` on any animated slotted controls (owned by children).
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on slotted buttons (owned by children).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import AppHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/app-header'
  import Default from '@aziontech/webkit/svg/azion/default'
</script>

<template>
  <AppHeader aria-label="Global header">
    <AppHeader.Start>
      <AppHeader.Brand
        href="/"
        aria-label="Azion home"
      >
        <Default />
      </AppHeader.Brand>
    </AppHeader.Start>
    <AppHeader.Center />
    <AppHeader.End />
  </AppHeader>
</template>
```

# App Layout

> The frame every signed-in product page renders inside. It places named regions — navigation, header, notifications, breadcrumbs, content, tools (the help panel) and the split panel — and owns how they open, close, resize and remember their state. It responds to its **own** width, not the viewport's: below `compactBelow` pixels the navigation and the tools turn into drawers and the split panel moves to the bottom. The regions are slots, so the shell (the `shell/console` block) keeps its own `Sidebar`, `AppHeader` and page content and only hands the frame to `AppLayout`.

- Import: `import AppLayout from '@aziontech/webkit/app-layout'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use AppLayout only to build a signed-in app shell other than the console; the console uses ConsoleLayout.
- A product shell needs a navigation rail, a global header and a scrolling content area that turn into a drawer-based layout on phones.
- A page offers contextual help beside the work (`HelpPanel` in the tools region) that the reader opens and closes.
- A list or table needs a resizable detail panel under it or beside it (the split panel), showing the selected item without leaving the page.
- Page-level flash messages (`Alert`) must sit above the content and stay visible while the content scrolls.

## Do

- One `AppLayout` per page, at the root. Do not nest them.
- Keep the navigation in the `navigation` slot and read its `drawer` scope flag to drop rail-only controls (resize, collapse) when it renders inside the drawer; call `closeNavigation` from the scope when an item is chosen in the drawer.
- Put the control that opens the navigation drawer in the header, and show it only when the header scope's `compact` is true.
- Put a help button in the header that calls `toggleTools`; the tools region carries its own close button.
- Use the split panel for the selected item of a collection. Close it when the selection clears.
- Pass `storageKey` when the reader's choices (split panel size and position, navigation and tools open) should survive a reload.
- Flash notifications belong in the `notifications` slot, one `Alert` per message, dismissible. Use toasts for results of actions that finish in the background.
- A page body that fills the screen (an empty state, a centred form) is `<main class="flex min-h-full flex-col">` in the default slot. Its height is what is left under the breadcrumbs, so it never scrolls by the breadcrumb row; do not subtract the breadcrumbs yourself.

## Don’t

- A single resizable split inside a page, with no shell around it → use `resizable`.
- A navigation rail on its own (resize, collapse, footer) → use `sidebar`; put it in the `navigation` slot.
- A one-off overlay for a task (a create form, a detail preview) → use `drawer`.
- Marketing and documentation pages → use the `shell/site` and `shell/docs` blocks.

## Related

- `sidebar` — the navigation rail that goes in the `navigation` slot; it owns its own width, resize and collapse.
- `app-header` — the bar that goes in the `header` slot.
- `help-panel` — the content of the tools region.
- `drawer` — what the navigation and tools regions become below `compactBelow`.
- `resizable` — a split between panes inside a page, without the shell.
- `alert` — the flash messages composed into the `notifications` slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `navigationAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the navigation drawer. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Navigation`). |
| `toolsLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the tools region, shown in its header. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Help`). |
| `toolsWidth` | `number` | `320` | false | Width of the tools region in pixels while not compact. |
| `splitPanelTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the split panel, shown in its header. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Details`). |
| `storageKey` | `string` | `''` | false | When set, the split panel size and position and the navigation and tools open state are kept in `localStorage` under it. |
| `compactBelow` | `number` | `768` | false | Width of the layout itself, in pixels, under which navigation and tools become drawers and the split panel moves down. |
| `navigationOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:navigationOpen`). |
| `toolsOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:toolsOpen`). |
| `splitPanelOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:splitPanelOpen`). |
| `splitPanelPosition` | `AppLayoutSplitPanelPosition` | `'bottom'` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:splitPanelPosition`). |
| `splitPanelSize` | `number` | `320` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:splitPanelSize`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The page content (the consumer's `<main>`). Fills the content region under the breadcrumbs, so a full-height body (`min-h-full`) takes the rest of the height without overflowing; taller content scrolls. |
| `navigation` | { drawer: boolean, closeNavigation: () => void } | The navigation rail. Rendered once: beside the content, or inside the navigation drawer when compact. `closeNavigation` closes the drawer, e.g. after an item is chosen. |
| `header` | { compact: boolean, openNavigation: () => void, toggleNavigation: () => void, toggleTools: () => void } | The global header, above content, tools and split panel. |
| `notifications` | — | Flash messages (`Alert`) above the breadcrumbs and the content; stays in place while content scrolls. |
| `breadcrumbs` | — | Breadcrumbs above the content, inside the scroll area; the page body fills the height left under them. |
| `tools` | — | The tools region's body, usually a `HelpPanel`. |
| `split-panel` | — | The split panel's body. |

## v-model

Each two-way value is a named `defineModel`, so its `update:*` event is generated, not hand-declared.
Unbound, each one keeps its own local state.

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:navigation-open` | `boolean` | `true` | `update:navigationOpen` | Whether the navigation region shows beside the content. Not used while compact, where navigation is a drawer. Same name on `ConsoleLayout`. |
| `v-model:tools-open` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:toolsOpen` | Whether the tools region (help) is open; while compact it drives the tools drawer. |
| `v-model:split-panel-open` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:splitPanelOpen` | Whether the split panel is open. |
| `v-model:split-panel-position` | `'bottom' \| 'side'` | `'bottom'` | `update:splitPanelPosition` | Where the split panel sits: under the content or beside it. Bottom while compact. |
| `v-model:split-panel-size` | `number` | `320` | `update:splitPanelSize` | Height (bottom) or width (side) of the split panel in pixels; emitted on every step. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `compact`; per region `open` / `closed`; the split separator `focus-visible` and `resizing`.
- `data-compact` on the root while the layout is narrower than `compactBelow`.
- `data-navigation`, `data-tools`, `data-split-panel` on the root: `open` | `closed`.
- `data-split-panel-position` on the root: `bottom` | `side` (always `bottom` while compact).
- `data-resizing` on the split separator while it is dragged.
- First render (server and client) is the wide layout; the compact layout applies after mount, once the layout has measured itself.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the separator shows `var(--accent)` on `focus-visible`; the region buttons are `IconButton` with their own ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the region controls in DOM order (navigation, header, content, split panel, tools). On the split separator: `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` grow and shrink a bottom panel; `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` grow and shrink a side panel (mirrored under RTL); `Shift` makes the step 64 px instead of 16 px; `Home` / `End` go to the minimum / maximum. `Escape` closes a compact drawer (from `Drawer`) and returns focus to the control that opened it. The split panel and tools bodies are focusable scroll regions (`tabindex="0"`, `role="group"` named by their heading), so a keyboard reader can scroll them when they hold no control.
- ARIA: the tools region and the split panel are `<section aria-labelledby>` their header title (`<h2>`); the separator is `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` in pixels, `aria-controls` the split panel and an accessible name from the catalog. The compact drawers are named by `navigationAriaLabel` and `toolsLabel`. The layout adds no landmark of its own around the content; the consumer's `<main>` and `Sidebar` `<nav>` are the landmarks.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the region titles; ≥3:1 for the separator against the surfaces.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the separator transition.
- Touch target: the separator's hit area is 16 px across (a `before:` pseudo-element) over a 4 px line; region buttons are 32 px `IconButton` (40 px on `pointer: coarse` from `IconButton`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Alert from '@aziontech/webkit/alert'
  import AppHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/app-header'
  import AppLayout from '@aziontech/webkit/app-layout'
  import Breadcrumb from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-root'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Command from '@aziontech/webkit/command'
  import HelpPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel'
  import IconButton from '@aziontech/webkit/icon-button'
  import KeyValueList from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-list'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
  import PageHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/page-header'
  import SearchTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/search-trigger'
  import SidebarMenuGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-menu-group'
  import SidebarMenuItem from '@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-menu-item'
  import SidebarMenuRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-menu-root'
  import Sidebar from '@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-root'
  import StatusIndicator from '@aziontech/webkit/status-indicator'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const toolsOpen = ref(true)
  const splitPanelOpen = ref(true)
  const notice = ref(true)

  const crumbs = [{ label: 'Services', href: '#' }, { label: 'web-app-prod' }]
  const searchOpen = ref(false)
  const searchPages = ['Applications', 'Workloads', 'Functions', 'Firewall']
</script>

<template>
  <div class="h-dvh">
    <AppLayout
      v-model:tools-open="toolsOpen"
      v-model:split-panel-open="splitPanelOpen"
      split-panel-title="web-app-prod"
      tools-label="Help: Services"
    >
      <template #navigation="{ drawer }">
        <Sidebar
          aria-label="Main navigation"
          :resizable="!drawer"
          :collapsible="!drawer"
        >
          <SidebarMenuRoot role="presentation">
            <SidebarMenuGroup>
              <SidebarMenuItem
                label="Home"
                icon="az az-home"
                href="#"
              />
              <SidebarMenuItem
                label="Services"
                icon="az az-applications"
                href="#"
                active
              />
              <SidebarMenuItem
                label="Variables"
                icon="az az-variables"
                href="#"
              />
            </SidebarMenuGroup>
          </SidebarMenuRoot>
        </Sidebar>
      </template>

      <template #header="{ compact, openNavigation, toggleTools }">
        <div class="@container w-full">
          <AppHeader aria-label="Console">
            <AppHeader.Start>
              <div class="flex w-full min-w-0 items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
                <IconButton
                  v-if="compact"
                  icon="az az-menu"
                  aria-label="Open navigation"
                  variant="outline"
                  size="medium"
                  @click="openNavigation"
                />
              </div>
            </AppHeader.Start>
            <AppHeader.Center />
            <AppHeader.End>
              <SearchTrigger
                collapsible
                @open="searchOpen = true"
              />
              <IconButton
                icon="az az-circle-help"
                aria-label="Help"
                variant="outline"
                size="medium"
                :aria-pressed="toolsOpen"
                @click="toggleTools"
              />
            </AppHeader.End>
          </AppHeader>
          <Command v-model:open="searchOpen">
            <Command.Input placeholder="Search the console" />
            <Command.List>
              <Command.Empty>No page matches your search.</Command.Empty>
              <Command.Group label="Pages">
                <Command.Item
                  v-for="page in searchPages"
                  :key="page"
                  :value="page"
                  >{{ page }}</Command.Item
                >
              </Command.Group>
            </Command.List>
          </Command>
        </div>
      </template>

      <template #notifications>
        <Alert
          v-if="notice"
          severity="info"
          closable
          @close="notice = false"
        >
          Scheduled maintenance on Nov 20 from 02:00 to 03:00 UTC. Services keep serving traffic.
        </Alert>
      </template>

      <template #breadcrumbs>
        <Breadcrumb :items="crumbs" />
      </template>

      <main class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-lg) p-(--spacing-md)">
        <PageHeader
          title="web-app-prod"
          description="The service that answers shop.example.com."
        />
        <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-(--spacing-xs)">
          <Button
            label="Show details"
            variant="outline"
            size="medium"
            @click="splitPanelOpen = true"
          />
        </div>
      </main>

      <template #split-panel>
        <KeyValueList aria-label="Service details">
          <KeyValueList.Item label="Status">
            <StatusIndicator
              severity="success"
              label="Active"
            />
          </KeyValueList.Item>
          <KeyValueList.Item label="Domain">shop.example.com</KeyValueList.Item>
          <KeyValueList.Item label="Last deploy">Nov 10, 2026, 14:32</KeyValueList.Item>
        </KeyValueList>
      </template>

      <template #tools>
        <HelpPanel aria-label="Help: Services">
          <HelpPanel.Header
            title="Services"
            description="Where your domains meet the code that answers them."
          />
          <HelpPanel.Group label="What is a service?">
            <p>A service binds one or more domains to the code and rules that answer them.</p>
          </HelpPanel.Group>
          <HelpPanel.Footer>
            <Link
              label="Services documentation"
              href="https://example.com/docs"
              target="_blank"
            />
          </HelpPanel.Footer>
        </HelpPanel>
      </template>
    </AppLayout>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/console-layout.md -->

# Console Layout

> The console chrome, composed once in the app: `AppLayout` with the navigation rail (`Sidebar` + `SidebarMenu`, the brand on top and the account at the foot), the global header (breadcrumbs, `SearchTrigger`, the app's own actions and the account avatar) and the `Command` search palette wired to the trigger and to ⌘K / Ctrl K. The navigation is data (`navigation`, each row with an `href` that is followed with the app's router when it is an in-app path), the active row follows the current route, and the page body is the default slot inside the layout's `<main>`. A page opens the palette with `useConsoleLayout().openSearch()`, sets its own trail with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`, and fills a fixed-height main with `data-layout-fill` on its root. Platform blocks are only page bodies rendered through this slot; they never carry the chrome themselves.

- Import: `import ConsoleLayoutRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/console-layout-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import ConsoleLayout from '@aziontech/webkit/console-layout'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use ConsoleLayout once at the app root of the Azion console; every page is its body.
- Every signed-in console page: put one `ConsoleLayout` in the app's root (around `RouterView`) and render each page block as its default slot.
- A product area that needs the console navigation, breadcrumbs, the ⌘K palette and the account menu without hand-composing `AppLayout`, `Sidebar`, `SidebarMenu`, `AppHeader`, `SearchTrigger` and `Command`.

## Do

- Compose the layout once, in the app's root, around `RouterView`; each route renders only its page body. Never copy the chrome into a page.
- Give every navigation row an `id` and an `href`: an in-app path (`/workloads`) is followed with the app's router when one is installed (a named route becomes a path through `router.resolve(...).href`), an external URL loads normally, and a row with no `href` is left to your `navigate` handler. Never `to`, `path` or `route` on a row (lint `webkit/prefer-href-in-menu-node`). Leave `activeId` empty so the active row follows the route; set it only for a page whose route matches no row.
- Pass a static trail through `breadcrumbs` (derive it from the route meta); leave it empty on first-level pages.
- A page that owns its trail (a loaded name, a control crumb) renders `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`: `items` are the crumbs, the default slot the trailing controls (a `Select` with `variant="ghost"`, `size="small"`, an `aria-label`, no `w-full`). It replaces the layout's trail while the page is mounted and renders nothing in place.
- Put the app's own header actions (`Create`, `Agent`) in the `actions` slot and render them icon-only while `compact`.
- Put the account menu groups (`DropdownMenu.Group`) in the `account-menu` slot; the layout renders the avatar and the trigger.
- Put an account switcher in `sidebar-header` (full width under the wordmark, the design sample's rail) and, below the compact breakpoint, in `header-leading` while `compact`; page-level flash messages go in `notifications`, and help or the notifications list in `tools` (toggled from a bell in `actions` with `toggleTools`).
- A page's control crumb is its `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb`, never `App.vue`'s `breadcrumbs` slot.
- A workspace page (editor, pinned panes) puts `data-layout-fill` on its root: the `<main>` becomes a fixed-height, non-scrolling region the root fills. Never size a body with `100dvh` or `calc(100dvh - var(--layout-header-height))` (lint `webkit/no-viewport-height-calc`, also run by the authoring ratchet over blocks and examples).
- Bind `v-model:navigation-open` when the rail's state must survive a reload or be driven from elsewhere (a `Collapse sidebar` / `Expand sidebar` command in the `search` slot); persist it in the app. The rail's own collapse control and the edge affordance keep working either way.
- Open the palette from inside a page with `useConsoleLayout().openSearch()` (imported from `@aziontech/webkit/use-console-layout`); never mount a second `Command`. `useConsoleLayout()` throws outside a `ConsoleLayout`, so a misplaced call fails loudly.
- A page body that also renders on its own (a block preview, a docs example, a test) calls `useConsoleLayout({ optional: true })`, which returns `null` outside a layout, and guards the call (`layout?.openSearch()`). Never wrap `useConsoleLayout()` in `try` / `catch`.
- The page entrance (`animate-page-enter`) plays on every route path change: the `<main>` is keyed on the path, so the page body remounts when the path changes and is kept when only the query or the hash changes. Keep state that must survive a path change (a list filter, a draft) in the route query or in the app's store, not in the page body; a `KeepAlive` belongs inside a page body (tabbed views), not around `RouterView`.
- The page body renders no `<main>` of its own and no `AppLayout`: the layout owns the landmark. Frame the body with `layout-boundary` + `layout-column` for list and form pages, or flush (`PageTabs` first) for detail pages.
- A destination appears once per screen (rule `webkit-navigation-levels`): never render a `SidebarMenu` in the page body: page navigation lives in the rail and a page has only its `PageTabs`. The rail holds two levels at most: a product with 3 or fewer resources lists them on level 1, a product with more is a drill row whose level lists them, and no drill level nests another. In development builds the layout scans the `SidebarMenu`s in its `<main>` after mount, on each route change and on page mutations, and when a row `href` has the same path (query and hash ignored) as a `navigation` row on screen (the top level, its inline children and the open drill level; a closed drill level is not on screen), it calls `console.warn` once per route with both labels and the route. Production builds drop the check (`import.meta.env.DEV`).

## Don’t

- A focused flow with no navigation rail (a creation wizard, sign-in) → render the page on its own or with the flow's own header.
- Public marketing pages → `SiteLayout`. Documentation → `DocLayout`.
- When the page needs the split panel → compose `AppLayout` directly; `ConsoleLayout` covers the navigation, header, notifications, tools and content regions.

## Related

- `AppLayout` — the frame this layout fills; it owns the compact drawers and the scrolling content region.
- `Sidebar`, `SidebarMenu` — the rail and the data-driven navigation tree (`navigation` is mapped onto `SidebarMenu` groups).
- `SearchTrigger`, `Command` — the header search and the palette it opens; the palette lists every navigation page.
- `Breadcrumb` — the header trail on wide layouts (`breadcrumbs`).
- `shell/console` — the block that shows this layout with sample console navigation.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `navigation` | `ConsoleLayoutNavGroup[]` | `[]` | false | The navigation tree: groups of rows, each `{ id, label, icon?, href?, tagValue?, disabled?, kind?, children?, groups? }`; an in-app `href` is followed with the app's router. |
| `activeId` | `string` | `''` | false | Id of the current row. Empty matches the current route against each row's `href`. |
| `breadcrumbs` | `BreadcrumbItemData[]` | `[]` | false | The trail shown in the header on wide layouts; each is `{ label, href? }` and the last one is the current page. |
| `home` | `string` | `'/'` | false | Where the brand mark links. |
| `account` | `ConsoleLayoutAccount` | `undefined` | false | The signed-in account, `{ name, email?, src? }`, shown at the foot of the rail and as the header avatar; nothing is rendered when absent. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Main navigation`). |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the palette's input. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Search pages and commands`). |
| `toolsLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the tools region (help, notifications). Empty uses `AppLayout`'s catalog (`Help`). |
| `searchOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:searchOpen`). |
| `toolsOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:toolsOpen`). |
| `navigationOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:navigationOpen`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `navigate` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, item: ConsoleLayoutNavItem)` | Fired when a navigation row or a palette page is chosen; the layout then follows its `href` (an in-app path with the app's router). A row without `href` is left to this handler. Event first. |
| `search-select` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: string \| number)` | Fired when a palette item from the `search` slot is chosen; `value` is that item's value. Event first. |
| `account-select` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: string \| number)` | Fired when an option of the `account-menu` slot is chosen, by click or by keyboard (`Enter` / `Space`), from the rail footer or the header avatar; `value` is the option's `value`. Event first. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The page body, rendered inside the layout's `<main>`; a body whose root carries `data-layout-fill` fills a fixed-height, non-scrolling main. |
| `actions` | { compact: boolean, toggleTools: () => void } | The app's header actions, between the search trigger and the avatar; render them icon-only while `compact`; `toggleTools` opens and closes the tools region (a notifications bell). |
| `header-leading` | { compact: boolean } | Content at the start of the header, before the breadcrumbs (an account or organization switcher). |
| `sidebar-header` | { compact: boolean } | Content in the rail under the wordmark, above the navigation (a full-width account or organization switcher); `compact` is true when the rail is the compact drawer (render nothing there to keep the switcher in `header-leading`). Rendered only when given; a region whose slot renders nothing (a false `v-if`) is hidden. |
| `breadcrumbs` | — | An app-wide composed trail that replaces the one built from `breadcrumbs`; a page's `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumb` replaces both; hidden while compact. |
| `notifications` | — | Flash messages (`Alert`) above the page, kept in view while the page scrolls. |
| `tools` | — | The tools region's body (a `HelpPanel` or the notifications list), opened with `v-model:tools-open`. |
| `search` | { query: string } | Extra `Command.Group`s (recent resources, commands) listed before the navigation pages in the palette. |
| `account-menu` | — | `DropdownMenu.Group`s of the account menu, opened from the account row in the rail and from the header avatar; a chosen option is reported by `account-select`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/console-layout-breadcrumb`

## Sub-components

The root ships a compound API via `index.ts` (`Object.assign` attaches the part; vue-tsc emits `index.d.ts`), and `index.ts` re-exports the root's types (`ConsoleLayoutNavGroup`, `ConsoleLayoutNavItem`, `BreadcrumbItemData`, `ConsoleLayoutAccount`). Root binding is PascalCase `ConsoleLayout`.

```
packages/webkit/src/components/layout/console-layout/
├── console-layout.vue          (root — the chrome, provides the context)
├── index.ts                    (compound Object.assign)
├── injection-key.ts            (the page context and the trail registry)
├── composables/use-console-layout.ts
├── console-layout.test.ts
└── console-layout-breadcrumb/console-layout-breadcrumb.vue
```

- `console-layout-breadcrumb/console-layout-breadcrumb.vue` — a page's own trail.
  - Props: `items: BreadcrumbItemData[]` default `[]` — the page's crumbs, each `{ label, href? }`; without a control crumb the last one is the current page.
  - Events: _none_ (crumb clicks are followed by the layout).
  - Slots: `default` — one or more controls that end the trail (a `Select` with `variant="ghost"`, `size="small"` and an `aria-label`); each top-level element is its own crumb (environment then version: two `Select`s); they keep the page's reactivity.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:search-open` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:searchOpen` | Whether the search palette is open; the trigger, ⌘K / Ctrl K and `openSearch()` set it. |
| `v-model:tools-open` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:toolsOpen` | Whether the tools region (help or notifications) is open beside the content; a drawer while compact. |
| `v-model:navigation-open` | `boolean` | `true` | `update:navigationOpen` | Whether the navigation rail is shown on wide layouts; `false` collapses it (the Sidebar's `open`). The rail's collapse control, its edge affordance and ⌘B / Ctrl B all write it. It has no effect while compact, where the rail is a drawer. Same name as `AppLayout`'s `navigationOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `compact` (from `AppLayout`: the rail becomes a drawer opened from the header, the breadcrumbs give way to the brand), the palette `open` / `closed`.
- `data-compact` and `data-navigation` come from `AppLayout` on the inner frame.
- Fill: a direct child of the `<main>` with `data-layout-fill` makes the main `h-full overflow-hidden` and the child `flex-1 min-h-0`; pure CSS, right in the server render.
- Page entrance: the `<main>` is keyed on the current route path (the router's `currentRoute.path`, or `location.pathname` on `popstate` without a router); a path change replaces the main and remounts the page body, so `animate-page-enter` replays. The first path read after mount (no router) and a change of only the query or the hash keep the main.
- Page trail: registered on mount, so the server render shows the layout's trail and the page trail replaces it after hydration (no mismatch); use `breadcrumbs` when the first server paint must show it.
- Active navigation row: `SidebarMenu`'s `activeId`; a row inside a drill level opens that level, a row inside an inline row expands it. On mount, when the rail (or the compact drawer) is rendered and whenever the active row changes, the rail's own scroller scrolls the minimum needed to bring the row into view, honouring the scroller's `scroll-padding` (the `ScrollArea` fade), with an instant jump (no smooth scroll); the page never scrolls.
- Rail header: the `sidebar-header` region sits under the wordmark with `--spacing-md` padding; it collapses with CSS (`:empty`) when the slot renders only a false `v-if`, so the server render and the client agree.
- Not applicable: `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid` (the page body owns its states).

## Accessibility

- Landmarks: the rail is the `Sidebar` `<nav>` named by `ariaLabel`; the header is `AppHeader` (`<header>`); the page body is inside the layout's single `<main>`. A page body must not render a second `<main>`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` runs rail (wordmark, `sidebar-header`, navigation) → header → page; `⌘K` / `Ctrl K` opens the palette (owned by `Command`); on wide layouts `⌘B` / `Ctrl B` toggles the rail and writes `v-model:navigation-open` (the Sidebar's `shortcut`, off while compact and while typing in a field); in the palette `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` move, `Enter` chooses, `Escape` closes and returns focus. The rail keyboard map is `SidebarMenu`'s; the compact drawer closes on `Escape` and returns focus to the hamburger (`AppLayout`).
- Names: the compact hamburger (`Open navigation`), the brand link (`Azion home`), the rail account trigger (`Account menu`, an icon button) come from the locale catalog; the avatar carries the account name. The header avatar trigger shows the initials, so its name starts with them (`JD, account menu`, `consoleLayout.accountMenuFor`) to meet WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name (a speech user says what they see); with an account image it has no visible text and is named `Account menu`.
- Account menu: choosing an option by pointer or keyboard emits `account-select`; the keyboard map inside the menu is `DropdownMenu`'s.
- Visible focus: every interactive part is a WebKit control with its own ring; the brand link and the avatar button use `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Choosing a row in the compact drawer closes it.
- A page's control crumb is the last item of the header's `Breadcrumb` list; it carries its own accessible name (`aria-label` on `Select.Trigger`, e.g. `Switch environment`).
