# Dashboard Grid

> A configurable dashboard grid: the reader arranges the cards. `DashboardGrid` owns the layout, an array of `{ id, span, height? }` bound with `v-model:layout`, and lays one `DashboardGrid.Item` per entry on a column grid that collapses to one column in a narrow container. While `editing`, the `ChartCard` inside each item shows its drag handle and resize corner, and those handles report to the board instead of to the page: drag a card onto another or press the arrow keys on its handle to reorder, drag its corner or press the arrow keys on it to resize. Every move and resize is clamped, written back to the layout and announced in a polite live region. Taken from Cloudscape's board and board item, on top of the existing `ChartCard` handles.

- Import: `import DashboardGridRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/dashboard-grid-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import DashboardGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/dashboard-grid'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A dashboard whose reader chooses the order and the size of its cards, and the product keeps that layout as a preference.
- A grid of cards that must be reorderable from the keyboard and announced to screen readers, not only by mouse.

## Do

- Keep the layout in the page and persist it wherever the product stores preferences; the board never stores it.
- Offer an explicit Edit layout toggle (`aria-pressed`) and turn `editing` on with it, so handles do not crowd the read-only view.
- Give every `DashboardGrid.Item` a `label` (the card's title): it is the name the live region announces.
- Offer Reset layout once the layout differs from the default.
- Bound the sizes (`min-span`, `max-span`, `min-height`, `max-height`) so no card becomes unreadable.

## Don’t

- A fixed dashboard whose layout the product decides → a plain CSS grid of `chart-card`s (see the `dashboard/analytics-dashboard` block).
- Two or three panes whose boundary the reader drags → use `resizable`.
- Reordering the rows of a list or a table → use the table's reorderable rows or `transfer-list`.
- A grid of resources the reader selects, not arranges → use `card-list`.

## Related

- `chart-card` — the card each `DashboardGrid.Item` holds; its `DragHandle` and `ResizeHandle` drive the board.
- `resizable` — split panes with a draggable divider, not a grid of cards.
- `card-list` — a selectable collection of item cards with a fixed layout.
- `page-header` — the title over the board, with the Edit layout and Reset layout actions beside it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `number` | `12` | false | Columns of the grid in a wide container; one column below `@3xl`. |
| `minSpan` | `number` | `3` | false | Fewest columns an item may span. |
| `maxSpan` | `number` | `12` | false | Most columns an item may span; capped at `columns`. |
| `minHeight` | `number` | `240` | false | Smallest height in pixels a resize allows. |
| `maxHeight` | `number` | `960` | false | Largest height in pixels a resize allows. |
| `editing` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the drag and resize handles of every card and lets the reader rearrange the board. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of items. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Dashboard`). |
| `layout` | `DashboardGridLayoutItem[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:layout`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item-move` | `(event: KeyboardEvent \| DragEvent, payload: { id: string; from: number; to: number })` | An item moved, by drop or by the keyboard; zero-based. The drop or key event comes first. |
| `item-resize` | `(event: PointerEvent \| KeyboardEvent, payload: { id: string; span: number; height: number \| undefined })` | A resize ended (pointer up or a resize key on the corner); that event comes first. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | One `DashboardGrid.Item` per layout entry, in layout order. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/dashboard-grid-item`

## Sub-components

The root ships a compound API: `index.ts` attaches `Item` to the root. The board provides its
context (`injection-key.ts`) to every `DashboardGrid.Item`, and each item provides a narrower item context
that `ChartCard` reads when it renders inside one: the card's `draggable` and `resizable` follow the
board's `editing`, its span, height and bounds come from the layout entry, and its handles' moves,
drags and resizes go to the board. `ChartCard` keeps working on its own outside a board.

- `dashboard-grid-item/dashboard-grid-item.vue` — One cell of the grid, an `<li>` that spans the entry's columns (capped at the grid's current column count) and, when the entry has a `height`, that many pixels.
  - Props: `itemId: string` (required — the `id` of its layout entry), `label?: string` (default `''` — the name the live region announces; empty uses `Item <position>` from the locale catalog).
  - Slot: `default` — the item's content, normally one `ChartCard`.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `dashboard-grid-item`.

Resulting layout:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/layout/dashboard-grid/
├── board.vue
├── board.test.ts
├── index.ts
├── injection-key.ts          (DashboardGridContext, DashboardGridItemContext, DashboardGridLayoutItem)
├── composables/
│   └── use-dashboard-grid-context.ts  (injects; throws outside a DashboardGrid)
└── dashboard-grid-item/
    └── dashboard-grid-item.vue
```

Exports:

```jsonc
"./dashboard-grid": "./src/components/layout/dashboard-grid/index.ts",
"./dashboard-grid-root": "./src/components/layout/dashboard-grid/dashboard-grid.vue",
"./dashboard-grid-item": "./src/components/layout/dashboard-grid/dashboard-grid-item/dashboard-grid-item.vue"
```

Exported types: `DashboardGridLayoutItem = { id: string; span: number; height?: number }`,
`DashboardGridMoveDirection = 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right'`.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:layout` | `DashboardGridLayoutItem[]` | `[]` | `update:layout` | Order, span and height of every item. The board emits a new array on every move or resize. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `editing`; on `DashboardGrid.Item`: `over` (a dragged item hovers it), and the card's own `dragging` / `resizing`
- `data-editing` on the root mirrors `editing`
- `data-over` on `DashboardGrid.Item` while it is the drop target
- `data-item-id` on `DashboardGrid.Item` carries its `itemId`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the board adds no focus stop; the `ChartCard` handles carry `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`.
- Keyboard map: on a card's drag handle, `ArrowUp` / `ArrowLeft` move the item one place earlier and `ArrowDown` / `ArrowRight` one place later (mirrored under `rtl`); focus stays on the moved handle. On the resize corner, `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` change the span by one column, `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` the height by 24 px, `Home` / `End` jump to the span bounds, `Escape` cancels a pointer resize.
- ARIA: the grid is a `<ul role="list">` named by `ariaLabel`; each item is an `<li>`. A visually hidden `<p aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">` announces each move (`<label> moved to position 2 of 6.`) and each resize (`<label> resized to 6 of 12 columns.`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the board renders no ink of its own; the drop ring uses `--ring-color`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the drop ring transition.
- Touch target: the handles are the card's; dragging is a pointer gesture with the keyboard as its alternative.

# Footer

> Page footer for marketing and product surfaces: the bottom-of-page counterpart to `AppHeader`. A canvas-colored shell divided into bands by hairline rules. Matches the Webkit Footer component set (Figma node 5467:1638, `Type=Default` / `Type=Mobile`). **Four bands.** Top to bottom: the link columns, a row carrying the social icons and the status/language pair, and the signature band (the brand beside its tagline, in its own `RegistrationFrame` with corner marks). **Two placements, chosen with `variant` — the same two `AppHeader` has, and the bands are identical in both.** `content` is the default: the bands run full bleed across whatever zone holds the footer, and the footer adds no inset of its own because every band already carries `--spacing-lg` inside it — the value `--layout-boundary-inline` resolves to — so the first column title opens on the page boundary by construction. `site` closes a framed marketing page: the bands take the site column (`layout-column-site`: capped at `--layout-measure-site`, inset by `--layout-boundary-inline` once the window is narrower than that), side rules run down both edges, two hatched `RegistrationFrame` gutters flank them from `2xl`, and a hatched band closes the frame below. Those three hold no content and stay out of the a11y tree. The hero band, the framed sections and this footer resolve to that one measure, which is the only reason the border-x running down the page is continuous; the top bar is deliberately one rung wider (`--layout-measure-site-header`). The frame apparatus belongs to `site` alone, and not as a matter of taste: on a full-bleed footer the side rules land on the zone's own edges, where a hairline reads as a seam against the bezel rather than as a frame, and the `flex-1` gutters — with no slack to grow into — collapse to zero width while still painting their borders and corner marks onto the bands' own edges. **The two Figma variants are one component switching by CSS**, and the switch is not one breakpoint: - The **column grid** folds from four columns to the 2×2 mobile grid below `md` (768px). - The **bands recombine at `md`**: stacked, their order is links → status/language → signature → social icons (the Mobile variant's order); from `md` the social icons and the status pair share one row above the signature. All four bands are cells of **one** grid, so each is a single element in a single place in the DOM at every width — the order is `order-*` when stacked and explicit row/column placement from `md`. A wrapper row that existed only on desktop would mean two copies of the markup, so two copies of the consumer's slot content. - **Row two sizes its two bands by content** (`md:grid-cols-[auto_auto]`), not in half: each band takes what it holds and the two share the slack, so the status pair never wraps while the social band still has room, and the social band wraps only when the zone is narrower than both together. A 50/50 split gave the social band 427px of an 853px docs reading column, 13px short of the brand mark and seven large icons — a premature wrap in every zone narrower than the viewport. - The **gutters appear at `2xl`** (1536px) in the `site` placement, not with the rest of the desktop presentation, because that is the first breakpoint past the measure itself (1388px). Gated any earlier they resolve to zero width and still paint their borders and corner marks on the measure's own edges — the gate moves with the measure, and was `xl` while the measure was 1192px. - Between the measure and that breakpoint the row therefore holds **one** child, so it carries `justify-center`: a capped item in an unjustified flex row is left-aligned, which would put the footer's frame up to 148px left of the centred frame it closes. With it the footer's column lands on the page column's own vertical wherever the cap is active — measured equal at 1440, 1536, 1920 and 2560. - Within the status pair, **`language` and `status` swap order** between the two variants (the phone leads with the select, the row ends with it), which is why they are two slots the row reverses rather than one cluster the consumer orders. Content (links, labels, languages, status, brand, tagline) always comes from the consumer; the component owns anatomy, tokens, and responsiveness.

- Import: `import FooterRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/footer-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Footer from '@aziontech/webkit/footer'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Footer to compose a footer in product or docs.
- Rendering page JSON, or you need a whole band with no custom content → the section (`site-footer-section`). Building an SFC by hand, needing slots, or nesting inside another band → the primitive (`footer`).
- The page-level footer of a site or application, paired with `AppHeader`.
- Grouped navigation links at the bottom of the page plus a brand/social/status bar.

## Do

- Compose every band from existing DS components (`Brand`, `IconButton variant="ghost" size="small"`, `StatusIndicator`, `Select`); never rebuild them inside the slots.
- Keep column titles short (one or two words) — they are group labels, not headings for prose.
- Give every social `IconButton` an `ariaLabel`; the footer cannot name them for you.
- Keep the social `IconButton`s at `size="small"`: a 28px box holds the brand mark and seven icons in 356px, which fits beside the status pair in the narrowest zone a shell gives the footer (the docs reading column at `lg`, 724px wide). At `large` the same row is 440px and wraps there.
- Provide four columns for the canonical desktop presentation; the grid folds to two columns below `md` on its own.
- Keep each band close to the canonical content (up to ~7 social icons; one status indicator; one language select; one brand lockup; a one-line tagline). Every band grows past its `min-h-14` floor rather than clipping, so a longer status string or an extra icon wraps safely — but a much heavier cluster belongs in the columns, not in a band.
- Give the `tagline` slot plain text, not a heading element: the footer already wraps it in the `.text-heading-xl` measure, and a real `h*` in a `contentinfo` landmark competes with the page's own outline.
- Pick the placement from the page, not from the look: `site` on a page that is a framed marketing column (its hero, sections and this footer share one measure), `content` — the default — anywhere the footer closes an app or docs zone. A `site` footer under an unframed page draws a frame nothing above it continues.
- Leave the gutters and the column frame alone — they are the `site` frame's own page material, and the placement decides them. A page that needs more air below the footer adds a `SectionGap`, and one that needs none is not this design.

## Don’t

- The bottom area of a panel, table, sidebar, or overlay → use that component's own footer part (`panel-footer`, `table-footer`, `sidebar-footer`, `popover-footer`).
- A single standalone link inside body content → use `link` instead of `Footer.Link`.

## Related

- `app-header` — the top-of-page chrome counterpart; same shell philosophy (regions composed by the consumer).
- `brand`, `icon-button`, `status-indicator`, `select` — the components consumers compose inside the bands; the footer reimplements none of them.
- `site-footer-section` — the marketing site's data-driven footer section, the one `SiteLayout` renders. Use `site-footer-section` for a site page fed from section JSON and `Footer` when composing the bands by hand; the two do not share code yet.
- `registration-frame` — the footer's own frame: the hatched gutters, the framed column and the signature box are `RegistrationFrame` instances (`borders` / `marks` / `hatch`).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the contentinfo landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Footer`). |
| `signature` | `'always' \| 'compact'` | `'always'` | false | Widths at which the signature band renders: `always`, or `compact` for below `lg` only, where a footer whose brand leads the social row from `lg` moves it into the band. Decided in CSS, so the server HTML and the hydrated page lay out the same. |
| `variant` | `'content' \| 'site'` | `'content'` | false | Where the footer sits: `content` is the default — the bands run full bleed across whatever zone holds the footer, opening on the page boundary; `site` closes a framed marketing page instead, capping the bands at the site measure and drawing the frame that page carries: the side rules, the hatched gutters and the corner marks, closing on a full-bleed bottom rule. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Root: the `Footer.Column` items; laid out as a 2-column grid that becomes 4 columns at `md`. |
| `social` | — | Root: the social icon buttons. Renders its own band; centered stacked, at the row's start from `md`. |
| `status` | — | Root: the system status indicator. Shares the status band with `language`. |
| `language` | — | Root: the language select. Rendered _before_ `status` when stacked and _after_ it from `md`, per the two Figma variants. |
| `brand` | — | Root: the brand lockup of the signature band. |
| `tagline` | — | Root: the one-line tagline; the footer wraps it in the `.text-heading-xl` measure. |
| `default` | — | `footer-column`: its `Footer.Link` items. |
| `default` | — | `footer-link`: the link label. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/footer-column`
- `@aziontech/webkit/footer-link`

## Sub-components

- `footer-column/footer-column.vue` — one navigation column: a muted title labelling a stacked group of `Footer.Link` items.
- `footer-link/footer-link.vue` — one text link inside a column; the root is the anchor itself, so consumer attributes (`target`, `rel`) land on the `a`.

## States

- Visual states: `default` on the shell and columns; `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `visited` on `footer-link`.
- Placement: `data-variant="content" | "site"` on the root (from `variant`); the bands read it through `group-data-[variant=site]:` for the cap and the bottom rule, the column `RegistrationFrame` draws its side rules and corner marks only in `site`, and the gutters render only in `site`.
- Signature placement: `data-signature="always" | "compact"` on the root (from `signature`); in `compact` the signature band carries `group-data-[signature=compact]:lg:hidden`.
- Each band renders exactly when its slot renders, read at render time rather than cached: a slot behind a `v-if` that turns off — or a slot the server rendered and the client does not — takes its band with it, so no empty bordered band is ever left under the bottom bar.
- No `data-state`; the shell has no interactive states — slotted children own their own.

## Accessibility

- Root renders as `<footer>` — the implicit `contentinfo` landmark — with `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`.
- The two hatched gutters carry `aria-hidden="true"`: they hold no content, so without it a screen reader announces two empty groups at the end of every page.
- Each `footer-column` renders a `<nav>` labelled via `aria-labelledby` pointing at its title (`useId`), so link groups are unique, navigable landmarks.
- Keyboard map: none on the shell; `Tab` moves through links in DOM order; `Enter` activates.
- Visible focus on links: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for column titles and links on `--bg-canvas`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the link color transition.
- Touch target: text links follow the platform convention for footer link lists (<40px height); justified deviation — targets are full-width-of-text with `--spacing-xs` separation.

# Page Header

> The heading that opens a console page: an h1 whose `size` picks the heading token by page level, a one-line description, and the actions the page owns on the right. When the row runs out of room the actions move below the copy together; on a phone they stack, each at full width. Four optional regions complete a detail page's header without local markup: a `breadcrumbs` trail above the title, an `icon` before it, `meta` (a status tag, a version) beside it, and `tabs` across the bottom. It replaces the header markup every list, detail, settings and create page used to copy by hand.

- Import: `import PageHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/page-header'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use PageHeader once per console page for the h1, description and page actions; a band inside the page uses SectionHeader.
- The top of any console page: a first-level list (`medium`), a detail tab or settings sub-page (`small`), a creation hub headline (`large`).
- A page that owns actions (Documentation, a create action) that belong next to its title.
- A resource detail page whose header carries the trail back to the list, the resource's icon, its status and the tabs of its sections (`breadcrumbs`, `icon`, `meta`, `tabs`).

## Do

- One PageHeader per page; it renders the page's only h1.
- Put the Documentation link first and the create action on the outer edge, both outlined at the medium size.
- Do not set `class="w-full"` on the action buttons; the header makes them full width on a phone.
- Set `titleId` when a form or landmark names itself with `aria-labelledby`.
- `breadcrumbs`: pass a `Breadcrumb` with `items`; its last entry is the current page and should match the title.
- `icon`: one decorative glyph or a square `Avatar`, at most 32 px; it is `aria-hidden` by default, since the title already names the page.
- `meta`: one or two small `Tag`s (status, environment). Longer facts (owner, created date) belong in the page body, not the header.
- `tabs`: a `Tabs` row of the page's sections. A page that already shows `PageTabs` above the header leaves this slot empty; never both.

## Don’t

- The heading of one band inside a page → use `section-header`.
- A settings band with a Hint and a card of rows → use `settings-section`.
- A documentation page heading → use `doc-page-header`.

## Related

- `section-header` — the h2 band heading inside a page.
- `page-tabs` — the second-level navigation strip that sits above a detail page's header; a header-local tab row goes in the `tabs` slot.
- `breadcrumb` — the usual content of the `breadcrumbs` slot.
- `tag` — the usual content of the `meta` slot (a status, an environment, a version).
- `button` — the usual content of the `actions` slot (outlined, `size="medium"`).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The page title, rendered as the page h1. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One sentence under the title that says what the page is for. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Heading scale of the title. |
| `titleId` | `string` | `''` | false | Id set on the h1, so a landmark or form can name itself with aria-labelledby. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | — | Rich description content (links, inline buttons); replaces the `description` prop. |
| `actions` | — | The actions the page owns, Documentation first and the create action on the outer edge. |
| `breadcrumbs` | — | The trail back to the parent pages, above the title row; usually a `Breadcrumb` with `items`. |
| `icon` | — | A leading glyph or square avatar before the title, decorative (`aria-hidden`). |
| `meta` | — | Short facts beside the title, such as a status `Tag`; wraps under the title when the row is narrow. |
| `tabs` | — | The tabs of the page's sections, across the full width under the title and actions. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop on the root and the h1
- Each region renders only when its slot is filled: `__breadcrumbs` (a full-width row above the title row), `__icon` (before the h1, `aria-hidden`), `__meta` (after the h1 on the same line, wrapping under it), `__tabs` (a full-width row after the copy and the actions). With no region slot the header renders exactly as before.
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/page-header`. Below `@md` of its own box the actions drop under the copy and each one stretches to the full width; from `@md` they sit beside the title at their own width. A header inside a drawer or a split view lays out for that box, not the window.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the controls in the `actions` slot.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the actions in DOM order; the header itself is not interactive.
- ARIA: the root is a `header` element and the title is the page's only `h1`; `titleId` lets a form or landmark reference it with `aria-labelledby`. The breadcrumb comes first in reading order (its own `nav` landmark), then the h1, the meta, the description, the actions and the tabs. The icon wrapper is `aria-hidden`.
- Keyboard map with regions: `Tab` reaches the breadcrumb links, then the actions, then the tabs (which own their arrow-key model).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title and the muted description.
- Touch target: the actions keep the Button sizes; on a phone they stretch to full width.

```vue
  import PageHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/page-header'

    description="View and manage your resources."
  >
    <template #actions>
      <Button
        label="Documentation"
        icon="az az-book"
        variant="outline"
        size="medium"
        href="https://example.com/docs/resources"
        target="_blank"
      />
      <Button
        label="Create Resource"
        icon="az az-plus"
        variant="outline"
        size="medium"
      />
    </template>
  </PageHeader>
</template>
```

# Resizable

> A group of adjacent regions whose shared edges the reader can drag. It is the layout primitive behind a workspace — an editor with a terminal under it and a preview beside it — where every region is content the reader is working in and the split between them is theirs to set. It exists because `Sidebar` was being used for both jobs. `Sidebar` is the app's NAVIGATION rail: it collapses to icons, it hides, it is the thing you leave to go somewhere. A terminal, a preview and a code editor are not places you navigate to — they are the work — and dressing two of them as navigation rails made a screen with three "sidebars" and one document, on an axis `Sidebar` does not even have (it has no horizontal edge, so a terminal under an editor had to hand-roll its own splitter). This component owns the EDGE; `Sidebar` goes back to owning navigation.

- Import: `import ResizableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/resizable-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Resizable from '@aziontech/webkit/resizable'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Two or more content regions share an edge the reader should be able to move (editor + terminal, editor + preview, list + detail).
- The split is a working preference the reader sets many times in a session, not a one-time layout decision.
- A region has to shrink to nothing and come back without losing its state (an editor's undo history, a scroll position).
- The layout needs a horizontal edge — one region above another — which no other component in the package provides.

## Do

- Give exactly ONE pane in a group no `basis`. That pane absorbs the remaining space, so the group always fills its container and the reader never sees a gap or a scrollbar they did not cause.
- Put the `basis` on the pane whose size the reader cares about (the terminal's height, the preview's width) and let the document be the flexible one.
- Keep the pane's own state alive when it is collapsed — collapse renders it at zero length, it does not unmount it. A code editor that loses its undo history when the reader drags an edge shut has lost the reader's work.
- Give every handle an `ariaLabel` naming the edge it moves ("Resize the terminal"), never the generic default: a screen with three handles otherwise reads as three identical controls.
- A control that reopens a collapsed pane belongs OUTSIDE that pane, in the surrounding chrome. A control that only exists inside the thing it hides cannot bring it back.

## Don’t

- The panel is the app's navigation rail → use `sidebar`, which owns the icon rail, the collapse and the nav semantics.
- The content is a temporary overlay over the page → use `drawer` (a panel that comes and goes) or `dialog`.
- The regions have a fixed relationship the reader should not change → use plain flex/grid layout with the layout tokens.
- The panel is one scrolling region with no movable edge → use `scroll-area`.

## Related

- `sidebar` — the navigation rail. Collapses to icons, hides, and carries nav semantics; reach for it when the panel is how the reader gets somewhere, not what they work in.
- `scroll-area` — one region that scrolls. A pane usually contains one.
- `drawer` — a panel that arrives over the page and leaves; a resizable pane is always there.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | false | Axis the panes are laid out on; horizontal places them side by side, vertical stacks them. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the group as a whole. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | On the root, the panes and handles in the order they appear. On a pane, its content. The handle takes no slot. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/resizable-handle`
- `@aziontech/webkit/resizable-pane`

## Sub-components

- `resizable-pane/resizable-pane.vue` — one region of the group.
- `resizable-handle/resizable-handle.vue` — the movable edge between two panes.

Neither part is an overlay, so neither is named `Trigger` or `Content` and neither carries `data-state="open|closed"`: the names come from this component's own anatomy — a group of PANES divided by HANDLES.

`resizable-pane` props:

- `basis` — `number`, default unset.
- `min` — `number`, default `96`.
- `max` — `number`, default `720`.
- `open` — `boolean`, default `true`.
- `collapsible` — `boolean`, default `false`.
- `ariaLabel` — `string`, default `''`.

`resizable-handle` props:

- `ariaLabel` — `string`, default `''`.
- `disabled` — `boolean`, default `false`.

`resizable-pane` events: `update:basis` (`number`) on every step of a drag and on a
keyboard nudge, and `update:open` (`boolean`) when a drag past the minimum or `Enter` on the
handle collapses the pane, or a drag back out restores it. Each is the `v-model` half of the props above.

`resizable-handle` emits nothing: it drives the pane beside it through the group's
context, so a consumer never wires one part to the other.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-orientation`: `horizontal` | `vertical` — on the root, and mirrored onto every pane and handle so each part styles itself off one fact.
- `data-state` is `closed` while the pane is collapsed (`open` false) and `open` otherwise
- `data-resizing` on the handle while a drag is in flight
- `data-disabled` mirrors the handle's `disabled` prop
- Reflow: the group clips on its main axis (`overflow-x-clip` / `overflow-y-clip`), so the hit area of a handle at the edge (a collapsed end pane) never adds overflow.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses each handle; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` move a handle in a horizontal group and `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` in a vertical one, one 24px step per press; `Home` sets the pane to its minimum, `End` to its maximum; `Enter` toggles a collapsible pane.
- ARIA: the handle is `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation` (the PERPENDICULAR of the group's axis — a separator between two side-by-side panes is itself vertical), `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` published from the pane it moves, `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`, and `aria-disabled` when disabled. Each pane is `role="group"` with its `ariaLabel`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the handle's colour transition
- Touch target: the handle draws a `--spacing-2xs` rail and extends its hit area to 16px across the axis with a pseudo-element, so the edge is grabbable without drawing a thick bar.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Resizable from '@aziontech/webkit/resizable'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const basis = ref(240)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="h-64">
    <Resizable
      class="h-full"
      orientation="horizontal"
      aria-label="Workspace"
    >
      <Resizable.Pane aria-label="Document"
        >Flexible — no basis, so it takes what is left.</Resizable.Pane
      >
      <Resizable.Handle aria-label="Resize the panel" />
      <Resizable.Pane
        v-model:basis="basis"
        :min="160"
        :max="480"
        aria-label="Panel"
        >Sized</Resizable.Pane
      >
    </Resizable>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/save-bar.md -->

# Save Bar

> The bar at the bottom of a settings or create page that holds the status of unsaved work and its Discard (or Cancel) and Save actions. `floating` overlays the bottom of the scroll region without moving the content and is shown while the form is dirty; `docked` takes its own row at the bottom; `plain` closes a form column saved as one unit, always shown; `fade` closes a wizard step with no border or surface, the step content fading into the canvas above Back and Next; `centered` floats the actions as a raised card centred over the bottom of a create page, always shown.

- Import: `import SaveBar from '@aziontech/webkit/save-bar'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A settings page whose changes are staged and saved together: show the floating bar while the form is dirty or saving.
- A create page or account form with one Save for the whole page (`plain`).
- A full-page wizard step: Back in `leading`, the step's primary action in `actions` (`fade`).
- A create page (Create Team, Create Zone, Create Function): Cancel and Create in a raised card centred at the bottom of the form, over the content, at every width (`centered`). This is the design sample's create-page footer; use it instead of a full-width `floating` bar there.

## Do

- Render the floating bar with `v-if="dirty || saving"` inside a `Transition`, so it slides in when the first change is made.
- Say what changed and when it takes effect in the status sentence; keep it to one line.
- Disable Discard and set `loading` on Save while saving.
- Do not build a centred action pill by hand (a sticky footer with a bordered card and a shadow): that is `variant="centered"`.
- `floating` and `docked` are for the dirty state of a settings page; `centered` and `plain` are for a create page or a form saved as one unit and stay on screen.

## Don’t

- A card that saves on its own → put the actions in the card footer.
- A drawer or dialog form → use the `PanelFooter` of `drawer` or `dialog`.
- A one-off confirmation → use `confirm-dialog`.

## Related

- `button` — the actions: an outlined Discard or Cancel, then a primary Save with `loading` while it runs.
- `settings-section` — the bands the bar saves.
- `confirm-dialog` — the guard shown when someone leaves with unsaved changes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'floating' \| 'docked' \| 'plain' \| 'fade' \| 'centered'` | `'floating'` | false | How the bar sits at the bottom of its scroll region. See the variant table below. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The status sentence on the left, such as You have unsaved changes. |
| `leading` | — | Replaces the whole leading region (the info icon and the sentence) with your own content, such as a `StatusIndicator` (Saving…, Saved) or an unsaved-changes count. Takes precedence over `default`. |
| `actions` | — | Discard or Cancel, then Save, on the right. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-variant` mirrors the `variant` prop on the root
- Floating inset: while a `floating` bar is mounted it publishes its measured height on the document root as `--save-bar-inset` (for a scroll region of its own, such as a code editor, to pad its bottom) and `--toast-offset-bottom` (so the `toaster` stacks above the bar), and updates both when the bar resizes. When the bar would cover the end of the content, the root grows to the bar's height so the last field can scroll clear of it; when there is nothing left to cover, the root stays at zero height. Both properties are removed when the bar unmounts or changes to another `variant`. The other variants publish nothing.
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/save-bar`. `floating` and `docked` put the message and the actions on one row from `@xl` of the bar; below it the actions stack full width under the message, Save on top. `plain` stacks the same way below `@md`. `fade` keeps `leading` (Back) and the actions on one row at every width, the actions at the inline end. `centered` keeps the card centred and one row at every width: the optional `leading` or `default` content first, then the actions; the card never grows wider than the bar and lets clicks through around it. The bar keeps `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` clear on phones.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the action buttons.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches Discard, then Save, in reading order (the column is reversed visually on a phone so Save sits on top).
- ARIA: the root is a `footer`; the status glyph is `aria-hidden`. The message region (`__message`, the `leading` / default slot) is a polite live region (`role="status"`), so a bar that appears when the form turns dirty announces its status sentence (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages) without moving focus.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the status sentence.

## Examples

### Floating

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import SaveBar from '@aziontech/webkit/save-bar'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const saving = ref(false)

  const save = () => {
    saving.value = true
    setTimeout(() => {
      saving.value = false
    }, 1200)
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="relative flex h-64 flex-col overflow-auto">
    <div class="layout-boundary-inline flex-1 py-(--spacing-lg) text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
      The settings form scrolls under the bar.
    </div>
    <SaveBar>
      You have unsaved changes.
      <template #actions>
        <Button
          type="button"
          label="Discard"
          variant="outline"
          size="medium"
          :disabled="saving"
        />
        <Button
          label="Save"
          variant="primary"
          size="medium"
          :loading="saving"
          @click="save"
        />
      </template>
    </SaveBar>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/scroll-area.md -->

# Scroll Area

> Structural layout primitive for scrolling regions: native overflow with themed thin scrollbars and keyboard scrolling. With `fade`, the edges that still have content to scroll to fade out, each sized by the distance left on that side (capped at 64px or a sixth of the viewport), so a list reads as continuing past its frame. A sticky header inside the viewport keeps its full opacity; the top fade starts below it.

- Import: `import ScrollArea from '@aziontech/webkit/scroll-area'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A region that must scroll inside a bounded box: a navigation list, a panel body, a wide table (`orientation="horizontal"`), a code region (`orientation="both"`).
- A long list whose edges should fade while more content lies beyond them (`fade`).

## Do

- Give it a bounded height, or a flex parent that constrains it. Without a limit the content never overflows and nothing scrolls.
- The root is focusable (`tabindex` 0) and scrolls with the arrow keys, Page Up/Down and Home/End. Set `aria-label` when no visible heading names the region.
- Pass `tabindex="-1"` only when the content is itself focusable and keyboard users can already reach all of it.
- Match `orientation` to the overflow axis: `vertical` clips horizontal overflow, and `horizontal` clips vertical overflow.

## Don’t

- The region is one of several the reader resizes by dragging → use `resizable`, with a ScrollArea inside a pane if its content overflows.
- It is an application navigation rail → use `sidebar`, which already scrolls its items.
- It is a code sample → use `code-block`, which already scrolls its lines.

## Related

- `sidebar` — scrolls its navigation inside a built-in ScrollArea.
- `code-block` — runs its code lines in a ScrollArea with `orientation="both"`.
- `resizable` — draggable regions; each pane can hold a ScrollArea.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both'` | `'vertical'` | false | Scroll direction: `vertical` (lists, sidebars), `horizontal` (wide tables), `both` for two-axis overflow. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when the region is not labelled by visible text; omit when content provides context. |
| `fade` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Fades the edges that still have content to scroll to, sized by the distance left on each side. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | — |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-fade` is present while `fade` is on and at least one edge has content beyond it; the per-edge fade lengths are exposed as `--scroll-area-fade-top|bottom|left|right` on the root.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: the viewport sets only `aria-label` (from the prop) and `tabindex` itself. Every other consumer attribute — `role`, `aria-*`, `id`, listeners — is forwarded to it, so a log body can be `role="log"` with `aria-live`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ScrollArea from '@aziontech/webkit/scroll-area'
</script>

<template>
  <div
    class="h-[200px] max-w-(--container-md) rounded-(--shape-control) border border-(--border-default)"
  >
    <ScrollArea
      orientation="vertical"
      aria-label="Scrollable content"
      class="h-full"
    >
      <div class="p-(--spacing-4) text-body-sm text-(--text-default)">
        Jokester began sneaking into the castle in the middle of the night and leaving jokes all
        over the place: under the king's pillow, in his soup, even in the royal toilet. The king was
        furious, but he couldn't seem to stop Jokester. And then one day, the king tripped over one
        of Jokester's whoopee cushions and fell into the moat. He was so embarrassed that he decided
        to make Jokester the official court jester.
      </div>
    </ScrollArea>
  </div>
</template>
```

# Section Header

> The heading of one band inside a page: an h2 with a one-line description, a copy-link button that appears when the heading is hovered or focused (when it has an `anchor`), and the band's own actions on the right. Below `md` the actions drop under the copy.

- Import: `import SectionHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/section-header'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use SectionHeader for the h2 heading of one band inside a console page; for marketing pages use SectionTitle, and for a settings band use SettingsSection.
- A band of a page that holds a card, a table or a list: Payment information on Billing, Get started on a resource, General in a create form.
- A band that someone should be able to link to (`anchor`).

## Do

- Keep the description to one sentence; put longer guidance in the band body.
- Set `anchor` on bands people link to, so the h2 takes the id and the copy-link button appears.
- Keep band actions to one or two outlined medium buttons.

## Don’t

- The page title → use `page-header`.
- A settings band whose guidance sits in a Hint and whose body is a card of setting rows → use `settings-section`.

## Related

- `page-header` — the page's h1.
- `settings-section` — the settings band with a Hint, a gutter copy-link and an optional disclosure; use it, not this, for a band of `SettingsRow`s.
- `section-title` — the marketing section heading (centred, left or horizontal); use it on site pages, this one in the console.
- `copy-button` — the copy-link affordance it renders.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The band title, rendered as an h2. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One sentence under the title. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Heading scale of the title (subset: no `large`). |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | Id of the h2 that a hash link targets; when set, a copy-link button appears beside the title on hover or focus. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | — | Rich description content (links, inline code); replaces the `description` prop. |
| `actions` | — | The band's own actions, on the right of the copy. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` / `focus-within` (reveals the copy-link button)
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop on the root and the h2
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/section-header`; the actions take the full width under the copy below `@md` of the box and sit beside it from `@md`.
- Hover-free devices: the copy-link stays visible where the primary pointer cannot hover (`@media (hover: none)`), so it is never a hover-only affordance.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the copy-link `CopyButton` and the actions carry their own focus ring; focusing the copy-link reveals it.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the copy-link button, then the actions; `Enter`/`Space` copies the link.
- ARIA: the copy-link button is named "Copy link to the {title} section" and announces "Link copied".
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title and the description.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the reveal.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import SectionHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/section-header'
</script>

<template>
  <SectionHeader
    title="Payment information"
    description="Where invoices are sent, and whether the plan renews on its own."
    anchor="payment-information"
  >
    <template #actions>
      <Button
        label="Update"
        variant="outline"
        size="medium"
      />
    </template>
  </SectionHeader>
</template>
```

<!-- components/separator.md -->

# Separator

> Thin separator line that visually splits content into groups. Renders as a full-width hairline (`horizontal`) or full-height hairline (`vertical`), and can carry centered content (an "Or"-style label) when the default slot or `label` prop is set. Unlike `ScrollArea` it adds no scrolling behaviour; it is a purely decorative-yet-semantic boundary exposing `role="separator"`.

- Import: `import Separator from '@aziontech/webkit/separator'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Separate groups of content inside a card, form, panel or menu.
- An "Or" break between two alternative paths (social sign-in and email) with `label`.
- A vertical rule between inline items in a toolbar or meta line.

## Do

- Size a vertical divider through its wrapper (`flex h-4 items-center`); its own `h-full` beats a height class passed to it, and in an `items-center` row it collapses to zero height.
- Keep `label` to a word or two; the default slot replaces it when you need inline markup.
- Use it to separate groups, not to add spacing; it renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`.

## Don’t

- The break between two page sections → use `section-gap`.
- A bounded region that scrolls → use `scroll-area`.

## Related

- `section-gap` — the frame that divides page sections, with its own rules and vertical air.
- `scroll-area` — scrolling container; Separator adds no scrolling.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | false | Layout axis of the separator line. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback centered text shown when the default slot is empty. |
| `decorative` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Purely visual line: renders role none instead of separator when there is no label. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Centered content; overrides `label` when provided. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-orientation` mirrors the `orientation` prop: `horizontal` | `vertical`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — the separator is non-interactive and not in the tab order.
- Keyboard map: not applicable — no interactive controls.
- ARIA: root carries `role="separator"` and `aria-orientation="{orientation}"`. A labelled divider keeps the `separator` role and is named by its label through `aria-labelledby` (a separator's children are presentational, so the text alone would not reach assistive technology). `decorative` marks a line that only draws (between items that are already grouped): without a label it renders `role="none"` and no `aria-orientation`, so assistive technology skips it. A labelled divider ignores `decorative` and stays a named separator. It defaults to `false` so existing dividers keep the `separator` role.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state — the muted label text meets the body-text ratio against canvas/surface.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states — not applicable; the component declares no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable; the component is non-interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Separator from '@aziontech/webkit/separator'
</script>

<template>
  <Separator orientation="horizontal" />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/separator.md](components/separator.md).

<!-- components/settings-row.md -->

# Settings Row

> One setting inside a flush `Card`: an `Item` whose content carries the title and description, with the control placed by what it needs. A typed or picked field sits in a right cell capped at the 3xs container so every field on the card ends at the same edge (`field`); a switch or a button sits hard right at its natural width (`compact`); a textarea, list, radio group or editor drops under the copy at the full measure (`stacked`). A child setting indents one or two levels under a rule (`depth`). The copy top-aligns with the control, and the row keeps its two columns at every width (the description clamps to two lines); `stackable` opts a row into moving a `field` control under the copy in a narrow box.

- Import: `import SettingsRow from '@aziontech/webkit/settings-row'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Every row of a settings card: account settings, build settings, create pages, resource settings.
- A field with a validation message under it (put the `FieldError` in the default slot after the control).

## Do

- The title is the label: give the control the same text as `aria-label`.
- Pick `variant` by the control: `field` for Input and Select, `compact` for Switch and Button, `stacked` for Textarea, radio groups and editors.
- Show a validation message only after Save was pressed.
- Use `depth` only for a setting that applies when the row above it is on, and render it with `v-if` on that state.
- Keep the default two columns on a phone: the title and the clamped description sit on the start side, the control on the end side, both aligned to the top. This is the console layout at every width.
- Set `stackable` only when the field needs the full measure to be usable in a narrow box (a long URL or a code value in a side drawer); never to fix a centred or cramped look.
- Let a tall control (an input group of three nameservers, a textarea) sit beside the copy: the title stays at the top of the row.
- Do not wrap the row or its copy in your own flex box to change the alignment or to stack it; use `variant` and `stackable`.
- Do not set `stackable` on a `compact` row: a switch or a button always stays at the end side.
- Keep the description to the one sentence that says what the setting does, and put the rest of a longer explanation in `hint`: the description clamps to two lines, and the Hint glyph beside the title reveals the full text on hover or focus.

## Don’t

- A stand-alone form field with a visible label above it → use `field` around the control (`Field`, `FieldLabel`, `FieldDescription`).
- A read-only list of label and value pairs → use `key-value-list`.
- A navigable list row → use `item` directly.

## Related

- `settings-section` — the band the card of rows sits in.
- `item` — the row primitive it renders; place rows in an `Item.List` inside the card.
- `field-error` — the required or invalid message under the control.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The setting name; the control takes the same text as its aria-label. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One sentence under the title that says what the setting does. |
| `variant` | `'field' \| 'compact' \| 'stacked'` | `'field'` | false | Where the control sits relative to the copy. |
| `depth` | `0 \| 1 \| 2` | `0` | false | Indent depth under a rule, for a setting that only applies when its parent is on. |
| `stackable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Below the md container of the row, move a field control under the copy at full width. |
| `hint` | `string` | `''` | false | Extra guidance in a Hint glyph beside the title; empty renders no glyph. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The control, plus the FieldDescription message under it when there is one. |
| `title` | — | Rich title content (a Tag); replaces the `title` prop. The `hint` glyph still renders after it. |
| `description` | — | Rich description content (links, inline code); replaces the `description` prop. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hinted` (a `Hint` glyph after the title when `hint` is set)
- `data-row-variant` mirrors `variant` and `data-depth` mirrors `depth` on the root; `data-stackable` is set when `stackable` is on
- Alignment: the copy and the control align to the top of the row, so a title stays level with the first line of a tall control.
- Responsive: the row is the `@container/settings-row`. By default the row keeps its two columns at every width: the copy shrinks (the description clamps to two lines with an ellipsis) and a `field` control keeps the end cell, capped at the 3xs container. With `stackable`, below `@md` of the row a `field` control moves under the copy at full width.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the control in the default slot.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the control; the row is not interactive.
- ARIA: the row is an `Item` (a `listitem` inside `Item.List`); the control carries `aria-label` equal to the title, and a message is linked with `aria-describedby`.
- Truncation: the two-line clamp of the description is visual only; the full text stays in the DOM, so assistive technology reads all of it. For sighted users, `hint` is the way to the full explanation: its glyph is a focusable button whose accessible name and tooltip are the hint text, reachable with `Tab` and revealed on hover or focus.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title and the muted description.

## Examples

### SettingsCard

```vue
<script setup>
  import Card from '@aziontech/webkit/card'
  import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'
  import Item from '@aziontech/webkit/item'
  import SettingsRow from '@aziontech/webkit/settings-row'
  import Textarea from '@aziontech/webkit/textarea'
  import { reactive } from 'vue'

  const form = reactive({ companyName: '', taxId: '', billingEmails: '' })
</script>

<template>
  <Card :padded="false">
    <template #default>
      <Item.List>
        <SettingsRow
          title="Company Name"
          description="The legal entity that owns this account."
        >
          <Input
            v-model="form.companyName"
            size="large"
            class="w-full"
            aria-label="Company Name"
          />
        </SettingsRow>
        <SettingsRow
          title="Tax ID"
          description="The tax identification number of the entity that owns this account."
        >
          <Input
            v-model="form.taxId"
            size="large"
            class="w-full"
            aria-label="Tax ID"
          />
        </SettingsRow>
        <SettingsRow
          title="Billing emails"
          description="Billing is forwarded to every address listed here. Separate each one with a semicolon ( ; )."
          variant="stacked"
        >
          <Textarea
            v-model="form.billingEmails"
            class="w-full"
            :rows="3"
            aria-label="Billing emails"
          />
        </SettingsRow>
      </Item.List>
    </template>
  </Card>
</template>
```

<!-- components/settings-section.md -->

# Settings Section

> A band of a settings page: an h2 with a `Hint` glyph that carries the one-sentence guidance, over the band body (usually a flush `Card` of `SettingsRow` rows). Bands stack at the section gap with no rule between them. An anchored band shows a copy-link button in the gutter when the heading is hovered or focused; a collapsible band turns the heading into a disclosure that unfolds the body along the grid track.

- Import: `import SettingsSection from '@aziontech/webkit/settings-section'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use SettingsSection for a band of a settings page whose body is SettingsRow rows; any other band heading is a SectionHeader.
- Every settings page and create page: a resource's Settings tab, Account Settings, a create form, a create drawer.
- An Advanced band that starts closed (`collapsible`).

## Do

- One sentence of guidance in `hint`; the title names the band in one or two words.
- Set `anchor` on bands people link to.
- Use `collapsible` only for an Advanced band whose defaults are right for most people; it starts closed.
- Stack the bands inside one form column (`layout-column-form`); the first band takes no top margin.

## Don’t

- A band whose heading carries a description line and actions → use `section-header`.
- The page title → use `page-header`.
- A disclosure list of several independent panels → use `accordion`.

## Related

- `settings-row` — the rows inside the band's card.
- `card` — the flush (`:padded="false"`) surface the rows sit on.
- `hint` — the guidance glyph beside the title.
- `section-header` — the band heading with a description and actions. Pick by content: a settings band of `SettingsRow`s (a Hint, a gutter copy-link, an optional disclosure) is `SettingsSection`; a console band heading with a description and its own actions is `SectionHeader`; a marketing section heading is `section-title`. The three share the h2 and the copy-link anchor; folding SettingsSection's heading onto SectionHeader is a planned refactor, not a behaviour change.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The band title, rendered as an h2. |
| `hint` | `string` | `''` | false | One-sentence guidance shown in a Hint glyph beside the title. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | Id of the h2 that a hash link targets; when set, a copy-link button appears in the gutter on hover or focus. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Turns the title into a disclosure that folds the band body. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Glyph shown before the title of a collapsible band (e.g. `az az-settings`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The band body, usually a flush Card of SettingsRow rows. |
| `title` | — | Rich title content; replaces the `title` prop text in the h2. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## v-model

- **`v-model:open`** — `boolean`, default `false`. Whether a collapsible band is unfolded; it updates when the disclosure toggles. Ignored unless `collapsible`.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` / `focus-within` (reveals the copy-link button)
- `data-state` on the root: `open` | `closed` when `collapsible`
- `data-state` on the body: `open` | `closed`, mirroring whether it is unfolded
- Only a collapsible band folds along the `0fr`/`1fr` grid track (`data-collapsible` on the body); a band that is not collapsible lays its body out in normal flow, so it has no track that can resolve to zero height.
- Responsive: the body is the `@container/settings-section`, so rows and fields inside lay out for the section, not the window.
- Hover-free devices: the copy-link button is shown inline after the title where the pointer cannot hover (`@media (hover: none)`), instead of floating outside the start edge on hover.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the copy-link and the disclosure button (plus `ring-offset` on the disclosure).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the copy-link, the disclosure and then the body; `Enter`/`Space` toggles the disclosure.
- ARIA: the disclosure is a `button` inside the h2 with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the body (`useId`); a folded body is `inert` and `aria-hidden`. The copy-link button is named "Copy link to the {title} section"; after a successful copy its glyph turns into a check and its name into "Link copied" for two seconds, then both return.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.

## Examples

# Sidebar

> Helps users move between views or sections. Composable application sidebar with optional header and footer regions; navigation content scrolls inside a built-in `ScrollArea`. It also owns **the rail gesture** — sizing the sidebar by dragging its trailing edge, and collapsing it out of the layout entirely. That belongs here rather than in each shell: the interaction is not a small one (a pointer drag that crosses the collapse boundary continuously, a keyboard equivalent, token-derived bounds, a phase-aware transition, and an affordance that brings a collapsed rail back), and every app that has a sidebar wants the same one. Two shells re-implementing it is how the two drift apart. Both halves are **opt-in and independent**: `resizable` adds the drag, `collapsible` adds the collapse trigger and the edge affordance. `collapsible="icon"` collapses to an **icon rail** instead of leaving the layout, and `shortcut` adds the Ctrl+B / Cmd+B toggle. With neither set the component renders exactly as it always has, with the host owning the width — every existing consumer is unaffected.

- Import: `import SidebarRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Sidebar from '@aziontech/webkit/sidebar'`
- Category: layout · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Sidebar only when not using ConsoleLayout, which already renders the rail; put a SidebarMenu inside it.
- The persistent navigation column of an app shell, with an optional header (brand, workspace switcher) and footer (profile, settings) around a scrolling `SidebarMenu`.
- The user should be able to resize the rail by dragging its trailing edge (`resizable`) or take it out of the layout and bring it back (`collapsible`).
- Wide work surfaces where the navigation should shrink to its icons rather than disappear (`collapsible="icon"`), so a destination stays one click away.
- The rail's size or collapsed state must survive navigation or reloads — bind `v-model:width` and `v-model:open` and persist them in the app.

## Do

- Put a `SidebarMenu` with `role="presentation"` in the default slot; the sidebar already renders the `nav` landmark and its `aria-label` (default `'Sidebar'`) names the region.
- Group the rows with `SidebarMenu.Group`; the sidebar has no group part of its own.
- Without `resizable` or `collapsible`, size the rail with a width class on the root; with either set, the sidebar owns the width and clamps it between `min-width-token` and `max-width-token`.
- When the sidebar is revealed after mount (for example leaving a mobile layout where it was hidden), call the exposed `measure()` so the rail does not keep a zero width.
- Keep the profile block in the `footer` slot; with `collapsible`, the collapse trigger renders in the same footer row.
- With `collapsible="icon"`, give every top-level `SidebarMenu.Item` and drill `SidebarMenu.SubTrigger` an icon: rows without one (and inline sub-menus) step aside in the rail. Use the `{ rail }` slot scope to compact header and footer content (an avatar without the name).
- Turn on `shortcut` for one sidebar per page only; Ctrl+B / Cmd+B is a page-wide key.

## Don’t

- Adjacent work areas the reader resizes (editor beside a preview, a terminal under it) → use `resizable`.
- Horizontal top-level navigation with dropdown panels → use `navigation-menu`.
- A temporary panel that slides over the page → use `drawer`.

## Related

- `sidebar-menu` — the navigation rows, groups and drill levels that go in the sidebar's default slot.
- `resizable` — draggable splits between content regions; the sidebar's rail gesture is for navigation only.
- `app-header` — the top bar that usually sits above the sidebar in an app shell.
- `console-layout` — the console layout template that composes the header, the sidebar and the page.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Sidebar`). |
| `resizable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Adds the drag handle on the trailing edge; dragging past the minimum collapses the rail. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean \| SidebarCollapsible` | `false` | false | Adds the collapse trigger; `true` or `'offcanvas'` takes a collapsed sidebar out of the layout (with the edge affordance that brings it back), `'icon'` keeps an icon rail. |
| `shortcut` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lets Ctrl+B / Cmd+B toggle `open` while the sidebar is collapsible. Ignored while focus is in an editable field. |
| `minWidthToken` | `string` | `'--container-3xs'` | false | Theme container token the sized width is clamped up to, read off the document at runtime. |
| `maxWidthToken` | `string` | `'--container-sm'` | false | Theme container token the sized width is clamped down to, read off the document at runtime. |
| `collapseAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the collapse trigger. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Collapse sidebar`). |
| `expandAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the control and the grab bar that bring a collapsed rail back. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Expand sidebar`). |
| `resizeAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the drag handle separator. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Resize sidebar`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |
| `width` | `number \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:width`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | { rail: boolean } | The navigation. `rail` is true while the sidebar is collapsed to its icon rail. |
| `header` | { rail: boolean } | Named slot. Use `rail` to compact the content in the icon rail. |
| `footer` | { rail: boolean } | Named slot. The collapse trigger renders after this content in the same row, under one full-width separator, so a profile block and the trigger read as one footer. In the icon rail the row stacks and the trigger becomes the expand button. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-footer`

## Sub-components

The compound `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar` (its `index.ts`) attaches every part for dot-notation —
`Sidebar.Header`, `Sidebar.Footer` — and `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-root` is the
standalone, tree-shakeable root with nothing attached. The flat sub-component paths below keep
working.

- `sidebar-footer.vue` — Public sub-component `sidebar-footer`.
- `sidebar-header.vue` — Public sub-component `sidebar-header`.

`Sidebar` does not import `SidebarMenu` and `SidebarMenu` does not import `Sidebar`. Two things pass between
them: the ring-offset surface below, and the sidebar context (`SidebarInjectionKey`, read with
`inject(…, null)` so a `SidebarMenu` outside a sidebar is unaffected), which tells the menu rows whether
the sidebar is an icon rail, which side their tooltips open on, the `Tooltip` component to wrap a rail row in (handed down so
`SidebarMenu` bundles no tooltip of its own), and how to expand it.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `true` | `update:open` | Whether the rail is in the layout. `false` collapses it: out of the layout (`collapsible` `true` / `'offcanvas'`) or down to its icon rail (`'icon'`) — by the trigger, the drag crossing the snap boundary, the keyboard nudge, or a double-click on the handle. Same name as shadcn's Sidebar `open`; the layouts that compose it call the same state `navigationOpen`. |
| `v-model:width` | `number \| null` | `null` | `update:width` | The sized width in px, already clamped to the token bounds and emitted continuously during a drag. `null` means _not sized yet_: the sidebar seeds it from its own natural width on mount, after which the gesture owns it. px is the model's native unit because it is the outcome of a pointer gesture; the **bounds** come from tokens (`minWidthToken` / `maxWidthToken`). |

Every model is inert unless `resizable` or `collapsible` is set. With neither, no inline width is
applied and the host's own `class="w-[280px]"` governs exactly as before. The models are declared
with `defineModel`, so their `update:*` events are not hand-declared.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state="closed"` on the root while the rail is collapsed (out of the layout, or down to the icon rail), `data-state="open"` otherwise
- `data-rail` on the root while `collapsible="icon"` and collapsed; the rail stays in the layout at
  `var(--size-14)`, is **not** `inert` or `aria-hidden`, renders no edge affordance, and its footer
  trigger becomes `__expand-button` (`Expand sidebar`). Menu rows inside it carry `data-rail` too:
  labels become screen-reader-only and move into a `Tooltip`, tags and group labels step aside,
  rows without an icon and inline sub-menus are hidden.
- `data-resizing` on the root and on the handle while a pointer drag is in flight
- `data-preview` on the collapsed edge zone while it is showing the rail's preview sliver
- `data-state` / `data-resizing` / `data-preview` are **reported state, not the motion
  driver**: the collapse/expand animation itself runs off the hidden checkbox's `:checked` (see
  Motion & Animations), so these attributes exist for consumer styling hooks and for tests, not
  because the component's own CSS depends on them for that transition.
- `data-hydrated` on the root once Vue has mounted — internal only (switches the native
  `resize: horizontal` pre-hydration fallback back off in favor of the JS-driven handle); not a
  documented consumer styling hook.
- `data-settled` on the root and on the panel two frames after mount — internal only (gates the
  rail's motion off until then, so a state restored at mount lands in place; see Motion &
  Animations); not a documented consumer styling hook.
- Region testids derived from the root: `__panel` (the fixed-width inner panel),
  `__collapse-input` (the hidden checkbox that carries the collapsed state, `!open`, for CSS — not an interactive
  control; see Accessibility), `__header`, `__nav`, `__scroll`, `__footer`, `__collapse` (the
  trigger), `__handle` (the drag separator), `__expand` / `__expand-button` (the collapsed
  affordance)
- A collapsed offcanvas rail carries `inert` + `aria-hidden`, so it holds no tab stops while it is out; an icon rail keeps its rows reachable

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
  The **scroll viewport is not a tab stop** (`tabindex="-1"` on the built-in `ScrollArea`): a scroll
  region needs one only when nothing inside it is focusable, and this one holds a `SidebarMenu` of rows —
  so `Tab` reaches the first row directly instead of the box around it.
  The region also keeps `var(--spacing-2xs)` of padding — and the same as `scroll-padding` — inside
  the clip, because the first row's focus ring (`ring-2` over `ring-offset-2`) reaches 4 px past the
  row and a viewport flush against it would cut the ring off.
  The **drag handle is a focusable `role="separator"`**, so the gesture has a keyboard equivalent:
  `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` nudge the width, `ArrowLeft` past the snap boundary collapses, and
  `ArrowRight` from the collapsed splitter brings the rail back. Pointer-wise that same collapsed
  splitter is click-to-restore as well as drag-to-size, so the edge is never a drag-only control.
  Right-to-left: the rail sits on the inline start, so in an `rtl` subtree the keys and the drag
  mirror (`ArrowLeft` and a leftward drag widen it, `ArrowRight` narrows it), the expand affordance
  slides in from the right, and its tooltip opens on the left.
- **Shortcut** (`shortcut`): Ctrl+B / Cmd+B toggles `open` from anywhere on the page, except
  while focus is in an input, a textarea, a select or a contenteditable host, and not when another
  handler already called `preventDefault`. The collapse and expand triggers announce it with
  `aria-keyshortcuts="Control+B Meta+B"`.
- **Icon rail** (`collapsible="icon"`): every row keeps its label as its accessible name (visually
  hidden, not removed) and shows it in a `Tooltip` on hover and focus, opening toward the inline
  end (`right`, `left` under `rtl`). Activating a drill row in the rail expands the sidebar first.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component. Each
  separator is named (`resizeAriaLabel` / `expandAriaLabel`) because a bare separator announces
  nothing about what it sizes; the collapse trigger is named by `collapseAriaLabel`.
- A focusable `role="separator"` is a **window splitter**, so both separators report their position:
  `aria-valuenow` (the sized width in px, `0` while collapsed), `aria-valuemin="0"` and
  `aria-valuemax` (the resolved `maxWidthToken`). `aria-valuemin` is `0` rather than the minimum
  width token because collapsed is a real position of this splitter — the rail never rests between
  1 px and the minimum, and reporting the token bound would put the collapsed position outside the
  range the control announces. Without these, `axe` reports `aria-required-attr` and a screen reader
  announces a separator carrying no information at all.
- A **collapsed rail carries `inert` and `aria-hidden`** — the content is still mounted so its width
  can animate, and it must not be reachable while it is out of the layout. That is why the control
  that brings it back is a sibling of the rail rather than inside it.
- The **hidden checkbox that mirrors the collapsed state (`!open`)** (`__collapse-input`) carries `aria-hidden="true"`
  and `tabindex="-1"`: it is a CSS state carrier, not a second control, so it is never reachable by
  keyboard or announced by a screen reader. The trigger's accessible name and role are unaffected —
  the consumer-facing control is still the `IconButton`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states; the width /
  transform / opacity transition is dropped entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive. The drag handle is a **justified
  deviation**: it is a `var(--spacing-xs)`-wide edge strip, which is the target a pointer resize
  wants, and it is not the only route — the trigger, the keyboard nudge, and double-click all reach
  the same state, so no capability depends on hitting it.

```vue
                      aria-hidden="true"
                  /></template>
                </DropdownMenuItem>
              </DropdownMenuGroup>
            </DropdownMenu>
          </div>
        </SidebarFooter>
      </template>
    </Sidebar>
  </div>
</template>
```
