<!-- components/sidebar-menu.md -->

# Sidebar Menu

> A vertical, hierarchical navigation menu. It owns no shell and no layout of its own: it is **injected into** a host built for it — `Sidebar`, or the rail of `ConsoleLayout` and `DocLayout` — and renders three structures through one compound: **groups** that separate rows under a title, **condensed rows** that own children and expand in place behind an indent rail, and **drill rows** that replace the menu with a second-level menu. Unlike `navigation-menu` — the horizontal megamenu — this menu is vertical, recursive, and owns a view stack. Its box model follows Cloudflare Kumo's `Sidebar` (<https://kumo-ui.com/components/sidebar/>): full-width rows, padding inside the row rather than on the list, and indentation carried by the nested list's `padding-left`. Per [`migration.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.claude/rules/migration.md) only that _structure_ is adopted — every _value_ is expressed in our own tokens (see [`styling.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.claude/rules/styling.md)). Kumo's raw utilities (`min-h-8.5`, `rounded-lg`, `gap-2.5`, `pl-7`, `my-3`, a `cubic-bezier` literal) are all things the token rules forbid outright; the mapping is in Tokens, and the single value with no token behind it is in Theme gaps.

- Import: `import SidebarMenuRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-menu-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import SidebarMenu from '@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-menu'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use SidebarMenu only for the navigation tree inside Sidebar, ConsoleLayout or DocLayout; a nested data hierarchy is a Tree, and row actions are a DropdownMenu.
- Any navigation region grouped by product or concern — placed inside `Sidebar` (a drawer included), or the rail of `ConsoleLayout` or `DocLayout`.
- A documentation tree that nests two or three levels and must show its indentation structurally.
- A settings-style area where activating a row should replace the menu with that row's own menu, then return.
- Navigation whose tree comes from a manifest or route config rather than hand-authored markup (use `groups`).

## Do

- Put every `SidebarMenu.Item` and `SidebarMenu.Sub` inside a `SidebarMenu.Group` or an **inline** `SidebarMenu.SubContent`. Those own the `<ul>`; a row outside one is a `<li>` with no list, which is invalid HTML. A group with no `label` is the correct way to express an unlabeled block — including inside a **drill** `SidebarMenu.SubContent`, which is a level container rather than a list precisely so it can hold groups.
- Treat a drilled level as a whole menu, because it is one: give it groups and labels the way the root has them. A second-level nav that is only flat rows is a missed opportunity, not a constraint of the component.
- Let the host own width, padding and scrolling. The menu fills the width it is given and adds no outer margin, so it drops into `Sidebar`, a drawer or the `ConsoleLayout` / `DocLayout` rail unchanged.
- Do not render a `SidebarMenu` inside a page body. Page navigation lives in the rail, two levels at most, and a page has only its tabs; a route appears once per screen. The lint `webkit/no-page-navigation-menu` warns on a `SidebarMenu` in a page body, and `ConsoleLayout` warns in development when one repeats a rail row.
- Keep padding **inside the row**, never on the list. Every list (`Group`'s `<ul>`, `SubContent`'s `<ul>`) is a bare `m-0 list-none p-0 flex flex-col`; the row owns `px-(--spacing-sm)` and `min-h-8`. That is what lets a row's hover surface span the full menu width instead of stopping short of a list inset.
- **The rail means parentage, not membership.** It is drawn only by an inline `SidebarMenu.SubContent`, where it ties children to the row above them. A `SidebarMenu.Group` draws none and indents nothing: its label already marks the section, so a rail there would spend the same ink saying something the label has said and dilute what the rail means everywhere else. A grouped row therefore sits flush with an ungrouped one.
- Indentation is the nested list's `padding-left`, not a margin on each row — so the rail, which is drawn relative to that padding box, stays aligned no matter what a row contains.
- One step of nesting is `--sidebar-menu-indent` = `calc(var(--spacing-sm) + var(--spacing-md))` (28 px), the step the reference sidebar uses. It is deliberately **narrower than the row's own icon column** (40 px), which is a chosen trade: a tighter tree, at the cost of a child's label landing slightly left of its parent's rather than aligned with it. Widening it to 40 px would align the columns and read as more indentation.
- **One content column, `var(--spacing-sm)`.** Every row type starts its content on it, whatever the row is: a group title's text, an icon-bearing row's **glyph** (its box pads by `var(--spacing-2xs)`, and the glyph's centring inside a `size-8` box carries it the rest of the way), and an icon-less row's label — a `SubTrigger` without a glyph included — (`pl-(--spacing-sm)` directly). A `SubTrigger` that does carry one (drill only) switches to the icon-bearing inset, so both cases land on the column. Nesting shifts the whole column by exactly one `--sidebar-menu-indent`, so the alignment cascades at every depth. Measured: level 1 content at 12 px for all four row types, level 2 at 40 px.
- **The rail descends from that column**, so `--sidebar-menu-rail-x` is `var(--spacing-sm)` — one value for every parent, not a per-row calculation. The elbow spans from that line to the child **row's left edge** (`--sidebar-menu-indent - --sidebar-menu-rail-x`) and stops there: it must never reach the child's content, because the row's box begins at the indent and its hover and selected surfaces fill that box, so a wider elbow would be drawn underneath them. **The rail lives in the gutter beside the rows, never on top of one.** Every token involved is fixed at all breakpoints, unlike `--spacing-lg` / `--spacing-xl`, which would drift the elbow.
- **A row renders no icon box when it has no icon.** An empty box misreports where the row's content starts, so the label sits off the column its siblings hold and the rail anchors to blank space. This rule is what makes the column hold.
- Hover and active are `::before` / `::after` **ghost layers** per the interactive-states standard ([`component-states.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.claude/rules/component-states.md)) — never a `transition-colors` on the row root, and never a `background-color` swap that discards the selected fill.
- Pick one affordance per meaning: `chevron-down` expands children in place, `chevron-right` replaces the menu. A **group title carries no affordance at all** — it separates rows without folding them, so it never competes with the rows it labels. Folding belongs to a row, which has a chevron and a rail to say which rows it owns.
- **The menu is typed in the `label` family, not `body`.** A menu row is compact UI text, which is what `.text-label-*` is for. Rows — `SidebarMenu.Item` and `SidebarMenu.SubTrigger` — are `.text-label-md` (14 px) in `var(--text-default)`, and `SidebarMenu.Back` keeps that same class even though it is a button rather than a row, so it reads at the rows' size instead of shrinking into chrome. **Only the first-level group title is smaller and muted:** `.text-label-sm` (12 px) in `var(--text-muted)`, which replaced the overline and is the one place the menu changes register. Hierarchy below that is carried by the indent and the rail, not by shrinking each level — and a component with two render branches must give both the same label class, or the same menu renders two sizes.
- **A row's destination is `href`, and only `href`.** A `SidebarMenuNode` (and `SidebarMenu.Item` / `SidebarMenu.SubTrigger`) renders as an anchor when it has an `href`; any other key (`path`, `to`, `url`, `route`) is not read, and the row renders as a button with no destination. `path` on the root is a different thing: `v-model:path`, the drill stack.
- **Vue Router:** put the route's path in `href` (for a named route, `router.resolve(to).href`), then take over the click in `@navigate`: `(event, node) => { event.preventDefault(); router.push(node.href) }`, and derive `active-id` from the current route. The row stays a real link (open in a new tab, copy link address) while the router does the navigation. A modified click (Ctrl, ⌘, Shift, middle button) should be left to the browser: skip `preventDefault` when `event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.shiftKey || event.button !== 0`.
- Prefer `groups` when the tree is data. Hand-composing a recursive tree with `v-for` means re-implementing recursion in the consuming app; the data path renders through the same sub-components.
- Draw the elbow with borders, not a glyph: `w-(--spacing-sm) h-4 -left-(--spacing-sm) border-l border-b border-(--border-default) rounded-bl-(--shape-control)` on the row's `::before`, and the continuation on its `::after`, hidden on `:last-child`. All tokens, no SVG, and it scales with the row.
- Do not nest more than three levels. Past that the indent eats the rail's readable width; restructure with a drill row instead.
- A drill row navigates **on its one activation**, not through a second target. Splitting the row into a link plus a drill affordance is what costs a second tab stop and nests interactive elements — that shape stays rejected. Instead the single button both pushes the level and emits `navigate`, so the consumer routes to the level's landing page as it opens: one target, one tab stop, and the user never opens a second-level menu while still looking at the page they came from. The landing page is still the first item inside the level, so the level reads complete on its own.

## Don’t

- Horizontal top-of-page navigation with hover-opened panels → use `navigation-menu` instead.
- A menu that floats over the page from a trigger → use `dropdown-menu` (rows + selection) or `popover` (arbitrary content) instead. `SidebarMenu` is a sidebar navigation tree (a `navigation` landmark of list rows, what shadcn calls `SidebarMenu`), not a `role="menu"` widget such as Radix `SidebarMenu` / `DropdownMenu`.
- A searchable flat command palette → use `command` instead.
- A single collapsible content region that is not navigation → use `accordion` instead.
- Mutually exclusive in-page view switching → use `tabs` (or `toggle-group` for a compact control) instead.
- The surrounding shell itself (brand header, scroll region, user footer) → that is `Sidebar`; this menu goes inside it.
- Navigation inside a page body → never a `SidebarMenu`. Page navigation lives in the rail, two levels at most, and a page has only its `page-tabs` (rule `webkit-navigation-levels`). A resource's own pages are its tabs, at most 7; more pages become sections of one tab's page.

## Related

- `sidebar` — the most common host. It supplies the landmark, the scroll region, and the header/footer; this menu is placed in its default slot. The two are independent — neither imports the other.
- `sidebar-menu-item` — **is** `SidebarMenu.Item`. The existing standalone component, attached to this compound and reachable both ways, and now documented here rather than in a spec of its own (see Sub-components). **Two changes are made to it**: an empty icon box no longer renders, and its two branches share one label class. Its wider visual redesign remains a separate, later `spec_version: 2` revision of this spec.
- `navigation-menu` — the horizontal megamenu. Different component, different axis; see the testid note in Sub-components.
- `accordion` — a **reference only**, for content disclosure rather than navigation. `SidebarMenu` borrows the _shape_ of its collapse (a `:css="false"` `<Transition>` driving `height` in JS, because CSS cannot animate to `auto`) and nothing else. `SidebarMenu` must **not** import, wrap, extend, or re-export `accordion` or any of its sub-components: a nav group is not an accordion — it has no heading-wrapped trigger, no single/multiple `type` model, no roving arrow-key model across items, and its rows are navigation, not panels. `Group` and `Sub` own their disclosure end to end. The timing itself comes from `menu/presets/transitions.ts`, not from accordion (whose inline `'height 150ms ease-out'` literal predates and violates the token rules § Forbidden in animations).
- `tag` — renders the optional trailing badge on a row via `sidebar-menu-item`'s `tagValue`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `groups` | `SidebarMenuGroupNode[]` | `[]` | false | Data-driven navigation tree; each entry renders through `SidebarMenu.Group` and its items through `SidebarMenu.Item` / `SidebarMenu.Sub`. Composes with the `default` slot rather than replacing it. |
| `activeId` | `string` | `''` | false | Id of the node rendered as active (`aria-current`) in data-driven mode. |
| `enterOnMount` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Plays the level entrance when the stack is already populated at mount, for a restored stack whose arrival is an entrance rather than a move inside a level the user was already in. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the navigation region. Empty uses the locale catalog (`SidebarMenu`). |
| `path` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:path`). |
| `openKeys` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:openKeys`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `navigate` | `(event: MouseEvent, node: SidebarMenuNode)` | A leaf row — or the **label** of a row that owns children, of either type, since such a row is a destination as well as a container — was activated in data-driven mode; `node` is the activated tree node. A row's **arrow** does not emit it: revealing children is a move inside the menu, not a navigation. A node with nothing to point at gives the consumer nothing to route to, which is the consumer's own check. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The composed anatomy. Rendered **before** the `groups` tree, not instead of it — so a `SidebarMenu.Back` can accompany a data-driven menu, which is the one row `groups` cannot express (a drilled level would otherwise have no pointer route back). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-menu-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-menu-sub`
- `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-menu-sub-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-menu-sub-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-menu-back`
- `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-menu-item`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: an `index.ts` beside `sidebar-menu.vue` attaches every sub-component so
`<SidebarMenu.Group>` / `<SidebarMenu.Sub>` resolve from one import; the standalone imports above remain the
tree-shaking path. Two contexts flow through `provide`/`inject` (`injection-key.ts`): the **root
context** (drill stack, active id, testid) and the **sub context** (open state, ids, nesting
level), so the consumer wires nothing.

`Sub` and `SubTrigger` carry `data-state="open|closed"`, and an inline `SubTrigger`'s arrow carries
`aria-expanded`, which is what makes `SubTrigger` / `SubContent` the correct anatomy names. `Group` is deliberately **not** split
into a Trigger + Content pair: its header is a label and a toggle glyph, nothing arbitrary, so a
`label` prop with a `default` slot fallback is the honest surface and keeps the common case one
element instead of three.

- `sidebar-menu-item/sidebar-menu-item.vue` — `SidebarMenu.Item`, the leaf navigation row.
  - **Two changes made to it**, both fixing drift against the rows around it:
    1. The leading icon box renders **only when `icon` is set**. An empty `size-8` box reserved a column the row did not use, pushing an icon-less row's label off the column its siblings hold and leaving the rail anchored to blank space.
    2. Its **two branches now share one label class**. The anchor branch was `.text-label-sm` (12 px) and the button branch `.text-body-sm` (14 px), so the same menu rendered two sizes depending on whether a row happened to carry an `href` — children came out _smaller than their parents_. Both are now `.text-label-md`.
  - Props: `label?: string` (default `''` — visible text of the row), `active?: boolean` (default `false` — marks the page you are on: applies the selected surface and `aria-current="page"`), `disabled?: boolean` (default `false` — blocks interaction), `icon?: string` (default `''` — Azion icon class for the leading glyph; empty renders **no icon box at all**), `href?: string` (default `''` — renders an anchor instead of a button when set on an enabled row), `target?: '_self' | '_blank'` (default `'_self'` — link target when `href` is set), `tagValue?: string` (default `''` — short text rendered in a trailing `Tag`; empty renders none), `tagVariant?: SidebarMenuItemTagVariant` (default unset — brand look of that trailing `Tag`, `primary | accent`), `tagSeverity?: SidebarMenuItemTagSeverity` (default unset — status colour of that `Tag`, `neutral | success | info | warning | danger`, wins over `tagVariant`; with neither set the `Tag` is `info`).
  - Events: `click` — `(event: MouseEvent, item: { label: string; href: string })`. `item` carries the row's `label` and `href`, identifying which row was activated (event-first per `event-payloads.md`).
  - Slots: `default` — replaces the label text; `tag` — replaces the trailing `Tag` (its presence alone renders the tag region, with or without `tagValue`).
  - **This spec is menu-item's only spec.** It previously carried its own `.specs/menu-item.md`, which is removed with this change: a sub-component of a compound is documented in the compound's spec, the way `sidebar-menu-sub` and `sidebar-menu-group` already are. The `./menu-item` export path stays public, so its API lives here (that is what `build-catalog.mjs` reads to give the path an entry in `catalog.json`).
  - **Deliberately deferred — this release is additive only.** The redesigned row (a `size-3` icon, `var(--primary)` on the selected icon, `var(--border-default)` on the selected surface, the box model below, and `::before` / `::after` ghost layers replacing its root `transition-colors`) is a **visual breaking change** and is therefore **out of scope here**. It lands later as a `spec_version: 2` revision of _this_ spec, on a major. Until then `SidebarMenu` renders today's row: correct behaviour, old visuals.
- `sidebar-menu-group/sidebar-menu-group.vue` — A section that separates rows under a title.
  - Props: `label?: string` (default `''` — the title text; omit for an unlabeled block), `ariaLabel?: string` (default `''` — accessible name when there is no visible `label`).
  - No `open` model and no `collapsible`: a section is not a disclosure.
  - **A root group plays the rail's own entrance** when the menu mounts with an empty stack and the root's `enterOnMount` is set — the case where the reader travelled _back out_ of a level and the host remounted, leaving the group no rendered off-canvas position to slide from. A group behind a _pushed_ level does not (it should stay put, not animate in behind the level), and a **nested** group never travels on its own: the level carries it.
  - Slots: `default` — the group's rows; `label` — replaces the header text.
- `sidebar-menu-sub/sidebar-menu-sub.vue` — The `<li>` that owns a row plus that row's children.
  - Props: `defaultOpen?: boolean` (default `false` — initial state when uncontrolled; ignored for `type="drill"`, whose visibility is the root's stack).
  - Model: `open` — `boolean`, default `undefined` (unbound: uncontrolled, starts at `defaultOpen`). Controlled via `v-model:open`; `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void`.
  - Slots: `default` — exactly one `SubTrigger` and one `SubContent`.
- `sidebar-menu-sub-trigger/sidebar-menu-sub-trigger.vue` — The row that owns children, and a **heading for them**.
  - **Geometry matches `SidebarMenu.Item` exactly** — height, padding (including `py`), gap, 32 px icon box, glyph size, and the unset root font-size that sizes that glyph — so its icon and label columns line up with the leaves around it.
  - **Typography is a row's, not a title's.** Its label is `.text-label-md` in `var(--text-default)` — the same treatment `SidebarMenu.Item` uses. Only a **first-level group title** is allowed to be smaller and muted (`.text-label-sm` in `var(--text-muted)`, the thing that replaced the overline); from there every row is 14 px, a trigger included, however deep it sits. A row that owns children is still a row.
  - **One anatomy, always: a row box holding a LABEL control and an ARROW.** The root is a plain flex **box** (`relative flex h-8 w-full items-center gap-(--spacing-2xs) pr-(--spacing-2xs)`, not interactive) — nesting is not an option, since neither an anchor nor a button may contain a button, so the row itself is never the control. **The arrow is always a real `IconButton`**: it is the affordance that says the row owns children, and it must not change shape according to whether the row also has a destination.
  - **`href` decides what the LABEL does — this is the component's central decision**, and therefore how much of the row reveals the children:
    - **With an `href`** the label is an `<a>` to that destination and the **arrow alone** reveals the children. Reaching them must not cost the reader the destination.
    - **Without one** the label is a `<button>` that **reveals the children too**, so the whole row does. There is no destination to protect, and leaving the arrow as the only live target is a 28 px box — **7 % of the row's area**, with the other 93 % doing nothing — which on a phone reads as a broken menu. This is the shape most containers have (a console module's settings drill, every one of the 28 container rows in the sample's docs tree), so it is the one that must be right by default.
    - `href` is the signal rather than a boolean because it is the same data every other row in this menu uses to say where it goes, and because it makes the behaviour fall out of the tree in data-driven mode: `SidebarMenuNode.href` already exists. It also follows [`root-element.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.claude/rules/root-element.md) — the root switches element on a **data** prop, never an `as`/`is` string.
    - The **link** is an `<a href>` carrying `sub.triggerId`, the icon column and the row's typography (`min-w-0 flex-1`, so it fills what the arrow leaves). A real anchor, so middle-click and open-in-new-tab work; the consumer intercepts a plain left click for SPA routing. It announces its activation through `click` and does **nothing else** — it neither expands nor pushes. **A disabled row drops its `href` outright** (an anchor with no destination is not a link) and takes `tabindex="-1"` + `aria-disabled`.
    - The **arrow** is an `IconButton variant="ghost" size="small"` (28 px box, 12 px glyph), on every row. With `type="inline"` it is a rotating `az az-chevron-down` that toggles the sub; with `type="drill"` a static `az az-chevron-right` that pushes the sub onto the root's stack and carries **no** `aria-expanded` — nothing expands, so the attribute would be a lie. Its accessible name is derived, since the glyph alone says nothing: `Expand <label>` / `Collapse <label>` for an inline arrow (it names the state it moves to, which `aria-expanded` then confirms) and `Open <label> menu` for a drill one. It overrides `IconButton`'s ring offset with the menu's own (`ring-offset-1` against `--sidebar-menu-ring-offset`) — both with `!`, because they conflict with utilities `IconButton` puts in the same class list, where stylesheet order rather than source order would otherwise decide. Its glyph colour goes through `iconClass` (onto the `i`) for the same reason, and a **disabled** arrow paints no fill (`bg-transparent!`) with `--text-disabled` ink, because `IconButton`'s filled disabled box made the arrow the brightest thing on a row whose label had dimmed away.
    - **`aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` sit on whichever control expands the children, and on exactly one of them.** With a link that is the arrow. Without one the **label** already reveals, so it carries them and the arrow becomes a **redundant pointer affordance** for the same action: `tabindex="-1"` + `aria-hidden="true"`, so it leaves the tab order and the accessibility tree rather than announcing a second control for one thing. One tab stop per row either way.
    - **The arrow keys work from the row's own control**: `ArrowRight` expands / pushes and `ArrowLeft` collapses, so a keyboard reader reaches the children without first tabbing to an arrow.
    - Focus returns, on pop, to **whichever control pushed the level** — the arrow when the label is a link, the label otherwise.
  - **An inline trigger carries no icon; a drill trigger may.** An inline row is a separator for the rows it expands _beneath itself_, in their own column — a glyph there competes with the rows it owns, so the column belongs to them and only the arrow sits on the trailing edge. A drill row has nothing beneath it (it **replaces** the menu), so it is read as one of the destinations it is listed among and takes an icon for the same reason they do. The component **enforces** this rather than trusting the caller: `showIcon` is `icon && type === 'drill'`, so an inline trigger handed an `icon` still renders none. When shown, the glyph uses `SidebarMenu.Item`'s own box (32 px, `pl-(--spacing-2xs)`, `size-4` glyph, muted → default on hover) so it lands on the same content column as the leaves around it.
  - **A trigger announces a navigation only when it has one to announce.** In data-driven mode a node with children emits `navigate` `(event, node)` from its **link**, which exists only when the node carries an `href` — so a container that is not a destination emits nothing at all, of either type. Revealing the children never emits: that is a move inside the menu, not a navigation.
  - Props: `label?: string` (default `''` — visible row text), `type?: 'inline' | 'drill'` (default `'inline'` — whether children expand in place or replace the menu), `icon?: string` (default `''` — leading glyph; honoured for `type="drill"` only, see above), `href?: string` (default `''` — the row's own destination, and the switch between the split and unsplit shapes above), `disabled?: boolean` (default `false` — blocks revealing and navigating; suppresses **every** control of the row).
  - Events: `click` `(event: MouseEvent, item: { label: string; href: string })` — `item` carries the row's `label` and `href`, as on `SidebarMenu.Item`; the **link** was activated, so it cannot fire on a row with nowhere to go. Declared rather than left to `$attrs` fallthrough: in the split shape the root is a box holding two controls, so a fallthrough listener would sit on that box and fire for the arrow too, making "reveal the children" also trigger the consumer's navigation.
  - Slots: `default` — replaces the label text.
- `sidebar-menu-sub-content/sidebar-menu-sub-content.vue` — The children of a sub, in one of two shapes depending on its trigger's `type`.
  - `type="inline"` — a nested bare `<ul>` (`relative m-0 list-none p-0 flex flex-col`) whose `padding-left` is `calc(var(--spacing-sm) * 2)`, with the connector rail drawn on its `li` children. **Kumo indents with padding alone and draws no rail; we keep the rail** — the one place this component deliberately adds to the reference, because the Figma frame specifies it and it is what makes a three-level docs tree readable.
  - It renders the anchor `SidebarMenu.Back` teleports into, at the top of its own box (see `sidebar-menu-back`).
  - `type="drill"` — **a second-level menu with the same anatomy as the root**, not a flat row list: a `<div role="group">` labelled by its trigger, so it holds `SidebarMenu.Group`s exactly like the root does. It therefore follows the root's composition rule — rows live inside a `SidebarMenu.Group` (an unlabeled one for a flat level), because a `<ul>` here could never contain a group's `<section>`. It mounts only while its sub is on the stack, draws no rail (a pushed level is not indented), and its own mount is the one phase CSS cannot tween, so a `<Transition>` supplies the from-frame. **That Transition must always exist before its child does**, so the level is withheld for one tick after its Teleport becomes renderable and every arrival — a live push and a restored stack alike — takes the same `enter` path. `appear` is deliberately **not** used: the Teleport's target is the root's level host, a ref the root sets in _its_ `onMounted`, which runs after this component's (children mount first) — so on a restored stack the Transition and its child would first render together and the appear hooks would not play, making the entrance depend on where the reader happened to come from.
  - A `SidebarMenu.Group` nested inside a drilled level is part of that level and never steps aside on its own — the level slides as one piece. Only a **root-level** group translates out on a push.
  - Slots: `default` — the nested rows.
- `sidebar-menu-back/sidebar-menu-back.vue` — The way out of a drill level.
  - **It is a button, not a row** — the one shape rule that separates it from everything beneath it. It hugs its label (`w-fit`, `max-w-full`, `px-(--spacing-sm)`, left-aligned) instead of spanning the rail with a centred label, so its hover surface is the size of the control rather than the width of a nav row. A full-width row with a centred label is exactly the shape of the rows below it, and reading as one of them makes the single control that leaves the level the hardest thing in it to find. Its chevron sits on the menu's content column (`--spacing-sm`), so it lines up with where a row's 32 px icon box centres its glyph — but it does **not** borrow that box: the chevron is tight against the label (`--spacing-2xs`), which is what keeps the label off the rows' label column. It still uses the same label class as every row, so it reads at the rows' size rather than shrinking into chrome.
  - **Its text names the destination, not the level the reader is in** — `Back to Settings`, the way a back button always reads. Naming the current level is what a _header_ does; on a left-aligned button beside a back chevron it would read as travelling to the place you are already standing. The destination is the level below the current one on the stack; when that is the menu **root** there is no trigger to name it, so the text falls back to a bare `Back` and `label` is how a consumer supplies the name (`Back to app`). The stack is read **live**, with no hold across the slide-out: naming the current level needed one (the stack empties the instant a pop begins), naming the destination never does — a pop to the root leaves the text unchanged, and a pop between levels hands the button to the incoming level, whose own destination is what the live stack now reports. The visible text is also the **accessible name** (there is no `aria-label`), so the two cannot disagree.
  - Props: `label?: string` (default `''` — names the destination, overriding the level below on the stack; set it to name the menu root, which has no trigger to name itself).
  - Slots: `default` — replaces the label text.

**Test ids.** The root derives `data-testid="sidebar-menu"` (its own name) and each part its own name (`sidebar-menu-item`, …). The 6.0 rename from `menu` to `sidebar-menu` also ended the old clash with the horizontal `navigation-menu`, whose root used the same `navigation-menu` string.

Resulting layout (no per-component `package.json` — the root `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`
resolves every path; `.d.ts` is generated at publish time, never committed):

```
packages/webkit/src/components/navigation/
└── sidebar-menu/
    ├── sidebar-menu.vue                    (root; owns the drill stack + data mode, provides root context)
    ├── sidebar-menu-item/                  (a real sub-component)
    │   ├── sidebar-menu-item.vue
    │   └── sidebar-menu-item.test.ts
    ├── index.ts                    (compound: Group / Item / Sub / SubTrigger / SubContent / Back)
    ├── injection-key.ts            (SidebarMenuContext + SidebarMenuSubContext)
    ├── composables/
    │   ├── use-sidebar-menu-context.ts     (throws outside <SidebarMenu>)
    │   └── use-sidebar-menu-sub-context.ts (throws outside <SidebarMenu.Sub>)
    ├── presets/
    │   └── transitions.ts          (height collapse timing; imports duration/curve from animate.js)
    ├── sidebar-menu-group/
    │   └── sidebar-menu-group.vue
    ├── sidebar-menu-sub/
    │   └── sidebar-menu-sub.vue
    ├── sidebar-menu-sub-trigger/
    │   └── sidebar-menu-sub-trigger.vue
    ├── sidebar-menu-sub-content/
    │   └── sidebar-menu-sub-content.vue
    └── sidebar-menu-back/
        └── sidebar-menu-back.vue
```

**Scope — additive only.** Every file in the `sidebar-menu/` tree above is **new**. Two existing files are
touched, neither in a way a consumer can observe as a break: `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`
by **adding** keys (no existing key changes target), and `sidebar.vue` by **adding one CSS variable**
to its `<nav>` (`--sidebar-menu-ring-offset`, beside the `--sidebar-menu-item-ring-offset` it already sets) so a menu
hosted there rings against the sidebar's surface. No existing prop, default, event, slot or
`data-testid` anywhere in the package is altered, and nothing is deprecated or removed. The release
is a `feat` (minor), never a `feat!`.

Exports to add to `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` (flat public names; category lives in the
folder only). 6.0 renamed every key from `./menu*` to `./sidebar-menu*`, with no alias:

```jsonc
"./sidebar-menu": "./src/components/navigation/sidebar-menu/index.ts",
"./sidebar-menu-item": "./src/components/navigation/sidebar-menu/sidebar-menu-item/sidebar-menu-item.vue",
"./sidebar-menu-root": "./src/components/navigation/sidebar-menu/sidebar-menu.vue",
"./sidebar-menu-group": "./src/components/navigation/sidebar-menu/sidebar-menu-group/sidebar-menu-group.vue",
"./sidebar-menu-sub": "./src/components/navigation/sidebar-menu/sidebar-menu-sub/sidebar-menu-sub.vue",
"./sidebar-menu-sub-trigger": "./src/components/navigation/sidebar-menu/sidebar-menu-sub-trigger/sidebar-menu-sub-trigger.vue",
"./sidebar-menu-sub-content": "./src/components/navigation/sidebar-menu/sidebar-menu-sub-content/sidebar-menu-sub-content.vue",
"./sidebar-menu-back": "./src/components/navigation/sidebar-menu/sidebar-menu-back/sidebar-menu-back.vue"
```

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:path` | `string[]` | `[]` | `update:path` | `v-model:path` — the drill stack as ancestor node ids, outermost first. Empty at the root level. **Persist it when the host remounts** (and always when a drill row navigates, which remounts the shell in most routers) or the level closes on the very navigation that opened it. A stack supplied this way is restored **with its label, its trigger, and its entrance**: every drill sub announces the first two to the root when its trigger mounts (not only when pushed), so the restored level still names itself in the a11y tree, `SidebarMenu.Back` can still name it as a destination from a deeper level, and popping still returns focus to the row that owns it; and the level _arrives_ rather than simply being there — see the restored-level row in Motion. |
| `v-model:openKeys` | `string[]` | `[]` | `update:openKeys` | `v-model:openKeys` — ids of the inline subs currently open. Persist it when the host remounts, or expansion resets and one sub appearing to close another. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `current page` (the `active` prop), `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed` — on `Sub`, `SubTrigger` and `SubContent`. A `Group` has none: it never closes.
- `data-type` values: `inline` | `drill` — on `SubTrigger` and `SubContent`. On a trigger they sit on its root, which is always the row **box** holding its label control and its arrow.
- `data-active` mirrors the `active` prop on `SidebarMenu.Item` (on the `li` and on its link or button, which also carries `data-disabled` and, with an `icon`, `data-icon`; the row styles switch on these, not on class bindings)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on `SidebarMenu.Item` and `SubTrigger` (on the row box and on its label alike, so a test can read it from either)
- `data-level` on `SubContent` — nesting depth, drives the indent step
- `data-motion` values: `push` | `pop` | `none` — on a drill level, so the direction of the slide is a Tailwind `data-[motion=…]` variant instead of a `:class` ternary (see Motion)
- `data-level` on `SubContent` also drives the indent step at each depth
- `data-node-id` on a `Sub` rendered from `groups` — carries the `SidebarMenuNode.id` so `update:path` reports real node ids rather than generated ones
- Empty: `groups` is `[]` and the `default` slot is empty → the root renders nothing; the empty
  message belongs to the host shell, not the menu.
- Icon rail: inside a `Sidebar` collapsed with `collapsible="icon"` (read from the sidebar context
  with `inject(SidebarInjectionKey, null)`; a menu anywhere else is unaffected), `SidebarMenu.Item` carries
  `data-rail`, centres its icon in a 32 px box, renders its label screen-reader-only and shows it in
  a `Tooltip`, and drops its tag; a `SidebarMenu.Item` without an icon and an
  inline `SubTrigger` (which never has an icon) are hidden, an inline `SubContent` is hidden, a
  `Group` title becomes screen-reader-only (it still names the section), and a drill `SubTrigger`
  shows its icon in a `Tooltip` with no arrow — activating it expands the sidebar, then pushes its
  level.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-1 focus-visible:ring-offset-[var(--sidebar-menu-ring-offset,var(--bg-canvas))]` — `ring-offset-1` per the interactive-states standard ([`component-states.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.claude/rules/component-states.md)), with the offset colour handed down by the host (`Sidebar` sets `--sidebar-menu-ring-offset` to its own surface, mirroring the existing `--sidebar-menu-item-ring-offset` pattern).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` move between rows; `Enter`/`Space` activates a row, toggles an inline `Sub`, or pushes a drill level; `ArrowRight` expands a collapsed inline `Sub` or pushes a drill level; `ArrowLeft` collapses an expanded inline `Sub`, or pops one drill level when the current level is not the root; `Escape` pops one drill level.
- ARIA:
  - The root renders a plain container with `role="navigation"` and `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`. It does **not** render `<nav>`: the menu is injected into a host that may already be a `<nav>` landmark (`Sidebar` is), and nesting landmarks duplicates them in the landmark list. When the host provides the landmark, the consumer suppresses the role by passing `role="presentation"` — and **the name goes with the role**: the root renders no `aria-label` under `role="presentation"` / `"none"`, because ARIA prohibits naming a presentational element and the a11y tree drops the name anyway. The consumer therefore suppresses the landmark with one attribute rather than remembering to unset `ariaLabel` as well.
  - `Group` is a `<section>` named by its title through `aria-labelledby` (id from `useId()`), or by `aria-label` when there is no visible title. It exposes **no** `aria-expanded` and contains no control — the title is text.
  - An inline `SubTrigger` puts `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` on **whichever control expands the children** — its arrow when an `href` makes the label a link, the label itself otherwise — and never on both. When the label owns them the arrow is `aria-hidden` + `tabindex="-1"`: a redundant pointer target, not a second announced control. An announced arrow is named `Expand <label>` / `Collapse <label>`, so the state is given twice over: by the name it moves to and by `aria-expanded`.
  - A drill `SubTrigger` carries **no** `aria-expanded` on any control — it replaces the view rather than expanding one. An announced drill arrow is named `Open <label> menu`. On push, focus moves to the level's `Back` button and the pushed `<ul>` takes `aria-label` from the trigger's label; on pop, focus returns to whichever control pushed it. A level that is not current carries **both `aria-hidden` and `inert`** while it is still mounted for the slide, so it leaves the accessibility tree and the tab order together (the pattern Kumo's `SlidingViews` uses).
  - `Back` is a `<button>` whose **visible text** names its destination (`Back to Settings`, or a bare `Back` when that destination is the unnamed root) and is therefore also its accessible name — it renders no `aria-label`, so the two cannot disagree (2.5.3 Label in Name).
  - An active `SidebarMenu.Item` rendered as an anchor carries `aria-current="page"`; a disabled row carries `aria-disabled` and is removed from the tab order.
  - In a sidebar icon rail every visible row keeps its label as its accessible name (visually hidden, not removed); the `Tooltip` repeats it on hover and focus toward the inline end (`left` under `rtl`).
  - The connector rail and every chevron are `aria-hidden="true"` — decorative, and the indentation already conveys the hierarchy.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state. The rail (`var(--border-default)`, ≈1.5:1) is exempt: it is decorative and carries no information the indentation does not, so 1.4.11 does not apply.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target — **justified deviation from ≥40×40 px.** Rows are 32 px tall, matching the Figma frame's `h-button-md` and the density a product navigation needs. Every target is full-row width (≥252 px), so all clear WCAG 2.5.8's 24×24 minimum. The Figma frame's 16×16 group toggle would have failed that minimum; it is moot here, because a group title is not a control at all.

<!-- components/skip-link.md -->

# Skip Link

> The first focusable element of a page: a link that is visually hidden until it receives keyboard focus, then appears at the top-start corner and jumps to the page's main content, so a keyboard or screen-reader user bypasses the repeated header and navigation (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks). On activation it also moves focus into the target, so the next `Tab` continues from the main content in every browser. It differs from `link` in that it is invisible at rest and owns its placement and focus hand-off.

- Import: `import SkipLink from '@aziontech/webkit/skip-link'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Every page shell (console, marketing site, docs) that renders repeated navigation before the main content: place it as the first child of the shell.
- A layout whose `<main>` (or other main landmark) carries the `id` the link targets (`main` by default).

## Do

- Render one skip link per page, as the first element inside the shell, before the header; do not wrap it in `nav` or move it into the header.
- Give the main landmark the `id` the link points at (`id="main"` for the default `href`); a missing target makes the link a no-op.
- Keep the label short and name the destination ("Skip to content"); override it with `label` or the default slot only when the target is not the main content.

## Don’t

- A link inside content that should always be visible → use `link`.
- Jumping between sections of one page (an in-page table of contents) → use `link` with a `#hash` `href`.
- A page with no repeated block before its content (a bare sign-in form) gains nothing from one; do not add it there.

## Related

- `link` — the always-visible navigation link; use it for any visible jump.
- `console-layout`, `site-layout`, `doc-layout` — the page shells that render the main landmark the skip link targets.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible label, the default slot's fallback. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Skip to content`). |
| `href` | `string` | `'#main'` | false | In-page hash of the element to jump to; the element with that `id` receives focus on activation. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The link text. Fallback: `label`, then the locale catalog. |

## States

- Visual states: `hidden` (at rest: clipped to 1 px and out of the layout, still in the tab order and the accessibility tree), `focused` (shown at the top-start corner of the viewport with the surface, border, shadow and focus ring), `hover` while shown (label underlined).
- Activation: when `href` is a `#hash` that resolves to an element, the element is focused; if it is not natively focusable and has no `tabindex`, it gets `tabindex="-1"` for the hand-off and loses it on `blur`. Native hash navigation (scroll and URL hash) still runs.
- A `href` that is empty, external or names no element: the link behaves as a plain anchor; no focus hand-off.
- Not applicable: `disabled`, `loading`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `empty`, `error`, `open`/`closed` — a skip link has none of these states; no `data-*` state attribute is rendered.
- Consumer attributes (`id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, listeners, `class`) land on the anchor through `v-bind="$attrs"`.

## Accessibility

- Pattern: a native `a href` (no ARIA role); its accessible name is the visible label. It is the first focusable element so it is reached by the first `Tab` (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks).
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`; the link is fully shown on any focus (`:focus`), so it is never focused while invisible (WCAG 2.4.7), and the border keeps the outline in forced-colors mode.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` (first in the page) focuses and reveals it; `Enter` activates: the page jumps to the target and focus moves into it; `Tab` from there continues inside the main content; `Shift+Tab` / moving focus away hides it again.
- ARIA: none needed; the hidden state is visual only (clipped, not `display: none`, not `aria-hidden`), so screen readers list it.
- Contrast: `--text-default` on `--bg-surface` ≥ 4.5:1 in light and dark; the ring token ≥ 3:1 against `--bg-canvas`.
- Motion: none (see `## Motion & Animations`).
- Touch target: min height 40 px while shown (44 px on coarse pointers).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
  import SkipLink from '@aziontech/webkit/skip-link'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md)">
    <SkipLink href="#skip-link-demo-content" />
    <nav
      aria-label="Product"
      class="flex flex-wrap gap-(--spacing-md)"
    >
      <Link
        label="Overview"
        href="https://example.com/overview"
        size="medium"
      />
      <Link
        label="Pricing"
        href="https://example.com/pricing"
        size="medium"
      />
      <Link
        label="Documentation"
        href="https://example.com/docs"
        size="medium"
      />
    </nav>
    <section
      id="skip-link-demo-content"
      aria-label="Content"
      class="text-body-md text-(--text-default)"
    >
      Focus lands here after the skip link is activated.
    </section>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/stepper.md -->

# Stepper

> A vertical rail that names the steps of one task, says which step the reader is on, and carries the progress between them on the line that joins the dots. It is the left column of a multi-step surface — a create wizard, a guided setup — while the content of the current step fills the column beside it. It is **vertical only**, by design. The rail runs the full height of the surface so the connector between two dots is the thing that measures progress; a horizontal variant would be a different component with a different job (a compact progress ribbon), not a prop on this one.

- Import: `import StepperRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/stepper-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Stepper from '@aziontech/webkit/stepper'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Stepper for the step rail of a multi-step task in the app; for an ordered create with its Cancel/Previous/Next footer use Wizard, and for a guided tutorial use TutorialPanel.
- A task is split into ordered steps and only one is on screen at a time (a create wizard, a guided setup).
- The reader needs to see how many steps are left and go back to one they already answered.
- A step can fail validation, or sit in flight, and the rail has to say so without leaving the step.

## Do

- Give every step a title that names the decision (`Where it runs`), not the control (`Select`).
- Keep steps reachable backwards and closed forwards: mark a step `disabled` until the one before it is answered.
- Set `status="error"` only after the reader tried to advance — a step is not wrong while it is unanswered.
- One `Stepper` per surface. Two rails on one screen ask the reader which task they are in.
- The rail is navigation, not the form. Put the fields in the content column, never inside a step's slot.

## Don’t

- Numbered instructions inside a document, where every step is read at once → use `doc-steps` (`DocSteps.Step`).
- Progress with no discrete, nameable steps (a percentage, an upload) → use `progress`.
- Switching between peer views that are not ordered and have no completion → use `tabs`.
- A provisioning log that reports what a server is doing, rather than what the reader must answer → use `flow-diagram`.

## Related

- `doc-steps` — the same numbered-dot shape for prose; static, never current, never navigable.
- `tabs` — peer views with no order and no completion.
- `progress` — continuous progress with no named steps.
- `flow-diagram` — a machine's stages, reported rather than navigated.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the step rail. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Steps`). |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `Stepper.Step` children, in the order they are numbered. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/stepper-step`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: an `index.ts` (beside `stepper.vue`) attaches the sub-component to the root so `<Stepper.Step>` resolves from one import; the standalone imports remain the tree-shaking path. The rail has no open/closed state, so there is no `Trigger` / `Content` — the anatomy name is `Step`, which is what the thing is. Numbering and the current step flow through `provide`/`inject` (`injection-key.ts`), so the consumer wires nothing: a step reads its own ordinal from its registration order and whether it is `active` from the root's `v-model`.

- `stepper-step/stepper-step.vue` — One dot, its title and description, and the connector down to the step below it.
  - Props: `value?: string` (default `''` — identity of this step; matches the root's `v-model` when it is the active one), `title?: string` (default `''` — what this step asks, in the reader's words), `description?: string` (default `''` — one line under the title saying what the step decides), `status?: 'pending' | 'running' | 'success' | 'error'` (default `'pending'` — what the owner knows about this step; the active step is derived from the root and is never set here), `disabled?: boolean` (default `false` — the step cannot be reached yet; not focusable and not clickable).
  - Slot: `default` — optional body under the description, inside the rail. It renders after the step's `button`, in the same `li` and aligned with the title column, so interactive content (a link, a Retry button) is never nested inside the button.

Resulting layout (no per-component `package.json`; the root `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` resolves every path, and `.d.ts` is generated at publish time):

```
packages/webkit/src/components/navigation/stepper/
├── stepper.vue                   (root; owns the model, provides the registry)
├── stepper.test.ts
├── index.ts                      (compound: attaches Step to the root)
├── injection-key.ts              (shared StepperContext)
├── composables/
│   └── use-stepper-context.ts    (injects; throws outside a Stepper)
└── stepper-step/
    └── stepper-step.vue
```

Exports to add to `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` (flat public names; category lives in the folder only):

```jsonc
"./stepper": "./src/components/navigation/stepper/index.ts",
"./stepper-root": "./src/components/navigation/stepper/stepper.vue",
"./stepper-step": "./src/components/navigation/stepper/stepper-step/stepper-step.vue"
```

`./stepper` and `./stepper-step` export the type `StepperStepStatus` (`'pending' | 'running' | 'success' | 'error'`), the type of `Stepper.Step`'s `status` prop, so an owner can type the status it derives.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The `value` of the step the reader is on, two-way through `defineModel`. A step whose `value` matches it derives `data-active` (`aria-current="step"`); activating an enabled step writes its own `value` back. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-status` on `Stepper.Step` mirrors `status`: `pending` | `running` | `success` | `error`
- `data-active` on the step the reader is on (unless it is `error` or `running`); `data-completed` on a `success` step that is not active
- `data-active` on the root mirrors `modelValue`
- Part markers: `data-slot="step-dot"`, `step-disc`, `step-description`, `step-connector`, `step-body`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-orientation`: `vertical`

The five dot looks, and what each one renders:

| Look | When | Dot | Connector below |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-status="pending"` | not reached, nothing known | outlined, muted, shows its number | muted track |
| `data-active` | `value` equals the root's `v-model` | outlined in `--secondary` with a filled inner disc | muted track |
| `data-completed` | the owner set `status="success"` | filled `--secondary`, `az az-check` glyph | filled `--secondary` |
| `data-status="error"` | the owner set `status="error"` | filled `--danger`, `az az-triangle-alert` glyph | muted track |
| `data-status="running"` | the owner set `status="running"` | outlined in `--secondary`, `Spinner` in place of the number | muted track |

`error` and `running` outrank active: a step that is both on screen and wrong must say it is wrong.
Active outranks `success`, so returning to an answered step shows where the reader is rather than
what they already did.

Two fixed measures hold the rail together. The title sits in a band the height of the dot, so a step
with no description reads as centred against its dot rather than hanging above it; and the connector
keeps a minimum segment the height of a dot, so the fill a completed step draws is always visible
even when the row carries nothing but its title.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves to each enabled step in order; `Enter` / `Space` activates the focused step and updates `v-model`. A `disabled` step is skipped by `Tab`. No roving tabindex — the rail is a list of links to steps, not a tablist.
- ARIA: the root is a `<nav>` with `aria-label` over an `<ol>`; each step is an `<li>` holding a `<button type="button">`. The active step's button carries `aria-current="step"`; a `running` step carries `aria-busy="true"`; a disabled step is natively `disabled`. The dot glyph and the connector are `aria-hidden="true"`, and each button carries an `sr-only` word naming its state so the rail reads as more than a list of titles.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every animated state
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the step button is a full-width row at least 40px tall

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Stepper from '@aziontech/webkit/stepper'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const step = ref('configure')
</script>

<template>
  <Stepper
    v-model="step"
    aria-label="Create network list"
  >
    <Stepper.Step
      value="host"
      title="Where it runs"
      description="The firewall that reads this list."
      status="success"
    />
    <Stepper.Step
      value="configure"
      title="Configure"
      description="Name it and add the addresses."
    />
    <Stepper.Step
      value="rules"
      title="Rules"
      description="What the firewall does with a match."
    />
    <Stepper.Step
      value="review"
      title="Review"
      description="Check the list before it goes live."
    />
  </Stepper>
```

# Tabs

> Switches between peer views of one page or panel, showing one at a time: Overview, Settings and Logs on a resource page. The tab row scrolls with edge fades when it outgrows its container, items can be closable or marked dirty, and the list follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with arrow-key navigation.

- Import: `import TabsRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/tabs-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Tabs from '@aziontech/webkit/tabs'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Tabs to switch between peer views of one page or panel; for the second-level navigation strip of a resource detail page use PageTabs.
- A page or panel holds several peer views and only one is shown at a time (Overview / Settings / Logs on a resource page).
- The tab row may outgrow its container — `Tabs.List` scrolls horizontally with edge fades instead of wrapping.
- Tabs that the user can close: set `closable` on the item and remove it from your data on `@close`.
- A tab whose form holds unsaved changes: set `dirty` on the item (bind it to `useUnsavedChanges().isDirty`) so the reader sees which section still needs a save.

## Do

- Give each `Tabs.Trigger` and its `Tabs.Content` the same `value`; the panel is linked to its tab by that value for `aria-labelledby` and visibility. `Tabs.Content` is the `role="tabpanel"`. The compound has exactly three parts, the shadcn / Radix names: `List`, `Trigger`, `Content` (6.0 removed the `Item`, `Panel` and `Root` members, synonyms of these).
- Any string or number is a valid `value`, spaces and punctuation included: the tab and panel ids are derived from it with every character outside `A-Z a-z 0-9 -` encoded, so `aria-controls` / `aria-labelledby` stay valid id tokens.
- Type a variable that holds the active tab or a list of tab definitions with the exported `TabsValue` (`ref<TabsValue>('overview')`), never `string | number` spelled out or a cast.
- Drive the active tab with `v-model` on the root, or seed it with `default-value`; with neither, the first enabled tab is selected on mount.
- `closable` only emits `close` with `(event, value)` — remove the tab and its panel from your data yourself; when the active tab unmounts, the root moves to the first enabled tab.
- `dirty` only marks the tab (a dot after the label, "Unsaved changes" for screen readers); guard the switch itself with `useUnsavedChanges().confirmLeave()` in the setter of the root's `v-model` when leaving must ask first.
- The selection always comes from the root's value. A row of pressed / unpressed pills outside a `Tabs` root is a `ToggleGroup`, not loose `Tabs.Trigger`s (6.0 removed the item's `selected` prop).
- Put spacing between the list and the panels on an element of your own around the panels (or on each `Tabs.Content`), not inside each panel. It always renders the panel and needs a `value` (6.0 removed its wrapper mode).
- Centre the tab row with `<Tabs.List align="center">`, never with a `justify-center` class or a centring wrapper; keep the default `start` for tabs that head a resource page or a settings form.

## Don’t

- Several sections may need to be open at once, or the content should expand inline → use `accordion`.
- The tabs switch the media of a marketing band → use `media-tabs`.
- It moves the reader between pages of the app → use `navigation-menu` or `sidebar`.

## Related

- `accordion` — stacked disclosure sections; more than one can be open and content expands below each header.
- `media-tabs` — the marketing band that switches an illustration per tab.
- `breadcrumb` — location in a hierarchy, not sibling views.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultValue` | `TabsValue \| null` | `null` | false | Initial active tab when uncontrolled. |
| `activationMode` | `'automatic' \| 'manual'` | `'automatic'` | false | `automatic` selects a tab as the arrow keys focus it; `manual` only moves focus, and `Enter` or `Space` selects (APG tabs with manual activation, for panels that are slow to render). |
| `modelValue` | `TabsValue \| null \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | — |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/tabs-list`
- `@aziontech/webkit/tabs-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/tabs-content`

## Sub-components

- `tabs-trigger.vue` — Public sub-component `tabs-trigger` (`@aziontech/webkit/tabs-trigger`), attached as `Tabs.Trigger`.
- `tabs-list.vue` — Public sub-component `tabs-list` (`@aziontech/webkit/tabs-list`), attached as `Tabs.List`.
- `tabs-content.vue` — Public sub-component `tabs-content` (`@aziontech/webkit/tabs-content`), attached as `Tabs.Content`.
- The root file is `tabs.vue`; `@aziontech/webkit/tabs-root` resolves to it with no part attached (the tree-shaking path).
- Every part spreads the consumer's attributes (`id`, `aria-*`, `dir`, `data-*`, listeners) on its own root element (`inheritAttrs: false` + `v-bind="$attrs"`), with `class` merged through `cn`.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `TabsValue \| null \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Active tab via `defineModel`. While unbound (`undefined`) the root is uncontrolled: it starts at `defaultValue`, else the first enabled tab. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values on panels: `active` | `inactive`
- Root: `data-tabs-root` (and the legacy `data-tab-view-root`, kept for selectors written against the v5 name).
- Panel motion: the incoming panel's inner element carries `data-motion="enter"` and `data-slide="start|end"` for the frame before it slides in; the attributes drop on the next animation frame.
- Dirty: `data-dirty` on a `Tabs.Trigger` with `dirty`; the dot is not the only cue for assistive tech (a hidden "Unsaved changes" joins the tab's name).
- Responsive: the tab list (`Tabs.List`) scrolls **horizontally** when the tabs exceed the available width (mobile / narrow viewports) instead of overflowing or wrapping; the scrollbar is visually hidden and the active indicator stays aligned while scrolling. Tabs keep their intrinsic width (`shrink-0`). A gradient edge-fade overlay on the scrollable side(s) (mirrored on `data-fade-start` / `data-fade-end`) hints at off-screen tabs; it fades in / out with the semantic `animate-fade-in` / `animate-fade-out` utilities, and a non-scrollable edge renders no overlay so the first / last tab is never covered at rest.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map (inside `Tabs.List`): `Tab` moves into the list onto the selected tab and out of it to the panel (roving `tabindex`: only the selected tab is `0`); `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` select and focus the next/previous enabled tab in DOM order (a tab inserted later with `v-if`, or moved by a keyed list, takes its rendered place) and wrap, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`useDirection`); `Home`/`End` select the first/last enabled tab; `Enter`/`Space` activate the focused tab; with `activationMode="manual"` the arrow keys and `Home`/`End` move focus only, from the focused tab, and the selection changes on `Enter`/`Space` or a click; `Delete` on a `closable` tab emits `close` (the tab carries `aria-keyshortcuts="Delete"`). Focus after a close is the consumer's call (the neighbouring tab, as `split-view#Sessions` does).
- Close control: the `closable` glyph is a pointer target only (`aria-hidden="true"`, no role, no `tabindex`, a `title` with "Close tab"); keyboard and screen-reader users close with `Delete`, the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern. A focusable close button cannot sit next to the tab: anything focusable inside `role="tablist"` that is not a `tab` fails axe `aria-required-children` (unallowed child), and inside the tab it is `nested-interactive`.
- ARIA: inside `Tabs.List` each item is `role="tab"` with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls` (when its panel is mounted); a `Tabs.Trigger` rendered on its own, outside any `Tabs`, is a toggle `<button>` with `aria-pressed` and no `tab` role, because a `tab` outside a `tablist` fails `aria-required-parent`. `Tabs.Content` is `role="tabpanel"` labelled by its tab.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state. The dirty dot is `var(--warning-foreground)` (≥3:1 on the canvas in both themes) and the tab's accessible name carries "Unsaved changes", so colour is never the only cue.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target: the tab item is 32 px tall (`var(--size-8)`) — a justified deviation from 40×40 px matching the Figma tab-item size token, mitigated by the full label + padding being the hit area and by the tab list's own keyboard model.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Tabs from '@aziontech/webkit/tabs'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const active = ref('tab-1')
</script>

<template>
  <Tabs
    v-model="active"
    class="w-full max-w-[40rem]"
  >
    <Tabs.List>
      <Tabs.Trigger
        value="tab-1"
        label="Tab Item"
      />
      <Tabs.Trigger
        value="tab-2"
        label="Tab Item"
      />
      <Tabs.Trigger
        value="tab-3"
        label="Tab Item"
      />
    </Tabs.List>
    <div class="mt-(--spacing-4) w-full">
      <Tabs.Content value="tab-1">
        <div class="rounded-(--shape-card) border border-(--border-default) p-(--spacing-4)">
          <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-default)">Content for tab 1</p>
        </div>
      </Tabs.Content>
      <Tabs.Content value="tab-2">
        <div class="rounded-(--shape-card) border border-(--border-default) p-(--spacing-4)">
          <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-default)">Content for tab 2</p>
        </div>
      </Tabs.Content>
      <Tabs.Content value="tab-3">
        <div class="rounded-(--shape-card) border border-(--border-default) p-(--spacing-4)">
          <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-default)">Content for tab 3</p>
        </div>
      </Tabs.Content>
    </div>
  </Tabs>
</template>
```
