<!-- components/popover.md -->

# Popover

> Anchored, **non-modal** overlay that opens from a consumer-supplied trigger and renders rich, interactive content — a header (title + optional description + close), a free-form body, and a footer for actions — in a floating panel anchored to the trigger. Use for inline forms, filter builders, and contextual detail or confirmation that needs interactive children. Unlike `tooltip` (plain text, non-interactive) and `dialog` (modal, centered, focus-trapped), the popover leaves the page interactive, anchors to its trigger, and closes on `Esc` or outside-click. It differs from `dropdown-menu`, which renders a menu of selectable options rather than free-form content.

- Import: `import PopoverRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Popover from '@aziontech/webkit/popover'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: app · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Use Popover for rich or interactive content (a form, actions) opened by a click and closed on purpose; a one-line hint is a Tooltip and a read-only hover preview is a HoverCard.
- Interactive content anchored to a trigger while the page stays usable: an inline form, a filter builder, a quick edit of one field.
- Contextual detail or a light confirmation that needs buttons or links inside it.

## Do

- Place `Popover.Trigger` first and `Popover.Content` after it. The trigger wires `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and the click toggle onto your element, so don't bind them yourself.
- Let `Popover.Trigger` show the pointer: its wrapper sets `cursor-pointer` (`cursor-not-allowed` when disabled), so a `Tag`, `Avatar` or icon slotted in reads as clickable. Don't put `cursor-pointer` on the slotted WebKit component — `webkit/no-style-override` blocks it.
- Include a `Popover.Title`. The panel takes its accessible name from it through `aria-labelledby`.
- Set `size` for forms and filter builders so the panel doesn't resize as content changes. Without it, the panel sizes fluidly between the `--container-3xs` and `--container-xs` tokens.
- Use `side="auto"` for triggers that can sit near a viewport edge.
- Use `side="end"` (or `"start"`) for a trigger in a narrow column or a sidebar, where the panel should open beside the trigger instead of covering the content below it. `start` and `end` follow the text direction, so the panel opens on the inline end in both `ltr` and `rtl`. Type a side held in a variable with the exported `PopoverSide` (and `PopoverAlign` for the alignment), never a cast.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open` (or `:open` + `@update:open`, whose handler receives a `boolean`).
- Set `dismissible` to `false` only when an outside click would discard input. Then give the user a way out: `Popover.Close` or a footer action.

## Don’t

- A short, non-interactive hint on hover or focus → use `tooltip`.
- A list of actions or options to pick from → use `dropdown-menu`.
- Choosing a form value from a list → use `select`.
- A blocking task that must be completed or cancelled first → use `dialog`.
- A long form or a secondary workflow → use `drawer`.

## Related

- `tooltip` — plain text only and non-interactive; opens on hover and focus, not on click.
- `dropdown-menu` — same trigger and anchoring model, but renders option rows and emits `select`.
- `dialog` — modal and centered, traps focus and locks scroll; the popover does neither.
- `drawer` — edge-anchored modal panel for longer content.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | `PopoverSide \| 'auto'` | `'bottom'` | false | Side of the trigger the panel opens on, flipped when it does not fit; `'auto'` picks the side with the most room at open time. |
| `align` | `PopoverAlign` | `'start'` | false | Alignment along the trigger edge. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `4` | false | Pixel gap between the trigger and the panel. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prevents the trigger from opening the panel and applies disabled tokens. |
| `size` | ``PopoverSize` (`'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'`)` | `undefined` | false | Panel width preset mapped to container tokens: `'small'` (`var(--container-xs)`), `'medium'` (`var(--container-sm)`), `'large'` (`var(--container-md)`). When omitted, the panel sizes fluidly between `var(--container-3xs)` and `var(--container-xs)`. Same name as the size preset of `Dialog`, `Drawer` and `ConfirmDialog`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound). |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Light-dismiss: when `true`, the panel closes on outside-click and `Esc`. Set `false` to keep it open until the trigger or `PopoverClose` closes it. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Place `<Popover.Trigger>` followed by `<Popover.Content>`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-close`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-footer`

## Sub-components

The root `Popover` owns open/closed state, anchoring/placement (exposing the computed `panelStyle`), outside-click + `Esc` dismissal, focus entry on open, Tab hand-off and focus return. Shared state flows through `provide`/`inject` (`isOpen`, `triggerId`, `contentId`, `titleId`, `descriptionId`, `setOpen`, resolved `side` and `align`, `size`, `panelStyle`, and the `panelEl` that `Popover.Content` assigns), so every sub-component is context-aware and the consumer wires nothing. **`Popover.Content` renders the single teleported, animated floating panel with its content inline** (the Select / Tooltip pattern — one `<Teleport>` + `<Transition>`, so the scale animation carries the whole panel on enter/leave); the panel element carries `role="dialog"`, the surface/border/radius/shadow tokens, the open/close `animate-popup-scale-*`, `--popup-origin` (via `panelStyle`), and `data-state` / `data-side` / `data-align`, and assigns itself to the root's `panelEl` so the root's placement/focus logic operates on it. Member names mirror this component's anatomy; `Trigger` / `Content` are valid here because the popover has a real `data-state="open|closed"`.

- `popover-trigger/popover-trigger.vue` — as-child trigger.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_ (the root handles `update:open`).
  - Slots: `default` with scope `{ isOpen: boolean }` — the consumer's trigger element. The trigger forwards aria + click; the consumer must not bind those itself.
- `popover-content/popover-content.vue` — renders the floating panel via a single `<Teleport to="body">` + `<Transition>`, with its default slot (`Popover.Header`, the free-form body, `Popover.Footer`) arranged inline a…
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the popover anatomy (`Popover.Header`, body content, `Popover.Footer`).
- `popover-header/popover-header.vue` — full-width header region with a bottom divider and `py var(--spacing-sm)` / `px var(--spacing-md)` padding, laid out as a row with the title/description block on the left and the…
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — `Popover.Title`, optional `Popover.Description`, and `Popover.Close`.
- `popover-title/popover-title.vue` — title text (`.text-body-sm`, `var(--text-default)`).
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — plain-text title.
- `popover-description/popover-description.vue` — supporting description text (`.text-body-xs`, `var(--text-muted)`).
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — plain-text description.
- `popover-close/popover-close.vue` — close control.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_ (root handles `update:open`).
  - Slots: _none_.
- `popover-footer/popover-footer.vue` — full-width footer region with a top divider and `py var(--spacing-sm)` / `px var(--spacing-md)` padding.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — action buttons (e.g. Cancel / Apply).

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void`. Fires on every open/closed transition: trigger toggle, `Popover.Close`, `Esc`, and outside-click. While unbound (`undefined`) the popover is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values (root, trigger, floating panel): `open` | `closed`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on root and trigger
- Cursor: the trigger wrapper shows `pointer`, and `not-allowed` with `data-disabled`
- `data-size` on the floating panel mirrors `size`
- `data-side` / `data-align` on the root mirror the `side` / `align` props (`'auto'` stays as `'auto'`)
- `data-side` / `data-align` on the floating panel mirror the resolved side and alignment after flipping (`'auto'` resolves to `'bottom'` or `'top'`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the trigger and the close button.
- Keyboard map:
  - On the trigger: `Enter` / `Space` toggles the panel. When it opens (by click or key), focus **moves to the first focusable element in the panel**; when the panel has none, focus stays where it was. A panel that is open on first render (`defaultOpen`, a bound `open`) does not take focus.
  - `Esc` closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger, from anywhere (trigger or panel).
  - `Tab` from the trigger moves to the first panel control. `Shift+Tab` on the first panel control returns to the trigger and keeps the panel open. `Tab` past the last panel control closes the panel and moves focus to the next focusable element after the trigger in the page (or, inside a `Dialog` / `Drawer`, inside that overlay, wrapping to its first control), so keyboard users can always leave a non-modal popover.
  - Outside-click closes the panel; focus is not forced back to the trigger on outside-click.
  - Nested overlays: the popover joins the shared overlay layer stack (`useOverlayLayer`) while open, so only the top layer handles `Esc`, `Tab` and outside-click. A popover opened from a `Dialog` closes on `Esc` without closing the dialog. A `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `DropdownMenu`, `Combobox` or `Tooltip` opened inside the panel is a higher layer even though it teleports to `body`: a pointer-down inside its list never counts as outside the popover, and `Esc` closes that list first, the popover on the next `Esc`.
  - Tests: `popover.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec), portalled children (overlay layer stack).
  - A text `<input>` or `<textarea>` as the trigger control keeps its textbox role and gets none of `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded` or `aria-controls`, which ARIA does not allow on a textbox (`aria-allowed-attr`); a field that opens suggestions should be a `Combobox`.
- ARIA: the slotted control (or the wrapper, when the slot has none) exposes `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, with a single tab stop and in the server HTML; the floating panel (rendered by the root) uses `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="false"`, `aria-labelledby` pointing at the `Popover.Title` id (without a title, at the trigger control's id, so the dialog always has a name) and `aria-describedby` pointing at the `Popover.Description` id (when present); `Popover.Close` is an `IconButton` with `aria-label="Close"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including the disabled trigger state (validated via `--text-muted` / `--text-disabled` tokens).
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on `animate-popup-scale-*`; `motion-reduce:transition-none` on `transition-colors` for hover/focus states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the trigger (consumer's element — flagged in docs); the close `IconButton` follows `IconButton`'s own target sizing.
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="dialog"` panel binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.
- `PopoverHeader` keeps its `header` tag with `role="none"`, so an open popover does not expose a `banner` landmark (pinned by `src/test/screen-reader.test.ts`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import PopoverClose from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-close'
  import PopoverContent from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-content'
  import PopoverHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-header'
  import PopoverRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-root'
  import PopoverTitle from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-title'
  import PopoverTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-trigger'
</script>

<template>
  <PopoverRoot>
    <PopoverTrigger>
      <Button
        variant="secondary"
        label="Open popover"
      />
    </PopoverTrigger>

    <PopoverContent>
      <PopoverHeader>
        <PopoverTitle>Popover title</PopoverTitle>
        <PopoverClose />
      </PopoverHeader>

      <div class="p-(--spacing-md) text-body-sm text-(--text-default)">
        This content is rendered inside the popover panel.
      </div>
    </PopoverContent>
  </PopoverRoot>
</template>
```

<!-- components/tooltip.md -->

# Tooltip

> Surfaces a short hint anchored to a trigger element when the user hovers, focuses, or long-presses it. Use for icon-only buttons, abbreviations, or any control whose meaning is not obvious from its label alone. **Not** for rich content or interactive children — use `popover` instead.

- Import: `import Tooltip from '@aziontech/webkit/tooltip'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Use Tooltip for a one-line plain-text name or hint on a control, shown on hover or focus; it cannot hold links. For rich or interactive content opened by a click use Popover; for a read-only rich preview on hover use HoverCard.
- Naming an icon-only control on hover and focus.
- Revealing the full text of a truncated label, or expanding an abbreviation.
- One short, plain-text hint that the user can do without.

## Do

- Wrap a focusable element. The tooltip opens on the wrapper's `focusin`, and the wrapper itself is not focusable.
- Keep `content` to a few words. It renders as plain text, with no markup.
- The tooltip describes its trigger (`aria-describedby`) but does not name it. Icon-only triggers still need their own accessible name.
- Use `disabled` to suppress the tooltip. An empty `content` also blocks opening, but it reads as a bug.
- Keep the default `delay` (200 ms) unless a dense toolbar needs a longer one.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.

## Don’t

- The content has links, buttons or more than one line of structure → use `popover`.
- An info glyph beside a field label or column header → use `hint`.
- A read-only rich preview (a definition, a glossed term in documentation prose) → use `hover-card`.
- Guidance or errors the user needs to complete a field → use `field-error`.

## Related

- `popover` — click-opened, interactive, with a header, body and footer.
- `hint` — the focusable info glyph that renders a `Tooltip` for you.
- `hover-card` — read-only rich preview on hover or focus; DocMarkdown's `<Tooltip>` tag renders one.
- `icon-button` — the most common trigger; it still needs its own `ariaLabel`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `string` | `—` | true | Plain text shown inside the tooltip. |
| `side` | `'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'start' \| 'end' \| 'auto'` | `'top'` | false | Side of the trigger the tooltip opens on, flipped when it does not fit; `'auto'` picks the side with the most room at open time. |
| `align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | `'center'` | false | Alignment along the trigger edge. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `8` | false | Pixel gap between the trigger and the tooltip. |
| `delay` | `number` | `200` | false | Hover-open delay in milliseconds. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables tooltip activation. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The trigger element. Tooltip anchors to its bounding box. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void` and fires once per open/closed transition (hover, focus, `Esc`). While unbound the tooltip is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-side`: `top` | `bottom` | `start` | `end` — the side the panel landed on after flipping, on the trigger wrapper and the panel
- `data-align`: `start` | `center` | `end` — the alignment the panel landed on
- `start` and `end` follow the text direction: under `dir="rtl"`, `side="start"` opens on the right and `align="start"` lines the panel up with the trigger's right edge
- `data-anchored` on the panel once its opening position has landed — the flag that lets a re-anchor animate while the entrance stays the open animation

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the trigger wrapper.
- Hoverable (WCAG 1.4.13): the panel takes the pointer. Leaving the trigger closes the tooltip after a 100 ms grace, and entering the panel within the grace keeps it open (so text can be read under magnification); leaving the panel closes it after the same grace. Tests: `tooltip.test.ts` › hoverable content.
- Touch: a long-press (500 ms `pointerdown` with `pointerType` `touch`) opens the tooltip; it hides 1.5 s after the finger lifts. A mouse press never opens it.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` onto the trigger opens the tooltip at once (no hover delay); `Escape` closes it and focus stays on the trigger; `Tab` away closes it; the tooltip never takes or traps focus. Tests: `tooltip.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- Nested overlays: while open, the tooltip joins the shared overlay layer stack (`useOverlayLayer`) as a transient layer (it never takes focus, so it does not pause a dialog's focus trap). Inside a `Dialog`, `Drawer` or `Popover`, the first `Escape` closes only the tooltip; the next one reaches the host. Tests: `tooltip.test.ts` › inside an open Dialog, Escape closes only the tooltip.
- ARIA: `role="tooltip"` on the panel; the slotted control references the panel via `aria-describedby` (merged into a WebKit `Button` / `IconButton` or native control at render, otherwise forwarded onto the first focusable element in the slot after mount; on the wrapper only when the slot has none). The wrapper itself has no `role` and no tab stop. `aria-hidden="true"` when `data-state="closed"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 — text against surface verified in both light and dark modes.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the panel; reduced-motion users get instant show/hide.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the trigger (the consumer's responsibility — flag in docs).
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="tooltip"` panel binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Tooltip from '@aziontech/webkit/tooltip'
</script>

<template>
  <Tooltip
    content="This is a Tooltip"
    side="top"
  >
    <Button
      label="Hover me"
      variant="outline"
      size="medium"
    />
  </Tooltip>
</template>
```

<!-- components/webkit-provider.md -->

# Webkit Provider

> Sets the language and text direction of every WebKit component below it. It wraps the app once, at the root, with the user's BCP 47 locale: components then read their built-in strings (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) from the locale catalog and format dates, numbers, file sizes, relative times and plurals with `Intl` for that locale. English is built in; Portuguese (`@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR`) and Spanish (`@aziontech/webkit/locales/es`) are separate entries the app imports and passes through `catalogs`, so an English-only app does not ship them. The catalogs are static imports, so the server and the client render the same strings and hydration never flips after the first render. Digits are Latin unless the tag picks a numbering system (`ar-u-nu-arab`): engines ship different CLDR defaults (Node and Chromium format `ar` with Latin digits, Safari with Arabic-Indic ones), so every `Intl` formatter receives the tag through `intlLocale`, and server and client render the same text. By default everything follows the person's device: an unset `locale` (and every component with no provider mounted) uses the device locale (`navigator.language`) for the `Intl` formats and picks its catalog when one is registered, falling back to English text. The server cannot know the device, so the server render and the hydrating client render `en-US`, and the device locale applies right after mount; an explicit `locale` (the user's saved choice) renders the same on both from the start. Only what people read follows the device: values that components hand back through `v-model` stay unambiguous (Calendar a `Date`, DateRangePicker ISO 8601 instants, TagEditor `key`/`value` pairs). It also carries the reference time of relative times (`now`), so a page that must render the same text on the server and the client, or an example, fixes it once instead of on every cell. The element it renders carries `lang` and `dir`.

- Import: `import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'`
- Category: provider · Surface: app · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Once at the root of every app, with the catalogs of the languages the app offers; pass `locale` when the user chose one (`pt-BR`, `en`, `es`), leave it unset to follow the device.
- Around one region that must read in another language than the rest of the page (a preview of an email in the customer's language).
- To rename a built-in string for the whole app (`messages`), instead of passing the same label prop to every instance.

## Do

- Mount one `WebkitProvider` at the app root and pass the locale the user chose, or leave it unset to follow the device; do not nest one per page.
- Register every language the app offers in `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), imported from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/<tag>`; a `pt-BR` or `es` locale with no registered catalog falls back to English and warns once in development.
- Use a full BCP 47 tag (`pt-BR`, not `pt`); a tag with no registered catalog falls back to the same language, then to English.
- Override built-in strings through `messages` (partial, deep-merged), not by forking components.
- Leave `dir` on `auto`: Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu locales turn the subtree right-to-left (a device locale does so only when its catalog is registered, so English text never reads right-to-left).
- Leave `now` unset in an app: relative times then read the real clock and `TableCellTime` re-renders every minute. Set it to a fixed moment where the text must not depend on when it renders: an example or a test (`const NOW = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 10, 12)`, sample dates counted back from it), or a server render whose markup the browser hydrates. Never compute that moment from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup: the server and the browser read different clocks.

## Don’t

- Translating your own product copy (titles, descriptions, button labels you pass in) → keep it in your app's own i18n; the provider only covers the strings WebKit ships.
- Changing one instance's label → pass the component's label prop (`aria-label`, `confirm-label`); a prop always wins over the catalog.
- Only flipping the layout for a right-to-left language → still use the provider with that locale; `dir` follows it.

## Related

- `use-locale` — the composable components use to read the active locale, translate a key and format with `Intl`; use it in your own components to match WebKit's formatting.
- `pagination` — reads its labels and the "Showing x to y of z" line from the catalog.
- `confirm-dialog` — reads Confirm and Cancel from the catalog when no label is passed.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `locale` | `string` | `''` | false | BCP 47 locale of everything below the provider; picks the catalog from `catalogs` (English is built in) and the `Intl` formats. Empty follows the device locale, `en-US` on the server and until mount. |
| `catalogs` | `Record<string, Messages>` | `undefined` | false | Extra catalogs keyed by locale tag, imported from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/<tag>` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`); a locale with no catalog falls back to English. |
| `messages` | `PartialMessages` | `undefined` | false | Partial catalog deep-merged over the built-in one, keyed by component group (`{ pagination: { next: 'Seguinte' } }`). |
| `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl' \| 'auto'` | `'auto'` | false | Text direction of the subtree; `auto` derives it from the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left). |
| `now` | `string \| number \| Date` | `undefined` | false | Reference time for every relative time below the provider (`TableCellTime`, `useLocale().formatRelativeTime`, the day groups of `ConversationHistory`, the relative ranges of `DateRangePicker` when their own `now` is unset); unset reads the real clock, ticking each minute. |
| `timeZone` | `string` | `''` | false | IANA time zone every `Timestamp` below the provider shows its local time in, and every `DateRangePicker` with no `v-model:time-zone` formats in (`America/New_York`, `UTC`), for an app-wide time zone picker; empty reads the browser's zone. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The app, or the part of it that shares this locale. |

## States

- No visual states; the root carries `lang` (the locale) and `dir` (`ltr` | `rtl`).
- `locale` unset: `lang` and the formats are `en-US` in the server render and during hydration, then the device locale after mount.
- `now` set: every relative time below reads it instead of the real clock; changing it re-renders them. An empty or unparseable value reads the real clock.
- `timeZone` set: every `Timestamp` below shows its local time in that zone and renders it on the server too, and every `DateRangePicker` without its own `timeZone` formats and edits its range in it; `useLocale().formatDate` and the other formatters are unchanged. Empty reads the browser's zone after mount.

## Accessibility

- `lang` on the root lets screen readers pick the right voice and pronunciation (WCAG 3.1.1 / 3.1.2).
- `dir` on the root mirrors reading order for right-to-left languages.
- Overlays that teleport to `body` (Dialog, Drawer, Popover, Tooltip, DropdownMenu, Select, MultiSelect, Toaster, DatePicker, DateRangePicker, PropertyFilter, NavigationMenu.Viewport, the doc overlays) read the provider through `usePortalLocale()` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-locale`) and set the same `dir` and `lang` on their teleported root, so they do not fall back to the document's direction and language. A consumer's own `<Teleport>` does the same with `v-bind="usePortalLocale().value"` on its root.
- Every assistive label WebKit ships (close buttons, pagination, sort state, empty states) is read in the provider's language.
- No focusable element of its own; it adds no role and no landmark.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import ConfirmDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/confirm-dialog'
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import PaginationRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-root'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const page = ref(1)
  const open = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider
    locale="pt-BR"
    :catalogs="{ 'pt-BR': ptBR }"
  >
    <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md)">
      <PaginationRoot
        v-model:page="page"
        :total="120"
      />
      <ConfirmDialog
        v-model:open="open"
        title="Remover domínio"
        description="shop.example.com deixa de responder por este recurso."
        size="small"
        @confirm="open = false"
      >
        <template #trigger>
          <Button
            label="Remover domínio"
            variant="outline"
            size="medium"
          />
        </template>
      </ConfirmDialog>
    </div>
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>
```
